cards.title: Geometric coordination of endothelial invasion and vascular patterning during epithelial morphogenesis
cards.abstract: As organs grow and remodel in three dimensions, developing vascular networks extend through the tissue while maintaining spatial coordination and establishing connections between distant sprouts. How local endothelial behavior generates vascular patterns within such deforming environments remains poorly understood. Here, using the developing mouse epididymis, we combine two-photon live microscopy, pharmacological perturbations, and mathematical modeling to investigate angiogenesis alongside epithelial tubule folding. Endothelial cells invade the organ interior while maintaining proximity to the deforming tubule. Live imaging reveals dynamic protrusions directed toward the epithelium and a characteristic sequence in which endothelial fronts approach the tubule, stop, and maintain their separation despite continued folding. ERK activity promotes endothelial extension and declines during the transition to distance maintenance. From these observations, we derive a minimal follow-and-stop rule that captures endothelial positioning relative to the changing epithelium. Extending this model to three dimensions reveals how epithelial folding can bring otherwise distant endothelial fronts together, creating opportunities for vascular connection. Explants exhibiting greater three-dimensional folding also show a higher observed frequency of endothelial connections. Our findings support a geometric framework in which local endothelial dynamics and tissue-scale deformation can jointly contribute to vascular patterning during organ morphogenesis.

cards.title: Cellular and molecular census of the pleiotropic disease locus Negr1 in zebrafish
cards.abstract: A major challenge in precision medicine is to understand the cellular origin of disease-causing genetic alterations. One prominent example is the Negr1 locus, where common non-coding variants are associated with an unusually broad range of human traits and conditions, including body mass index (BMI), major depression, schizophrenia, autism-spectrum conditions and anorexia. Yet, no coding loss-of-function allele has been established as causal. These observations suggest that distinct Negr1-expressing cell populations underlie distinct traits. However, this hypothesis is difficult to test in tractable experimental systems without first determining where this gene may act. To overcome this limitation, we generated a knock-in reporter at the zebrafish Negr1 locus and combined single-cell transcriptomics with whole-brain registration and single-neuron projection mapping. We found that Negr1 is expressed in a graded manner across neuronal classes of the brain and retina, radial glia and astrocyte-like cells, and most consistently in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Projection mapping suggests three conserved hubs formed by olfactory bulb projection neurons, tectal periventricular projection neurons and cerebellar eurydendroid cells. Our findings are consistent with the idea that Negr1 pleiotropy arises from dose perturbation of a rather broadly expressed gene. More generally, this integrative approach to produce granular multimodal datasets should enable high-resolution etiological studies in models of human disease.

cards.title: Obesity and skeletal fragility: revisiting an old paradigm.
cards.abstract: Obesity has traditionally been considered protective against osteoporosis because of its association with higher bone mineral density (BMD). However, emerging evidence demonstrates that individuals with obesity remain at increased risk of peripheral fractures despite preserved BMD. This review summarizes current evidence on the complex relationship between obesity and skeletal health, including underlying mechanisms, fracture patterns, assessment strategies, and management considerations. Studies indicate that fracture risk in obesity is site-specific, with a greater propensity for peripheral fractures. Visceral adiposity, bone marrow adipose tissue, chronic low-grade inflammation, altered adipokine signaling, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and obesity-related comorbidities contribute to impaired bone quality and skeletal fragility. Conventional Dual Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) may underestimate skeletal risk in obesity, while newer tools such as trabecular bone score (TBS) version 4.0, peripheral quantitative computerized tomography (pQCT) may improve risk assessment. Weight-loss interventions, including lifestyle modification, Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA), and bariatric surgery, provide substantial metabolic benefits but may increase fracture risk if skeletal health is not adequately addressed. Obesity should no longer be regarded as protective for bone health. Although BMD is often normal or elevated, obesity is associated with alterations in bone quality and increased fracture susceptibility. Comprehensive skeletal assessment, incorporation of lifestyle measures to preserve bone health, and appropriate osteoporosis therapy are essential. Future research should focus on obesity-specific fracture prediction tools, advanced imaging modalities, and dedicated clinical guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis, and management of osteoporosis in individuals with obesity.

cards.title: Preserving Nanotherapy-Induced Allogeneic Murine Islet Graft Tolerance During Distal Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Skin Infection
cards.abstract: Eliminating lifelong immunosuppression can make islet transplantation a durable alternative to insulin therapy for type 1 diabetes. As short-course tolerogenic regimens are developed to replace lifelong immunosuppression, it is critical to test their robustness against perturbations such as hospital-acquired infections, which transplant recipients routinely encounter. Herein, we investigated whether rapamycin-loaded polymersomes (rPS), a subcutaneous nanotherapy that induces long-term murine islet allograft survival, can preserve host defenses in a Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin infection, and whether the resulting immune response from this distal infection relative to graft location erodes rPS-induced tolerance. rPS maintained neutrophil antibacterial activity despite inhibiting oxidative mechanisms in vitro, and rPS-treated mice demonstrated normal recovery following MRSA challenge. However, MRSA skin infection caused a decline of ~43% in recipient survival for rPS-treated mice, despite surviving recipients retaining glucose-stimulated insulin responsiveness. This erosion of allograft acceptance coincided with a burst of IL-6 within 24h of the infection followed by elevated TNF-[a] and neutrophilia at 13 days post-infection. Combining rPS with a single dose of methylprednisolone reduced IL-6 and TNF- without altering neutrophilia, nearly doubling survival among infected recipients to 80%. Our findings demonstrate that partial dampening of inflammatory insults can restore superior islet allograft acceptance following perioperative infection.

cards.title: N-terminal cysteine independent effects of oxidative stress on the stability of RGS4 and 5
cards.abstract: Oxidative post-translational modifications on the sulfhydryl group of cysteines can occur spontaneously or enzymatically. The enzymatic dioxygenation of N-terminal cysteines has emerged as a new oxygen sensing paradigm, catalysed by 2-aminoethanethiol dioxygenase (ADO) in mammals. Conflicting evidence has been reported in recent years on whether this reaction can occur spontaneously in the absence of ADO. Here we sought to address whether cellular oxidative stress can interfere with ADO-catalysed N-terminal cysteine dioxygenation. Using a system to produce titratable intracellular levels of H2O2, we demonstrate that the stability of RGS4 and 5 is not affected by physiological levels of oxidative stress, whether ADO is present or not. However, cytotoxic levels of oxidative stress induced by tert-butyl hydroperoxide did induce a substantial increase in RGS4/5 protein stability that occurred independently of the Cys N-degron pathway. This effect of tBHP was abolished by Fe2+ chelation, lysosomal pH perturbation, and lipid peroxide scavenging. We conclude that N-terminal cysteine dependent proteolysis of RGS4/5 is not sensitive to physiological oxidative stress, but these proteins can be stabilised during the process of oxidative stress-induced cell death through an N-terminal cysteine independent mechanism.

cards.title: LCN2+ Astrocytes Mark a Pro-inflammatory Astrocyte State Associated with Secondary Brain Injury After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis
cards.abstract: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is a cerebrovascular disorder with unique pathophysiological characteristics. Although the mortality rate during the acute phase has declined in recent years, the cellular mechanisms underlying secondary brain injury and long-term neurological dysfunction after CVT remain poorly understood [1,2]. In this study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of brain tissues from a murine CVT model to systematically characterize the cellular landscape following CVT and identified a reactive astrocyte state characterized by high expression of Lcn2. This astrocyte subset was markedly enriched after CVT. Notably, despite the absence of significant changes in the overall proportion of astrocytes, this population exhibited enhanced inflammatory/cytokine response signatures, ferroptosis-related stress responses, and vascular-immune microenvironment remodeling programs, suggesting that the major alteration of astrocytes after CVT is driven primarily by state transition rather than cellular expansion. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that Lcn2+ astrocytes were predominantly localized at the late stage of the trajectory and displayed sustained upregulation of multiple inflammation- and stress-associated genes, supporting their characterization as a late-stage reactive astrocyte state under CVT conditions. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed extensive predicted interactions between this subset and myeloid cells, vascular-associated cells, as well as neuronal/synaptic populations, indicating its potential involvement in dynamic remodeling of the lesion microenvironment. Cross-model integration analysis further revealed the presence of Lcn2-high astrocytes in the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model; however, their expression breadth and intensity were generally weaker than those observed in CVT, suggesting that this cellular state may represent a common reactive framework following cerebrovascular obstruction, while being particularly pronounced in CVT. Furthermore, genetic deletion of LCN2 alleviated CVT-induced brain tissue injury in vivo, providing functional evidence supporting the detrimental role of the LCN2-associated pathological state. Collectively, our study identifies a distinct Lcn2-high reactive astrocyte state after CVT that is closely associated with inflammatory amplification, ferroptosis-related stress, and microenvironmental remodeling. These findings provide new cellular insights into the mechanisms underlying secondary brain injury after CVT and highlight potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

cards.title: Biological age uncertainty reveals discordant aging and predicts human healthspan
cards.abstract: Biological aging clocks typically summarize complex biological profiles as a single age estimate, yet how uncertain these estimates are and whether this uncertainty represents a distinct, biologically meaningful dimension of human aging remain unclear. Here, we develop a probabilistic framework across nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolomic, plasma proteomic and routine blood test (RBT) profiles in more than 450,000 UK Biobank participants to derive biological age gap (BAG) and biological age uncertainty (BAU) from the mean and width of predicted-age distributions. BAU was weakly correlated with BAG and increased with age-signal disagreement across individual molecules and organs, linking uncertainty to discordant aging across biological systems. Higher BAU predicted mortality, loss of healthspan and multimorbidity independently of BAG, with mortality hazard ratios of 1.24 (95% CI, 1.23-1.26) and 1.40 (95% CI, 1.37-1.43) per standard deviation for NMR- and proteomic-derived BAU, respectively. Adding BAU to conventional clinical models improved 10-year risk discrimination; moreover, longitudinal increases in NMR-derived BAU tracked subsequent health decline, and mortality associations were replicated using RBT-derived BAU across three independent external cohorts. Multi-omics and physiological analyses linked BAU to inflammation, metabolic dysregulation and tissue remodeling beyond BAG. Genetic analyses further revealed overlapping but distinct architectures of BAU and BAG, with BAU showing stronger genetic correlations with frailty and cardiometabolic diseases, and tissue and functional mapping implicating hepatic, immune and lipid-metabolic processes. This study establishes a framework for characterizing biological age through both its mean deviation and uncertainty, defining BAU as an independent dimension of human aging that links discordant aging to future healthspan.

cards.title: Integrated metabolomics and proteomics from voxelated cortical hemispheres of adult rhesus monkeys
cards.abstract: The spatial organization of molecular networks across cortex likely contributes to differences in local circuit vulnerability in aging and Alzheimer's disease; yet many existing molecular datasets sacrifice spatial structure, sampling only a handful of regions per brain. Here, we present a framework for generating spatially registered, paired metabolomic and proteomic maps across an entire cortical hemisphere of an adult rhesus monkey, at millimeter resolution. One hemisphere each from two animals was harvested under controlled conditions, approximately flattened, and hand dissected at different sampling resolutions (roughly 2.5 and 4 mm/side) into tissue voxels. Each voxel was split after homogenization and extraction to provide matched aliquots for targeted metabolomics and deep untargeted proteomics. To handle these high dimensional data, we developed PChclust, a principal component guided feature clustering algorithm. For cross omic integration, we developed a spatially regularized sparse canonical correlation analysis (sr-sCCA), which incorporates spatial neighborhood structure via graph Laplacian smoothing. We recover meaningful biology: Molecular similarity between neighboring voxels decayed with distance in both modalities, confirming that voxelation captures spatially organized biological variance. The sr-sCCA identified joint proteome-metabolome components with coherent cortical gradients that were conserved across animals. Pathway enrichment analysis recovered brain relevant ontologies and reconstructed complete metabolic circuits from single voxels.

cards.title: Ophthalmic AI With Just Ten Examples: Comparing Multimodal Large Language Models, Vision Foundation Models, and Vision-Language Models
cards.abstract: Purpose: To compare multimodal large language models (MLLMs), vision foundation models (VFMs), and contrastive vision-language models (VLMs) for ophthalmic image interpretation with no labeled examples (zero-shot) or as few as 10 labeled examples per class (10-shot). Design: Retrospective benchmarking study. Subjects: 4 public datasets (UCSD, IDRiD, REFUGE, ASOCT-MSDC) and 3 private datasets (OHTS, BPEI-DLS, WashU-OCT) of anterior- and posterior-segment ophthalmic imaging. Methods: Nine AI models were evaluated across 3 architectural families: MLLMs (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemma-4-31B-it), VFMs (DINOv3, RETFound, VisionFM), and VLMs (CLIP, EyeCLIP, SigLIP2). Models were assessed on disease classification, disease risk and severity grading, anatomical assessment, and lesion localization in fundus and OCT imaging. MLLMs were also compared with a 3D VFM (OCTCube-M) for whole-volume OCT classification. MLLMs were evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot, without additional training. Vision models (VFMs and VLMs) were adapted by linear probing and fine-tuning on the same 10-shot set and on the full training dataset (FD). Main Outcome Measures: Disease classification performance (macro-averaged F1, AUROC, quadratic weighted kappa [QWK]), anatomical localization accuracy, and cross-dataset generalization. Results: For retinal OCT disease classification, 10-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.94, versus 0.59 (10-shot) and 0.96 (FD) for vision models. For diabetic retinopathy and macular edema grading, 10-shot MLLMs achieved QWKs of 0.69 and 0.73, versus 0.48 and 0.57 (10-shot) and 0.72 and 0.79 (FD) for vision models. For lesion localization, 10-shot MLLMs achieved an F1 of 0.75, versus 0.70 (10-shot) and 0.86 (FD) for vision models. For vertical cup-to-disc ratio estimation (OHTS), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a mean absolute error of 0.14, versus 0.21 (10-shot) for vision models. For whole-volume OCT classification (WashU-OCT), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.71, versus 0.50 (10-shot) and 0.82 (FD) for vision models. Conclusions: Open-weight MLLMs given 10 labeled examples per class outperformed VFMs and VLMs trained on the same examples in most tasks and approached the performance of fully trained VFMs and VLMs in selected disease classification and grading tasks. MLLMs also demonstrated promising zero-shot performance on non-public clinical datasets without task-specific training. By reducing the need for large labeled datasets and task-specific model adaptation, MLLMs could broaden who can develop and validate ophthalmic AI.

cards.title: A Vma13-targeted thiadiazole-succinimide disrupts V-ATPase dependent arginine-polyamine homeostasis to block Candida albicans escape from macrophages
cards.abstract: Invasive candidiasis caused by Candida albicans is a life-threatening nosocomial infection with limited therapies and high morbidity and mortality among immunocompromised patients. Within host phagocytes, C. albicans catabolizes arginine to produce ammonia and fuels polyamine biosynthesis, which correlates with phagosomal alkalinization and yeast-to-hypha morphogenesis, facilitating macrophage escape and systemic dissemination. However, new antifungal strategies blocking this fungal escape remain scarce. Here, we characterize the thiadiazole-succinimide derivative ETSI, an arginine-dependent antifungal small molecule with minimal direct growth inhibition under arginine-free conditions yet robust anti-C. albicans activity in arginine-rich microenvironments mimicking the macrophage intracellular niche. Mechanistically, ETSI targets the vacuolar Vma13 to inhibit vacuolar H-ATPase (V-ATPase), dissipating vacuolar proton (H+) gradients and leading to cytoplasmic H+ retention. The accumulated cytoplasmic H+ traps intracellular ammonia and blocks its external release, while impaired vacuolar metabolite sequestration further triggers cytotoxic accumulation of arginine and polyamine metabolites. This dual metabolic perturbation suppresses phagosomal alkalinization, retains C. albicans in yeast form and blocks macrophage escape. ETSI is the first small molecule blocking C. albicans escape via disrupted Vma13/V-ATPase dependent arginine-polyamine homeostasis. This work identifies an intracellular metabolic vulnerability and establishes a niche-targeted antifungal strategy distinct from classic growth-suppressive drugs for treating invasive candidiasis.

cards.title: A 209‐Site <scp>DNA</scp> Methylation Predictor of Chronological Age Evaluated Under Empirical and Random Missingness
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT DNA methylation age prediction from incomplete profiles requires evaluation under empirical and random missingness. We evaluated whole‐blood chronological‐age prediction using 524 development and 132 held‐out GSE40279 samples and an external GSE73103 cohort ( n = 355). Feature‐stability analysis across 750 prespecified perturbation conditions identified a 209‐CpG primary panel and a 52‐CpG stringent sensitivity subset. The primary predictor combined five‐nearest‐neighbor reconstruction (KNN5) with Ridge regression. In the internal holdout, intact‐profile prediction achieved a mean absolute error of 4.24 years, a root‐mean‐square error (RMSE) of 5.38 years, and Pearson r = 0.934. Under masks derived from 42 empirical templates of formalin‐fixed paraffin‐embedded detection failure, KNN5 reduced RMSE by 0.365 years relative to development‐set mean replacement (95% bootstrap interval for the difference, −0.546 to −0.205), with larger reductions at higher missingness burdens. The reconstruction advantage persisted in complementary development analyses after randomization preserving both sample‐level and CpG‐level failure counts. External predictions remained associated with chronological age ( r = 0.835), despite age‐dependent calibration bias. Mixture analyses showed that background accuracy was central to target recovery as mixture asymmetry increased. These findings support local reconstruction within a stability‐selected CpG panel for chronological‐age prediction under the evaluated empirical and random missingness conditions.

cards.title: Reduced cerebral blood flow and metabolic rate trigger an adaptive mitochondrial remodeling program in a Down syndrome mouse model
cards.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central feature of Down syndrome (DS), yet how trisomy 21 affects brain bioenergetics across scales--from gene transcription to cellular function to whole-brain metabolism--remains poorly understood. Here, we use the Dp16(1)Yey/+ (abbreviated Dp16) DS mouse model, which carries ~115 triplicated gene orthologs of human chromosome 21, to address this major knowledge gap and to provide direct in vivo evidence of brain-wide metabolic deficit in DS. Using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) approaches, we show that Dp16 mice have reduced cerebral blood flow and metabolic rate of oxygen, with effects more pronounced in males than in females. Despite the suppression of cerebral metabolic rate, mitochondrial respiratory capacity and ATP synthase activity are largely preserved across brain regions, with sex differences noted. Transcriptomic analyses reveal marked upregulation of mitochondrial OXPHOS genes and the convergence of biological pathways related to proteostasis and mitochondrial function across brain regions, with male cortex and female cerebellum showing the biggest change. Collectively, our data suggest that a brain-wide metabolic deficit in Dp16 mice triggers an adaptive mitochondrial remodeling program across the brain to support bioenergetic demands. This compensatory response, however, is insufficient to normalize the metabolic dysfunction in Dp16 mice. Our findings underscore the value of integrating functional assessments at the organismal and tissue levels with transcriptomic changes to gain a systems view of physiologic perturbations and adaptations in the DS brain which may influence phenotypic outcomes.

cards.title: Neuropsychiatric symptom clusters and plasma proteomic signatures across cognitive ageing and dementia in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional analysis of the EVCD-RDC cohort
cards.abstract: Background: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are common across cognitive ageing and dementia, but their molecular correlates are poorly understood in sub Saharan African populations. We examined associations between individual NPS, empirically derived NPS dimensions, and plasma proteomic profiles in older adults in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Methods: In this cross sectional analysis of the EVCD RDC cohort, NPS were assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). Plasma proteins were quantified using the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120. Of 1044 participants in the full cohort, 779 had available proteomic data. Multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, education, and estimated glomerular filtration rate, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Exploratory factor analysis identified latent NPS dimensions. Findings: The full cohort included 1044 participants, of whom 779 comprised the proteomics cohort. Higher NEFL was associated with greater NPI symptom burden (Beta=0.349, 95% CI 0.201 to 0.497; FDR<0.001; N=674). Higher IL6 (Beta=0.805, 0.362 to 1.248) and CCL13 (Beta=0.434, 0.191 to 0.678) were associated with higher GDS scores (both FDR=0.032; N=693). Higher APOE protein was associated with nighttime behaviour (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.42 to 3.11; FDR=0.025). Three NPS dimensions were identified. NEFL was the only factor level association surviving FDR correction (behavioural/motor: Beta=0.222, 95% CI 0.127 to 0.318; FDR<0.001; N=644). Interpretation: NPS showed heterogeneous plasma protein correlates, with the most robust findings implicating neuroaxonal injury and inflammatory signalling. Longitudinal replication in African cohorts is needed.

cards.title: Decoding the Physical Mechanisms of Protein-Small Molecule Association by Multiscale Kinetic Monte-Carlo Simulations
cards.abstract: Protein-small molecule association involves multiple recognition stages governed by distinct physical interactions, yet resolving their kinetic contributions remains computationally challenging. Here, we develop a multiscale Monte Carlo framework that combines an atomistic, conformationally flexible ligand with a coarse-grained protein binding pocket and an atomistic steric envelope. Association is decomposed into three stages: molecular encounter, pocket entry, and productive binding. We evaluate the framework using ten protein-ligand complexes representing nine distinct targets, with experimentally derived association rates spanning nearly four orders of magnitude. Simulated pocket-entry rates exhibit the strongest correspondence with experimental kinetics (Pearson r = 0.617; Spearman {rho} = 0.758), whereas productive-binding rates show closer agreement in absolute magnitude. Systematic perturbations of electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and ligand torsional flexibility reveal stage-dependent sensitivities. Initial encounter is comparatively insensitive to these perturbations, while hydrophobic attraction and conformational flexibility influence pocket entry. Productive binding exhibits additional sensitivity to local interactions, with excessive hydrogen-bond strengthening potentially hindering native-pose formation. Probability-derived kinetic-stage barriers and normalized mechanism descriptors further reveal heterogeneous recognition behavior across protein targets. Together, this framework provides a computationally efficient and interpretable approach for investigating protein-ligand association pathways and their physical determinants across diverse molecular systems.

cards.title: spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization
cards.abstract: Recent advances in spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled profiling of gene expression in a spatial context, which has led to the generation of large-scale single-cell and spatial atlases with computationally-derived cell type or spatial domain labels. An increasingly important task with these data has become the transfer of cell type or spatial domain annotations from a given reference (or source) atlas into a new target tissue or sample. The reference and target datasets could be at different resolutions or measured on different experimental platforms. Here, we present a method to perform cross-platform transfer learning that takes as input single-cell or spatial domain labels from a reference atlas or dataset and transfers the labels to a target dataset at a similar or different resolution. Specifically, we use non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) on the reference data to identify factors associated with labels of interest and project these factors into the target dataset to label each new observation. We use a multinomial model with the factors as covariates and labels as the response to predict labels in the target dataset. In contrast to existing approaches, the advantage of our approach is interpretability, without compromising on accuracy. We demonstrate the performance of the method in two human brain tissues and show that our model identifies spatially coherent domains in the target datasets with concordance of marker gene expression. We implement spaTransfer in open-source software as an R package (github.com/cindyfang70/spaTransfer).

cards.title: Tuning inhibitor susceptibility of human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase to rescue tyrosine catabolism in the presence of β-triketones
cards.abstract: Human 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPD) catalyses a key step in tyrosine degradation via homogentisate in liver and kidney cells. Pharmacological inhibition of HPD with nitisinone (NTBC) is standard treatment for tyrosinemia type 1 (HT1) and alkaptonuria (AKU). Although life-changing, continuous NTBC treatment limits metabolic flexibility and complicates emerging gene- and cell-based therapeutic approaches. Engineering HPD variants that retain catalytic activity during NTBC exposure could facilitate restoration of tyrosine metabolism, yet the molecular determinants of inhibitor tolerance remain poorly understood. Here, we applied Knowledge Gaining Directed Evolution (KnowVolution) to enhance NTBC tolerance while considering enzyme activity, predicted stability, and MHC-II peptide binding. Random mutagenesis, site-saturation mutagenesis, and computational analyses identified beneficial substitutions that improved enzyme activity in the presence of NTBC. These substitutions are predominantly located outside the catalytic cavity, suggesting that NTBC tolerance may involve distal structural effects rather than direct modification of inhibitor-binding residues. Recombination of selected substitutions, guided by activity and computational predictions of stability and MHC-II binding, yielded multi-substitution HPD variants with markedly increased NTBC tolerance. The leading variant, HPD-M8, exhibited up to 40-fold greater NTBC tolerance than wild-type HPD and increased tolerance to structurally related {beta}-triketone inhibitors, without an overall increase in predicted MHC-II binder burden. Computational analyses suggested altered catalytic access-pathway energetics without major perturbation of the conserved catalytic machinery, consistent with a possible contribution of distal substitutions to inhibitor tolerance. Together, these findings provide insight into HPD inhibitor tolerance and establish a foundation for future HT1 and AKU therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Function-oriented microglial transcriptional scores in Alz-heimer's disease: resolving terminal functions beyond activa-tion states
cards.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) staging based on amyloid-{beta}, tau, and neurodegeneration does not capture heterogeneous microglial functions. Existing transcriptomic scores indicate microglial activation or state similarity but do not resolve post-activation functions and are not directly comparable across scales. Herein, we develop a function-oriented framework comprising seven harmful-and seven adaptive-associated gene modules, selected from predefined mechanisms and direct functional evidence. Using SEA-AD micro-glia/perivascular macrophage nuclei, we compute do-nor-brain-region pseudobulk scores on a fixed P10-P90 reference scale and validate them against matched protein, activity, and tissue endpoints. H3 is related to cytokine/chemokine proteins; H4 and A5 are related to the same isoprostane readout in opposite directions; and A3 is related to dense-core plaque fraction. Benchmark comparison shows modest incremental fit but distinct out-come-specific information. In external GSE146639, eight modules remained FDR-significant, although harmful and adaptive arms are highly collinear; H7 and A2 are replicated in external proteomics. Downsampling, leave-one-gene-out, and alternative scoring analyses supports technical stability, and single-cell reconstruction supported a state-resolved basis. These scores summarize relative engagement of damage-related and adaptive programmes, enabling mechanistic comparison across donors and brain regions, but remain observational, are not intended for clinical decision-making, and require further validation.

cards.title: A systems perspective on monoallelic inborn errors of immunity.
cards.abstract: The genetic architecture of inborn errors of immunity continues to grow in complexity, exposing the limitations of variant-centric concepts that have long shaped the field. While complete loss-of-function genotypes have been instrumental in defining essential gene functions in human immunity and inflammation, they have also entrenched binary interpretations of causality that fail to account for pleiotropy, variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance-especially in monoallelic disease. Monoallelic variants often perturb signaling rather than abolishing it. The integration of these perturbations into molecular and cellular systems, and eventually immune circuits, governs phenotypic expression. Here, we revisit and extend classic concepts of genetic dominance and genetic pleiotropy and suggest that these are not sole properties of alleles but emerge from the complex and dynamic behavior of molecular, cellular and immune systems to buffer genetic variance.

cards.title: From meal text to carbohydrate to postprandial glucose rise: QLoRA fine-tuning of the Qwen3-4B language model and gradient-boosting prediction in type 2 diabetes
cards.abstract: Background. In people with type 2 diabetes (T2D), postprandial glucose weighs on glycaemic control, and carbohydrate counting is difficult. Patients can describe their meal but rarely quantify it. Objective. To assess (1) whether a small open large language model (LLM), fine-tuned on public data, estimates the carbohydrate content of a meal described in words, and (2) what this carbohydrate adds to the prediction of the postprandial glucose rise in two public cohorts. Methods. Step 1: the Qwen3-4B LLM was fine-tuned with QLoRA on Nutrition5k dishes and compared with an automatically matched USDA food composition table and with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B used without training, on test dishes (internal control) and on 100 real meals of ShanghaiT2DM patients, whose reference carbohydrate was computed from the recorded quantities. Step 2: the maximum glucose rise between 0 and 120 minutes ({Delta}Gmax) was predicted by personalised gradient boosting (M2), compared with a spline linear regression and with the Chronos-2 foundation model, using only information available at meal start and person-level cross-validation, in ShanghaiT2DM (people with T2D recruited in two Shanghai hospitals; carbohydrate estimated by the LLM) and CGMacros (free-living adults in Santa Barbara, California; carbohydrate entered in the dataset, no text). Step 3: the model was transferred between datasets. 95% confidence intervals (CI) were obtained by cluster BCa bootstrap (2,000 resamples). Results. On the 100 real meals, the carbohydrate mean absolute error (MAE) of the fine-tuned model was 12.2 [9.9, 15.2] g, almost half that of the table (22.6 g; paired difference -10.5 [-16.8, -6.0] g) and nearly a third of that of the same model without fine-tuning (34.3 g), with a bias of -10.3 g; on test dishes it was 2.2 [2.0, 2.5] g. Personalised gradient boosting (M2) reached a correlation between predicted and observed rises of r = 0.63 [0.55, 0.69] in CGMacros (1,286 meals, 45 adults) and 0.49 [0.42, 0.54] in ShanghaiT2DM (2,339 meals, 99 people with T2D), about twice the linear reference (r = 0.32 and 0.23); for a rise above 50 mg/dL, its area under the ROC curve (AUROC) was 0.80 and 0.74, versus 0.64 and 0.68 with pre-meal glucose alone. Adding carbohydrate to pre-meal glucose changed r by 0.095 [0.068, 0.128] in CGMacros and by 0.004 [-0.010, 0.017] in ShanghaiT2DM; difference between datasets: 0.091 [0.060, 0.126]. Applied from one dataset to the other, the model lost correlation ({Delta}r = -0.11 [-0.17, -0.05] towards ShanghaiT2DM and -0.12 [-0.19, -0.04] towards CGMacros). The full "text [->] LLM [->] glucose" chain was evaluated in ShanghaiT2DM only. Conclusion. An open 4-billion-parameter LLM, fine-tuned with QLoRA on public data and usable offline, almost halves the error of carbohydrate counting for real meals described in words compared with an automatically matched table, with an underestimation of large meals. Personalised gradient boosting, based on pre-meal glucose and the person's usual response, doubles the correlation of a linear reference for predicting the glucose rise in both cohorts. Carbohydrate improved this prediction in CGMacros but not in ShanghaiT2DM; the two datasets differ in many respects, and the cause of this gap is not established.

cards.title: Type 1 immunity linked to CMV exposure improves long-term survival in sepsis without shock
cards.abstract: Dysregulated immune responses are at the core of sepsis pathology and can drive both acute organ dysfunction and long-term morbidity and mortality. To better understand the association between specific immune histories, perturbations and sepsis outcomes, we combined immune phenotyping, functional cytokine production assays and antibody repertoire profiling. While sepsis immune profiles were highly heterogeneous, we identified a strong association between the frequency of CXCR3-expressing CD4 memory T cells at time of enrollment and six-month survival in sepsis without shock. Surprisingly, the same population was linked to improved organ function trajectories in septic shock patients but did not influence six-month survival, highlighting the importance of considering physiological states to define immune predictors. Finally, phage display profiling revealed that these Th1 cells were generally expanded in CMV-seropositive individuals, suggesting that previous and latent infections may modulate sepsis outcomes.

cards.title: Identifying and targeting abnormal mitochondrial localization associated with psychosis
cards.abstract: Therapeutics working by novel mechanisms are needed for patients with psychiatric conditions. Cell-based assays to identify candidates that reverse observed abnormalities, even if in subsets of patients, could accelerate the process. Here, we imaged peripheral cells (skin fibroblasts) of 168 individuals, stained for DNA, actin, and mitochondria. We found mitochondria tend to be farther from the cell border for patients who experience psychosis (including subsets of individuals with bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and schizoaffective disorder), a phenotype not seen in patients diagnosed with major depression. Because the phenotype could be identified by a single metric, we could query existing databases of cells stained for their mitochondria and treated with various chemical or genetic perturbations. We identified compounds and genes both negatively and positively affecting the psychosis-associated phenotype, including some known to impact psychiatric conditions. Developing therapeutics with novel mechanisms is a complex multi-step challenge. This cell-based assay holds promise for virtual and physical screening to identify candidates for treating psychiatric conditions.

cards.title: Mapping the spatial architecture of glioblastoma from core to edge delineates niche-specific tumor cell states and intercellular interactions
cards.abstract: Treatment resistance in glioblastoma (GBM) is largely driven by the extensive multi-level heterogeneity that typifies this disease. Despite significant progress toward elucidating GBM's genomic and transcriptional heterogeneity, a critical knowledge gap remains in defining this heterogeneity at the spatial level. To address this, we employed spatial transcriptomics to map the architecture of the GBM ecosystem. This revealed tumor cell states that are jointly defined by gene expression and spatial localization, and multicellular niches whose composition varies along the tumor core-edge axis. Ligand-receptor interaction analysis uncovered a complex network of intercellular communication, including niche- and region-specific interactions. Finally, we found that CD8+GZMK+ T cells colocalize with LYVE1+ CD163+ myeloid cells in vascular regions, suggesting a potential mechanism for immune evasion. These findings provide novel insights into the GBM tumor microenvironment, highlighting previously unrecognized patterns of spatial organization and intercellular interactions, and novel therapeutic avenues to disrupt tumor-promoting interactions and overcome immune resistance.

cards.title: Protruding Geometry Provides Potential Homing Sites of Circulating Tumor Cells
cards.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) must adhere to the vascular endothelium to initiate metastasis, yet the role of vessel wall topography remains unclear. We present an integrated microfluidic platform combining defined protruding geometries, live cell imaging, and controlled perfusion to study CTC homing. Using a multiscale device that reproduces hierarchical vascular branching, we show that CTCs accumulate preferentially at locations with protruded geometry, including bifurcations, sharp corners and positively curved segments. At these hotspots, a viscoelastic, polymer-like network assembles, capturing CTCs and accompanying progressive multicellular aggregation. This network undergoes stretching and elastic recoil even under laminar flow. Mechanistically, knockdown of DSG2 and ITGB3 reduces retention, suggesting a potential anti metastasis strategy targeting molecular mechanical coupling. Computational fluid dynamics simulations indicate that hotspots coincide with pronounced velocity and pressure perturbations. Our experiments identify local geometry as a critical determinant of CTC arrest and provide a platform for studying the physical mechanisms of metastatic homing.

cards.title: Sequence sensitivity of open chromatin reveals constrained regulatory elements underlying human traits
cards.abstract: Open chromatin regions (OCRs) delineate cell-type-specific regulatory landscapes across the genome, yet their functional importance varies considerably. Here, we introduce CAMBUS (Chromatin Accessibility Mutation Burden Score), a machine-learning framework that quantifies the sensitivity of predicted chromatin accessibility to sequence perturbation to prioritize functionally important OCRs. Applying CAMBUS to 29 immune cell types, we identified 66,043 CAMBUS-defined OCRs (cOCRs), without directly incorporating human genetic variation or existing evolutionary constraint metrics. Nevertheless, cOCRs were strongly enriched in independently defined constrained regions (odds ratio (OR)=11.45 (95% confidence interval (CI) 9.33-14.05), P=4.7 x 10-68), and active regulatory elements, with enrichment for super-enhancers remaining after adjustment for established constraint metrics and sequence features (OR=6.18 (95% CI 3.80-10.05), P=2.1 x 10-13). cOCRs also showed cell-type-specific enrichment for the heritability of immune-mediated diseases and for putative causal variants identified by statistical fine-mapping across European and East Asian ancestries, including rare variants. Integration with statistical fine-mapping further linked 1,533 putative causal variants across 70 complex traits to cell-type-specific cOCRs, revealing plausible regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits. Together, CAMBUS provides a region-centered framework for identifying regulatory elements whose predicted activity is sensitive to sequence disruption and that are enriched for evolutionary constraint, complementing existing regulatory and constraint annotations for interpreting non-coding genetic variation.

cards.title: A Unified Framework for Batch Correction and Imputation in Modern Mass Spectrometry Proteomics
cards.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics, including single-cell applications, are often confounded by batch effects, inter-laboratory variation, and signal drift that can obscure biological interpretation. NMFBatch addresses these sources of unwanted variation through a unified framework that combines non-negative matrix factorization with generalized additive modelling to jointly capture discrete and continuous technical effects from protein expression data. It handles missing values directly through masking and on-the-fly imputation. Benchmarking across reference datasets, plasma proteomics cohorts, simulations, and single-cell data demonstrated that NMFBatch reduced technical variation while preserving biological structure. These results establish NMFBatch as a robust framework for batch correction, harmonization, and integrative proteomics analysis from protein expression data.

cards.title: Epigenetic clocks and accelerated biological aging in people living with HIV: Emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
cards.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has significantly improved survival among people living with HIV. However, many people living with HIV develop cardiovascular, metabolic, neurocognitive, musculoskeletal, and frailty-related conditions earlier or more frequently than HIV-negative individuals of a similar chronological age. DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks provide a method for estimating biological age and may help explain this increased burden of age-related disease. This short review aims to summarize current evidence on epigenetic age acceleration in people living with HIV, describe the biological mechanisms that may contribute to accelerated aging, examine the effects of antiretroviral therapy and sex-related factors, and discuss the possible clinical applications of epigenetic clocks. First-generation epigenetic clocks, including the Horvath and Hannum clocks, generally indicate that people living with HIV are approximately 5 to 7 years biologically older than HIV-negative individuals of a similar chronological age. However, these clocks may be affected by HIV-related changes in immune-cell composition. Newer measures, including PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, Retro-Age, and immune-composition-resistant clocks, assess different aspects of biological aging, such as physiological decline, mortality risk, the pace of aging, and retroelement-associated methylation. HIV-associated epigenetic aging appears to involve persistent viral activity, chronic immune activation, inflammation, immunosenescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, altered one‑carbon metabolism, glutathione deficiency, cellular senescence, and treatment-related metabolic or mitochondrial effects. Antiretroviral therapy may reduce epigenetic age acceleration, but it does not consistently restore biological age to the level observed in HIV-negative individuals. Sex, menopause, metabolic dysfunction, and body composition may also influence the relationship between epigenetic aging, frailty, and mortality. Epigenetic clocks may improve the assessment of biological aging in people living with HIV and could support risk stratification, early identification of frailty, and evaluation of interventions. However, longitudinal validation, standardized methods, adjustment for immune-cell composition, and evidence linking clock changes with meaningful clinical outcomes are required before these biomarkers can be used routinely in HIV care.

cards.title: A microbiota-driven neuroepithelial feed-forward circuit drives gastroesophageal junction tumorigenesis
cards.abstract: The gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) is continuously exposed to refluxed bile acids and microbial perturbations, yet how these environmental cues are converted into persistent oncogenic signaling is unknown. Here we show that bile acid remodeling enriches the oral commensal Prevotella melaninogenica at the GEJ, where bacterial succinate activates both vagal sensory neurons and SUCNR1-expressing tuft cells. Activated tuft cells release 15-deoxy-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (15-d-PGJ2), which sensitizes sensory neurons and sustains nerve remodeling, while neuronal CGRP drives expansion and tuft-cell differentiation of neuro-responsive epithelial progenitors through RAMP1. This self-reinforcing microbiota-neuron-epithelium circuit promotes dysplastic progression, and its genetic or pharmacological disruption, including with the approved CGRP antagonist rimegepant, suppresses tumor development, revealing an interceptable mechanism linking environmental dysbiosis to cancer initiation through neural circuits.

cards.title: Early dopamine elevation modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male juvenile mice
cards.abstract: Alterations in dopaminergic signaling and exposure to early-life stress are both implicated in the developmental origins of psychiatric disorders, yet little is known about how these factors interact during sensitive periods of brain maturation. We investigated whether increased dopamine availability during early postnatal development modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male C57BL/6 mice. From postnatal day (PD) 1 to PD14, mice received L-Dopa plus benserazide, maternal separation (3 h/day), their combination, or the corresponding control conditions. We assessed mice behavior between PD28 and PD32 using novel object recognition, open-field, elevated plus-maze, marble-burying, and forced-swim tests, followed by hippocampal volumetric analysis. Early L-Dopa exposure produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. In females, L-Dopa increased rearing without altering horizontal locomotion and modified open-arm exploration and stress-coping behavior, whereas in males it increased open-arm exploration and reduced climbing frequency. Maternal separation produced distinct effects in females and males and reduced repetitive digging/burying behavior in both sexes. Importantly, maternal separation frequently modified rather than potentiated the effects of L-Dopa. In both sexes, combined maternal separation and L-Dopa opposed several L-Dopa-associated alterations in open-field, elevated plus-maze, and forced-swim behaviors. Recognition memory was largely preserved across experimental conditions. L-Dopa also reduced hippocampal volume selectively in females, whereas hippocampal volume was higher in females exposed to maternal separation plus L-Dopa than in those receiving L-Dopa alone. Multivariate analyses revealed overlapping rather than treatment-specific behavioral clusters, indicating substantial individual heterogeneity and sex-dependent shifts in multidimensional behavioral profiles. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient alterations in dopamine availability and maternal separation interact non-additively during early postnatal development. Their consequences depend on sex, behavioral domain, and developmental timing, supporting a model in which neurochemical and environmental perturbations dynamically shape behavioral trajectories rather than simply producing cumulative developmental damage.

cards.title: Neuronal FICD shapes motivated behavior through modulation of dopamine receptor dynamics
cards.abstract: Motivated behaviors rely on dopaminergic signaling, which in turn depends on the correct folding and trafficking of receptors through the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Within the ER, the AMPylase enzyme FICD acts as a molecular rheostat through its modification of the chaperone BiP, dynamically tuning the organelle's responsiveness to folding perturbations and cellular stress. While the biochemistry of FICD is well-established, its role in complex animal behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FICD as a conserved contributor to the generation of motivated behavior. In Drosophila, pan-neuronal knockdown of dFic significantly reduces feeding, spontaneous locomotion, and reward-seeking behavior. These alterations occur without disrupting circadian architecture, motor capacity, or homeostatic hunger, indicating a specific loss of motivational drive. Depleting dFic within subsets of dopamine receptor-expressing (Dop1R1) neurons recapitulates these behavioral alterations. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that dFic depletion does not induce a canonical unfolded protein response, pointing to a specific post-transcriptional alteration rather than global ER stress. At the molecular level, dysregulated dFic alters the localization and abundance of Dop1R1. Finally, we demonstrate that this regulatory axis is evolutionarily conserved, as loss of FICD similarly diminishes motivated behaviors in C. elegans and mice. Together, these findings implicate FICD in the generation of motivated behavior and link dynamic control of ER proteostasis to dopamine-receptor maturation.

cards.title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
cards.abstract: Background: Machine Learning (ML) has shown promise in histopathological diagnosis, but rare tumours, like duodenal epithelial neoplasms, are challenging because large, labelled datasets are difficult to assemble. We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. Methods: We assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. Results: In leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. Conclusions: We present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

cards.title: A low-adhesion mechanism enables axon growth in the developing brain
cards.abstract: During development, axons grow through complex tissue environments to wire the brain. Axon growth speeds measured in cell culture are incompatible with the distances axons must cover in vivo. Yet how axons achieve the growth speeds required to establish long-range connectivity within a narrow embryonic developmental window, and by what mechanism, remains unknown. Here, using long-term live imaging in brain sections, mouse genetics, molecular and pharmacological perturbations, together with AxoVivo, a newly developed intravital imaging platform that resolves subcellular structures, including growth cones and cytoskeletal dynamics, in living mouse embryos, we show that axons of cortical projection neurons (CPNs) employ a low-adhesion mechanism to grow. Even as growth cones change shape and turn, axons grow an order of magnitude faster than in vitro. The actin motor myosin II controls the growth cone actin cytoskeleton and its morphology but not axon growth itself, which is instead promoted by microtubule stabilisation. Finally, super-resolution shadow imaging (SUSHI) revealed that growth cones do not pull on the surrounding extracellular matrix. Taken together, this low-adhesion mechanism driven by protruding microtubules ensures the rapid growth necessary for long-distance wiring of the developing nervous system.

cards.title: Inferotemporal cortex stimulation is perceived before its onset
cards.abstract: Neural response latency measures when stimulus-evoked activity becomes detectable, but it does not reveal when the brain assigns the causal contribution of that activity to events in the external world. We define this temporal adjustment as projected delay and measure it in the macaque inferotemporal cortex using optogenetic stimulation and behavior. Two rhesus macaques performed a cortical perturbation detection task in which a visual masker appeared at different times relative to stimulation. Detection was selectively impaired when the masker began 200 ms before stimulation. We then tested this timing using Perceptography, a method that optimizes image perturbations to mimic stimulation-evoked visual events. Image perturbations presented 200 ms before stimulation elicited higher false-alarm rates than perturbations presented at stimulation onset. Here, we show that stimulation-evoked visual events in inferotemporal cortex depend preferentially on visual information originating approximately 200 ms before the cortical perturbation. This projected delay exceeds typical inferotemporal response latencies and suggests temporally extended readout mechanisms relevant to causal models of visual perception and the timing of cortical visual prostheses.

cards.title: Hormonal remodeling and molecular mechanisms in postmenopausal osteoporosis: Pathogenesis and therapeutic implications (Review).
cards.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO) is a prevalent metabolic bone disorder characterized by accelerated bone loss, reduced bone mineral density, and increased fragility fracture risk. Although estrogen deficiency is considered a central driver of PMO, increasing evidence indicates that bone loss after menopause results from broader endocrine remodeling involving multiple hormones. Estrogen decline and the accompanying rise in follicle‑stimulating hormone (FSH) are characteristic of the menopausal transition. Alterations in the parathyroid hormone (PTH)‑vitamin D axis, oxytocin (OT) and calcitonin (CT) may also influence skeletal homeostasis, although their patterns and causal contributions are less consistently established in postmenopausal women. These pathways are discussed as interacting components of an endocrine framework with differing levels of supporting evidence. These coordinated hormonal alterations disrupt bone remodeling through several mechanisms, including impaired bone mechanical homeostasis, dysregulated osteoimmune interactions, altered calcium metabolism, and gut microbiota‑bone axis imbalance. Collectively, these changes promote osteoclast activation, suppress osteoblast function, and accelerate skeletal deterioration. Current therapeutic approaches, such as hormone replacement therapy, bisphosphonates, selective estrogen receptor modulators, and PTH analogs, have improved the management of PMO but remain limited by safety concerns or restricted long‑term efficacy. Emerging approaches, including FSH blockade, selected phytoestrogen‑related interventions, modified CT delivery, and OT‑related pathways have different levels of supporting evidence; most specific experimental strategies require human efficacy and safety validation before clinical application. An improved understanding of hormonal interactions and endocrine network remodeling may facilitate the development of more precise and individualized strategies for the prevention and treatment of PMO.

cards.title: How high is too high? Severe hyperparathyroidism and bone mineral disease in children on hemodialysis.
cards.abstract: Bone mineral disease is highly prevalent and a key contributor to morbidity and mortality in the pediatric hemodialysis population. Clinical tools to manage this are limited, with no consensus on optimal parathyroid hormone (PTH) targets to guide therapies. Limited data suggest infants and young children may be more prone to hyperparathyroidism but evidence is lacking. A longitudinal retrospective cohort study was conducted to investigate relationships between PTH, age, and bone outcomes in a cohort of children ages 0-12 years who received hemodialysis between 2002 and 2023. Records were reviewed for biochemical bone mineral values and adverse bone outcomes, defined by fracture and/or evidence of bone disease on imaging. The study included 638 observations of 52 patients with median age 8.4 years (IQR 3.4, 11.3). Severe hyperparathyroidism (PTH > 1000 pg/mL) was more common in children 0-3 years old (30%) than in those 4-12-years old (17%). Multivariable regression showed PTH decreased by 5.7% with each yearly increase in age, adjusting for hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia (p = 0.0001). Children 0-3 years old with severe hyperparathyroidism had > eightfold higher odds (OR 8.77, p = 0.0001) of adverse bone health outcomes, adjusting for hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and time on dialysis. Severe hyperparathyroidism is more common in infants and children 0-3 years old and is associated with adverse bone outcomes. Moderately elevated PTH did not identify children at risk for bone mineral disease in this cohort. More sensitive age-specific biomarkers are needed for early identification and intervention to improve bone health in the pediatric dialysis population.

cards.title: Alzheimer's Disease-Associated Proteomic Changes in Olfactory Stem Cells Show Pathway-Level Transcriptomic Overlap
cards.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive, neurodegenerative disorder and the leading cause of dementia worldwide. Although recent therapeutic advances have provided some disease-modifying potential, there is currently no curative treatment for AD, highlighting the need for improved disease models and early biomarkers. Olfactory mucosal stem cells, which can be expanded in vitro as olfactory neurosphere-derived (ONS) cells, represent a promising source for biomarker discovery because olfactory tissue is more accessible than central nervous system tissue and has been reported to exhibit AD-related pathological changes. In this study, we used subcellular fractionation-based proteomics, reconstructed bulk proteomics and integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analyses to characterise alterations in ONS cells derived from healthy control, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD individuals. Fraction-specific proteomics identified cytoplasmic and nuclear-enriched protein abundance changes, including alterations in proteins and pathways associated with cytoskeletal organisation, RNA processing, intracellular trafficking, autophagy and mitochondrial/metabolic processes. Reduced LC3B abundance in cytoplasmic AD ONS cells was supported by western blot analysis, although LC3B abundance alone does not indicate altered autophagic flux. Reconstructed bulk proteomics identified 40 FDR-significant proteins in AD compared with HC, defining an AD-associated protein signature enriched for extracellular matrix, cytoskeletal, organelle-associated and RNA-processing pathways. Despite proteomic enrichment of mitochondrial and metabolic pathways, Seahorse Mito Stress Test analysis did not identify significant group-level differences in mitochondrial respiration. Integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analysis revealed partial RNA-protein concordance and pathway-level overlap across disease-associated processes. Together, these findings support the use of patient-derived ONS cells as a model for investigating AD- and MCI-associated molecular changes and highlight protein signatures for further validation.

cards.title: SNX13 and SNX14 interorganelle tethers suppress lysosome membrane damage and neurodegeneration
cards.abstract: Lysosome membrane permeabilization (LMP) is an emerging signature of neurodegenerative diseases, yet the mechanisms that enable an effective repair are largely undefined, particularly in neurons. Here, we reveal sorting nexin (SNX) proteins SNX13 and SNX14 maintain lysosome membrane lipid composition to support efficient LMP repair and neuronal survival. We identify loss of function mutations in SNX13 in children manifesting a previously unrecognized cerebellar neurodegenerative disorder. Consistently, Snx13 ablation in mice causes cerebellar Purkinje cell death and signatures of ataxia-like motor deficits. We show loss of SNX13 or its ataxia-linked paralog SNX14 perturbs lysosome morphology, positioning, and acidity and causes increased susceptibility to lysosome damage. Using lysosome immunoprecipitation and proteomics, we comprehensively map lysosome proteome remodeling during membrane damage and repair, finding that SNX13 or SNX14 deficiency blunts recruitment of repair machinery, including ESCRTs and PITT pathway proteins, to damaged lysosomes. Mechanistically, we determine SNX13 and SNX14 support lysosome integrity through interorganelle lipid crosstalk. We define SNX13 and SNX14 as lipid binding proteins that localize to ER-lysosome junctions, where they support lysosomal phosphoinositide levels in response to membrane damage. In line with this, loss of SNX13 or SNX14 impairs lysosome PtdIns4P signaling. Altogether, our work reveals a conserved mechanism of interorganelle lipid crosstalk by SNX13/14 family proteins that safeguards lysosome membranes, maintaining them competent for repair, and is defective in cerebellar neurodegeneration.

cards.title: Foundation Models Improve Perturbation Response Prediction
cards.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to genetic or chemical perturbations is a long-standing goal in biology. Recent applications of foundation models to this task have yielded contradictory results regarding their superiority over simple baselines. We conducted an extensive analysis of the utility of pretrained embeddings (including but not limited to biological foundation models) for perturbation response prediction, covering over 600 embedding-task pairs. While some foundation models fail to outperform simple baselines, others yield consistent improvements. However, the strongest pretrained embeddings are those derived from prior knowledge. We also developed methods for integrating multiple pretrained embeddings to make better predictions. Our results confirm that pretrained embeddings can enable more accurate simulations of cellular behavior.

cards.title: The limbic navigation system as a hierarchical RNN
cards.abstract: Path-integration-trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can reproduce grid-like and head-direction-like representations, but most existing models rely on low-dimensional velocity inputs and do not capture the hierarchical organisation of the brain's self-localisation circuit. We introduce a hierarchical recurrent neural network (HRNN) that separately processes angular velocity and linear speed to perform simultaneous angular and positional path integration. Trained on these tasks, the HRNN generalises to longer timescales than seen during training and develops neural response properties resembling all the key cell types: angular velocity cells, head direction cells, speed cells, conjunctive and pure grid cells. The learned circuit also recovers key motifs of the navigation system, including attractor dynamics and asymmetric connectivity patterns. Perturbation analyses reveal functional information flow across the hierarchy, consistent with experimental observations. Finally, introducing theta-paced mutual inhibition between two learned angular-velocity subpopulations enables the HRNN to reproduce the bidirectional theta sweeps observed in empirical data. These results establish hierarchical task-driven RNNs as a biologically interpretable framework for linking neural representations, circuit motifs, and population dynamics in spatial navigation, while enabling targeted in silico perturbations and the generation of experimentally testable predictions.

cards.title: Enabling Spatially Resolved Gene Expression Analysis in a Multilayer Paper-Based In Vitro Tumor Model
cards.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is a defining feature of solid tumors, yet molecular analysis of three-dimensional (3D) in vitro tumor models is often performed as a bulk measurement, potentially obscuring position-dependent cellular responses. Here, we establish an analytical workflow for spatially resolved gene-expression analysis in a multilayer paper-based 3D tumor model by addressing the challenge of RNA recovery from cell-laden paper-Matrigel scaffolds. Using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, multiple RNA extraction strategies were systematically evaluated across conventional culture, Matrigel, paper, and composite paper-Matrigel environments. Conventional silica-column extraction yielded only 3.39 {+/-} 0.93 ng/L RNA from the composite scaffold, whereas TRIzol-chloroform extraction increased recovery to 201.13 {+/-} 38.32 ng/L. The optimized workflow subsequently enabled independent RNA recovery from all eight layers of a multi-layer paper-based in vitro tumor, with concentrations ranging from 113.06 {+/-} 5.00 to 245.26 {+/-} 15.76 ng/L and purity suitable for downstream qRT-PCR analysis. Layer-resolved profiling of untreated cultures revealed distinct spatial patterns in HIF1A, HIF2A, VEGFA, and GLUT4 expression across the multilayer construct. To evaluate the workflow under pharmacological perturbation, cultures were exposed to 5 M doxorubicin (DOX) for 48 h. Relative cell viability exhibited a non-monotonic spatial profile, whereas DOX-induced HIF1A and VEGFA expression generally became more pronounced toward the deeper layers when each treated layer was compared with its corresponding untreated control. Collectively, these results establish a workflow for converting individually addressable regions of a multilayer 3D tumor model into spatially resolved transcriptional measurements, enabling analysis of both baseline spatial heterogeneity and position-dependent molecular responses to pharmacological perturbation.

cards.title: The Alzheimer's disease risk gene ABCA7 regulates microglial lysosomal and lipid homeostasis and promotes phagocytosis to maintain neuronal health
cards.abstract: Background: Loss of function mutations in the lipid transporter ABCA7 have been linked to increased risk for late onset Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although rare and common variants in ABCA7 associated with AD alter the coding sequence and are predicted to impair protein function, the precise cell-type consequences of ABCA7 deficiency remain incompletely defined. Methods: We used CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) that were deficient for ABCA7 (ABCA7-KO) and their wild-type (ABCA7-WT) isogenic counterparts and subsequently performed unbiased proteomics on differentiated astrocytes (iAs), neurons (iNs) and microglia (iMGs). ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs produced the largest proteomic changes, so we therefore conducted additional functional analyses to define its effects on microglial lysosomal activity, phagocytosis, and lipid metabolism. In addition, we leveraged CRISPR/Cas9 to correct the ABCA7 rs3752246 AD risk variant in patient-derived iPSCs and compared proteomic and functional phenotypes between corrected iMGs and isogenic mutant carriers. Finally, we examined the functional consequence of ABCA7-deficient microglia on neurons. Results: ABCA7-KO iMGs were deficient for proteins involved in lysosome function, measured by down-regulated lysosomal proteomic signatures, as well as reduced DQ-BSA activity and reduced LAMP1+ area. Additionally, ABCA7-KO iMGs displayed impaired phagocytic capacity and increased inflammatory markers, including MHC proteins CD1A and CD1E, and IL-18. Multi-omic integration of lipidomic and proteomic profiles nominated a dysregulated metabolic network characterized by altered phospholipid steady-state metabolism and increased lipid peroxidation in ABCA7-KO iMGs. This was complemented by an accumulation of polyunsaturated triacylglycerols and lipid droplets, suggesting that ABCA7 deficiency disrupts intracellular lipid dynamics. This was supported by the alleviation of lysosomal and lipid droplet phenotypes through the inhibiting the synthesis of triacylglycerols. Concordantly, proteomic and functional analyses revealed lysosomal dysfunction in rs3752246-mutant iMGs, suggesting a shared ABCA7-dependent mechanism underlying AD risk. Tri-cultures of iNs, iAs and iMGs revealed that ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs worsened AD-relevant neuronal measures such as tau phosphorylation and synapse number. Conclusions: This work supplies evidence for the important role of ABCA7 in microglia and provides unique insights into the molecular and functional consequences of reduced ABCA7 function in lysosomal and lipid regulation, paving a path forward to a more comprehensive understanding of AD molecular subtypes and personalized therapeutics.

cards.title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease
cards.abstract: Background: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood. Methods: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis. Results: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI. Conclusions: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

cards.title: Subcellular spatial proteomics of the close animal relative, Capsaspora owczarzaki
cards.abstract: Capsaspora owczarzaki is one of the closest relatives of animals and an increasingly tractable model for investigating the evolution of multicellularity. However, very little cell biological work has been done on the sister linages to animals. Subcellular spatial proteomics (SSP) is a technique that can localize thousands of proteins to subcellular compartments in a single experiment by combining cell fractionation with sensitive mass spectrometry. To provide broad insight into the localization of the Capsaspora proteome, we performed SSP based on a label-free version of LOPIT-DC (Localisation of Organelle Proteins by Isotope Tagging after Differential ultraCentrifugation). We detected 6,466 proteins, corresponding to 68.4% of the predicted Capsaspora proteome, and assigned high-confidence localizations to 3,106 of them across 13 subcellular compartments. This study serves as a proteomic dataset to resolve cellular compartmentalization in a close relative of animals, enabling downstream evolutionary, biological, and functional analyses. Investigators interested in using these data prior to publication are encouraged to contact us to avoid overlap and to facilitate coordinated and collaborative use of this resource.

cards.title: Subcellular spatial proteomics of the heterotrophic nanoflagellate, Cafeteria roenbergensis
cards.abstract: Cafeteria roenbergensis is the best-studied free-living heterotrophic nanoflagellate, an abundant marine bacterivore and the host of the giant virus CroV, yet almost nothing is known about how its cell is organized. To provide broad insight into the localization of its proteome, we used subcellular spatial proteomics (SSP), based on a label-free version of LOPIT-DC (Localisation of Organelle Proteins by Isotope Tagging after Differential ultraCentrifugation), in which organelles are separated by differential centrifugation and each protein is assigned to a compartment from its abundance profile across fractions. We detected 5,948 proteins (5,889 protein groups), corresponding to 69.7% of the predicted C. roenbergensis proteome, and assigned high-confidence localizations to 2,945 proteins across 14 subcellular compartments, including basal body/cilia, cytosol, ER, Golgi, lysosome, membrane-trafficking, mitochondria, nucleoplasm, nucleus, peroxisome, plasma membrane, proteasome, ribosome, and spliceosome. This study serves as a proteomic dataset to resolve protein compartmentalization in a free-living heterotrophic stramenopile, enabling evolutionary, biological and functional insight and analysis. Investigators interested in using these data prior to publication are encouraged to contact us to avoid overlap and to facilitate coordinated and collaborative use of this resource.
