cards.title: El Niño, capture success, and wing fluctuating asymmetry in Drosophila sturtevanti Duda, 1927
cards.abstract: Fluctuating asymmetry (FA) is widely used as a proxy for developmental instability, although reduced rather than increased FA, has occasionally been reported under particularly challenging conditions, possibly because environmental filtering removes less developmentally stable individuals. Here, we investigated temporal variation in wing shape asymmetry in males of Drosophila sturtevanti collected in 2022, 2024, and 2026 at the same sampling site, an urban Atlantic Forest fragment. Sampling in 2022 and 2026 were completed during single field expeditions in early April, whereas in 2024 repeated collections were required until mid-May because of markedly low capture success. We therefore examined whether this difference was associated with unusual environmental conditions and whether FA was higher in 2024, as expected under greater developmental perturbation. Daily temperature and relative humidity were examined from early March onward, encompassing approximately one month before adult emergence. The 2024 sampling period was warmer and drier than the corresponding periods in 2022 and 2026 and coincided with the final phase of the strong 2023-2024 El Niño event. Contrary to our prediction, FA was significantly lower in 2024. The magnitude of directional asymmetry remained similar among years, although the spatial pattern of the DA vector differed between 2024 and 2026. The coincidence of reduced capture success and reduced FA is consistent with the hypothesis that adverse conditions may impose demographic filtering, such that individuals expressing greater developmental instability are less likely to contribute to the sampled adult population.

cards.title: Human Th17 state classification reveals a selective vulnerability in acylcarnitine metabolism in type 2 diabetes
cards.abstract: Th17 cells are categorized as non-pathogenic (Th17np) and pathogenic (Th17p), states defined primarily in murine autoimmune models. In contrast, studying these states in humans remains difficult because these subsets lack validated identifiers. We developed a nanovial-based single-cell ELISA to isolate cytokine-secreting human Th17 cells and define Th17np vs Th17p cell transcriptional states. These signatures enabled predictive classification and flow-cytometric identification across tissues and diseases. Application of these strategies with single-cell metabolic modeling and functional profiling revealed that Th17np cells predominate in type 2 diabetes yet exhibit impaired fatty acid oxidation capacity despite elevated carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A). CRISPR perturbation and pharmacologic inhibition identified acylcarnitine metabolism as a regulator of Th17 state balance and exposed a selective metabolic vulnerability in type 2 diabetes. This framework links human Th17 cell pathogenicity to lipid metabolism.

cards.title: A Mathematical Model of Reliability-Dependent Sensory Reweighting in Quiet Standing
cards.abstract: Human quiet standing relies on vestibular, proprioceptive, and visual information whose contributions change with sensory context. Posturography characterizes this reweighting through responses to visual and support-surface perturbations, but a compact account of how sensory reliability propagates from state estimation to postural action remains incomplete. We develop a minimal quiet-standing model in which sensory reliability is encoded by channel-specific precision parameters that weight sensory prediction errors. A one-link inverted pendulum with intrinsic ankle stiffness estimates posture by minimizing an active-inference free-energy objective and selects ankle torque by minimizing the same objective under a restorative sensory goal. A fixed-point analysis predicts in closed form the perturbation-induced belief bias, each channel's state-update contribution, the steady posture, and a linear stability condition from the precisions, goal dynamics, and intrinsic stiffness. Closed-loop simulations in 115 trials matched the predicted equilibria to within 0.001degrees wherever the loop settled, and the two conditions predicted unstable diverged or drifted. Reducing an unreliable channel's precision eightfold reduced perturbation-driven posture shifts by 82%, with a matching decrease in that channel's state-update contribution; intrinsic stiffness left this reduction essentially unchanged for visual and sensory-only perturbations but bounded it for physical support tilts; a global precision reduction did not reduce the shift; and a within-trial precision switch showed belief updating, not a separate action gain, carrying the change to ankle torque. The results give a compact mathematical account of postural sensory reweighting as relative, context-selective precision control in a closed multisensory loop.

cards.title: Improving phosphoproteomic kinase activity inference by contextual refinement of Kinase Library relationships
cards.abstract: Kinase activity inference from phosphoproteomic data relies on kinase-specific substrate sets defined by kinase-substrate relationship (KSR) priors. Kinase Library (KL) expands candidate substrate coverage using experimentally derived kinase specificity profiles, but its predictions reflect sequence compatibility rather than established intracellular regulation. We benchmarked KL-expanded KSR priors using 222 perturbation phosphoproteomic samples covering 396 annotated activation or inhibition events across 78 kinases. Broad KL expansion increased the number of scoreable kinases from 108 to 391, but reduced perturbed-kinase discrimination, directional accuracy and ranking performance. Higher error rates occurred among kinases with limited curated substrate support, while broad expansion also increased redundancy among inferred activity profiles. To improve the reliability of motif-derived relationships, we constrained KL-derived KSRs using predicted protein co-localization and protein-association evidence. Protein-association filtering consistently improved inference performance, reduced activity redundancy and provided a more favorable accuracy-coverage balance than co-localization filtering. The selected protein-association-filtered prior retained activity estimates for 308 kinases with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) above 0.75 and extended inference to 200 kinases not scoreable using curated KSRs, which were significantly enriched for dark kinases. These newly scoreable kinases showed structured activity patterns across perturbation contexts and interpretable signaling associations. Our results show that protein-association evidence can refine motif-derived KSR priors while preserving broad kinome coverage, providing a practical framework for more reliable phosphoproteomic kinase activity inference.

cards.title: High-resolution temporal profiling reveals synchronized dynamics of the mouse gut microbiome
cards.abstract: Background The gut microbiome undergoes diurnal oscillations entrained by host circadian rhythms and feeding behavior, and disruption of these oscillations has been linked to metabolic dysfunction. However, the temporal organization of microbial activity within these oscillatory cycles remains poorly understood, largely because conventional sampling approaches lack the temporal resolution needed to resolve rapid microbial dynamics. Results To address this gap, we developed a fully automated fecal collection system that enables continuous sampling from individual mice at minute- to hour-scale resolution without manual intervention. Using this platform, we collected fecal samples at hourly intervals over 14 consecutive days from individually housed mice. To reconstruct genome- and function-level trajectories from these data, we developed a cost-effective method (GORIN) that combines full-length 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with long-read metagenomic references. Applying a newly developed phase-analytic method (NPPD) to determine the instantaneous phase of each genome and functional gene, we found that the gut microbiota is organized into two phase-coherent groups corresponding to the light and dark phases of the host circadian cycle. These two groups differed in gene content, suggesting distinct carbohydrate utilization strategies, with the light-phase community enriched in mucosal glycan-degrading enzymes, whereas the dark-phase community was enriched in carbon storage metabolism and motility-related functions. Within each phase, microbial taxa and functional genes displayed reproducible temporal succession across individual mice. Perturbations, including cage transfer and antibiotic treatment transiently disrupted phase synchronization, as measured by the phase order parameter, followed by gradual recovery of phase coherence. Conclusions These findings reveal reproducible phase-synchronized temporal organization in the mouse gut microbiome, with community-level phase relationships that can be quantified and tracked over time and following perturbation. The automated sampling platform, genome-resolved profiling framework, and phase-analytic metrics introduced here provide a scalable strategy for characterizing community-level temporal dynamics in host-associated microbial ecosystems, with potential applications for understanding how disruption of microbial temporal organization contributes to dysbiosis.

cards.title: Fine-tuned Medical Vision-Language Model (MedGemma 1.5 4B) with and without Structured Radiologist Descriptors versus EU-TIRADS for Malignancy Risk Stratification of Thyroid Nodules at Ultrasound: A Tunisian Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
cards.abstract: Purpose. To evaluate a medical vision-language foundation model fine-tuned on thyroid ultrasound images, with or without the radiologist's structured descriptors, against expert-rated EU-TIRADS for the classification of thyroid nodules as benign or malignant. Materials and Methods. This retrospective study included nodules that underwent ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA) between January 2019 and August 2025 in two Tunisian centers, with consecutive recruitment, together with a selection of images from an international public dataset. Of 1,580 nodules, 1,456 (272 malignant; 1,280 patients) with an interpretable cytological or histological reference standard were allocated at patient level to training (n = 942), validation (n = 258) and a test set sealed before training (n = 256; 51 malignant). MedGemma 1.5 4B was fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation under four input configurations: the image with nodule biometry, with or without age and sex (A, B); A with chain-of-thought supervision (C); and A plus the eleven qualitative descriptors of the radiologist's structured report (D). The EU-TIRADS category was never a model input. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were compared with DeLong's test and a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 0.05; EU-TIRADS >= 4 was the prespecified comparator, with >= 5 as a sensitivity analysis. Results. Config D reached an AUROC of 0.953 (95% CI 0.909-0.976), versus 0.948 (0.894-0.972) for EU-TIRADS (difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.016 to +0.025), which met the non-inferiority criterion; Configs A-C, without the qualitative descriptors, reached 0.883-0.892 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.045 versus EU-TIRADS). At >= 4, EU-TIRADS had a sensitivity of 98.0% and produced 94 false positives among 205 benign nodules; at a threshold fixed on validation data, Config D reclassified 72 of them as negative while missing two additional cancers. Against EU-TIRADS >= 5 (sensitivity 92.2%, specificity 95.1%), Config D at its native threshold (88.2%, 94.1%) did not classify more nodules correctly (McNemar p = 0.22), and at its two other thresholds it classified fewer nodules correctly (p = 0.004 and 0.007). Raw probabilities were miscalibrated (expected calibration error 0.117 for Config D), and Platt scaling within the test set reduced this error to 0.019-0.040. Conclusion. Given the ultrasound image together with the radiologist's structured descriptors, the fine-tuned model matched expert EU-TIRADS discrimination and, against the >= 4 threshold, reclassified most false positives as negative, a gain concentrated in category 4 and based on only three cancers in category 4. It is best positioned as a report-standardizing second reader in the EU-TIRADS 4 gray zone, pending prospective external validation.

cards.title: Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean
cards.abstract: Deep learning has enabled virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology, offering a scalable approach to molecular profiling of routinely archived tissue without molecular assays. However, reliable uncertainty estimates are essential for identifying potentially inaccurate predictions, and it remains unclear whether existing methods provide useful information about prediction reliability. Here, we present a systematic benchmark of uncertainty estimation for virtual spatial transcriptomics across three cancer cohorts spanning melanoma, lung, and kidney tumors. We evaluate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using probabilistic likelihoods and approximate Bayesian methods alongside histology-free and training-free baselines, assessing both calibration and error informativeness. Across cohorts and methods, uncertainty is associated with prediction error, but the predicted mean largely explains this association. After accounting for the mean, uncertainty provides only weak information about larger errors. Moreover, good calibration does not imply informative uncertainty, with simple distributions fitted without histology achieving comparable calibration. We therefore distinguish calibrated from informative uncertainty and argue that uncertainty should provide information about prediction error beyond the predicted mean. This benchmark provides a framework for systematic uncertainty evaluation in virtual spatial transcriptomics. Code availability: https://github.com/ratschlab/uncertainty-vst-2026

cards.title: Cost-utility analysis of deep learning-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening using chest radiographs: implications of diagnostic thresholds and confirmatory testing.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis often goes undetected until a fracture occurs. Using a deep learning model to analyze routine chest radiographs may cost-effectively identify at-risk individuals. Economic benefit depends on how common the disease is, how the model is calibrated, and whether patients follow through with confirmatory bone density testing and pharmacological treatment initiation. Osteoporosis is common among postmenopausal women and often unrecognized until fragility fractures occur, despite its clinical and economic burden. Deep learning (DL)-based opportunistic screening using existing chest radiographs is a potential approach, but its economic value may vary with disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and care pathway completion. To assess the economic value of a DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening approach among Taiwanese postmenopausal women. A cost-utility analysis was conducted from the Taiwan healthcare perspective using a hybrid decision tree and Markov model. The model simulated a cohort of 50-year-old postmenopausal women over a 50-year horizon. Model inputs, including diagnostic performance, long-term outcomes, costs, and utilities, were derived from published literature, preferably local sources. Additional analyses examined alternative prevalence settings, sensitivity and specificity combinations, and confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation rates. In the base case, assuming full care-pathway completion, DL-based screening was cost-effective versus no screening, with an ICER of 21,827 per QALY, below the willingness-to-pay threshold of one GDP per capita in Taiwan. The approach became cost-effective when osteoporosis prevalence exceeded 14.3%. Across the diagnostic continuum, a sensitivity of 86.6% and specificity of 76.3% generated the greatest economic benefit. DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening was cost-effective under full care-pathway implementation. Its value depended on disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and completion of confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation, and was not maintained under real-world examination estimates observed in Taiwan. Strengthening the post-screening care pathway is therefore central to realizing this value.

cards.title: Multiple non-redundant functions underlie the essentiality of lipopolysaccharide in Gram-negative bacteria
cards.abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is well known for its immunostimulatory activity and its contribution to the permeability barrier of the Gram-negative outer membrane. Yet LPS is essential for growth in nearly all Gram-negative bacteria, even under laboratory conditions where its barrier function should be less critical. LPS contributes to envelope mechanics, membrane biogenesis, and cell division, but whether any of these functions accounts for its essentiality remains unclear. Here, we systematically tested these possibilities by depleting LPS in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Osmoprotection largely preserved cell-envelope integrity but not viability, demonstrating that the mechanical contribution of LPS alone cannot explain its essentiality. Genetic perturbations that increase peptidoglycan rigidity or alter phospholipid homeostasis partially improved growth, supporting independent roles for LPS in envelope mechanics and membrane biogenesis. An unbiased suppressor screen further identified activation of the MarA regulon as a potent mechanism for surviving LPS depletion. Protection required transport by the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump, revealing an unexpected connection between efflux and cell-envelope homeostasis. Thus, LPS essentiality emerges from multiple non-redundant contributions to Gram-negative cell-envelope physiology.

cards.title: Normative Temperature, Demographic Categories, and the Limits of Infrared Thermometry
cards.abstract: Objective. Temperature readings are routinely stratified by race and ethnicity, though significant group differences may reflect physiology, instrument noise, or categorization rather than biology. This study tests whether these categories partition facial infrared thermography measurements beyond individual variation and baseline device noise. Approach. A secondary analysis of thermography data (n = 951 adults) compares inner-canthus maximum (TCEmax) and full-face maximum (Tmax) temperatures across five administrative categories via one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), mixed-effects modeling, Bland-Altman analysis against oral reference, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis. Main results. ANOVA returns significant group differences (p < 0.001; eta-squared = 0.04 for TCEmax, 0.03 for Tmax), but the total spread (0.2 to 0.3 degrees Celsius) is comparable to device accuracy and within-subject variability. Individual variation accounts for 95% of TCEmax variance, and adding simulated Gaussian noise to participant-level temperatures (sigma = 0.10 to 0.30 degrees Celsius) preserves the complete group-mean rank order in as few as 37.5% of iterations. Significance. Testing whether a group difference survives perturbation at the scale of instrument accuracy offers a check against treating significance alone as evidence of physiology. Here, observed group differences are small relative to measurement variability, and their physiological interpretation remains uncertain, with implications for clinical tools that treat administrative categories as biologically meaningful.

cards.title: Carbendazim Disrupts Cellular Homeostasis and Proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans: A Global Proteomic Approach
cards.abstract: The extensive use of the broad-spectrum fungicide carbendazim (CBZ) has raised increasing environmental concerns due to its persistence and toxicity, leading to regulatory restrictions in several countries. Despite its widespread occurrence, the molecular mechanisms underlying CBZ toxicity in non-target organisms remain poorly understood. Here, we employed quantitative proteomics to characterize the systemic molecular response of Caenorhabditis elegans following exposure to a sublethal concentration of CBZ (0.01 mg.mL-1) from the L1 larval stage to day 1 of adulthood. A total of 273 differentially abundant proteins were identified in the N2 strain. Functional enrichment analysis revealed coordinated alterations in biological processes associated with protein synthesis, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, energy and lipid metabolism, intracellular trafficking, chromatin organization, and redox homeostasis, indicating extensive cellular reprogramming in response to CBZ exposure. Protein-protein interaction network analysis further identified ribosomal proteins and translation-associated factors as the principal hub proteins, suggesting that disruption of the translational machinery represents a central molecular event underlying CBZ toxicity. Collectively, these findings show that CBZ's biological effects extend beyond its established role as a microtubule-disrupting fungicide, affecting multiple interconnected cellular pathways involved in maintaining homeostasis. This study provides the first comprehensive proteomic characterization of CBZ toxicity in C. elegans, offering new mechanistic insights into its mode of action and highlighting the utility of integrative proteomics for assessing the impact of environmental contaminants on non-target organisms.

cards.title: Rigidity-Aware Geometric Pretraining for Protein Design and Conformational Ensembles
cards.abstract: Generative models have recently advanced de novo protein design by learning the statistical regularities of natural structures. However, current approaches face three key limitations: (1) Existing methods cannot jointly learn protein geometry and design tasks, where pretraining can be a solution; (2) Current pretraining methods mostly rely on local, non-rigid atomic representations for property prediction downstream tasks, limiting global geometric understanding for protein generation tasks; and (3) Existing approaches have yet to effectively model the rich dynamic and conformational information of protein structures. To overcome these issues, we introduce RigidSSL (Rigidity-Aware Self-Supervised Learning}, a geometric pretraining framework that front-loads geometry learning prior to generative finetuning. Phase I (RigidSSL-Perturb) learns geometric priors from 432K structures from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with simulated perturbations. Phase II (RigidSSL-MD) refines these representations on 1.3K molecular dynamics trajectories to capture physically realistic transitions. Underpinning both phases is a bi-directional, rigidity-aware flow matching objective that jointly optimizes translational and rotational dynamics to maximize mutual information between conformations. Empirically, RigidSSL variants improve designability by up to 43% while enhancing novelty and diversity in unconditional generation. Furthermore, RigidSSL-Perturb improves the success rate by 5.8% in zero-shot motif scaffolding and RigidSSL-MD captures more biophysically realistic conformational ensembles in G protein-coupled receptor modeling. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZhanghanNi/RigidSSL.git.

cards.title: Homeostatic feedback model of energy metabolism with adaptive enzyme levels exhibits problem solving behavior
cards.abstract: Metabolic networks are typically viewed as homeostatic systems that stabilize flux, energy charge, redox balance, and metabolite availability under perturbation. However, it remains unclear whether the same feedback architectures that support metabolic robustness can also generate learning-like, experience-dependent adaptation. Here, we develop a coarse-grained dynamical model of mammalian energy metabolism to test whether prior perturbation can improve future metabolic responses. The model represents core glucose, glutamine, fatty acid, and oxidative phosphorylation pathways as coupled ordinary differential equations with Michaelis-Menten-type fluxes, product-inhibition feedback, adaptive enzyme-capacity regulation, and explicit ATP costs for enzyme adjustment. Rather than aiming to reproduce quantitative fluxes for a specific cell type, the framework is designed to expose how metabolic feedback, regulatory cost, repeated perturbation, and environmental variability interact. We use this model to ask whether adaptive enzyme regulation enables improved recovery after repeated challenges, whether such effects depend on energetic control costs, and whether environmental variability broadens or constrains the set of reachable adaptive states. This approach provides a tractable way to investigate how homeostatic metabolic regulation may give rise to experience-dependent metabolic plasticity.

cards.title: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
cards.abstract: Background: Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods: Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MTRNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive MTRNR1 assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed in an international EQA programme. Results: Materials were homogeneous, workflow-compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates between 87.5 and 100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions: Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme deployment demonstrated feasibility in decentralised settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.

cards.title: Staphylococcus aureus GpsB, Stk, and VraSR form a cell wall surveillance network to maintain cell envelope integrity and mediate antibiotic resistance
cards.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is an alarming threat to public health worldwide. Specifically, drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus remains a major contributor to global mortality. Therefore, in-depth understanding of antibiotic resistance mechanisms is urgently needed to inform alternative therapeutic strategies. We previously showed that GpsB is a critical regulator of cell wall synthesis in S. aureus. GpsB executes its regulatory role via protein-protein interactions. Yet, how GpsB function is modulated in this organism has remained unclear. Intriguingly, a prior proteomics report indicated that GpsB is phosphorylated at six different residues by the sole serine/threonine kinase Stk. Hence, we explored the physiological significance of GpsB phosphorylation. We identify three phosphosites that are each independently sufficient to drive GpsB phosphoregulation, which likely alters its partner preference. We find that cells lacking gpsB exhibit heightened fosfomycin sensitivity, and that this is exacerbated by stk deletion. Our findings reveal that GpsB collaborates with Stk and the VraSR cell wall stress response system to coordinate the demand-driven availability of cell wall precursors. Collectively, this report establishes GpsB as a pivotal peptidoglycan supply chain sentinel that together with Stk and VraSR forms an integrated cell wall stress monitoring network that maintains cell envelope homeostasis and aids in antibiotic resistance.

cards.title: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
cards.abstract: Animals have a remarkable ability to act autonomously---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. To understand how biological autonomy may emerge from optimizing intrinsic goals, we use recent whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (\textit{Drosophila melanogaster}) that identify neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than $10$ seconds in advance. Combined with a neuromechanical digital twin of \textit{Drosophila}, these recordings allow us to test whether intrinsically motivated artificial agents with realistic embodiments quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. We implement a hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agent whose policy operates over a discrete library of motor primitives---fixed low-level controllers that actuate joint dynamics---closely matching ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents with no external reward using $20$ intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. We evaluate frozen policies in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled after the fruit-fly experiment, allowing us to compare spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decode future turn direction from both kinematics and neural activations on the same timescales observed in flies. We find that DIAYN---a hierarchical competency algorithm that learns a discrete set of policies maximizing behavioral entropy and the separability of their induced sensory observations---achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance with the fruit fly. Surprisingly, DIAYN's learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this behavioral diversity optimizes a concrete computational goal of maximizing state-space coverage at the \emph{population} level. Furthermore, DIAYN agents' latent activity closely captures the specific sum-difference rule in interhemispheric encoding of future kinematics in biological flies. Together, these results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.

cards.title: Association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of long-bone fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: To assess the association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of extremity long-bone fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 601 adults who underwent internal fixation for extremity long-bone fractures and completed at least 12 months of follow-up. METS-IR was calculated using pre-operative body mass index, fasting blood glucose, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Potential confounders were selected by LASSO logistic regression with ten-fold cross-validation. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the independent and nonlinear associations between METS-IR and fracture nonunion. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed to examine whether the association was consistent across different clinical subgroups. Of the 601 patients, 139 developed nonunion. METS-IR was higher in patients with nonunion than in those who achieved union (45 ± 5 vs. 36 ± 5, P < 0.001). After adjustment for LASSO-selected covariates, each one-unit increase in METS-IR was associated with higher odds of nonunion (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.24-1.38; P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant overall association and evidence of nonlinearity (P for overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.037). The association was generally consistent across sex, diabetes status, injury mechanism, and reduction method, while an interaction was observed for age (P for interaction = 0.029). Higher METS-IR was independently associated with fracture nonunion and showed a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. METS-IR may provide additional metabolic information for identifying patients at increased risk of impaired fracture healing.

cards.title: Benchmarking LLM-based Information Extraction Tools for Medical Documents
cards.abstract: Background: Medical documents are a crucial resource for medical research around the world. While troves of valuable health data exist, they are largely computationally inaccessible as hard copies of unstructured text. Moreover, the persistent prevalence of fax machines in medical settings contributes to further degradation of document quality. Manual data extraction from these documents is time-consuming and resource intensive. However, large language models (LLMs) have recently shown great promise for automated digitization and information extraction (IE), greatly improving upon previous technologies in terms of accuracy. Objective: Here we aim to survey the landscape of LLM-based IE tools with respect to their applicability to biomedical documents and to systematically benchmark them on synthetic documents with paired reference extractions. We put special focus on locally executable tools and models that suit privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Methods: We reviewed LLM-based IE tools from the literature and assessed them with respect to their suitability for use in biomedical research. We found only one of these tools (NuExtract2) to satisfy our selection criteria and compared it to LLM foundation models prompted to perform extractions. We created 200 mock molecular test reports with paired reference data using a bespoke procedural generation approach and evaluated the tools' performance across different prompting strategies, input modalities, and document qualities. Results: We found model performance to be very sensitive to input modalities and quality. The best overall performance was observed for the proprietary GPT 4.1-mini, with an F1 score of 79.2% averaged across quality levels and modalities. The best performing open-weights model was Mistral-small 3.1 with an average F1 score of 76.2%. The NuExtract2 model was the only one able to run on regular laptop computers, but did not perform well. Surprisingly, we found the choice of one-shot over zero-shot prompts to only have a small effect size on extraction performance in most cases. Conclusions: LLMs place the automatic processing of highly complex medical documents in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings within reach, but still require human oversight. Availability: Source code and data are available on GitHub and on Zenodo, respectively.

cards.title: CBAM-enhanced MaxViT-Tiny for gastrointestinal endoscopy image classification: Robustness, explainability, and external validation
cards.abstract: Automated classification of the huge number of images generated during gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is required for reliable and interpretable diagnosis, but there is concern about the vulnerability of deep models to adversarial perturbations. In the current study, a MaxViT-Tiny backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) head is used for 8-class classification of the Kvasir endoscopic images. After deleting duplicate images, 3,996 images remained, which were split into a training set (70%), a validation set (15%) and a test set (15%); the model was compared with five backbones using the same CBAM head under three random seeds. The proposed model obtained the highest test accuracy of 94.33%, a macro F1 score of 0.9431, and a macro area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9975, with a mean accuracy of 93.72 {+/-} 1.06% across all seeds. White-box FGSM, PGD, CW-L2, and MI-FGSM attacks greatly reduced the accuracy: after adversarial fine-tuning, the accuracy under FGSM was 74.17%, while the accuracy under PGD and MI-FGSM was below 4%, showing poor cross-attack generalization. A preliminary attack detector obtained an AUC of 0.857. Grad-CAM++, Score-CAM, and GradientSHAP sometimes identified clinically relevant regions, but also sometimes focused on non-anatomical artefacts. High accuracy on clean images, even with attention augmentation, therefore does not imply high accuracy on adversarial images or reliable explanations, and the model needs further verification on independent datasets and multi-centre validation before clinical use.

cards.title: GOLDEN: Gene expression and allele-informed decomposition for genetic heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomic data
cards.abstract: Motivation Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables exploration of cellular interactions, including immune responses. However, current methods rely on pathologists, with limitations in addressing genetic heterogeneity, where niches harboring nonclonal cells, including placental or allograft tissues, are present. Deciphering these interindividual mixtures remains challenging. Results For deciphering interindividual heterogeneity in ST, we developed GOLDEN (Gene expressiOn and aLlele-informed DEcomposition for geNetic heterogeneity), which involves an allele-aware multitask network that encodes spot-level expressions into shared latent representations. Incorporating allele features, dual heads classify spot identity (target, nontarget, or mixed) and estimate target fractions. We utilized synthetic ST data with spot-level ground truth using semiallogeneic single-cell profiles. For these synthetic benchmarks, GOLDEN achieved reliable deconvolution, with high correlation (Pearson's r = 0.977) and low error (mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.045) in fraction estimation and consistent predictions across real-world STs. These predictions were genetically validated. Using GOLDEN, resolving spot-level genetic heterogeneity is feasible. Availability and implementation GOLDEN and the simulation code for ST are available at https://github.com/othertics/GOLDEN.

cards.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement
cards.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics platforms such as Xenium require a predefined gene panel, and the genes in that panel are detected less efficiently, and to gene-specific degrees, in the spatial assay than in the single-cell reference used to choose them. We present X-SPEAR, a framework that couples DART marker selection with probe-level off-target assessment. DART learns short, interpretable Boolean gene rules and assembles several gene-disjoint rules per cell type. Its detection-aware training thins the reference to per-gene detection rates measured in a different, already completed experiment, so no Xenium data from the target tissue are needed before the panel is ordered. On held-out Xenium data from ovarian cancer, mouse brain and cervical cancer, DART substantially outperformed existing marker-selection methods at matched panel size, by 0.04-0.11 macro-F1 over Wilcoxon rank-sum, 0.04-0.08 over COSG and 0.10-0.18 over NS-Forest, and it reached Wilcoxon's best accuracy with 42-69% fewer genes. Ablations show that most of this gain comes from detection-aware training, which also improves other rank-based selectors and requires a detection profile measured with the same assay chemistry. At similar accuracy, DART's rule structure adds rules that faithfully summarise the downstream classifier, robustness to single-probe loss across 45 retinal ganglion cell subtypes, and better resolution of closely related cell states. We are applying X-SPEAR to design a Xenium panel for mouse retinal ganglion cell subtypes, and its in situ evaluation is in progress. X-SPEAR is available as an open-source Python package.

cards.title: Real-Time Neurotransmitter Sensing in Midbrain Organoids Using 3D Carbon Cup Electrodes
cards.abstract: Real time, chemically selective detection of neurotransmitter release in brain organoids remains a challenge due to their complex three dimensional architecture and limited optical accessibility. We introduce 3D printed carbon cup electrodes (CCEs) -pyrolyzed, multi level pillar structures - designed to confine a single organoid, increase electroactive surface area, and enable amperometric recordings of oxidizable neurotransmitters. The CCEs exhibit excellent electrochemical performance and reproducibility, supporting diffusion controlled dopamine redox behavior without interference from culture medium. Using ventral midbrain (vMB) organoids at two maturation stages (Day 30 and Day 90), we demonstrate real time detection of potassium evoked dopamine release directly from organoids. Mature organoids exhibit higher peak currents, correlating with increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression confirmed by immunocytochemistry. Embedding organoids in Matrigel significantly attenuates dopamine signals, indicating a diffusion barrier that limits stimulant access and/or dopamine transport to the electrode. Repetitive stimulations reveal progressive depletion of dopamine stores, consistent with diminished vesicular release. Chemical perturbations using 6 hydroxydopamine and verapamil further validate the platform by producing substantial reductions in dopamine release accompanied by loss of TH neurons. These results establish CCEs as a powerful tool for label free, real-time monitoring of neurotransmission in human organoids, with potential for multiplexed sensing and integration of enzymatic detection strategies for non electroactive neurotransmitters.

cards.title: Glucose-Lowering Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes-Associated Sarcopenia: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence and a Muscle-Centred Framework.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognised as a clinically important comorbidity in diabetes mellitus, particularly in older adults and individuals with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Because skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, declines in muscle mass, quality, strength and physical performance may exacerbate insulin resistance and glycaemic instability and increase the risks of frailty, disability, falls, fractures, cardiovascular events and mortality. Contemporary glucose-lowering therapies have transformed diabetes care through established cardiorenal benefits and weight reduction, yet skeletal muscle outcomes are rarely prespecified or systematically assessed in pivotal trials. This evidence gap is especially relevant for weight-reducing agents such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, which are often associated with reductions in dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived or bioelectrical impedance analysis-derived lean-mass estimates. However, these changes should be interpreted cautiously, as they often occur in the context of overall weight loss and may be influenced by alterations in body water. In addition, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry- or dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived lean-mass estimates do not directly quantify contractile skeletal muscle. Accordingly, reductions in lean-mass estimates alone are insufficient to infer clinically meaningful muscle loss without concurrent assessment of muscle strength or physical performance. This narrative review summarises the bidirectional mechanisms linking diabetes and sarcopenia and appraises major glucose-lowering drug classes from a muscle-centred perspective. It integrates mechanistic insights with human evidence on muscle-relevant outcomes, including body composition, strength and physical performance, and addresses practical safety and monitoring considerations in sarcopenia-prone phenotypes, including sarcopenic obesity. We also propose a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating Cardiorenal-Muscle Quadrant Framework that considers glycaemic efficacy and cardiorenal benefit alongside muscle reserve, functional status and treatment-related risks, with emphasis on functional monitoring, resistance exercise, nutritional optimisation and individualised glycaemic targets in older or frail adults.

cards.title: Rational Design of a Photoactivated Fluorescent Probe for Thiol-ene Mediated Protein Labelling
cards.abstract: Fluorescent labelling of biomolecules enables the visualization and tracking of molecular processes in cells, providing insights into cellular function and disease mechanisms. Despite recent advances in bioorthogonal labelling, efficient and site-selective strategies for targeting alkene functionalities remain limited. Here, we report AbzSH, a compact aminobenzamide-based fluorescent thiol probe for selective alkene labelling through thiol-ene ligation. Photoinduced ligation proceeds under mild, radical-mediated conditions in aqueous media and exhibits broad substrate compatibility, including carbohydrate, amino acid, and steroid scaffolds. The method is readily extended to protein labelling, enabling selective modification of both chemically functionalized proteins and engineered proteins containing genetically encoded alkene motifs. Efficient and chemoselective labelling was further demonstrated in complex cell lysates, highlighting the robustness of the approach in biologically relevant environments. Collectively, these results establish AbzSH as a versatile fluorescent probe for alkene-directed biomolecular labelling and provide a broadly applicable platform for chemical biology, molecular imaging, proteomics, and drug discovery.

cards.title: A hippocampal digital Twin reveals latent structure in freely flying bats
cards.abstract: Concurrent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), large-scale neuronal recording, and behavioral tracking have enabled increasingly powerful predictive models of brain-behavior relationships. Yet predictive accuracy does not automatically yield interpretable principles of neural organization, particularly during natural behavior, where the relevant variables computed are often unknown in advance. Here, we developed a functional digital twin of the hippocampus, trained jointly on large-scale neural activity and self-directed three-dimensional flight in freely flying bats. A multimodal, multitask transformer accurately predicted both neural activity and behavior, outperformed standard approaches, and generalized across recording sessions. Interrogating the model's representations suggested a form of hippocampal generalization across self-selected trajectories that was not apparent in physical coordinates, but was plainly visible in the model's low-dimensional latent space. We confirmed this organization directly in the recorded neural activity: neurons fired at corresponding stages of spatially distinct paths connecting the same origin and destination, preserving their relative firing order even as their firing fields shifted with the path. Analysis of neuron-specific readouts further identified functional relationships among neurons that generalized from flight to waking rest and sleep, brain states never used for training, and differed systematically between the hippocampal subregions CA1 and CA3. Together, these results show how AI-based functional digital twins can complement conventional analysis by generating testable hypotheses about neural organization during natural behavior.

cards.title: Discoidins are cytosolic lectins that recognize methylated L-rhamnose epitopes on mycobacterial glycolipids and glycopeptidolipids upon vacuole damage
cards.abstract: Mycobacteria are surrounded by a dynamic, glycolipid-rich envelope that governs virulence and immune recognition, yet how cytosolic lectins sense its organization during intracellular infection remains unclear. Here, we show that Dictyostelium discoideum discoidins act as cytosolic sensors of mycobacterial envelope exposure. During infection, Mycobacterium marinum damages the limiting vacuolar membrane, triggering recruitment of all canonical isoforms (DscA, DscC, DscD, and DscE) to distinct foci around bacilli. Discoidins are not recruited after sterile endolysosomal damage, indicating that, unlike galectins, they recognize non-self surface-associated bacterial glycans rather than exposed host glycans. DscA and DscE display distinct glycan specificities. Combining transposon mutagenesis, synthetic glycan arrays, biochemical fractionation, and envelope mutants, we identify a restricted set of lipid-associated determinants enriched in methylated L-rhamnose motifs within LOS-, PGL-, and GPL-related structures. Recognition requires the conserved beta-galactoside-binding pocket of the H-type lectin domain, and isoform-specific synthetic disaccharides inhibit binding to intact bacteria. Analyses exclude AG-PG, AM/LAM, alpha-glucan, and TDM as major ligands and identify LOS and GPL-like glycolipids as dominant targets. PDIM/PGL or LOS disruption reduces discoidin binding to intact bacteria, although some ligands remain detectable in envelope extracts, underscoring the importance of accessibility. LOS deficiency also reduces DscA recruitment to intracellular bacilli. Therefore, binding of discoidins to glycan epitopes depends on ligand presence and accessibility, as well as on envelope perturbations and unmasking of specific glycolipids and glycopeptidolipids. These findings reveal pathogen envelope glycans as direct targets of cytosolic lectin surveillance and establish discoidins as probes of mycobacterial envelope remodeling during infection.

cards.title: Mitochondrial and bioenergetic processes are enriched in large-but are reciprocally depleted in small extracellular vesicles
cards.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are a promising class of drug delivery carriers for a broad range of therapeutic applications. We have previously demonstrated that brain endothelial cell (BEC)-derived large EVs (>200 nm in particle diameter) increased mitochondrial function in recipient BECs and improved therapeutic outcomes in a mouse model of ischemic stroke. In the current study, we demonstrate using size-resolved quantitative proteomics and gene-set enrichment analysis that mitochondrial and bioenergetic processes are enriched in large- but are reciprocally depleted in small EVs (exosomes, <200 nm in particle diameter). These results are striking and reveal the selective packaging of mitochondrial cargo in large but not small EVs. These strong mechanistic data anchor the rationale for the continued development of large EV mitochondria as a potential approach for the treatment of multiple diseases associated with mitochondrial dysfunction.

cards.title: Time-resolved proteomic analysis of hepatitis B virus infection
cards.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its impact on host proteome dynamics during early infection remains poorly defined. Here, we performed time-resolved label-free quantitative (LFQ) proteomics to characterise the host response to HBV infection in human HepG2 hepatoma cells. Across five time points spanning the first three weeks of infection, we quantified 5,365 unique proteins, including two HBV proteins (C/preC-derived and S), revealing subtle yet coordinated changes in the hepatocellular proteome. Early infection was characterised by selective alterations in cytoskeletal organisation, extracellular matrix components, and focal adhesion pathways, alongside enrichment of complement-associated proteins. Notably, we identified a transient, specific increase in the abundance of complement component C5 without a corresponding change in C3, indicating differential regulation of complement pathway members during infection. These findings define a temporally resolved proteomic landscape of HBV host interactions and uncover previously underappreciated complement dynamics consistent with a selective and restrained host response. Together, this provides a framework for mechanistic studies of early viral infection and host adaptation.

cards.title: Impact of bisphosphonate drug holidays on bone mineral density and osteoporotic fracture risk: real-world evidence from a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Bisphosphonate drug holidays can reduce rare adverse effects, but their skeletal impact is unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, ALN holiday caused modest BMD loss and BTMs rise without increased fracture risk; effects of ZOL holiday were minimal. This study suggests bisphosphonate drug holidays are safe for selected patients with regular monitoring. Bisphosphonate (BP) drug holiday prevents rare adverse effects of BPs in osteoporotic patients, but its effect on bone mineral density (BMD), bone turnover markers (BTMs), and fracture risk is still unclear. This study aimed to investigate BMD/BTM variations and clinical fracture risk for patients undergoing BP drug holidays. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, patients who received ≥4.5 years of alendronate (ALN) or ≥3 doses of zoledronate (ZOL) were included. BMD at the lumbar spine (LS), femoral neck (FN), and total hip (TH), BTMs, and 3-year fracture incidence were assessed between drug holiday (ALN: n = 71; ZOL: n = 20) and ongoing treatment groups (ALN: n = 59; ZOL: n = 47). Compared with ongoing ALN therapy, initiating drug holiday resulted in moderate declines in BMD at LS (-2.23%, 95% CI: -3.70% to -0.76%), TH (-1.62%, 95% CI: -2.68% to -0.56%), and FN (-1.89%, 95% CI: -3.49% to -0.28%) within 1 year. BTMs all rose significantly over 1 year, yet remained below pretreatment levels for at least 3 years. In contrast, there were no significant differences in BMD (1-year LS: -0.47%, 95% CI: -2.38% to 1.43%, TH: -1.07%, 95% CI: -2.77% to 0.64%) and BTM changes between ZOL groups at 1- and 2-year follow-up. No significant differences in clinical fragility fractures were observed between ALN groups (9.9% vs. 6.8%; HR 1.45) and ZOL groups (5% vs. 6.4%). Our findings support that BP drug holidays are feasible for selected patients with adequate BMD. ZOL conferred more sustained skeletal protection than ALN, particularly at the LS, whereas ALN discontinuation was associated with earlier and more pronounced BMD decline and BTM elevation; annual monitoring of BMD and BTMs appears particularly important during the ALN drug holiday period.

cards.title: Ground-truth evaluation of sparse autoencoder features on spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings
cards.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are increasingly used to extract interpretable features from the embeddings of biological foundation models. Because SAEs trained with different random seeds learn different features, reproducibility across seeds has become a common test of whether these features can be trusted. We asked whether reproducible features are also meaningful, using embeddings whose concepts are known: five spatial transcriptomics embeddings of two colorectal cancer sections and Geneformer embeddings of single-cell RNA profiles, with cell lineages as concepts; synthetic data with planted cell states; and the residual stream of a small language model, with token classes as concepts. Varimax rotations of the same embeddings were almost perfectly reproducible, yet rotation features (PCA, varimax and ICA) covered at most three of seven lineages and three of eight token classes. Single SAE fits showed the opposite profile: they covered most concepts with purer gene programs but reproduced only 27-46% of their features. A consensus over five SAE fits combined the two strengths. It was reproducible (78-98% across sources) and as pure as single fits: 11-40% of its features carried marker genes of another lineage, against 44-70% for varimax. Against the strongest baseline, varimax sparsified to the SAE's sparsity, the consensus covered as many concepts on PCA and Geneformer embeddings and more on learned spatial and text embeddings. The consensus also had costs. It covered fewer lineages than single fits and, like all SAEs, missed weak planted states that rotations recovered; neither a longer single fit nor a second SAE trained on the consensus residual recovered what it discarded. Reproducibility alone therefore ranks features poorly: SAE features should be reported with the number of known concepts they cover and the purity of their gene programs, against a rotation of the same embedding sparsified to the SAE's sparsity.

cards.title: Early-onset spontaneous murine mammary tumors show increased lymphocyte representation and reduced MHC antigen presentation
cards.abstract: Simple Summary Not all breast tumors behave the same way, and part of the reason may be inherited rather than caused by the tumor itself. Using mice that carry the same cancer-causing HER2/neu gene but differ in genetic background, we found that introduction of the PWK/PhJ genetic background was associated with tumors that appeared about a month earlier. These early tumors contained a larger proportion of immune cells, including T and B cells, but the T-cell population showed reduced expression of genes associated with cytotoxic activity. At the same time, the tumors had lower levels of proteins and genes that let the immune system recognize tumor cells, alongside higher levels of structural proteins that can make tissue stiffer and easier for cancer to invade. These findings suggest that genetic background shapes not only how quickly breast tumors arise but also how well the immune system can recognize them, a distinction that may matter for future immune-based treatments. Background/Objectives: Genetic background modifies cancer risk and phenotype in humans, but its influence on the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation machinery in ErbB2 (HER2/neu)-driven breast cancer is not well defined. We used a genetically diverse mouse cross to test whether the wild-derived PWK/PhJ background alters immune representation and antigen presentation in a NeuT model of HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. Methods: Previously, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping using Diversity Outbred mice and r/qtl2 identified candidate loci driving tumor onset and growth. The wild-derived PWK/PhJ genetic background was predicted to harbor genes that regulated early onset of HER2/neu-driven tumors. BALB NeuT and (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT female mice were monitored twice weekly for spontaneous mammary tumor onset and growth. Tumor immune composition was profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Protein abundance was measured by data-independent acquisition proteomics in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue (n=5 per genotype). Single-nucleus multiome (RNA + ATAC), bulk RNA-seq, and H3K27ac datasets from the same strain comparison were analyzed for focused MHC II cross-layer analyses. Results: As predicted, (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT mice developed tumors significantly earlier than the parental BALB NeuT mice (10 vs. 15 weeks of age; p < 0.0001). In the scRNA-seq dataset, F1 tumors showed greater representation of Cd3e-expressing T cells and a Cd79a-expressing B-cell population not detected in BALB NeuT tumors, and a distinct neutrophil cluster; F1 T cells also showed lower expression of the cytotoxicity-associated genes Tox, Ltk, Nkg7, and Gzmb relative to BALB NeuT tumor-infiltrating T cells. Proteomics identified 46 differentially abundant proteins (25 higher, 21 lower in F1), with coordinate down-regulation of Stat1, Tapbp, Parp9, and Dtx3l alongside MHC class I and II proteins and up-regulation of extracellular-matrix and elastic-fiber proteins. Focused cross-layer analysis showed lower whole-tumor expression of a Stat1/MHC II-associated gene set together with reduced epithelial chromatin accessibility at selected regions near Cd74 and H2-Aa. Conclusions: The PWK/PhJ genetic background is associated with earlier HER2-driven tumor onset, greater lymphocyte proportion, and reduced activity of a STAT1-associated antigen-presentation program despite similar post-onset tumor growth kinetics.

cards.title: Informing risk stratification and vaccine policy via a predictive mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection
cards.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 human challenge studies enabled unprecedented high frequency temporal measurements of immune determinants of viral control. We integrated prior knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 replication, innate, cytotoxic T cell and antibody responses into a dynamic model which captured viral-load kinetics in seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype virus. The model predicted measured innate and adaptive immune dynamics. Perturbation analyses indicated that innate immunity limits peak viral load, whereas antibodies principally mediate clearance while cytotoxic T cells become critical in antibody deficiency. Pre-existing antibodies suppressed both viral replication and subsequent immune activation- a prediction validated in a second challenge study of seropositive participants infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The model explains how specific immunodeficiencies may increase susceptibility to severe or persistent infection, supporting clinical risk stratification. It suggests that T cell-targeted vaccination strategies may provide limited protection without effective neutralising antibodies, and that attenuated boosting after low-dose exposure requires repeated vaccination to reduce breakthrough infections, informing public health policy.

cards.title: The essential role of connective-tissue cells during axolotl limb regeneration
cards.abstract: Axolotls (Ambystoma mexicanum) are known for their remarkable limb-regeneration abilities, which involve the formation of the blastema, a specialized structure consisting of progenitor cells contributed by all major tissues of the limb. Lateral plate mesoderm (LPM)-derived connective tissue (CT) cells dedifferentiate and play a critical role in blastema formation and subsequent limb regeneration. However, the complexity of the blastema cellular composition and the extent of CT participation and necessity have not been rigorously explored. To address this gap, we conducted spatial transcriptomics using a select array of probes, revealing that CT cells constitute up to 75% of the blastema cells. Genetic ablation of CT cells significantly delays or truncates limb regeneration, underscoring their necessity during this process. Analysis of the molecular profile during blastema formation identifies a temporally ordered gene expression pattern reflecting sequential phases of CT cell dedifferentiation, proliferation, and redifferentiation. Finally, a cell-cell communication inference identifies a CT-cell-autonomous FGFR1/AKT1 signaling axis as a cell-intrinsic molecular requirement for limb regeneration. Together, our work reaffirms the central role of CT cells in axolotl limb regeneration and lays the foundation for identifying molecular mechanisms that govern blastema formation during the initial phases of limb regeneration.

cards.title: Histology-aware Inference of Cell-cell Communication in Spatial Transcriptomics
cards.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is fundamental to tissue organization and function, yet inferring communication from spatial transcriptomics (ST) remains challenging because molecular and spatial information does not fully capture the anatomical context of signaling. Paired hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained images provide complementary insights into tissue architecture and cellular morphology, which remain underutilized as the explicit contextual constraint of CCC inference. Here we present HARMONIC, a histology-aware graph learning framework for anatomically contextualized CCC inference from ST and H&E images. HARMONIC uses conditional mutual information to model dependencies among tissue architecture, ligand-receptor-mediated signaling, gene expression and morphology, and integrates these representations through self-supervised graph learning. Across synthetic and biological datasets spanning platforms, species and tissues, HARMONIC suppresses less anatomically plausible interactions while recovering context-supported signaling across tumor-immune interfaces, necrotic transitions, anatomical compartments and microvascular structures. These findings establish tissue architecture as the explicit contextual constraint of spatial CCC inference.

cards.title: Single Cell Proteomics reveals partial uncoupling of the Glycerol-3-Phosphate shuttle to compensate for Electron Transport Chain dysfunction in Alexander Disease GFAP mutations
cards.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare genetic leukodystrophy caused by dominant mutations in the gene coding for the astrocytic intermediate filament protein Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP). Understanding disease mechanisms is complicated by the fact that mutant GFAP promotes further GFAP accumulation, making it difficult to distinguish mutation-specific effects from those caused by elevated GFAP levels. Here, we performed mass spectrometry-based single cell proteomics to investigate proteomic alterations associated with increasing levels of wildtype GFAP and a common AxD-causing mutant GFAP R239C. By analyzing individual cells spanning a broad range of GFAP expression levels, we separated dosage-dependent effects from mutation-specific responses. Cells expressing high levels of wildtype GFAP increasingly resembled R239C-expressing cells at the proteomic level, supporting a role for GFAP accumulation in disease pathogenesis. In contrast, mutant GFAP specifically correlated with increased mitochondrial antioxidant enzymes and remodeling of the proteasome tailored toward ATP- and ubiquitin-independent degradation of oxidized proteins. Integration with proteomics data from patient-derived cortical organoids revealed increased abundance of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and respiratory chain assembly factors without corresponding changes in mitochondrially encoded proteins, suggesting impaired electron transport chain (ETC) assembly. Consistent with this, AxD cells displayed reduced oxygen consumption, increased glycolytic activity, enhanced utilization of the cytosolic part of the glycerol-3-phosphate (G3P) shuttle, and accumulation of triacylglycerides and lipid droplets. We propose that ETC dysfunction promotes partial uncoupling of the G3P shuttle, allowing sustained regeneration of cytosolic NAD to support glycolysis while diverting G3P toward lipid synthesis and storage. By regenerating NAD through the G3P shuttle rather than lactate fermentation, AxD astrocytes may sustain glycolytic flux while preserving lactate production, an important metabolic substrate for neighboring neurons. Together, our findings identify ETC dysfunction as a central feature of AxD and suggest that metabolic adaptation through the G3P shuttle links mitochondrial dysfunction to glycolytic reprogramming and lipid accumulation. More broadly, these results provide new insight into how astrocyte dysfunction drives molecular pathways implicated in neurodegeneration.

cards.title: stem.MAP: Identification of cell-type-specific protein complexes in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
cards.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) experiments on mESC. Our resource, stem.MAP, identifies 3,986 complexes encompassing ~133,000 unique interactions, and 8,616 proteins. stem.MAP captures variant complexes critical for stem cell function including the PRC2, BAF and NuRD complexes. stem.MAP also discriminates mutually exclusive interactions specific to embryonic stem cells (e.g. Eif4ebp2 - Eif4e). Finally we observe 1,388 high confidence stem.MAP interactions found only in mESC CF-MS data, many with support from AlphaFold modeling and a gastruloid coregulation network. We make stem.MAP protein complexes available through our web resource: stem.proteincomplexes.org. We anticipate stem.MAP will be beneficial to the study of early development and we expect our proteomics-based machine learning workflow to be applicable to the creation of any context-specific protein interaction network.

cards.title: Functional Data Clustering of Filopodia Dynamics
cards.abstract: Notch signaling plays a significant role in tissue patterning. During patterning of the fruit fly dorsal thorax peripheral nervous system, basal filopodia extend the spatial range of cell-cell communication, yet it is still unclear how Notch is activated in long range signaling via filopodia interaction. Filopodia undergo dynamic length changes during their lifetime, which could supply the mechanical pulling force required for notch activation. However, their dynamics are often characterized using individual scalar values such as maximum length and extension rate which could obscure more intricate dynamics. Our hypothesis is that signaling filopodia exhibit distinct and recurrent temporal patterns which can be identified by a consideration of their complete lifetime trajectories. Our work analyzes 60 filopodia trajectories at the basal surface of the fly dorsal thorax during patterning. Length profiles were smoothed using cubic B-splines and clustered by first reducing them to their dominant functional principal component followed by the application of various clustering algorithms. We found that 94.29% of the overall trajectory variation is explained by the first four functional principal components which account for variations in maximal length, extension and retraction rate, duration of stationary phase and length fluctuation frequency. Five recurrent temporal profiles (dynamic extension modes) with varying trajectory shapes and physical attributes, were identified using trimmed K-means. These findings demonstrate that whereas the major source of structural variation in filopodia profiles remains the length, extension rate and retraction rate, nontrivial combinations of these create distinct dynamic modes of extension which provide new insight into their length profiles. Our work thus offers a quantitative framework for future research connecting filopodia dynamic extension modes to productive Notch activation.

cards.title: A healthy donor kidney aging signature estimable from PAS histology and its association with progression of diabetic kidney disease
cards.abstract: Background. As kidneys age, their cells change in arrangement and gene expression. Whether these changes are also present in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and whether they relate to how quickly kidney function is lost, is not known. Methods. Zero-time biopsies from 24 healthy living kidney donors (aged 36-66 years) and biopsies from 28 patients with DKD were profiled by single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics with a 5,101-gene panel. In the donors, we identified how cell neighborhoods and cell-type gene expression change with age and summarized the expression changes as tissue-aging scores. The scores were applied unchanged to DKD and related to the rate of eGFR decline after biopsy in 24 patients, with adjustment for age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria. We also estimated the scores from routine periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) slides, using models that did not include the patient being scored. Results. In older donors, immune cells were less often found next to tubular epithelium, and contacts between endothelial cells and podocytes and between stromal and epithelial cells were fewer, although cell proportions changed little. Expression of stress-response and cell-cycle regulators (FOXO3, CDKN1A, BBC3, PINK1, IRAK1, SOCS1) increased. Changes in cell contacts in DKD tissue largely followed the same direction as those in older donors. In DKD, higher tissue-aging scores were associated with faster eGFR loss independently of age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria (overall score, partial {rho} = -0.61); this held for tubular, endothelial, immune, and parietal epithelial cell scores but not for the podocyte score. Scores estimated from PAS slides correlated with the transcriptomic scores (mean {rho} = 0.62) and were also associated with faster eGFR loss (partial {rho}, -0.44 to -0.56). Conclusions. Healthy kidney aging involves a selective loss of cell contacts together with a coordinated stress-response program. DKD kidneys that carry this aging phenotype lose function faster, and the phenotype can be estimated in part from the routine diagnostic PAS slide.

cards.title: A Kernel-Spectral Index for Single-Neuron Input-Output Complexity
cards.abstract: The computational capacity of individual neurons in the brain is a central problem in computational neuroscience and an increasingly relevant link between neuroscience and AI. Recent work fitting artificial neural networks to detailed cortical pyramidal neurons showed that reproducing their millisecond-precision input-output behavior can require temporal convolutional networks with five to eight layers, suggesting that cortical neurons may function as deep computational units inside brain circuits. Yet current quantitative studies of single-neuron complexity are largely surrogate-based; consequently, the obtained results are difficult to interpret, and the process often demands massive computational resources. We introduce the Spectral Complexity Index (SCI), a white-box measure that represents presynaptic histories with an explicit kernel geometry and quantifies how many ordered spectral modes are needed to explain somatic response energy. Across 35 biophysically detailed human and mouse cortical neuron models, SCI yields a statistically significant separation of the two species, strongly agrees with the DNN-based Functional Complexity Index on these cells (Spearman correlation: {rho}=0.797), and remains stable under sampling and kernel perturbations. Additionally, compared to existing methods such as FCI, the computational cost of SCI is reduced to approximately 1/10 or less. SCI turns single-neuron complexity from a black-box surrogate property into an interpretable spectral object, enabling reproducible, fast, and efficient comparisons of neuronal computation across cells and species.

cards.title: Smaller Cortical Responses to Balance Perturbations in Parkinson's Disease with Freezing of Gait
cards.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) is among the most disabling symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD) and is associated with balance impairment and increased falls risk, yet remains challenging to understand due to its episodic and context-dependent nature. Altered supplementary motor area (SMA) function at rest and before self-initiated movements has been implicated in FoG; however, whether this extends to functionally relevant balance behavior is unknown. A loss of balance in response to support surface translations during standing elicits a perturbation-evoked N1 potential, an error assessment signal linked to SMA activity. We therefore predicted that people with FoG would have smaller and later N1 responses than people with PD without FoG and older adults. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) during backward support-surface translations in 29 people with PD (71 {+/-} 7 years), including 13 people with a history of FoG (FoG+) and 16 people without FoG (FoG-), and 26 older adults (OA; 67 {+/-} 6 years). N1 amplitude and latency were quantified at a central midline electrode and defined as the largest negative peak 100-300 ms post-perturbation. N1 responses were similar between OA and FoG- ({Delta} = 4.0 {micro}V and 2.8 ms, respectively). In contrast, FoG+ had smaller N1 amplitudes than FoG- ({Delta} = 18.1 {micro}V, p = 0.001) and OA ({Delta} = 14.1 {micro}V, p = 0.003), and both differences persisted after adjusting for age. FoG+ also had later N1 latencies than OA ({Delta} = 26.5 ms, p = 0.029), with a similar but non-significant difference versus FoG- ({Delta} = 23.6 ms, p = 0.091); after adjusting for age, these latency differences were not retained. These findings suggest that perturbation-evoked cortical activity is altered in FoG, potentially reflecting altered SMA function, and may provide a functionally relevant marker of FoG susceptibility.

cards.title: Environment-Aware DNA Language Model for Stress-Responsive Genomic Prioritization in Maize
cards.abstract: Abiotic stresses such as heat and drought severely reduce the productivity of major crops including maize, with adverse implications for agricultural sustainability. Despite progress in characterizing stress resilience, identifying genomic regions associated with stress response remains challenging due to complex genotype-by-environment interactions. Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), inspired by advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-training on DNA sequences to capture regulatory patterns; however, their adaptation to plant stress-response analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an environment-aware DNA-LLM framework that incorporates stress-specific prompt tokens into AgroNT, a transformer-based plant GFM, using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The model learns stress-conditioned genomic representations that exhibit distinct structures across environmental contexts. We further formulate a prioritization method that uses stress-induced shifts in these representations relative to the control condition together with stress-token-associated transformer attention patterns to identify putative stress-responsive genomic regions. The framework was evaluated on the Genomes-to-Fields (G2F) dataset, comprising over 4,000 maize hybrids grown across 38 locations over 8 years, using grain yield under heat, drought, and combined heat-drought stress. Flowering traits were used to assess generalizability of the stress-conditioned representations across phenotypes. The prioritized regions were assessed using spatiotemporal differential gene-expression profiles, stress-associated quantitative trait loci, and transcription-factor characterization. Regulatory motif analysis further revealed stress-associated motifs enriched within the prioritized sequences as well as model-emphasized high-attention regions. Functional annotation of genes proximal to prioritized regions highlighted roles in transcriptional regulation, signaling, and metabolic pathways relevant to abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of stress-conditioned transformer-based sequence modeling for environment-aware genome-to-phenome analysis in crop improvement.
