cards.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. Not applicable.

cards.title: TiSAM: fusing spatial and histopathology foundation models for whole-slide image segmentation
cards.abstract: Semantic segmentation of whole-slide images (WSIs) quantifies tissue composition and architecture, but existing models require extensive annotation and lose accuracy as the number of tissue classes increases or on heterogeneous, cross-scanner datasets. Here, we present the Tissue Segment Anything Model (TiSAM), which fuses SAM3 spatial features with UNI2-h pathology features within a multi-scale decoder. Because public benchmarks contain few tissue classes, we release MegaMouse, comprising 36,833 annotations of 52 tissue classes from 12 mouse organs, and an 11-class human pancreas dataset. TiSAM achieved the highest overall performance across four public datasets compared to existing convolutional neural network and vision transformer models, maintained high accuracy on MegaMouse, and maintained high accuracy in the human pancreas dataset when trained on as few as 5 annotated WSIs where previous integrations of SAM with pathology foundation models did not. TiSAM segmentations were also more consistent across eight slide scanners compared to other models. These results establish TiSAM as a general and highly adaptable framework for tissue segmentation, enabling studies containing many tissue classes, limited annotations, or images from multiple scanners.

cards.title: Wide-angled proteomics in giant cell arteritis reveals complement pathway activation
cards.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is an immune-mediated vasculitis that can cause serious morbidity including sight loss, stroke and aortic aneurysm. There is an unmet need for blood-based biomarkers and novel therapeutics. We measured plasma protein levels using the SomaScan v4.1 platform, comprising 7,273 protein measurements (SOMAmers) reflecting 6,596 unique protein targets. We profiled the proteome in 113 patients who presented acutely with possible GCA. 56 had biopsy-proven GCA and 57 did not have GCA (non-GCA). We found 144 SOMAmers increased and 151 reduced in GCA. Dysregulated biological pathways included IL6-JAK-STAT3 signalling, chemokines for both myeloid (e.g. CXCL2, CXCL3, CCL18, CCL23) and lymphoid cells (e.g. CXCL9, CXCL13), and the complement system (e.g. C9, CFHR5, C5a, Factor B). Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assays (ELISAs) confirmed elevated plasma levels of C5a, the terminal complement complex, Factor B and CFHR5 in GCA. We developed a 26-protein signature that distinguished GCA from non-GCA (area-under-the curve, AUC, 0.93) and validated the diagnostic signature in external datasets. Our data implicate terminal complement pathway activation in GCA, raising the possibility of complement-directed therapies. We show proof-of-principle that a multiplex protein biomarker could be used as a diagnostic adjunct in suspected GCA.

cards.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood. Publicly available bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets for OP and RA were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify shared gene modules associated with both diseases. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses were performed to characterize common biological pathways. Machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were used to identify and validate shared hub genes and to construct diagnostic models. Immune cell infiltration was evaluated using CIBERSORT, and the cellular localization of hub genes was further validated using scRNA-seq analysis. WGCNA identified 329 genes shared between OP- and RA-associated modules, which were significantly enriched in muscle-related processes, cytokine signaling, and immune-inflammatory pathways. RF analysis identified three shared candidate genes: ANO5, IL27RA, and CNTN3. Among these, ANO5 and IL27RA demonstrated consistent expression evidence and literature support, whereas CNTN3 emerged as a computationally nominated candidate requiring cautious interpretation and experimental validation. An SVM-based model incorporating these genes demonstrated robust predictive accuracy in both OP and RA validation cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct yet coordinated immune landscapes, with hub genes showing significant correlations with T cells, macrophages, B cells, and plasma cells. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed that ANO5 was predominantly expressed in macrophages and fibroblasts, IL27RA was mainly enriched in T cells, whereas CNTN3 showed minimal enrichment at the single-cell level in both OP bone and RA synovial tissues. This integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study identifies shared molecular signatures and immune-related mechanisms underlying OP and RA. ANO5 and IL27RA emerge as robust candidate regulators linking immune dysregulation and bone remodeling, whereas CNTN3-although identified by machine learning-requires cautious interpretation and further investigation due to limited supporting evidence. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of RA-associated OP and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for their comorbidity.

cards.title: Lactylated MOESIN links gut metabolism to TGF-β-driven immune remodeling and bone protection in diabetic osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Diabetic osteoporosis is characterized by impaired bone homeostasis and immune dysregulation. We investigated how fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modulates microbial metabolism, immune signaling, and bone remodeling using a pilot clinical cohort and diabetic mouse models. The clinical component was treated as a safety/feasibility study with exploratory longitudinal BMD and serum biomarker endpoints. In experimental DOP models, FMT improved bone microarchitecture and reduced inflammatory and bone-resorption markers. Descriptive analysis of external PBMC scRNA-seq data (GSE274561) provided immune-cell context, while an independently replicated external splenic CD4+ T-cell dataset (GSE267853; CONT n = 3, DM n = 3) provided disease-context support for Treg/Th17 and TGF-β/SMAD dysregulation. Replicated flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and functional perturbation experiments supported FMT-associated restoration of the Treg/Th17 balance and activation of lactate-MOESIN-TGF-β signaling in the experimental models.

cards.title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using CT-Derived Volumetric Bone Mineral Density Reference Curves.
cards.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) scans are a widely available yet underused resource that can be leveraged for opportunistic osteoporosis screening. This study aimed to develop sex- and site-specific reference curves for volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) to define dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-anchored percentile thresholds for osteoporosis classification, and to evaluate whether these thresholds identified individuals who subsequently sustain a major osteoporotic fracture (MOF). A retrospective cohort of 4,418 clinical CT scans was analyzed, including a subset of 1,088 scans with corresponding DXA imaging within one year. MOF incidence and timing following CT were obtained from linked administrative health data. CT images were segmented with deep learning models to extract the first lumbar vertebra (L1) and femoral neck from which vBMDs were assessed using internal calibration. Sex-specific vBMD centile curves were generated for each region using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape. A receiver operating characteristic analysis with the Youden index defined percentile thresholds that aligned with DXA-defined osteoporosis. Clinical relevance was assessed by determining the proportion of participants classified as osteoporotic by the CT-derived percentile thresholds who subsequently sustained a MOF, and by evaluating the association between CT-defined osteoporosis and time to incident fracture using Cox proportional hazards models. The cohort included 2,368 males and 2,050 females. At the vertebral body, 66.3% (n=67) of female and 41.9% (n=26) of male fracture cases had vBMD values below the CT-defined osteoporosis threshold, consistent with osteoporosis. Among these, 44.8% (n=30) of females and 76.9% (n=20) of males had not undergone DXA screening. Individuals classified as osteoporotic based on CT-derived thresholds had up to 2.86 times higher risk of sustaining an MOF across all vertebral sites in both sexes. These findings indicate that CT-derived vBMD percentile thresholds offer clinically meaningful cut-points for opportunistic screening and support their use as a diagnostic flag for further evaluation.

cards.title: Structural Basis for Human Milk Oligosaccharides Recognition by Evolutionarily Dominant Norovirus Genogroup II Genotypes
cards.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) contain glycan motifs similar to histo-blood group antigens and may act as soluble decoys that reduce viral attachment. However, the molecular basis of HMO recognition by the P domain of the major capsid protein VP1 of different norovirus genotypes is not fully understood. Here, we combined ligand-based and protein-based NMR experiments with X-ray crystallography to study HMO binding to the P domain of the latent GII.2, dominant GII.4 and emerging GII.17 noroviruses genotypes. Screening of 12 HMOs by STD NMR showed binding of all fucosylated HMOs to GII.4 and GII.17 and none for non-fucosylated HMOs. In contrast, GII.2 showed little or no detectable binding under the same conditions. Seven crystal structures of GII.4 or GII.17 with complexed HMOs supported fucose anchoring via five conserved residues. The remaining sugar moieties formed genotype-specific secondary interactions with an extended, shallow and solvent exposed binding surface whose shape is dictated by divergent surface loops. GII.4 recognition is mainly driven by hydrogen bonds whereas GII.17 relied more strongly on water-mediated interactions. Chemical shift perturbation from NMR titrations (CSP NMR) of GII.4 corroborated the fucose interactions and gave dissociation constants of 20-33 mM, consistent with weak and rapidly exchanging interactions.

cards.title: Physiological Waveform Features Based Aging Clocks Associate with Cardiovascular Disease
cards.abstract: Aging affects the morphology of photoplethysmography (PPG) and arterial blood pressure (ABP) waveforms. Here, we demonstrate that machine learning (ML) models trained on features derived from PPG or ABP waveforms can predict an individual's age. We further investigated whether the discrepancy between predicted and chronological age (Age-Gap) could serve as a measure of cardiovascular health by testing its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD). From a large perioperative dataset of 17,327 surgical patients, high-fidelity PPG and ABP waveforms were analyzed, and over 840 time-, frequency-, and statistical-domain features per cardiac cycle were extracted using a signal-processing-based tool. These features were then used to develop ML-based aging clocks, PPGAge and ABPAge, trained on PPG and ABP features, respectively. For each aging clock, we evaluated five ML models: Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, Lasso, and Elastic Net. Individuals were classified as having accelerated, normal, or delayed aging based on their Age-Gap relative to the model-specific mean absolute error (MAE, rounded up to the nearest whole year): accelerated aging was defined as Age-Gap [≥] +MAE, normal aging as -MAE [≤] Age-Gap < +MAE, and delayed aging as Age-Gap < -MAE. LightGBM provided the best age predictions for both aging clocks, with Pearson correlation coefficients (r) of 0.92 and 0.92 and R-squared values of 0.81 and 0.82 for PPGAge and ABPAge, respectively. Moreover, we found that accelerated aging was significantly associated with higher odds of CVD for both aging clocks, PPGAge (odds ratio, 1.87 [95% CI, 1.59-2.21], p<0.001) and ABPAge (odds ratio, 2.28 [95% CI, 1.51-3.43], p<0.001). Additionally, delayed aging was significantly associated with lower odds of CVD for PPGAge (odds ratio, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.58-0.80], p<0.001). Our findings suggest that aging clocks based on high-fidelity PPG or ABP waveform features may serve as novel biomarkers for identifying individuals with higher odds of CVD.

cards.title: A compact motif vocabulary is differentially interpreted across human cell types
cards.abstract: How a common genome generates diverse human cell types may depend less on distinct cis-regulatory vocabularies than on context-dependent use of a shared one. We have developed CNN-CR, an interpretable neural network that learns regulatory motifs while predicting gene expression across 116 human biosamples. Promoter regulation proves highly compressible: dozens of recurrent motif families retain most of the predictive information of much larger cell-type-specific vocabularies and generalize to cellular contexts excluded from their discovery. These motifs are conserved at their binding sites and enriched at fine-mapped regulatory variants. Cellular context acts at two levels: chromatin state gates which motif instances are available for regulatory use, whereas reader identity determines how accessible motifs are interpreted. ChIP-seq data reveal frequent shifts in reader occupancy across cell types, and genome-scale perturbations support corresponding context-dependent reader functions. Thus, regulatory diversity can emerge through differential access to and interpretation of a compact shared DNA vocabulary.

cards.title: Msp300 Links Autophagy to Nuclear Morphodynamics
cards.abstract: Autophagy is a fundamental cellular process that maintains homeostasis and enables adaptation to stress by degrading damaged or superfluous components. While its core machinery is well characterized, the interplay between autophagy and nuclear architecture remains poorly understood. In this study, we identify the LINC complex protein Msp300 as a novel interactor of the autophagy protein Atg8a in Drosophila melanogaster. Msp300 belongs to the KASH (Klarsicht/ANC-1/Syne Homology) domain protein family, known for its role in nuclear positioning through interactions with the cytoskeleton. The KASH domain anchors Msp300 in the outer nuclear membrane, where it pairs with SUN domain proteins across the nuclear envelope to form the LINC complex, a mechanical bridge between the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton. Yeast two-hybrid screening revealed an interaction between Atg8a and Msp300 isoforms E and G, mediated by a canonical LC3-interacting region (LIR). Localization studies show Msp300 associates with Atg8a within the cytoplasm and at the nuclear periphery under both basal and elevated autophagy conditions. Functional perturbations through stress assays indicate that this interaction influences event in and around nucleus, establishing a link between autophagy and nuclear architecture. By exploring the role of Msp300 isoforms E and G in shaping not only nuclear organization but potentially endoplasmic reticulum, through autophagy machinery, this study introduces a new dimension to nuclear envelope biology and opens opportunities to explore how steady state homeostasis, stress adaptation and cytoskeletal connectivity are coordinated at the nuclear periphery.

cards.title: Filament assembly confers the mechanical resilience of the IFI16 restrictosome
cards.abstract: Interferon-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) is a mammalian innate immune sensor composed of a filament-forming pyrin domain (PYD) followed by tandem HIN200 domains that bind nucleic acids. First recognized as a major regulator of inflammatory responses against cytosolic double-stranded (ds)DNA, IFI16 filaments have been implicated in several key mechanical processes involving both host and pathogens, including viral replication restriction, latency regulation, replication-stress responses, and DNA-damage responses. Moreover, IFI16 filaments are ultra-stable, a key trait believed to drive its autoantigenicity. Although recent studies reported that IFI16 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) via disordered linkers and multivalent protein-dsDNA interactions, whether such a metastable entity provides a framework for the mechanical activities of IFI16 remains unknown. Here, we show that PYD-driven filament assembly confers the mechanical stability of IFI16 condensates by compacting DNA into ultra-stable tangles capable of withstanding forces sufficient to induce duplex deformation. By contrast, HIN200-dsDNA complexes are much more sensitive to ionic perturbation, DNA pretension, and mechanical interference. Together, we demonstrate that filament assembly allows IFI16 to act as a mechano-sensitive restrictor.

cards.title: Neuronal and glial transcriptional states vary with proximity to tangle-bearing neurons in the human entorhinal cortex
cards.abstract: More neurons die in Alzheimer's disease than form tangles, and tangle-bearing neurons can persist for decades, so tangles alone cannot explain degeneration. We combined 6,000-plex spatial transcriptomics with PHF1 immunofluorescence (167,176 cells; 9 donors) and imaging mass cytometry (170,195 cells; 62 donors), measuring each cell's distance to the nearest tangle. Tangle-bearing layer 2-3 excitatory neurons were enriched late along a trajectory of increasing microtubule-associated, synaptic and V-ATPase expression, with elevated p62 and K48-ubiquitin. Tangle-free neurons shared more of this state the closer they lay to a tangle, including higher chaperone and autophagy scores, p62 and nuclear size. Nearby glia had higher disease-associated scores, with astrocytes expressing less GFAP. Excitatory, but not inhibitory, neuron loss was greatest in subtypes closest to tangles and cortical depths richest in phosphorylated tau. Selective neuronal vulnerability may reflect not only a neuron's susceptibility to forming a tangle but also where it lies relative to one.

cards.title: A Senescence-Related Signature for Risk Stratification and Predicted Immunotherapy Response in Breast Cancer: Integrative Pathology and Multi-Omics Analysis.
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence exerts context-dependent effects on breast cancer progression and therapeutic response through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment; however, its pathological manifestations, cellular organization, and clinical significance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated whole-slide pathology images, bulk transcriptomic profiles, single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical data to systematically characterize senescence-associated features in breast cancer. Quantitative pathology and deep-learning features were extracted from hematoxylin and eosin-stained images, and a senescence-related signature (SRS) was constructed using machine-learning survival models. The SRS effectively stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups and showed consistent performance across the internally divided TCGA-BRCA subsets, with high-SRS patients exhibiting significantly poorer survival. Single-cell analyses revealed that senescence activity was predominantly enriched in epithelial and endothelial cells, whereas fibroblasts acted as major signal-sending populations and mediated enhanced collagen-related communication with tumor cells. Low-SRS tumors displayed greater immune-cell infiltration, higher immune-checkpoint expression, higher immunophenoscores, and more favorable Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE)/immunophenoscore (IPS)-based predicted response profiles, while also exhibiting distinct drug-sensitivity profiles. Integrative pathological, transcriptomic, and spatial analyses further identified STARD10 as a senescence-associated candidate enriched in tumor regions and spatially concordant with senescence-marker expression at the spot level. Functional experiments showed that STARD10 knockdown reduced cellular metabolic activity in CCK-8 assays and suppressed migration and invasion, attenuated senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related cytokine expression, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish an integrated pathology- and multi-omics-derived senescence-related signature for prognostic stratification and characterization of TIDE/IPS-based predicted immunotherapy-response profiles in breast cancer, while identifying STARD10 as a candidate biomarker and a potential target for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

cards.title: Ecological networks balance connectivity with flexibility to perturbations
cards.abstract: Food webs become progressively sparser as species richness increases, yet the number of interactions grows faster than linearly, placing communities between the limiting expectations of constant degree and constant connectance. Similar scaling has also been documented in other interaction networks, but whether they share a common architectural regime, and what general principle could generate it, remain unresolved. Here, we show that 1,533 ecological networks spanning different interaction types broadly converge on an intermediate link--species scaling regime, with an overall exponent of 1.43. We interpret this pattern through a thermodynamic trade-off in which increasing network connectivity enhances signal propagation while reducing the diversity of independent modes contributing to the network's response to perturbations. Optimizing this trade-off yields a scaling exponent of 1.45, closely matching the empirical estimate, while randomly adding or removing interactions generally reduces thermodynamic efficiency in empirical networks. These results support a propagation--response-diversity trade-off as a plausible systems-level principle underlying how ecological network complexity grows with diversity.

cards.title: Stochastic population growth and its implications for mutation dynamics under carrying capacity constraints
cards.abstract: Mathematical models of mutation processes often assume deterministic population growth, although biological populations are continuously subjected to random fluctuations. Here, we extend a model inspired by the classical Luria-Delbruck framework by introducing stochastic perturbations into population growth while assuming a constant mutation rate. Using Ito calculus, we derive an analytical solution for a stochastic logistic growth model with carrying capacity. By comparing the stochastic model with its deterministic counterpart, we demonstrate that random perturbations can substantially influence population variability, particularly as the population approaches its carrying capacity. While deterministic growth levels off, stochastic fluctuations persist and may become increasingly important relative to the underlying growth dynamics. The magnitude of these effects depends on the relationship between population growth and stochastic volatility. We illustrate the model using real life within-host SARS-CoV-2 infection data and discuss its implications. Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for stochastic population dynamics when modelling mutation-related processes in capacity-limited microbial populations.

cards.title: Programmable Biochemical Logic Computation Through Repurposing Natural bZIP Protein Interaction Networks
cards.abstract: Protein dimerization networks can implement biochemical logic, but their practical realization has largely relied on designing or optimizing protein-protein interaction affinities, creating a major barrier to experimental implementation. Here, we ask whether computation can instead be extracted from interaction networks already generated by evolution. We repurpose experimentally characterized basic leucine zipper (bZIP) interactomes from Nematostella vectensis, Ciona intestinalis, and Homo sapiens as programmable biochemical logic substrates while keeping all measured binding affinities fixed. Using mass-action equilibrium modeling coupled with genetic optimization, we identify accessory monomer concentrations and output dimers that reconfigure these natural networks to perform Boolean operations. Unengineered bZIP clusters computed up to 15 of the 16 possible two-input Boolean functions, including nonlinearly separable XOR and XNOR operations, and up to 13 functions within a 17-gate three-input benchmark. Computational versatility depended on network architecture and input selection, revealing design constraints inherent to natural interactomes. Stochastic perturbation analysis further showed that many optimized configurations preserve logic-state separation under substantial concentration variability. Finally, a nondimensional scaling framework provides a route for translating simulated concentration regimes toward cell-free implementation. Together, these results demonstrate computationally that natural protein interaction networks contain latent, evolutionarily encoded computational capacity that can be accessed through concentration tuning rather than de novo protein engineering.

cards.title: SMFnet reveals principles of combinatorial transcription factor assembly
cards.abstract: Combinatorial assembly of transcription factors (TFs) opens chromatin at cis-regulatory elements (cREs) to establish cell-type-specific gene expression. Dissecting the role of individual TFs and their collective function has been limited by the diversity of TF binding-site arrangements across cREs. A single regulatory sequence can support multiple configurations of TF and nucleosome occupancy, raising the possibility that distinct chromatin states reflect different TF assemblies. Predictive models linking regulatory sequence to chromatin accessibility collapse these distinct molecular states into population averages, obscuring how TF assemblies shape accessible chromatin. Here, we introduce SMFNet, a generative diffusion model that predicts distributions of single-molecule chromatin accessibility profiles from DNA sequence, and PRISM, which identifies sequence features associated with individual molecular states. Together, these approaches enable us to systematically associate single molecule chromatin states at cREs with specific TF binding motifs. Experimental perturbation of these motifs redistributes the corresponding states as predicted by SMFNet, supporting their interpretation as TF-dependent configurations underlying chromatin opening. We then use controlled in silico motif screens to systematically dissect individual and combinatorial TF contributions to chromatin opening. Individual TFs show distinct chromatin-opening signatures, differing in accessible-region width and nucleosome-positioning precision even when associated with similar levels of chromatin accessibility. Combining motifs reveals partner- and spacing-dependent effects on chromatin accessibility, TF occupancy and nucleosome positioning. Genetic perturbation of TF binding sites using natural variation at endogenous cRE confirms that TF-specific properties shape chromatin accessibility in vivo. Together, our findings reveal sequence-encoded principles of combinatorial TF assembly during chromatin opening.

cards.title: Sex differences in latent inhibition and their implications for psychotic disorders
cards.abstract: Latent inhibition (LI) refers to the reduced ability to learn or express learning about a stimulus following prior exposure to it without consequence. It has been extensively studied to investigate associative learning and memory as well as the aberrant attribution of salience to irrelevant stimuli in both humans and animals, a process which is thought to underpin hallucinations and delusions in psychosis. Despite sex differences observed in numerous aspects of psychosis, few studies have attempted to characterise sex differences in LI. This systematic review outlines the current evidence of sex differences in LI in both human and rodent studies, showing predominantly inconclusive and conflicting evidence for sex differences. However, the majority of cases in which sex differences were found were in studies that assessed the impact of additional factors on LI such as drug administration, juvenile handling, and oestrous phase, and demonstrated interactions between sex and these additional factors. Hence, there is stronger evidence for sex differences in vulnerability to perturbations in LI. Furthermore, we present data demonstrating sex differences in latent inhibition of contextual fear conditioning and associated gene expression in the hippocampus in rodents, suggesting sex differences in hippocampal processing underpinning latent inhibition at both the behavioural and neurobiological levels. Although there have been relatively few studies demonstrating sex differences in LI identified by the systematic review, the data suggest that in hippocampally dependent forms of LI, sex differences may be more apparent, which may be of relevance in relation to sex differences in the presentation of psychosis.

cards.title: Digital molecular kinetics enabled by large-scale nanopore arrays for multidimensional biophysical profiling
cards.abstract: While widely used, traditional technologies like surface plasmon resonance (SPR) are limited by narrow temporal windows (transient capture and baseline drift), dynamic heterogeneity, and poor physiological temperature performance. Meanwhile, early nanopore approaches are often constrained by limited throughput and heavy reliance on customized modification schemes. Here, we present a digital molecular kinetics (DMK) platform based on large-scale nanopore arrays. By introducing a universal coupling and probe reporting system, DMK achieves broad versatility across diverse molecular pairs, including proteins, peptides, small molecules, DNA, and polymerase complexes. In addition to accurately recovering classical SPR association and dissociation rate constants, by harnessing massive single-molecule event analysis, DMK breaks traditional performance boundaries: it facilitates robust thermodynamic-kinetic profiling across a wide temperature range, resolves distinct conformations in heterogeneous samples, enables ultra-low dissociation rate quantification via maximum likelihood estimation, and reveals energy wells via voltage gradients for binding analysis against environmental perturbations. Furthermore, DMK enables the capture of rapid binding events missed by SPR, offering a new perspective on molecular interaction complexity. This platform offers an effective alternative and upgrade to SPR, opening a digital paradigm for complex molecular analysis and drug discovery.

cards.title: Janusein and EB Cooperate to Enhance Microtubule Plus-end Catastrophe
cards.abstract: Microtubule (MT) plus ends are organized by end-binding (EB) proteins, yet how EB-associated factors modulate the transition from growth to catastrophe remains incompletely understood. Using spatially resolved proximity proteomics, we identified Janusein (ZC2HC1A) as a conserved, poorly characterized MT-associated protein (MAP). At low expression levels, Janusein tracked MT plus ends and reduced EB comet velocity; at higher levels, it redistributed to the MT lattice and was associated with MT bundling and widespread MT loss. Loss of Janusein resulted in spindle defects in human cells. In vitro, Janusein alone facilitated MT elongation through its C-terminal fragment, but promoted MT catastrophe through its N-terminal fragment in the presence of EB proteins. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses suggest that an N-terminal loop may perturb lateral contacts between adjacent MT protofilaments. Together, these findings identify Janusein as an unconventional MAP that functionally cooperates with EB proteins to promote MT catastrophe.

cards.title: Centered cross-context perturbation transfer on the public 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge benchmark
cards.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses across cellular contexts requires transferring both expression direction and differential-expression priority. We developed a compact numerical method that combines public perturbation summaries with a differential-expression kernel fitted to H1 CRISPRi training targets. The method centers an independent KOLF2.1J source on known training targets, transfers its response signs and magnitude ranks, and uses isotonic regression to render predicted expression means. We evaluated the frozen model retrospectively on the released public TEST100 of the 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge, using an external KOLF source released in 2026. The model achieved DES 0.371834, PDS 0.8614, and MAE 0.302206. With reconstructed historical anchors, its composite score was 0.341344, compared with the archived champion score of 0.340052, a difference of +0.001292. The comparison showed higher DES and lower PDS, with zero normalized MAE contributions for both methods. Source centering also improved development PDS across all three TRAIN folds and official VALIDATION. These results demonstrate a practical numerical approach to cross-context perturbation transfer and differential-expression ranking.

cards.title: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review.
cards.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain unclear. This systematic review of eight randomized controlled trials (n = 493) evaluating dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived bone mineral density reports findings separately for each agent, without pooling, because the trials evaluated four pharmacologically distinct agents differing markedly in weight-lowering potency. The evidence is sparse for every agent and is insufficient to establish the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in this population. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the randomized evidence on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers in adults with overweight or obesity, reporting findings separately for each individual agent. This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review (INPLASY202630076) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (January 2015 to July 2026). Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with mean baseline body mass index (BMI) > 25 kg/m², compared a GLP-1 RA with placebo or another antidiabetic therapy for ≥12 weeks, and reported BMD assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Because the included trials evaluated pharmacologically distinct agents that differ substantially in weight-lowering potency, results were synthesized narratively and reported separately by agent; no meta-analysis was performed. Eight RCTs (n = 493) were included. Three trials were at low risk of bias (Eriksson 2019; Hygum 2020; Hansen 2024) and five raised some concerns, principally regarding the randomization process and selective reporting; no agent is supported by more than one trial at low risk of bias. (Cai 2021 contributes two treatment arms assessed separately, giving nine comparisons in the risk-of-bias assessment.) Evidence was unevenly distributed across agents: semaglutide and dulaglutide were each evaluated in one trial, liraglutide in two, and exenatide in five. Five of the eight trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes, including all four that randomized an insulin comparator arm; three enrolled adults without diabetes, of which one was defined by obesity alone. By study-level mean baseline BMI, five trials lay in the obese range ( ≥ 30 kg/m²) and three in the overweight range (25 to <30 kg/m²). The single semaglutide trial (Hansen 2024; n = 64; low risk of bias), which produced the largest weight loss of any trial (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -6.8 kg vs placebo), reported reduced lumbar spine BMD (ETD - 0.018 g/cm², p = 0.007), reduced whole-body BMD (mean difference [MD] -0.02 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.03 to -0.01), and increased C-terminal telopeptide (CTX; MD 166.50 pg/mL; 95% CI 66.60 to 266.40). Liraglutide was evaluated at two doses with divergent results. At the weight-management dose of 3.0 mg daily, in the only trial conducted in adults with obesity and without diabetes (Jensen 2024; ETD - 6.7 kg vs placebo), lumbar spine BMD (MD - 0.019 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.034 to -0.004) and total hip BMD (MD - 0.013 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.024 to -0.002) were reduced. At the diabetes dose of 1.8 mg daily (Hygum 2020; -3.8 kg), no site changed materially (lumbar spine MD 0.00 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.01). Exenatide trials were inconsistent, ranging from 0.03 g/cm² (95% CI 0.02 to 0.03) at the lumbar spine (Renyuan 2015) to -0.04 g/cm² (95% CI - 0.15 to 0.07; Akyay 2023). Certainty of evidence was very low for every agent. The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required. INPLASY202630076.

cards.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics.
cards.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

cards.title: Rapid experience-dependent tuning of spinal and transcortical stretch reflexes supports goal-directed movement
cards.abstract: The short-latency stretch reflex (SLR) is the fastest sensorimotor response in human limbs. The spinal SLR scales with background muscle activity and is affected by recent movement history. But adaptive plasticity of spinal reflexes has classically been studied through operant conditioning, which induces an arbitrary change in reflex size over days to weeks. In contrast, rapid, experience-dependent feedback adaptation is often attributed to transcortical mechanisms underlying the long-latency reflex (LLR). Whether task constraints can progressively shape the SLR within a single session remains unclear. Here, naive human adults (n = 16; 9 females, 7 males) performed an instructed-delay reaching task while holding a robotic manipulandum which delivered brief haptic perturbations during action preparation. We recorded high-density surface electromyography (64-channel arrays) from the pectoralis major and posterior deltoid to investigate reflex gains. Pre-perturbation muscle activity showed no systematic goal-directed change. With a long-enough preparatory delay (750 ms), SLR gains decreased progressively with experience when the planned movement was expected to stretch the homonymous muscle, rather than shorten it. This tuning occurred in both muscles, was evident within individual participants, and was accompanied by a corresponding decrease in reflexively generated force opposing perturbations toward the cued target. No such tuning was detected with a short preparatory delay (250 ms). LLR responses were goal-directed from the first trial blocks and progressed in a comparable manner across the session, at both preparatory delays. Our study shows that spinal feedback circuits can progressively adapt within a single session to support the performance of goal-directed movements.

cards.title: Age-driven miR-29 trades youthful plasticity for epigenetic fidelity
cards.abstract: Throughout life, somatic cells must preserve their identity while retaining the capacity to adapt. How this balance shifts with ageing and rejuvenation remains unclear. Here we identify miR-29 as a central point of convergence between the transcriptional programmes of physiological ageing and two routes to rejuvenation: induced reprogramming and the natural reset of early development. miR-29 rises with ageing, falls in both rejuvenation settings and shows the most conserved age-associated increase across vertebrates. miR-29 inhibition opposes transcriptional ageing, whereas mimics promote an older transcriptional state. Methylome analysis reveals a broader function: inhibition releases the miR-29 brake on remodelling, and mimic treatment reinforces it. This release increases methylation at repeat-associated CpGs and lowers epigenetic-clock estimates through unequal contributions in opposite directions. Inhibition also amplifies stimulus-induced methylation changes but reduces fidelity to lineage-specific methylation patterns. We extend this relationship to cancer, where low miR-29 expression marks tumours with younger epigenetic-age estimates yet greater methylation divergence from their tissue of origin. These findings identify miR-29 as a control point linking ageing, rejuvenation and cancer, and support a maladaptive trade-off model in which epigenetic fidelity is preserved at the expense of the plasticity needed for methylome maintenance and adaptation.

cards.title: TFAM Dependent Mitochondrial Fitness Limits CD8⁺ T Cell Immunopathology and Sustains Protective Immunity during Viral Pneumonia
cards.abstract: During respiratory virus infections, CD8 T cells kill virus-infected cells and establish antigen-specific immune memory, but excessive or dysregulated responses can also contribute to lung immunopathology. The development and maintenance of optimal CD8 T cell effector and memory responses depend on mitochondrial fitness, which can be compromised across multiple physiologic and pathologic conditions. However, how impaired mitochondrial fitness affect antiviral CD8 T cell responses remains poorly understood. Here, we used a CD8 T cell-specific TFAM-haploinsufficient mouse model to induce moderate mitochondrial stress without the severe mitochondrial dysfunction associated with complete TFAM loss, providing a genetically controlled model of mitochondrial perturbations relevant to physiologic conditions. TFAM insufficiency disrupted mitochondrial integrity and cellular bioenergetics and increased mitochondrial DNA and oxidative stress in CD8 T cells. During primary influenza A virus (IAV) infection, TFAM-insufficient CD8 T cells exhibited heightened cytotoxic activity and inflammatory responses associated with lung immunopathology, followed by progressive functional exhaustion, diminished antigen-specific responses, and impaired protective immunity. Consistent with the physiologic relevance of these findings, CD8 T cells from older individuals exhibited reduced TFAM expression and mitochondrial function. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that moderate mitochondrial stress can alter the trajectory of antiviral CD8 T cell responses, promoting pathogenic effector activity during acute infection while compromising subsequent protective immunity.

cards.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
cards.abstract: Existing supervised and self-supervised EEG models mainly learn within-segment discriminative or reconstructive representations, leaving transitions between adjacent EEG segments underexplored. We propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model for EEG seizure detection that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment from the current EEG state, conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals. A learnable query-based fusion module aggregates the multimodal synchronized signals into a compact physiological condition. Pretraining uses no seizure labels; downstream detection retains only the frozen EEG encoder and a linear probe. On the SeizeIT2 dataset with a strict patient-wise split, the model achieved an AUPRC of 0.3748, ROC-AUC of 0.8025, and balanced accuracy of 0.7308, outperforming official database baselines (SVM with hand-crafted features and ChronoNet), an external baseline (DSAINet), and a foundation model (NeuroLM). Ablations show a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder, supporting multimodal-conditioned latent transition learning for wearable EEG representation learning.

cards.title: Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer
cards.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables region-resolved investigation of tumor metabolism, yet translating gene expression into reliable metabolic flux predictions remains challenging because genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs). Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomic data from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor, spanning normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3 and 3+4 tissues, with Human-GEM using an E-Flux framework incorporating defined nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. An initial naive implementation produced TICs in all twelve flux solutions, with total internal fluxes 190-890-fold higher than those obtained using the revised workflow. All flux solutions were certified free of TICs, and 94.7% of 17,592 loopless flux bounds were determined exactly. Within the analyzed tissue, predicted metabolic similarity was associated with spatial region (permutation p = 0.023) but not histological state (p = 0.52), revealing model-predicted heterogeneity even between regions sharing the same Gleason grade. Flux-based target prioritization identified fatty acid uptake-associated genes (CD36, FABPs, and SLC27A1/4), although the dominant uptake signal was confined to one malignant region, suggesting a localized metabolic hypothesis rather than an established therapeutic vulnerability. Analysis of the zinc-citrate-aconitase axis further demonstrated that zinc-dependent citrate redistribution was absent under baseline conditions and emerged only when oxidative demand, elimination of a cytosolic aconitase bypass, and strong mitochondrial aconitase inhibition coincided. These findings establish the importance of thermodynamic quality control and physiologically informed constraints in spatial metabolic modeling, while distinguishing computationally feasible flux predictions from experimentally validated metabolic mechanisms. The resulting framework provides a reproducible foundation for investigating spatial metabolic heterogeneity and prioritizing testable hypotheses for future experimental validation.

cards.title: Distinct spatial organization of human hippocampal perfusion and microvascular pulsatility across age
cards.abstract: Arterial pulsation can modulate neuronal activity through mechanosensitive pathways in mice, but whether vascular pulsatility is similarly related to neural organization in humans remains unclear. Here, using 7T MRI in 35 young and older adults, we mapped cerebral perfusion and microvascular volumetric pulsatility index (mvPI) across the unfolded hippocampus and integrated these measures with histological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic reference maps. Perfusion and mvPI exhibited distinct spatial organization and age-related differences. In young adults, perfusion preferentially corresponded to parvalbumin-interneuron density and beta/gamma distribution, whereas mvPI was associated with theta-band distribution. A number of associations detected in young adults were not detected in the older adults maps. Spectral simulations showed qualitative similarity to heartbeat-related phase resetting as one possible explanation for the mvPI-theta relationship, while spatial transcriptomics revealed perivascular enrichment of PIEZO2, a candidate mediator of vascular mechanotransduction. Together, these findings establish perfusion and tissue-level pulsatility as distinct dimensions of human hippocampal vascular organization and provide a framework for investigating their relationships with neural dynamics across aging.

cards.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
cards.abstract: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge." Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge. The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

cards.title: Blood-based PhenoAge may reflect disease burden rather than biological aging in cancer
cards.abstract: PhenoAge, a blood-based biological aging clock, is associated with cancer outcomes, a finding taken as evidence that biological aging shapes prognosis. In 3,067 patients undergoing primary tumor resection, PhenoAge acceleration rose with tumor stage. One or two of its eight blood components, differing by cancer type, carried the prognostic signal, and replacing its general-population weights with equal weights did not weaken it. In cancer, PhenoAge may reflect disease burden rather than biological aging.

cards.title: Sustained Maternal Cortisol Elevation Links Metabolic Stress to Fetal Growth Restriction in a Guinea Pig Model of Undernutrition
cards.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) resulting from maternal undernutrition is commonly attributed to insufficient nutrient substrate delivery to the fetus. However, the contribution of maternal physiological stress responses to this outcome remains poorly characterized. Using the well-established guinea pig maternal nutrient restriction (MNR) model, we conducted a comprehensive retrospective analysis to interrogate the hypothesis that maternal stress physiology actively mediates fetal growth outcomes beyond simple substrate limitation. Maternal salivary and serum cortisol were significantly elevated in MNR dams throughout pregnancy despite no baseline differences at conception, indicating that hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation was specifically triggered by the combined physiological demands of pregnancy and nutritional constraint. The sustained cortisol elevation was accompanied by acute metabolic perturbations at mid-pregnancy, including hypoglycemia and depleted circulating lipids. While most acute metabolic disturbances resolved by near-term, cortisol remained elevated, and MNR fetuses exhibited parallel cortisol elevation alongside sustained growth restriction. Maternal weight divergence emerged only in late gestation and was driven primarily by reduced conceptus weight. Maternal organ analysis revealed selective hepatic enlargement with apparent lipid accumulation in MNR dams near-term. Overall, these findings help to reframe nutrition-related FGR as a condition in which maternal adaptive stress responses, reduced nutritional components and placental insufficiency are mechanistically intertwined, with important implications for the design of effective interventions beyond simply nutrient supplementation.

cards.title: The microbiota of a wild butterfly species over three decades of climate change
cards.abstract: As microbes can support essential functions related to many aspects of host physiology, changes in microbial communities can affect host physiology and fitness. Although the effects of thermal conditions on host-associated microbiomes have been demonstrated in laboratory settings, how climate change might affect the structure and functionality of microbial communities in wild populations remains poorly understood. We took advantage of the long-term field survey of the Glanville fritillary butterfly (Melitaea cinxia) metapopulation on the [A]land Islands, in the Baltic Sea, to fill this gap. We investigated whether bacterial communities associated with larvae showed gradual temporal change in response to slow environmental warming across a 28-year period, or whether these communities responded through abrupt change following a sudden drought event that triggered bottlenecks in their butterfly host population. Using 16S rRNA metabarcoding and metagenomic sequencing, we first showed that M. cinxia harbours a set of stable resident bacteria, including Pseudomonas, Telluria, and Enterobacteriaceae bacteria. We also characterized a gradual shift in the M. cinxia associated bacterial community over three decades of increasing temperatures and decreasing precipitations. This shift was not unidirectional for all bacterial taxa, as the dominant Telluria and Pseudomonas showed opposing responses to environmental trends. Additionally, the 2018 extreme drought, which triggered acute host population bottlenecks, was associated with a severe disruption of M. cinxia microbiota, and the loss of key Enterobacteriaceae taxa. However, the M. cinxia bacterial community appeared to recover towards pre-drought structure in subsequent years, suggesting resilience to acute climatic perturbations in this system.

cards.title: Ubiquitin ligase RNF126 exerts functions in lysosomal damage response and lysosomal homeostasis maintenance
cards.abstract: The response to lysosomal membrane permeabilization involves extensive ubiquitylation at the lysosome; however, the ubiquitin ligases identified so far cannot account for the complexity of the response. Using extensive spatial proteomics, we identified RNF126 as a new ligase that is robustly recruited to lysosomes in response to a range of different damage triggers across distinct cell types. Recruitment is mediated independent of BAG6 via an arginine-rich stretch in the low-complexity region of RNF126 to mostly unacidified lysosomes in the perinuclear region. Ubiquitin remnant mass spectrometry identified several damage-induced RNF126 substrates, among them known lysosomal damage response components and potential new factors that might drive regeneration from lysosomal damage. Consistently, RNF126 deletion resulted in persistent lysosomal swelling. In addition, we uncovered a constitutive role of RNF126 in lysosomal homeostasis maintenance. Hence, our findings identified the ubiquitin ligase RNF126 as novel lysosomal health regulating factor with functions in homeostasis and stress conditions.

cards.title: Benchmarking Recording-Level Clinical Speech De-identification for Privacy-Preserving Clinical Audio
cards.abstract: Transcript-based de-identification protects textual records but leaves sensitive health information (SHI) directly audible in source recordings, limiting trustworthy reuse of clinical audio. However, standardized evaluations of recording-level SHI detection remain limited. We established the SREDH-AICUP 2025 benchmark to evaluate recording-level SHI detection systems and characterize the approaches. All 22 qualifying systems combined automatic speech recognition with downstream SHI detection, whereas we additionally evaluated end-to-end detection from audio. Pipeline baselines outperformed the end-to-end baseline in transcription (MER, 0.123 vs 0.155) and SHI detection (macro-F1, 0.507-0.653 vs 0.422). Synthetic Mandarin speech-text augmentation enabled the end-to-end model to detect Mandarin SHI that was not identified without augmentation (macro-F1, 0.171 vs 0). Foundation models showed category-specific differences in SHI recognition, and type-aware adaptive routing improved macro-F1 from 0.656 to 0.697. These findings establish standardized reference performance, characterize current system designs, and demonstrate how language-specific augmentation and category-aware model integration can improve recording-level SHI detection.

cards.title: Reprogramming bone homeostasis: The recoupling-oriented framework of bidirectional regulation strategies for osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Current osteoporosis treatments reduce fracture risk by suppressing bone resorption, stimulating bone formation, or combining both effects. Yet these clinical benefits do not show whether formation has resumed at sites where bone was previously resorbed. This Review uses a remodeling recoupling framework to examine this resorption-to-formation transition. We define recoupling as restoration of the sequence from resorption through reversal to osteoblast recruitment and bone formation. This differs from bidirectional regulation, in which osteoblast activity increases and osteoclast activity decreases without evidence that the two responses are linked. We review the cellular communication, signaling pathways, cell-survival mechanisms, and systemic conditions that influence this transition. We also assess candidate targets and treatments according to the strength of clinical, human, animal, and mechanistic evidence. The available evidence is strongest for established therapies and several human-supported pathways, whereas many proposed targets and delivery approaches remain preclinical. This framework may help guide treatment sequencing, patient selection, bone-targeted delivery, and the development of measures that determine whether formation follows resorption.

cards.title: Do LLM Proposers Improve Budgeted Search for Ionizable Lipids?
cards.abstract: Efficient lipid design under limited experimental budgets is a central challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. We introduce LEAF (Lipid Evolutionary Adaptive Framework), a matched-budget protocol for testing whether language-model proposers improve combinatorial molecular search relative to classical baselines. The study uses a 30,044-candidate ionizable-lipid space, a frozen Gaussian-process oracle fitted to experimental potency labels, and a separate active-learning surrogate. Four language models evaluated over eight seeds and three splits show no significant improvement over genetic-algorithm or random-search baselines. For Llama 8B, 79.1% of acquisition-selected queries repeat previously evaluated archive members. Removing duplicates reduces the performance gap on some splits but increases proposal cost and can prevent budget exhaustion. Larger models reduce duplication without establishing superiority or equivalence. Exploratory scored prompts and stricter novelty controls yield positive median differences against the genetic algorithm, yet wide intervals and shared-seed dependence preclude stronger conclusions. A validated single-assay reanalysis preserves the chemotype-cold deficit at a smaller numerical scale, and exploratory expected hypervolume improvement does not reverse the result. Follow-up checks address whether proposers genuinely use injected evidence. These checks include a zero-shot leakage probe, rank-only and chain-of-thought-rationale prompts, a score-shuffle perturbation, an evidence-conflict probe, and a genuine reasoning-mode proposer. They show measurable engagement with supplied information without a corresponding performance gain. LEAF isolates proposal quality as the experimental variable and documents a concrete failure mode of zero-shot LLM proposers under controlled budgets.

cards.title: Recovering Hidden Neural Oscillatory Modes from Partial Observations through Delay Embedding and Perturbation
cards.abstract: Characterising the oscillatory behaviour generated by neural interactions is central to systems neuroscience because these dynamical properties are linked to brain function. However, inferring latent neural dynamics is challenging because recordings sample only part of the system. Time-delay embedding allows dynamical modes to be estimated from partial recordings, using methods such as Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel DMD). Despite its promise, two questions remain: what dynamical information is recoverable through time-delay embedding, and how can recovery be improved? We address both questions using control theory. Our framework centres on factorising the Hankel matrix of delay-embedded observations into an observability matrix and a trajectory matrix with the form of a controllability matrix. We show that their ranks impose complementary constraints on what any delay-embedding method can recover: delay embedding can increase observability rank, while perturbation can increase trajectory rank by exciting otherwise inactive modes. We validate this framework using Hankel DMD in simulations and human electrocorticography (ECoG). In both, perturbation increased the number of fast-decaying mode estimates, whereas greater delay depth increased the number of reliably estimated modes and, in ECoG, extended their frequency range. These results clarify what partial recordings can reveal about neural dynamics and how to reveal more.

cards.title: Impact of cardiometabolic and renal phenotypes on the prevalence of type 2 diabetes in the geriatric population of Añisok, Equatorial Guinea: A prospective cohort study (2024-2025).
cards.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) represents a growing global health challenge, with management increasingly focused on organ protection and mitigating cardiometabolic-renal risk. In sub-Saharan African geriatric populations, the interplay between frailty, hypertension, and obesity presents critical diagnostic and management challenges. This prospective cohort study evaluated the baseline prevalence of T2D and the prospective risk of major adverse clinical outcomes associated with a concomitant high-risk cardiometabolic phenotype among older adults in Añisok, Equatorial Guinea. A total of 1,702 older adults (aged 60-100 years) were enrolled and followed prospectively from July 2024 to December 2025 (median follow-up: 18.6 months). Participants were stratified at baseline into a High Cardiometabolic Risk Cohort (n = 1,500; concomitant presence of obesity [BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2] AND hypertension [BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or active antihypertensive treatment]) and a Low-Risk / Control Cohort (n = 202; normotensive and BMI < 30 kg/m2). Baseline prevalent T2D, prospective incident T2D (among baseline non-diabetics, n = 612), composite Major Adverse Cardiometabolic and Renal Events (MACRE), acute renal function decline, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and peripheral vascular complications were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance and logistic regression models. The overall baseline prevalence of T2D across the entire cohort was 64.0% (n = 1,090; 95% CI: 61.7%-66.3%). Among baseline non-diabetic participants (n = 612), the prospective 18-month incidence of T2D was 31.4% (n = 192). Over follow-up, composite MACRE occurred in 17.5% (263/1,500) of the high-risk cohort versus 4.5% (9/202) in the control cohort (adjusted Relative Risk [aRR] = 3.41, 95% CI: 1.75-6.66; p < 0.001). The high-risk phenotype was also independently associated with prospective peripheral vascular necrosis (aRR = 5.82, 95% CI: 1.44-23.51; p = 0.013) and baseline target-organ damage (aOR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.84-2.58; p < 0.001). The prospective absolute risk difference (ARD) for composite MACRE between primary exposure cohorts was 13.0% (95% CI: 9.8%-16.2%), while the overall cumulative target-organ complication ARD was 18.8% (95% CI: 15.2%-22.4%). In secondary subgroup analysis stratified by baseline prevalent diabetes status, diabetic participants (n = 1,090) accumulated 263 composite MACRE events (24.1%) compared to 9 events (1.5%) in non-diabetic participants (n = 612; ARD = 22.6%, 95% CI: 19.8%-25.4%; p < 0.001). Concomitant obesity and hypertension are independently associated with a significantly higher prevalence of target-organ involvement and prospective risk of cardiorenal and vascular complications in older adults in rural Equatorial Guinea. These findings highlight the need for early multi-organ risk screening in primary care settings across resource-limited central African populations.

cards.title: Investigating Factors Influencing the Long-Term Outcome of Teriparatide Treatment on the Risk of Hip Fracture. Is sequential treatment essential?
cards.abstract: Teriparatide (TPTD) is an anabolic therapy for severe osteoporosis. Clinical trials have shown its efficacy in reducing vertebral and non-vertebral fractures, data on hip fracture prevention in real-world settings and the impact of sequential antiresorptive (AR) therapy remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Hungarian National Health Insurance Database, which covers the entire population (~9.7 million). Patients with osteoporosis who received TPTD between 2010 and 2023, with treatment initiated by January 1, 2022. Hip fractures were tracked from day 180 after TPTD initiation for up to five years. Adherence was assessed via medication possession ratio. Post-TPTD AR therapy (bisphosphonate or denosumab) and the timing of its initiation were evaluated as factors influencing hip fracture risk. Poisson regression models were applied, adjusting for demographics, prior fractures, and healthcare utilization. Among 8,893 eligible patients, 574 hip fractures occurred during follow-up. High adherence was associated with reduced hip fracture risk by 20% (p<0.05). The number of fractures prior to treatment was also associated with fracture risk, increasing it by 11% (p<0.05). Delayed AR initiation was closely related to a proportional increase in risk, which grew proportionally with the time elapsed between the two treatments. In a cohort of patients exhibiting high adherence, deferring AR treatment for over 90 days post-TPTD therapy was associated with an increase of 19% in hip fracture risk when subsequent treatment involved bisphosphonates, and a 31% increase when denosumab was utilized as the follow-up therapy. The efficacy of teriparatide treatment was associated with patient adherence and the number of prior fractures. Neglecting to initiate AR treatment following teriparatide therapy, or starting it late, was strongly linked to an increased risk of hip fractures. Our findings provide real-world data supporting timely initiation of AR therapy post-TPTD for sustained fracture prevention.

cards.title: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in patients with rheumatic diseases: clinical characteristics, associated factors, and fragility fractures.
cards.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely used in the treatment of rheumatic diseases because of their potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. However, prolonged GC exposure is associated with glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) and an increased risk of fragility fractures. To determine the prevalence of reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and densitometric osteoporosis and to investigate factors associated with BMD and fragility fractures in patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy. This cross-sectional medical records review study included 223 patients with rheumatic diseases receiving GC therapy who underwent osteoporosis screening. Clinical characteristics, GC exposure, fragility fractures, laboratory parameters and femoral neck and lumbar spine dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) results were recorded. Patients were classified by the lowest T-score using World Health Organization criteria as normal (T-score > - 1.0), osteopenia (- 2.5 < T-score ≤ - 1.0) or osteoporosis (T-score ≤ - 2.5); reduced BMD denoted osteopenia or osteoporosis. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with fragility fractures. Mean age was 59.9 ± 10.9 years; 93.3% were female. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common diagnosis (54.3%). Among 214 patients with available DXA classification, 16.4% had normal BMD, 55.6% osteopenia and 28.0% osteoporosis; thus, 83.6% had reduced BMD. Patients with reduced BMD were older, had longer disease duration, longer GC treatment duration and higher cumulative GC exposure than those with normal BMD (p < 0.05). T-scores were inversely correlated with age, disease duration, GC treatment duration, daily GC dose and parathyroid hormone levels (all p < 0.05). Fragility fractures occurred in 38.1% of patients, and 67.9% of those with fractures and available DXA classification had normal BMD or osteopenia rather than densitometric osteoporosis. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, older age (OR 1.22 per year, 95% CI 1.15-1.29), female sex (OR 10.40, 95% CI 1.14-94.84) and longer disease duration (OR 1.07 per year, 95% CI 1.01-1.13) were independently associated with fragility fractures. Reduced BMD was common among patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy and was associated with older age, longer disease duration and greater GC exposure. Most fragility fractures occurred in patients without densitometric osteoporosis, suggesting that BMD alone may not fully reflect fracture risk in this population. • Reduced BMD (T-score ≤ - 1.0) was present in 83.6% of patients with rheumatic diseases receiving long-term GC therapy, whereas densitometric osteoporosis (T-score ≤ - 2.5) was present in 28.0%. • Fragility fractures were frequent, and approximately two-thirds of patients with fractures did not have densitometric osteoporosis. • Older age, female sex and longer disease duration were independently associated with fragility fractures, highlighting the need for fracture risk assessment beyond BMD alone.

cards.title: Biomarkers of ageing and lung function trajectory: a multi-omics study in a UK birth cohort
cards.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accelerated biological ageing and cellular senescence are pathogenically implicated in COPD and may represent therapeutic targets. Adverse early-life lung function trajectories offer opportunities to prevent COPD but their relationship with epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers remains unexplored. We investigated using conventional epidemiological and Mendelian randomisation (MR) methods. METHODS: Outcomes were the two lowest of five FEV1 trajectories (Persistently Low and Below Average) previously identified using latent profile analysis (ages 8-30) in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children. Exposures included nine measures of blood-derived epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and thirteen senescence-associated plasma proteins (ages 7-9). We used logistic regression to estimate odds of lower trajectory membership by exposure and bidirectional one-sample MR to investigate causation. RESULTS: Higher plasma CXCL10 (OR 1.29 per SD; 95% CI 1.03, 1.57), IL6 (OR 1.29; 1.03, 1.57) and IL33 (OR 1.23; 1.04, 1.44) were associated with Persistently Low lung function trajectory, with little evidence for associations between EAA and lower trajectories. MR provided little evidence that genetically predicted plasma proteins influenced risk of lower trajectories, but lower genetically proxied childhood FEV1 predicted higher plasma CXCL10 at ages 9 ({beta} -0.34; -0.65, -0.03) and 24 ({beta} -0.38; -0.67, -0.08). INTERPRETATION: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, predict low lung function trajectory into early adulthood. Lower childhood lung function may causally relate to persistently increased plasma CXCL10. Future research should investigate IL33 as a potential therapeutic target in low lung function trajectory and persistent systemic inflammation as a mechanism for associated multimorbidity.

cards.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Geriatric Heart Failure: Evidence, Safety, and Clinical Implementation.
cards.abstract: This review summarizes the rationale, efficacy, safety, and implementation of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in older adults with heart failure (HF). SGLT2i have become an integral part of contemporary HF therapy, with benefits demonstrated across the ejection fraction spectrum. Age subgroup analyses from randomized trials, frailty analyses, meta-analyses, and real-world cohorts suggest that benefits on HF hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes are largely preserved in older and frail patients. Observational data in patients aged ≥ 75 and > 80 years further support potential effectiveness in very old and multimorbid populations. However, geriatric vulnerability modifies clinical implementation, particularly regarding volume status, renal function, risk of falling, genitourinary infections, nutritional status, cognition, polypharmacy, and self-care capacity. Available evidence suggests that SGLT2i remain effective and are generally well tolerated in older patients with HF. Older age alone should therefore not preclude SGLT2i therapy. In geriatric HF, treatment decisions should be individualized according to frailty, comorbidity burden, safety risks, functional status, self-care capacity, and goals of care.
