cards.title: Intravital single-molecule microscopy reveals protein kinetics in live mammalian tissues
cards.abstract: Quantifying individual protein behavior in living mammalian tissues remains challenging. Here we introduce intravital single-molecule microscopy (iSiMM), an imaging and analysis framework that combines instant structured illumination microscopy guided tissue navigation with highly inclined and laminated optical sheet illumination. In live mice, iSiMM enables single-emitter detection and tracking of endogenously expressed fluorescently tagged proteins at 30 ms per frame. Trajectory-based modeling quantifies diffusion coefficients and model-defined bound and free fractions, while localization-density reconstructions map molecular organization. We illustrate the approach using the actomyosin cytoskeleton, resolving isoform-specific mobility and responses to physiological stimulation and genetic perturbation. Single-molecule detection in pancreas and skeletal muscle, including after in vivo transfection, further demonstrates feasibility across additional tissues and labeling strategies. iSiMM provides a framework for investigating molecular behavior in the physiological context of living mammalian tissues.

cards.title: A pilot study of a computed tomography volumetric analysis technique to determine severity of injury and prognosis for OTA 42A-C open tibial diaphyseal fractures.
cards.abstract: This pilot study evaluated a novel computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric analysis tool for open tibial fractures. We hypothesized that the volumetric injury ratio (VINJ/VUNINJ), a quantitative comparison of injured with contralateral uninjured limb segments, would correlate with clinical outcomes and serve as a prognostic marker. A retrospective review of a tibial fracture registry was conducted at a single academic institution (2014-2024). Eligible patients were older than 18 years old with preoperative bilateral lower extremity CT imaging, high-energy injuries, and ≥6 months of follow-up. Demographics, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), injury features, and outcomes including fracture-related infection (FRI), amputation, and nonunion were collected. Tissue volume was measured at the fracture midpoint and 5 cm proximal and distal, with corresponding contralateral measurements. VINJ/VUNINJ was calculated, and logistic regression estimated complication risk. The primary endpoint was a composite complication (FRI, amputation, or nonunion). Discrimination was assessed using AUROC and compared with the Gustilo-Anderson (GA) classification via the DeLong test. The Youden Index identified an optimal risk threshold. Power analysis estimated sample size requirements for a future validation study. Fifteen patients met inclusion criteria (mean age 36.1 ± 13.5 years). GA distribution: 60% II, 6.7% IIIa, 26.7% IIIb, and 6.7% IIIc. The volumetric model (log[p/(1-p)] = -110.964 + 100.011 × VINJ/VUNINJ) demonstrated a trend toward improved discriminatory ability compared with the GA model (AUROC: 0.944 vs 0.769, P = 0.068). A Youden-derived threshold (0.539) classified 5 patients (33.3%) as high-risk; all developed complications compared with 10% in the low-risk group (100% vs 10%, P = 0.001). Power analysis indicated that detecting a twofold increase in complications would require ∼23 patients per arm (46 total). This pilot study introduces a CT-based volumetric ratio as a quantitative tool for risk stratification in open tibial fractures. Findings suggest superior prognostic accuracy compared with GA, supporting prospective validation in larger patient cohorts.

cards.title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
cards.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

cards.title: Scaling a context-aware genomic model for condition-specific edit design in plants
cards.abstract: Engineering agronomically relevant traits in crops often requires changing a gene's activity in a specific tissue, developmental stage or environmental condition while preserving its roles in other contexts. Designing such selective changes requires predicting how cis-regulatory sequences are interpreted in different biological states, as the same edit can have different effects across contexts. Genomic models have made substantial progress in predicting gene expression from DNA sequence, yet sequence-only predictors do not receive an explicit description of biological states. We introduce CROP-1 (Context-aware Regulatory Output Prediction model), which combines DNA sequence with transcription factor binding motifs and measured expression to predict gene activity as a function of both sequence and regulatory state. On a held-out test set spanning six plant species, CROP-1 achieves a median per-gene Pearson correlation across contexts of 0.831, compared with 0.486 for its parameter-matched sequence-only counterpart, and 57-246% higher median correlations than three genomic foundation models fully fine-tuned on the same task. Prediction accuracy also improves with scale: increasing model capacity reduces validation error by 48%, while expanding training data to include more diverse biological contexts reduces it by 58%. We then use gradient-based sequence optimisation to translate a desired gene expression pattern into candidate edits of its cis-regulatory sequence, targeting up- or down-regulation in one context while preserving expression in others. In soybean and tomato, edit designs with 1-20 nucleotide substitutions produce strong predicted target responses and much smaller average changes across non-target contexts. By connecting scalable learning of sequence-state relationships to selective edit design, CROP-1 provides a computational foundation for controlling where, when and under which conditions endogenous crop genes are active.

cards.title: The prognostic value of a laboratory-based frailty index (FI-Lab) in carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections: a multicentre cohort study.
cards.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) infections remain a major cause of mortality despite advances in antimicrobial therapy. Frailty, reflecting cumulative physiological decline, may strongly influence outcomes beyond age or comorbidity. This study evaluated whether a 30-item Frailty Index-Laboratory (FI-Lab), calculated within 48 h of admission, independently predicts early (7-day) and short-term (30-day) mortality among hospitalized patients with CRAB infections. We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study including adults with microbiologically confirmed CRAB infection admitted to four Infectious Diseases Units in Apulia, Italy (Bari, Foggia, Taranto-Moscati, Bisceglie) between January 2020 and August 2025. The FI-Lab, derived from 30 biochemical parameters, quantified the proportion of abnormal laboratory values (range 0-1). Cox regression models assessed associations between FI-Lab and mortality, adjusting for age, comorbidity, SOFA score, septic shock, infection site, therapy type, and other covariates. Among 199 patients (mean age 70 ± 15 years; 38.2% male), the median FI-Lab was 0.56 (IQR 0.45-0.68). Seven-day, 30-day, and in-hospital mortality were 12.6%, 19.1%, and 20.6%, respectively. Each + 0.10 increase in FI-Lab was associated with higher 7-day (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.22-1.89), 30-day (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.36-2.08), and in-hospital (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.32-2.01) mortality (all p < 0.01). Patients with respiratory infections had significantly higher 30-day mortality than those with bloodstream infections (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.05-2.51, p = 0.029). No mortality difference was observed between cefiderocol- and colistin-based regimens. FI-Lab demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUC = 0.89 for 30-day mortality). The FI-Lab independently predicted early and short-term mortality in CRAB infections, outperforming traditional indices and highlighting the prognostic weight of biological frailty. The strong impact of respiratory infection and the absence of therapy-related differences suggest that host vulnerability may outweigh antimicrobial choice in determining outcomes. FI-Lab, easily derived from routine tests, could be integrated into clinical algorithms for early risk stratification in multidrug-resistant infection.

cards.title: Urban, regional and remote outcomes following TAVR for Queensland patients: a retrospective cohort study
cards.abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) offers a minimally invasive approach to treat severe aortic stenosis (AS) but can only be performed at centres meeting strict regulatory requirements. It remains unclear whether this requirement restricts TAVR access for patients residing in rural Australia, and whether such people experience poorer outcomes than metropolitan counterparts as a result. Methods This multicentre retrospective cohort study used Australian Cardiac Outcomes Registry data. All Queensland residents who underwent TAVR between April 2018 and 27 March 2026 were included. Rurality was assigned by postcode using the Modified Monash Model (MMM) and grouped as urban (MMM1), regional (MMM2-4), or remote (MMM5-7). The primary outcome was 12-month mortality and was investigated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Findings Among 6813 patients, 4246 (62%) were urban, 2092 (31%) regional, and 475 (7%) remote. Twelve-month all-cause mortality did not differ by rurality (urban: 211 [5.0%]; regional: 103 [4.9%]; remote: 23 [4.8%]; {chi}2=0.991, log-rank P=0.929), a finding confirmed in multivariable analysis. At the time of TAVR, regional and remote patients were younger, more comorbid, had more severe AS, and lower STS scores than urban counterparts. Clinical frailty score, non-transfemoral access, STS score, atrial fibrillation or flutter, and moderate-severe chronic lung disease independently predicted 12-month mortality. Interpretation TAVR outcomes were comparable between rurality groups, suggesting equitable care within Queensland's centralised TAVR model. However, registry data only captures patients who underwent TAVR and may miss older rural patients facing barriers to AS diagnosis, referral, or procedural workup. Funding There was no funding or sponsor involvement.

cards.title: Cumulative antiresorptive exposure and dentoalveolar procedures increase medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw risk in U.S. veterans treated for fracture prevention.
cards.abstract: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a rare but serious complication of bisphosphonate (BP) or denosumab therapy. Prior studies evaluating MRONJ risk factors largely involve cancer populations, small samples, claims-based data, or limited covariate assessment. We sought to determine MRONJ risk factors among patients receiving antiresorptives for osteoporosis. A retrospective cohort study of adults ≥50 years in the U.S. Veterans Health Administration with comprehensive dental benefits prescribed ≥1 oral (alendronate, risedronate, ibandronate) or intravenous (zoledronic acid, ibandronate) BP or denosumab between 10/1/1999-12/31/2022 was performed. Individuals with non-osteoporosis indications or dosing regimens, other BP or anabolic osteoporosis medication use, or missing covariates were excluded. Demographics, clinical characteristics, and medications were determined. Invasive dentoalveolar procedures were ascertained using Current Dental Terminology codes. Natural language processing of electronic medical records identified MRONJ events through 12/31/2023. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs). Baseline characteristics were fixed, while comorbidities, medications (including cumulative antiresorptive exposure), and dental procedures were modeled as time-varying, updated at 90-day intervals. Among 42,378 Veterans contributing 381,437 person-years, 44 developed MRONJ. Cumulative 20-year MRONJ incidence was 0.18% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.13-0.25%). In multivariable-adjusted analyses, Multiracial versus White race (HR: 5.47; 95% CI: 1.31-22.91), baseline body mass index (HR: 0.89 per 1 kg/m2 increase; 95% CI: 0.84-0.96), cumulative antiresorptive exposure (HR: 1.34 per 1-year increase; 95% CI: 1.15-1.56), and recent invasive dentoalveolar procedure (HR: 4.40; 95% CI: 1.70-11.38) were independently associated with MRONJ. MRONJ incidence was very low among patients receiving antiresorptives for osteoporosis, although associations of cumulative antiresorptive exposure and dentoalveolar procedures with MRONJ risk may inform shared decision-making.

cards.title: Patients' lived experiences of fractures during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a qualitative study.
cards.abstract: Fractures during or after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy were experienced as "a small price to pay" relative to cancer survival. Despite their functional and psychological impact, patients emphasized the importance of rehabilitation and more transparent communication regarding fracture risks. While bone fractures following immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy have been increasingly reported, patients' lived experiences and the associated functional and psychological consequences are not well understood. This study aimed to evaluate patients' descriptions of their fracture experiences during and after their ICI therapy. In this qualitative descriptive study, 15 patients who experienced fractures during or after ICI therapy were interviewed. Participants were recruited between March 2024 and July 2025. Semi‑structured interviews were audio‑recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis approach. Coding was conducted independently by a single researcher and subsequently reviewed by the full research team. The analysis showed that fracture experiences were interpreted within the context of a core theme: "a small price to pay." Participants viewed fractures as less important when compared with the risk of mortality from cancer. They demonstrated different pathways of adaptation and recovery, highlighting the importance of physical rehabilitation and the need for empathy from healthcare providers. Additionally, although patients were unaware of the association between immunotherapy and bone fractures, they noted that this information would not have changed their initial desire to receive treatment, although it would have been helpful in providing them with better insight and a greater sense of control. Bone fractures in ICI recipients have a significant impact on patients' overall functioning, although they do not diminish patients' desire to continue treatment. Providing patients with information about these risks helps them prepare for injury prevention and manage the unintended consequences.

cards.title: Risk factors for revisions in patients following total hip arthroplasty and hemiarthroplasty due to femoral neck fractures.
cards.abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and hemiarthroplasty (HA) are established treatments for displaced femoral neck fractures (FNF), yet factors associated with revision following either procedure remain poorly defined. This study evaluated demographic, clinical, and laboratory predictors of revision after THA and HA for FNF. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary trauma centre including 2,522 patients treated with arthroplasty for FNF (885 THA, 1,637 HA). Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and pre- and postoperative laboratory parameters were compared between patients who underwent revision and those who did not. Variables significant on univariate analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine optimal cutoff values for significant continuous predictors. Revision occurred in 93 of 885 THA patients (10.5%) and 43 of 1,637 HA patients (2.6%) (p < 0.001). In the THA cohort, patients requiring revision were younger (65.4 vs. 72.5 years, p < 0.001), had shorter hospital stays (5.4 vs. 7.5 days, p = 0.001), higher postoperative haemoglobin (10.5 vs. 9.6 g/dL, p < 0.001), and lower postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (10.8 vs. 15.7 mg/dL, p = 0.007). Multivariable analysis identified younger age (OR 0.94 per year, 95% CI 0.91-0.98; p = 0.003), higher postoperative haemoglobin (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01-1.66; p = 0.044), and lower postoperative CRP (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.90-0.99; p = 0.029) as independent predictors of revision. ROC analysis identified age < 60 years (AUC 0.66) and postoperative haemoglobin ≥ 10.55 g/dL (AUC 0.63) as optimal thresholds. In the HA cohort, only postoperative lymphocyte count differed significantly between revision and non-revision groups, precluding multivariable analysis. Revision following arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture was substantially more common after THA than HA. Among THA patients, revision was associated with younger age and markers of better postoperative physiological recovery rather than medical frailty. These findings suggest that revision risk after fracture-related THA may largely reflect the greater activity level and longer survivorship of healthier patients, information that may assist preoperative counseling and individualized procedure selection.

cards.title: BioCluster: Clustering and Zero-Shot Labeling of Ecological Images Using Foundation Models
cards.abstract: The increasing automation of biodiversity monitoring is generating large volumes of ecological images requiring taxonomic identification, creating a substantial annotation bottleneck. Assigning species-level labels requires considerable time and expert knowledge, limiting scalability. We propose BioCluster, a framework for unsupervised clustering and zero-shot labeling of ecological images using foundation models. The framework extracts image embeddings from pretrained models and groups images into taxonomic clusters without task-specific training. Species labels are assigned through zero-shot text matching against the taxa expected in the dataset. We investigate dimensionality reduction and six clustering algorithms for organizing fine-grained imagery. A per-image uncertainty score combines clustering and labeling information to sort images into three confidence tiers, so experts can focus on uncertain and unlabeled cases. We evaluate it on two moth and two bird datasets, with one annotated camera-trap collection per taxonomic group. For these camera-trap datasets, per-image species-level accuracy reached 84% on DK-Moth and 83% on HUGO-Bench Aves. An interactive report presents clusters and zero-shot labels by confidence tier and prioritizes cases requiring expert review. The framework provides a training-free approach for organizing and labeling ecological image collections, reducing manual annotation while retaining expert oversight and demonstrating the potential of foundation models for scalable, semi-automated annotation.

cards.title: Research Progress on the Precise Classification and Individualized Diagnosis and Treatment of Nocturia.
cards.abstract: Nocturia is a common urological symptom whose prevalence increases progressively with age. It not only impairs sleep and quality of life but also increases the risk of adverse events, including falls and fractures. Clinical management remains limited by inadequate evaluation of underlying etiologies, imprecise phenotyping, and suboptimal therapeutic responses. To facilitate standardized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, we reviewed and summarized relevant literature published over the past decade. Focusing on four major subtypes, nocturnal polyuria (NP), diminished bladder capacity (DBC), global polyuria (GP), and sleep disorder-predominant nocturia (SDP), we developed a clinical framework integrating precise assessment, phenotypic classification, and individualized treatment. This review compares the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying different phenotypes, identifies the voiding diary as the cornerstone of assessment, and proposes a streamlined three-step clinical phenotyping algorithm. A stepwise treatment strategy tailored to different subtypes is outlined, incorporating psychological counseling, lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, physical therapy, and surgery. This review provides a reference for the precise and individualized management of nocturia and highlights the potential future roles of digital assessment and multidisciplinary care.

cards.title: Metagenomic contextualization of proteins with state space models
cards.abstract: Genomic foundation models have emerged as powerful tools for learning representations of biological sequences, but existing approaches predominantly rely on Transformer architectures, whose quadratic attention complexity limits their ability to capture long-range genomic context. This limitation is particularly relevant for metagenomics, where sequencing data have increased more than 500-fold since 2011, generating increasingly large and diverse datasets. For example, gLM2, a Transformer-based mixed-modality genomic language model, was trained with a context window of 4,096 tokens, limiting its ability to capture extended genomic context within metagenomic contigs. Developing scalable architectures capable of processing longer sequences while integrating protein and nucleotide information is therefore essential for advancing genomic foundation models. We introduce Nammu, a 167-million-parameter, bidirectional Mamba-based genomic foundation model that integrates protein and nucleotide sequences within a 20,000-token context window. Leveraging the linear scaling of state-space models, Nammu was trained using a curriculum learning strategy on the OpenMetaGenomic (OMG) corpus, first incorporating 64 million protein sequences followed by 32 million mixed-modality metagenomic contigs. Despite using approximately 37\% fewer training tokens than gLM2, Nammu outperformed this Transformer-based model in taxonomic classification across all evaluated taxonomic ranks on a marine metagenomic dataset from the Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation (CAMI). On the exact-feature-unmatched CAMI II Strain Madness test set, Nammu achieved higher all-contig genus-classification accuracy than Kraken2 (0.9182 versus 0.8142). Nammu further outperformed gLM2 (150M) in KEGG Orthology prediction using deep-sea metagenome-assembled genomes. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of state-space architectures for scalable, multimodal genomic representation learning and highlight their ability to support accurate taxonomic and functional predictions from metagenomic sequences.

cards.title: Patient-specific management in high-risk revision total hip arthroplasty: mid-term outcomes of a next-generation constrained acetabular liner.
cards.abstract: Managing recurrent instability in revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) requires a personalized approach, as traditional constrained liners often yield suboptimal results due to locking-mechanism failure and limited impingement-free range of motion. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term clinical outcomes of a novel constrained acetabular liner (CAL) when utilized as a patient-specific solution for a high-risk cohort undergoing complex rTHA. By tailoring the constraint to individual biomechanical deficits, this next-generation device seeks to mitigate historic failure modes. We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients who underwent 37 rTHA procedures with a next-generation CAL at a single urban academic center between March 2017 and October 2023. Average follow-up was 4.7 years (range, 0.3 to 9.7 years). The most common indication for rTHA was instability (70.3%), followed by infection (16.2%), aseptic loosening (10.8%), and polyethylene wear (2.7%). Just over one third of patients (37.5%) had undergone a prior revision. Preoperative constructs included fixed-bearing (37.8%), dual-mobility (32.4%), CAL (24.3%), static spacer (2.7%), and hemiarthroplasty (2.7%). In most procedures (70.3%), the CAL was implanted into a pre-existing acetabular cup, whereas 29.7% involved both cup and liner revision. Following rTHA, no cases of implant wear, breakage, acetabular cup aseptic loosening, or periprosthetic fracture were observed. Six patients (18.8%) underwent a total of sixteen subsequent reoperations after CAL implantation-10 for instability and 6 for infection. Among instability-related reoperations, 4 involved revision to a new next-generation CAL. Survivorship free from all-cause reoperation was 83.8% at one year and 72.6% at latest follow-up. This study demonstrates favorable mid-term clinical outcomes and reoperation-free survivorship following complex revision THA using a novel constrained acetabular liner system. For patient cohorts suffering from severe recurrent dislocation, this next-generation CAL provides an effective, tailored tool in the surgical armamentarium by adapting to unique patient anatomy and soft-tissue compromises. Further research with larger sample sizes and extended follow-up is needed to assess long-term durability.

cards.title: Decision benchmarking reveals when protein foundation models add experimental value
cards.abstract: Protein engineering is shifting from model-based variant scoring to deciding what to measure next. This exposes a limitation of fixed-dataset benchmarks, which rank predictors without showing when their advantage survives as evidence accumulates. We therefore introduce decision benchmarking across 217 ProteinGym assays, 2.47 million variants and 95 predictors to evaluate whether models and measurements improve decisions at matched cost. Zero-shot accuracy explained less than one-fifth of the variation in discovery after calibration. Calibrated priors exceeded budget-matched additivity at 20-100 measurements, but the advantage narrowed as component measurements accumulated. Measured additivity then overtook zero-shot models after 50-100 measurements for top-variant discovery and around 500 for global ranking. The same principle showed that double-mutant measurements improved prediction in models using mutation identity, whereas prediction-guided acquisition improved discovery. Evidence-based routing improved strategy selection. Decision benchmarking thus identifies which strategy adds value given the information already available and the decision that follows.

cards.title: [Thoracic trauma in Hungary today: heritage, current challenges and future directions].
cards.abstract: Thoracic trauma is an important contributor to morbidity and mortality among severely injured patients. While the management of immediately life-threatening intrathoracic injuries is relatively well defined, the treatment of severe blunt chest wall injuries, particularly multiple rib fractures and flail chest, remains variable across institutions. This review aims to summarize the current situation of thoracic trauma care in Hungary, with special emphasis on chest wall injuries and the role of surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF). SSRF should no longer be regarded as an isolated technical procedure, but as part of the complex, multidisciplinary management of patients with rib fractures. Therapeutic decision-making should be based not only on the number of fractured ribs, but also on fracture pattern, chest wall instability, pain, respiratory mechanics, pulmonary parenchymal injury, the patient's physiological reserve, overall injury severity and timing of surgery. The development of thoracic trauma care in Hungary requires a shared indication language, protocol-based imaging, early reassessment, multimodal analgesia, physiotherapy, transparent regional referral pathways and auditable outcome measurement. The existing Hungarian expertise in trauma surgery, thoracic surgery, emergency medicine and intensive care provides a realistic basis for establishing a structured, nationally applicable model of thoracic trauma care. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(42): 1686-1692.

cards.title: Hip Structural Analysis and Multiple Fragility Fractures: Evidence from a Large Cross-Sectional Clinical Cohort.
cards.abstract: Hip structural analysis parameters (HSAP) are associated with hip fracture risk, but associations with multiple fragility fracture phenotypes remain poorly characterised. We analysed 11 DXA-derived HSAP in patients referred between June 2004 and November 2019. Five mutually exclusive fracture phenotypes were defined: no fracture, single hip fracture, single non-hip fracture, multiple non-hip fractures, and multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture. Separate multinomial logistic regression models were fitted for each HSAP reported as odds ratio (OR) per standard deviation increase, adjusted for FRAX covariates and left femoral BMD. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied across all tests. A right-hip sensitivity analysis assessed bilateral consistency. 35,647 patients were included (mean age 64.5 years, 82% female). Of 13,777 (38.6%) with a fragility fracture, 1044 (2.9%) had a single hip fracture, 9723 (27.3%) a single non-hip fracture, 2268 (6.4%) multiple non-hip fractures, and 742 (2.1%) multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture. After multiple testing correction, no meaningful associations were observed for isolated hip or non-hip fracture phenotypes. Multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture were independently associated with greater hip axis length (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.28 to 1.63), neck diameter (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.38), and centre of mass to upper neck margin distance (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.21 to 1.51). HSAP were significantly associated with multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture rather than isolated fracture phenotypes, potentially reflecting local structural vulnerability and broader biomechanical instability.

cards.title: Sex shapes capillary flows and oxygen extraction in the middle-aged mouse brain
cards.abstract: Sex differences in brain aging are well documented, but their origin within the cerebrovascular hierarchy remains unclear. Here we show that cortical blood flow is higher in female than male mice at 15 months of age, at a point when an earlier sex difference in pulsatility and resistance indices has already converged, pial vessel diameter shows no difference between sexes, and estrogen levels are similar between sexes. Using an indicator-dilution and intravascular oxygen measurements using two-photon microscopy, we found that capillary transit-time heterogeneity (CTH) scales more steeply with mean transit time in females, consistent with a passively regulated capillary network, and that this is accompanied by reduced oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) without deficit in arterial oxygen delivery. Spatial transcriptomics reveals that sex differences are organized into distinct regional programs, most prominently in white matter, where a male-associated myelin and axonogenesis signature accompanies reduced white matter volume in females. These molecular and structural differences coincide with elevated hippocampal microglial reactivity and an altered spatial search strategy in females, without any detectable differences in circulating markers of stress, blood-brain barrier integrity, or immunity. Together, these findings indicate that sex differences in the aging brain are expressed at the level of capillary flow regulation and regional tissue programs rather than through bulk cerebral blood flow alone, and that elevated blood flow in females can mask, rather than reflect, adequate tissue oxygenation.

cards.title: DeepD enables efficient genome modeling and controllable long-context sequence generation across domains of life
cards.abstract: Genome foundation models hold great potential for advancing biological research, but modeling diverse complex genomes and generating controllable genome-scale sequences remain challenging. We present DeepD, a phylogeny-informed sparse mixture-of-experts model operating at single-nucleotide resolution over a 1-million-token context while reducing active computation. Pretrained on unselected whole-genome sequences across all domains of life, DeepD learns genic and intergenic sequence features and supports broad sequence-to-function prediction across species. DeepD performs well in human protein fitness and disease variants effect prediction, such as BRCA1 and BRCA2, with particular strength in regulatory regions, such as promoter and transcription-factor binding sites. Expert routing captures exon-intron boundaries, transposable elements, and distal cis-regulatory elements. DeepD also generates experimentally validated core promoters with specified transcriptional strengths. Finally, the Context-Anchor-Body strategy enables generation of complete yeast chromosome sequences and megabase-scale Arabidopsis segments, preserving gene structure and order while introducing variations within natural ranges. Together, DeepD is an efficient genome foundation model that unifies accurate sequence-to-function prediction with controllable genome-scale generation, advancing predictive and generative design of complex genomes.

cards.title: Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics
cards.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies enable the identification of spatially variable genes that can shed light on tissue structure and function. However, spatial variability of gene expression can be due not only to biological function but also technical artifact. We develop a model for spatially variable capture that forms part of a bursty transcription model, allowing us to distinguish biological variability from spatially variable technical noise. Our approach is implemented in a program called stipple, which we demonstrate can be useful for identifying and interpreting spatial gene expression variation from spatial transcriptomics assays.

cards.title: PlantGeneAnn: a high-accuracy ab initio plant gene annotation tool fine-tuned from a genome foundation model
cards.abstract: Structural annotation remains a bottleneck for translating the growing catalog of high-quality plant genomes into biological insights, as current pipelines rely on RNA-seq and homologous protein evidence that are often unavailable for non-model species. Existing ab initio tools are constrained by model scale and perform poorly in complex plant genomic regions. We present PlantGeneAnn, a plant-optimized ab initio gene annotation tool fine-tuned from a genome foundation model. It combines a Mamba-MoE DNA encoder with a U-Net-style embedding decoder and a semi-Markov decoding pipeline. Trained on 40 angiosperm species, PlantGeneAnn establishes a new state-of-the-art (SOTA) across a stringent 20-species benchmark, significantly outperforming Helixer, Tiberius, and ANNEVO at exon-, intron-, and locus-levels, with mean F1 scores of 0.856, 0.880, and 0.707, respectively. It also enables efficient customized fine-tuning: LoRA fine-tuning increased the locus-level F1 of the out-of-distribution bryophyte Physcomitrium patens from 0.581 to 0.736, with performance plateauing at 40% of the fine-tuning data. Notably, PlantGeneAnn requires substantially lower peak memory usage than other baseline tools, allowing annotation of large plant genomes on standard personal workstations. PlantGeneAnn thus provides accurate, hardware-friendly ab initio annotation for diverse plant genomes, particularly newly assembled genomes, population-scale projects, and non-model plants.

cards.title: Impact of clinical frailty on mortality after elective surgery in patients aged ≥ 90 years admitted to critical care: a binational intensive care registry analysis.
cards.abstract: Increasing numbers of patients aged ≥ 90 years require elective surgery. Frailty is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of peri-operative risk, but high-quality evidence to understand the impact on outcomes in this age group is limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Adult Patient Database. Patients aged ≥ 90 years admitted to ICU following elective surgery were included, encompassing planned and unplanned ICU admissions. Frailty was assessed at ICU admission using the Clinical Frailty Scale and patients categorised as non-frail or frail. Propensity score matching was performed to balance age; sex; acute illness severity; and comorbidities. Primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU mortality; in-hospital mortality; return to pre-admission residence; and ICU and duration of hospital stay. The matched cohort comprised 5398 patients (2699 without frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 1-4) and 2699 living with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 5-8)), with good post-matching covariate balance. Mortality in ICU was low and not significantly different between patients who were frail and non-frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (matched hazard ratio (HR) 1.66, 95%CI 1.22-2.27, p = 0.001) and higher 1-year mortality (matched HR 1.66, 95%CI 1.47-1.87, p < 0.001). Patients without frailty had higher odds of returning to their pre-admission residence at hospital discharge than patients living with frailty (matched OR 1.45, 95%CI 1.29-1.62, p < 0.001). Patients who were frail experienced longer hospital stays and higher rates of postoperative complications, including delirium and acute renal failure. Among patients aged ≥ 90 years undergoing elective surgery with postoperative intensive care admission, frailty is strongly associated with prolonged recovery and worse short and long-term outcomes. Incorporation of frailty assessment into peri-operative pathways may improve risk stratification, shared decision-making and personalised care for patients aged ≥ 90 years.

cards.title: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes
cards.abstract: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.

cards.title: Inherent limitations of zero-shot mutation prediction in protein engineering
cards.abstract: Predicting mutation effects is critical for protein engineering. A commonly pursued strategy is zero-shot prediction with deep-learning models, whose performance is typically evaluated using aggregate benchmark scores that obscure multidimensional biological tradeoffs. Here, we evaluate sequence, structure, and hybrid foundation models across curated datasets to expose the practical limitations of zero-shot predictions. We demonstrate that model performance is highly variable and heavily influenced by experimental noise and competing phenotypic goals. Notably, predictions from competing models often correlate more strongly with one another than with experimental outcomes. While current models effectively filter deleterious mutations and enrich high-scoring variants for natural functions, they struggle to identify precise optimal mutations and consistently fail to predict mutations that drive new-to-nature functions. These models learn from evolutionary constraints that tend to oppose the extreme biophysical optimizations required in targeted engineering. Consequently, zero-shot scoring serves as a valuable initial filter but cannot substitute for task-specific prediction.

cards.title: Covariance Nonstationarity is Evident in Spatial Transcriptomics and Provides a New Categorization of Spatially Varying Genes
cards.abstract: Gaussian process models underlie many spatial transcriptomics tools but typically assume stationary covariance. To test this assumption, we use approximate Bayes factors from R-INLA to compare stationary and non-stationary Matern covariance functions across 12 Visium datasets; covariance non-stationarity is substantially evident as it appears in 3% to 50% of genes across datasets. We find that gene sets associated with effector functions are enriched among genes favoring non-stationary spatial covariance.

cards.title: Effects of gliflozins on bone health of patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
cards.abstract: Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are a crucial therapy for chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet concerns persist regarding their impact on bone metabolism. This systematic review evaluates the skeletal safety and metabolic effects of SGLT2i in patients with CKD. A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies was conducted. Data on study design, population characteristics, baseline kidney function, bone-related comorbidities, and outcomes (osteoporosis, fractures, falls, amputations, and bone mineral markers) were summarized. Risk of bias was evaluated according to the included category. The analysis revealed that while one RCT and a cohort study reported a significantly increased risk of bone fracture and amputation, this finding was not replicated in other subsequent cohort studies and other RCTs, which generally showed non-significant differences. Of note, the reporting of bone-related outcomes was inconsistent throughout the literature, and a substantial proportion of the evidence derives from studies primarily designed for patients with type 2 diabetes, largely involving early-stage CKD subgroups. One study suggests that SGLT2i may favorably modulate markers of CKD-mineral bone disease (MBD), reporting reduced risk of hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, high parathyroid hormone, and low vitamin D levels. The reviewed literature primarily included data on empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin. Mostly, SGLT2i demonstrated a possible reassuring skeletal safety profile in CKD. Initial safety concerns regarding fractures have not been consistently supported, although evidence in moderate-to-advanced CKD remains limited. Long-term, prospectively defined skeletal outcomes are needed to confirm these findings and clarify class effects.

cards.title: Computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation of tibial fractures.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame (TSF) for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation (UEF) of tibial fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 18 patients with tibial misalignment after UEF between February 2019 and February 2024. Using the TSF technique, X-ray parameters (deformity, frame, and mounting) were entered into software to generate a six-axis correction prescription. Reduction time, number of X-ray exposures, total external fixation duration, clinical fracture healing time, complications, and functional recovery were recorded. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final visual analogue scale (VAS) scores because the paired differences were not normally distributed; data are presented as mean (range) or median (interquartile range [IQR]). All 18 patients were followed up for a mean of 14.9 months (range: 12-18 months). Satisfactory reduction was achieved in all cases after TSF adjustment. Mean reduction time was 19.0 minutes (range, 15-24 minutes), and patients received a mean of 1.4 X-ray exposures (range, 1-3). Clinical fracture healing occurred after a mean of 24.0 weeks (range, 21-29 weeks), and total external fixation lasted a mean of 25.2 weeks (range, 22-30 weeks). Johner-Wruhs ratings at final follow-up were excellent in 15 patients and good in 3 (100% excellent/good). Median VAS scores improved from 7 (IQR, 6-8) before surgery to 1 (IQR, 0-2) at final follow-up (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z = -3.77, P < .001). Superficial pin tract infections developed in 3 patients (16.7%; 3/18) and were controlled with oral antibiotics and dressing changes. No patient had deep infection, pin loosening, nonunion, or bone exposure. In this small, single-arm retrospective cohort, all 18 patients achieved satisfactory reduction with computer-assisted TSF, and adjustment times were short. No patient underwent secondary open reduction or fixation. These preliminary findings suggest that TSF may serve as a feasible minimally invasive option for correcting early malalignment following UEF of tibial fractures; however, multicenter controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these results.

cards.title: Zebrafish models for investigating skeletal muscle aging and sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle strength, mass, and function during aging, driven by impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered metabolism, regenerative failure, and neuromuscular decline. Experimental models are needed to determine how these processes drive muscle degeneration and identify testable therapeutic mechanisms. Zebrafish combine whole-animal physiology with genetic manipulation, live imaging, and scalable phenotypic analysis, making them well suited to this purpose. Natural-aging, telomerase-deficient, dexamethasone-induced, high-fat-diet, and genetically defined zebrafish models each reproduce distinct structural, functional, metabolic, regenerative, or neuromuscular changes relevant to sarcopenia. In this Review, we compare study designs, measured endpoints, and mechanistic evidence to distinguish age-associated phenotypes from responses to induced stresses or defined molecular perturbations. Natural-aging models capture spontaneous age-associated changes in muscle structure, performance, and mitochondrial integrity; telomerase-deficient models reveal defects in tissue maintenance and regeneration; and dexamethasone- and high-fat-diet-induced models enable controlled analysis of proteostatic and metabolic stress. Genetic models directly test relationships between molecular perturbations and muscle phenotypes. Current studies, however, have notable limitations: swimming performance reflects whole-animal physiology rather than muscle strength, many markers do not directly measure pathway activity, and some models represent specific stress rather than primary sarcopenia. Across these models, shared phenotypes do not establish a common causal mechanism; model-specific findings require validation during natural aging and in mammalian and human studies.

cards.title: Physiological mapping and prediction reveal stress-responsive translation initiation landscapes
cards.abstract: Translation initiation defines the protein output of the transcriptome, but its physiological dynamics in cells and tissues remain incompletely characterized. Here we develop TISCA2, an inhibitor-free method that captures eIF5B-associated initiating ribosomes to map translation initiation sites genome-wide. By directly identifying start sites rather than inferring translation from elongating-ribosome periodicity, TISCA2 improves the detection of short and overlapping translons. Translation of a subset of TISCA2-identified translons is supported by N-terminal proteomics and HLA-I immunopeptidomics. The arsenite-induced integrated stress response broadly redistributes start-site usage, reducing upstream initiation in favor of downstream initiation. TISCA2 further reveals tissue-specific initiation landscapes in vivo, with increased detection of downstream candidate start sites in the testis. Finally, we develop IncepTIS, a sequence-based deep learning model that predicts position-resolved and condition-dependent initiation landscapes. IncepTIS-guided optimization generates de novo mRNA 5' leaders with stress-responsive initiation patterns. Together, TISCA2 and IncepTIS provide an experimental and computational framework for mapping, predicting and engineering translation initiation in mammalian cells and tissues.

cards.title: Compartment-Resolved Matrisome Shifts During Postnatal Tendon Maturation in Mice
cards.abstract: Tendons acquire their load-bearing capacity during the first month of postnatal growth, driven by the extensive remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM). While the role of specific individual components to this process have been well characterized, a comprehensive assessment of how the tendon matrisome changes during this critical window is lacking. This, in part, is due to the challenges associated with solubilization of mature ECM, which is underrepresented by conventical proteomic approaches. To address this, we performed compartment-resolved proteomics on murine Achilles and plantaris tendons at postnatal days 0 (P0), P14, and P28. Sequential extraction methods leveraged a CHAPS-soluble fraction, capturing cellular and soluble matrisome proteins, from the insoluble mature ECM fraction, solubilized by guanidine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine hydrochloride and separately analyzed by label-free quantitative LC-MS/MS. Analysis shows that the two compartments followed distinct trajectories during maturation. The insoluble matrix was dominated by collagenous proteins, which increased from 95% to over 99% of the identified signal intensity, and its composition was largely established by P14. Within the soluble matrisome compartment, collagens increased from 50% to over 60% by P14, accompanied by dynamic regulation of proteins implicated in collagen processing (P4HA1, PCOLCE), crosslinking (LOX, LOXL2), and regulators of collagen fibril assembly and growth (DCN, BGN, FMOD, THBS3, THBS4). Beyond these established regulators, we observed dynamic regulation of less-characterized fibril-associated proteoglycans (KERA, OGN, CHAD), matricellular (COMP, POSTN, MATN2), and angiogenic regulatorily proteins (SERPINF1, ECM1). Together, this work establishes a comprehensive protein-level reference for postnatal tendon maturating, provides new insights into the molecular regulation of functional tendon development.

cards.title: A digital twin roadmap for adult spinal deformity.
cards.abstract: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is a high-risk, high-cost domain in which preoperative planning plays a critical role in determining alignment goals, surgical strategy, and the balance between deformity correction and treatment-related complications, yet decisions still rely heavily on static radiographs, classification systems, and surgeon experience. In parallel, medical digital twins, continuously updated, patient-specific computational models that simulate alternative treatment paths, are emerging in other medical disciplines but have not been formally articulated for ASD. In this narrative review, we adapt the recently proposed five-component medical digital twin framework (patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and synchronization policy) to adult spinal deformity by mapping each component to ASD-specific data sources, computational models, clinical workflows, and validation pathways. We outline how existing tools in ASD, including classification systems, frailty and bone-health metrics, biomechanical modeling, motion analysis, mobile health data, and machine learning risk calculators, can serve as inputs to an ASD digital twin. We highlight priority use cases, such as choosing the magnitude of surgery, bone-health-aware planning, pelvic fixation and rod strategy, and selection among open, hybrid, and minimally invasive approaches, all reframed as comparative simulations with explicit uncertainty bands. Finally, we propose a staged roadmap, from minimal viable twins evaluated via retrospective replay, to shadow-mode deployment, to oversighted clinical pilots, while detailing challenges in data harmonization, model validity, governance, and equity. Rather than claiming that a mature ASD digital twin exists today, this work offers a practical blueprint for how digital twins could evolve into auditable, patient-specific decision-support tools that augment, rather than replace, surgeon judgment in spinal deformity surgery.

cards.title: [Healthcare structures and diagnostic strategies for spinal trauma in childhood and adolescence : Results of a survey in German-speaking countries].
cards.abstract: Spinal injuries in childhood and adolescence are rare, accounting for 1-4% of all fractures. This study aimed to record the structures of healthcare and diagnostic strategies in German-speaking countries, evaluate the structural resources and assess the awareness and implementation of the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations. An anonymized online cross-sectional survey was conducted between July and September 2023 among members of orthopedic, trauma and pediatric surgical societies. The questionnaire consisted of 31 items covering demographics, clinical protocols (standard operating procedures, SOP), infrastructure, case volumes and clinical case studies regarding diagnostics. The questionnaire was developed by consensus within the working group; no formal pilot testing or validation was performed. As the access link could be forwarded freely within the societies, a response rate cannot be calculated; the proportion of fully completed questionnaires (159/169; 94.1%) and the item-level completeness (98.8%) are reported instead. Of the 169 participants (79.9% orthopedics/trauma surgery), 50.3% worked at supraregional trauma centers. Hospitals with higher case volumes (> 8 cases/year) had significantly more frequently diagnostic SOP (37% vs. 10%), pediatric-specific computed tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (CT/MRI) protocols (84% vs. 53%) and specialized orthotic inventories (65% vs. 34%). Only 25.5% of respondents had read the thematic issue containing the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations. In the case vignettes the decision for primary MRI was significantly influenced by patient age (more frequent in younger children), medical specialty (neurosurgery with a higher tendency for MRI) and seniority (chief physicians more likely to order MRI than attending physicians), whereas no statistically significant effect was demonstrable for awareness of the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations or for institutional case volume. The care of the very rare pediatric spinal trauma in German-speaking countries remains highly heterogeneous. As the publication of treatment recommendations alone has been insufficient to unify clinical practice, the findings suggest that national guidelines combined with structured implementation strategies, e.g., defined minimum standards, imaging algorithms developed jointly with (pediatric) radiology and structured training formats, could contribute to more uniform care.

cards.title: Joint association of frailty and depressive symptoms with new-onset chronic kidney disease in middle-aged and older adults: a longitudinal analysis from the CHARLS cohort.
cards.abstract: Although frailty and depressive symptoms have both been associated with the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), their joint association with incident CKD and potential mediation pathways remains unclear. This analysis used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Frailty was quantified using a 35-item deficit-accumulation frailty index and depressive symptoms were defined using the CES-D-10. New-onset CKD was ascertained by self-reported physician diagnosis or an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Cox regression models were used to estimate associations, and mediation analyses were conducted to explore potential explanatory pathways. During a mean follow-up of 6.87 years, 327 of 6,854 participants (4.8%) developed CKD. Depressive symptoms and frailty were each independently linked to incident CKD, with HRs of 1.50 (95% CI: 1.19-1.88) and 1.95 (95% CI: 1.52-2.49), respectively. Participants with coexisting depressive symptoms and frailty showed the greatest risk compared with those with neither condition (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.59-2.77). In mediation analysis, frailty accounted for an estimated 66% of the observed association between depressive symptoms and CKD. Coexisting frailty and depressive symptoms were associated with the highest risk of incident CKD. Mediation analysis suggested that frailty may partly explain the observed link between depressive symptoms and CKD. Concurrent screening for depressive symptoms and frailty may help improve CKD risk stratification in aging adults.

cards.title: timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing
cards.abstract: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) can enable precise and accurate quantification of analytes at high-sensitivity, but the rate at which samples can be analyzed remains limited. Throughput can be increased by data-independent-acquisition (DIA) using short separation times and by multiplexing samples in the mass domain with plexDIA; yet multiplexing along one dimension scales throughput only linearly with plex. To enable combinatorial scaling of proteomics throughput, we developed a complementary DIA strategy that multiplexes samples in the time domain, termed `timePlex'. timePlex staggers and overlaps the separation periods of individual samples. This strategy is orthogonal to isotopic multiplexing, which enables combinatorial multiplexing in mass and time domains, and thus multiplicatively increased throughput. We demonstrate this with a 27-plex (3-timePlex and 9-plexDIA) exceeding 1,200 samples (4M protein datapoints) per day. These results establish timePlex as a framework for multiplexing both label-free and labeled samples that supports sensitive and accurate protein quantification and combinatorial scaling.

cards.title: An Integrated Experimental and Informatics Strategy Enables Large Proteoform Identification in Top-Down Proteomics
cards.abstract: Top-down proteomics enables identification and characterization of intact proteoforms, preserving information on co-occurring sequence variations and post-translational modifications. However, identifying large proteoforms remains challenging due to an exponential decrease in signal-to-noise ratio with increasing molecular weight, interference from coeluting smaller species, unresolved precursor isotopic envelopes, difficulty obtaining informative MS/MS spectra, and limitations of current informatics tools. To address these challenges, here we present an integrated experimental and informatics strategy combining protein separation, data acquisition, precursor mass assignment, and MS/MS interpretation. First, we demonstrate that online two-dimensional liquid chromatography coupling size-exclusion and reversed-phase separations enables facile detection of large proteoforms. We then utilize a precursor mass correction strategy to enable conventional database searching of data-dependent acquisition (DDA) data containing isotopically unresolved precursors. Finally, we use data-independent acquisition (DIA) optimized for large proteins to enhance fragment signal and enable identification through intact-mass-guided candidate discovery and MS/MS validation. Applied to human heart tissue, the integrated strategy identified 703 nonredundant proteoforms from 236 unique proteins, including 65 proteins >30 kDa and 22 proteins >50 kDa, with identifications extending to 223 kDa. This integrated strategy bridges the detection-to-identification gap for large proteins and expands the accessible mass range of discovery top-down proteomics.

cards.title: The Findings Workflow: An agentic, collaborative, provenance-tracked framework for scientific data analysis with Claude Code
cards.abstract: Scientists presented with quantitative data often face two related problems: confidence that an analysis is statistically and computationally correct, and provenance sufficient to reproduce the resulting figures and conclusions. Large language models (LLMs) can make sophisticated analyses accessible through a collaborative, conversational interface, but unstructured use can worsen both problems by producing plausible but incorrect results and obscuring the steps that produced them. Here we present the Findings Workflow, a free, open-source Claude Code plugin designed to retain the flexibility of conversational LLM-assisted analysis while placing it within a structured, verifiable, and reproducible environment. The workflow uses staged, gated progression to ensure the science, metadata, and data are understood and tested data loaders are built before downstream analysis begins. Specialized subagents perform statistical analysis, programming, visualization, research, reporting, and validation, with independent review incorporated throughout. The plugin also provides vetted analysis templates, conventions, and methodological guidance that serve as trusted sources of opinion when deciding how analyses should be performed. Scientists remain actively involved throughout, exploring their data and directing the analysis through natural-language conversation, while the workflow supplies structure, verification, and persistent state around that collaboration. Findings are recorded automatically together with the data, code, methods, figures, and provenance needed to reproduce them. We demonstrate the workflow with a worked example that reproduces central findings from a published plasma extracellular vesicle proteomics dataset examining Alzheimer's disease (Mag-Net). Together, these features are designed to make LLM-assisted scientific analysis easier to trust, inspect, and reproduce without sacrificing its conversational and exploratory nature.

cards.title: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling.
cards.abstract: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

cards.title: Dietary fibre responses emerge through host-dietary regime interplay: Apple pectin modulates immune reactivity in adult zebrafish
cards.abstract: Dietary fibres are rarely consumed independently. Instead, they form part of an overall diet that includes dietary fibres from different sources, in varying amounts and consumed under different feeding patterns. Here, we tested how dietary regimes containing apple pectin, oat {beta}-glucan, or cellulose shaped the host. We analysed gut microbiome composition by 16S rRNA sequencing, measured brain and intestinal SCFA profiles by targeted metabolomics, and assessed immunomodulation by measuring gene expression systemically in the blood and locally in the spleen, as well as intestinal enzyme activity. The dietary intervention was conducted for 12 weeks on adult female and male zebrafish (Danio rerio). Our results show that the gut microbial composition can be relatively stable across different dietary fibre exposure patterns yet still vary significantly between the sexes. Additionally, the effect of sex on the gut microbiome may become more evident when dietary fibres are administered at high dosages, but intermittently. Dietary fibre regimes can alter intestinal short-chain fatty acid profiles more readily than brain profiles, which show a stronger sexually dimorphic response. Interestingly, apple pectin modulated the zebrafish immune response through interactions dependent on the overall regime, tissue, sex, and host immune status. Notably, tissue il1b gene expression differed depending on how apple pectin was administered and the host's physiological state. Collectively, our study emphasises the highly context-specific effects of dietary fibres, shaped by the dynamic interplay between the overall dietary regime and intertwined host factors.

cards.title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
cards.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness. In antibody sequencing, it improved recovery of peptides spanning the variable-constant boundary, deamidation calls, and assembly, while preserving recall of hypervariable regions inaccessible to database search. Peptide priors thus bring reference knowledge into DNPS without limiting discovery.

cards.title: Self-reported geriatric impairments and treatment toxicity in older patients with multiple myeloma.
cards.abstract: Frailty influences treatment outcomes in older patients with multiple myeloma (MM), yet existing frailty tools capture limited geriatric domains and are incompletely studied in the context of contemporary therapies. We prospectively evaluated patient-reported comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) domains and their associations with treatment toxicity and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) in older adults with MM. Patients aged ≥60 years with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory MM initiating a new therapy completed electronic CGA and PRO questionnaires at baseline and 4 months. Outcomes included clinician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity, treatment adaptations, health care use, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). A cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) was derived from CGA and HRQOL domains. Among 90 patients (mean age, 72 years), geriatric impairments were common, particularly physical function domains. High-grade nonhematologic toxicities were significantly associated with older age, comorbidities, patient-reported functional limitations, and anxiety. Toxicity rates on the PRO version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) were higher than on CTCAE, highlighting a discordance between physician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity. Frailty was present in 22% and associated with worse baseline HRQOL and increased high-grade nonhematologic toxicity but not treatment adaptations or health care use. Average CGA and HRQOL scores remained stable over 4 months, although individual trajectories varied. Patient-reported geriatric impairments are prevalent in older adults with MM and strongly associated with nonhematologic toxicities even in the contemporary treatment era. Physician-reported CTCAE may not fully reflect patients' symptom burden. Heterogeneity in individual geriatric trajectories during treatment emphasize the need for longitudinal assessment. This study was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05918185.

cards.title: The aging secretome as a candidate driver of bone remodeling imbalance: myokines, adipokines, and senescence-associated secretory factors
cards.abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on the spatial and temporal coupling of osteoclastic resorption to osteoblastic formation. With aging, this balance shifts toward net bone loss alongside sarcopenia, marrow adipose expansion, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These parallel changes may be linked by a shared set of secreted signals, termed here the aging secretome. We distinguish functional remodeling imbalance, defined as a sustained shift between formation and resorption, from direct uncoupling, in which a resorption-to-formation coupling signal is demonstrably disrupted. The aging secretome comprises three principal arms: muscle-derived signals, including myostatin, irisin, and myogenic extracellular vesicles; fat-derived signals, including leptin, adiponectin, and marrow adipocyte lipotoxicity; and senescence-associated secretory factors, particularly those involving senescent osteocytes, TNF-α, and IL-6. Inflammaging is treated as a shared contextual amplifier rather than a separate signaling arm. These pathways converge on key regulators of skeletal remodeling, including RANKL, Wnt–sclerostin, and IGF-1. This framework also provides a common context for comparing pathway-specific interventions, such as activin type II receptor blockade and sclerostin inhibition, with broader approaches targeting senescence or inflammation. An early phase 2 senolytic trial was negative overall, with only an exploratory signal in women with high senescent-cell burden. The aging secretome should therefore be viewed as an organizing framework whose individual pathways and relative contributions require further validation in human bone.

cards.title: Prognostic associations between patient-reported outcomes and progression-free and overall survival in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%: results from the RATIONALE-305 trial.
cards.abstract: In RATIONALE-305, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival (OS) versus placebo plus chemotherapy in advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC) with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor area positivity (TAP) score ≥ 5% and in all patients. Here, we present a three-component joint model (JM) developed to evaluate associations between patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and risk of progression-free survival (PFS) and OS events. Longitudinal PRO data were analyzed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22. The JM linked: (1) a linear mixed model (LMM) for change from baseline in PRO scores; (2) a Cox model for time to recurrent symptomatic deterioration (RS-D); and (3) a Cox model to evaluate the RS-D event frailty prediction of PFS and OS. 475 patients in the PD-L1 ≥ 5% subgroup (tislelizumab + chemotherapy, n = 238; placebo + chemotherapy, n = 237) were evaluated. In PFS and OS LMMs, tislelizumab + chemotherapy versus placebo + chemotherapy was associated with improved GHS/QoL (global health status/quality of life) (p = 0.01) and reduced dietary restrictions (p = 0.05). In the OS LMM, tislelizumab + chemotherapy was associated with reduced upper GI symptoms (p = 0.01) and reductions in dietary restrictions (p = 0.02). RS-D in GHS/QoL, pain, and dietary restrictions were leading predictors of PFS risk. Across all QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22 domains, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly reduced the risk of progression or death (PFS HRs 0.55-0.65; 35-45% reduction) and death (OS HRs 0.65-0.73; 27-35% reduction); all p ≤ 0.01. PROs have significant prognostic value for disease progression and survival in patients with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%. NCT03777657 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov ).

cards.title: AltORF-encoded microprotein recruits primary-ORF-encoded dehydrogenase to cell poles upon heat shock
cards.abstract: Alternative open reading frames (altORFs) initiating from in-frame or out-of-frame start sites within annotated protein-coding genes represent a largely unexplored source of protein-coding potential and remain poorly understood in terms of regulation, function, and impact on physiology. Here we investigate Escherichia coli GndA, encoded by an out-of-frame altORF within gnd, which encodes 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase. We observe that the GndA protein is induced by heat shock, consistent with the initial identification in a quantitative membrane proteomics screen, but is unstable, while the levels of the stable Gnd dehydrogenase are unchanged. Using translational fusion assays and in vivo RNA structure probing, we show that an internal complementary sequence upstream of gndA acts as a thermo-responsive secondary RNA structure controlling GndA translation. Mutagenesis of either gnd or gndA reduce heat shock survival of E. coli indicating both gene products are important for resistance. GndA fractionates with membranes consistent with in silico predictions that the protein forms an amphipathic -helix. In contrast, Gnd is predominantly cytoplasmic but shows GndA-dependent relocalization to cell poles upon heat shock. Together, our results demonstrate that an altORF-encoded microprotein is required for stress-dependent relocalization of its primary ORF partner, revealing a functional interplay between proteins encoded by overlapping ORFs in bacterial stress adaptation.

cards.title: In-silico Tandem Mass Spectral Libraries for the Blood Exposome and Metabolomics Workbench Databases: Application of Gemini Large Language Model
cards.abstract: Human body contains endogenous metabolites, nutrients and xenobiotics chemicals. These chemicals can be detected in a biospecimen using high-resolution mass spectrometry instruments, yielding metabolomic and exposomic datasets. Mass spectral libraries are critical components of these workflows to annotate experimental data with chemical information. In this data descriptor, we report mass spectral libraries for human-relevant small molecules, that are generated using Google Gemini large-language model. Using an optimized chain-of-thought prompt and instructions, we have generated mass spectra for each compound at high/medium/low energy fragmentation level. Each spectrum was reported in the NIST MSP text format for easy to use by metabolomics software. These libraries cover 91,231 unique 2D structures from the Blood Exposome Database and the Metabolomics Workbench data repository. Technical validation was shown by comparing the Gemini-generated spectra against NIST 23 mass spectral database, which demonstrated 55% accuracy. LLMs represent a useful and accessible tool for expanding in-silico spectral libraries to annotate compounds in the HRMS data for human biospecimens and may accelerate the compound annotation in metabolomics and exposomics.
