cards.title: Increased EV yield and bioactivity of matrix-bound nanovesicles compared to conditioned culture medium-derived extracellular vesicles
cards.abstract: Aim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoparticles secreted by cells for cell-cell communication functions, such as wound repair, but low yields often limit their use. Several isolation methods have been explored to increase EV yield from conditioned culture medium (liquid-EVs); however, few studies compare isolation techniques and yield between liquid-EVs and matrix-bound nanovesicles (MBVs), a novel EV subtype embedded within the extracellular matrix. Methods: We isolate liquid-EVs and MBVs from mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) using size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and ultracentrifugation (UC) across various timepoints (14, 21, 24, 30 days). EVs are characterized by their yield, size, morphology, protein concentration, surface marker expression (CD9, CD81, ALIX), zeta potential, and influence on fibroblast wound closure. Results: We find that isolation method influences yield, where both SEC isolated liquid-EVs and MBVs yield higher particle counts and protein compared to UC. Interestingly, we find that regardless of isolation method, MBVs have a significantly higher yield than liquid-EVs from the same culture (15.6-fold higher using UC and 7.49-fold higher using SEC). Culturing for 24 days yielded the greatest number of MBV particles and protein. We performed a fibroblast scratch assay to assess bioactivity and found that liquid-EVs decreased wound closure compared to a medium control, whereas MBVs did not. Conclusion: Our work suggests SEC maximizes particle and protein yields for MSC-EVs. By achieving much higher yields of MBVs compared to liquid-EVs, and their promise as a wound repair strategy, we offer an alternative EV choice when EV yields are an issue towards translation.

cards.title: Mouse Neural Organoids Model the Mature In Vivo Synaptic Proteome
cards.abstract: Neural organoids represent a promising approach for modelling neural circuits and neurological disease, yet their utility depends on whether they can recapitulate the molecular complexity of mature brain synapses. Here, we optimized a protocol to generate mature forebrain organoids from mouse embryonic stem cells and used time-resolved proteomics to define the emergence of synaptic proteins during maturation. Using fluorescence-activated synaptosome sorting coupled with mass spectrometry, we quantified the synapse-enriched proteome and found a high correlation with matched in vivo synaptic proteomes. These findings demonstrate that complex mature synaptic molecular architecture is present within an in vitro organoid environment.

cards.title: Combined Anterior-Posterior vs. Posterior-Only Fusion in Adult Spinal Deformity Radiographic, Clinical, and Mechanical Outcomes With Longitudinal Mixed-Effects Analysis.
cards.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo compare radiographic, clinical, and mechanical outcomes of posterior-only versus combined anterior-posterior fusion in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients undergoing long-segment thoracolumbar fusion with pelvic fixation.MethodsConsecutive ASD patients undergoing instrumented fusion ≥7 levels with pelvic fixation at a single center (2016-2023) were stratified by surgical approach. Longitudinal radiographic changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation. Mechanical complications were evaluated with Kaplan-Meier survival and Cox proportional hazards analysis.Results207 patients were included (posterior-only, n=115; combined, n=92). Mean age was 62.1 ± 11.1 years (77.8% female), with mean follow-up of 46.2 ± 21.2 months. The combined approach demonstrated significantly greater DiD estimates for lumbar lordosis (-7.8° to -9.2°, all p<0.001), relative pelvic version mismatch (+3.4° to +4.2°, all p<0.001), and GAP score (-1.8 to -2.1, all p<0.001) at all postoperative timepoints. DiD estimates were stable across three covariate specifications. Rod fractures occurred in 14.8% of posterior-only versus 3.3% of combined patients (p=0.008), with superior rod fracture-free survival in the combined cohort (log-rank p=0.019). In the primary Cox model, the combined approach showed a non-significant trend toward lower rod fracture hazard (HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.10-1.24, p=0.10). Patient-reported outcomes improved comparably in both groups.ConclusionsIn long-segment ASD fusion with pelvic fixation, the combined anterior-posterior approach was associated with greater sustained sagittal correction and lower rod fracture rates, while both approaches provided comparable clinical improvement.

cards.title: Chemical proteomics suggests sofosbuvir is metabolically attached to proteins through a UMPylation-like pathway.
cards.abstract: Sofosbuvir is a pronucleotide prodrug (ProTide) that releases a uridine monophosphate analogue, which could modify proteins chemically or through UMP-transferring enzymes. Using an alkyne-tagged probe and chemical proteomics, we identified about 120 labelled proteins and a UMPylation-like (+774.31 Da) modification on cathepsin Z, suggesting that nucleotide prodrugs may enter protein nucleotidylation pathways.

cards.title: ChEBI-N - Enrichment Analysis with the ChEBI Ontology
cards.abstract: Introduction: Biological and chemical ontologies are structured representations that can be used to map entities such as metabolites onto broader chemical and biological categories. Enrichment analysis applied to such ontologies identifies classes whose representation within a set deviates from an expected background distribution, helping to interpret complex metabolomics measurements. Objectives: This study aimed to develop a tool for ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) ontology-based enrichment analysis, named ChEBI-N (ChEBI eNrichment). It is a successor of the previous tool BiNChE, with new features that broaden its applicability. Methods: We reimplemented BiNChE and extended it to accept SMILES or InChI strings as well as ChEBI IDs. These broaden applicability to datasets with entities that are not yet present in ChEBI. We also constructed organism-specific background populations. Results: We demonstrate the tool on three published metabolomics datasets covering wine, cheese, and human plasma samples. ChEBI-N correctly highlighted relevant enriched classes in all three datasets, such as flavonoids in the wine dataset and fatty acid classes in the cheese dataset. Comparing organism-specific and full-ChEBI backgrounds shows that restricted backgrounds reduce the inflated significance of generic classes, although the most enriched classes remain largely consistent. Conclusion: ChEBI-N is an extended successor to BiNChE for ontology-based enrichment analysis of metabolomics data, offering a hypothesis-generating complement to existing metabolomics analysis pipelines. Availability: ChEBI-N is freely available at chebin.hastingslab.org or as a Python package (pypi.org/project/chebin), with source code at github.com/ontology-tools/chebin, archived at Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23264219) and Software Heritage (swh:1:rev:133a41792704eb7f1db746f36a5ae97e9247b2b7).

cards.title: Predictors of Interfacility Transfer in Head and Neck Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Study.
cards.abstract: Traumatic head and neck (H/N) injuries frequently present to level III/IV trauma centers, yet many require care available only at higher-level facilities. This study aims to characterize transfer patterns in H/N trauma patients initially treated at level III/IV centers. The National Trauma Data Bank was queried for adults with H/N trauma initially presenting to level III/IV trauma centers between 2007 and 2015. Univariate analysis compared cohort characteristics, while multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors of transfer. In total, 18,454 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 5923 (32.1%) were transferred. Cut/piercing and striking injuries were associated with greater transfer odds (aOR: 1.328, 1.653), while motor vehicle trauma was associated with decreased odds (aOR: 0.845, 95% CI: 0.763-0.937). Transfer was associated with jaw dislocation (aOR: 1.871, 95% CI: 1.228-2.852) and H/N burns (aOR: 8.832, 95% CI: 7.131-10.940). Mandibular (aOR: 2.53, 95% CI: 2.19-2.93), skull base (aOR: 1.379, 95% CI 1.229-1.547), and malar/maxillary fractures (aOR: 1.314, 95% CI: 1.163-1.486) increased transfer odds, while nasal bone fracture decreased odds (aOR: 0.817, 95% CI: 0.741-0.901). Isolated H/N injury increased transfer odds (aOR: 1.379, 95% CI: 1.247-1.526). Transferred cohorts most commonly underwent diagnostic imaging and simple bedside procedures prior to transfer. Interfacility transfer is driven primarily by injury patterns rather than physiologic instability, likely reflecting anticipated need for subspecialty surgical intervention. Understanding injury-specific transfer predictors may optimize trauma systems and resource utilization while ensuring timely specialized care.

cards.title: Cost Analysis of Maxillofacial Trauma Treatment in Three Major Ministry of Health Malaysia Hospitals.
cards.abstract: Maxillofacial trauma imposes a considerable burden on healthcare systems. The Facial Injury Severity Scale (FISS) may help to estimate treatment complexity and healthcare resource requirements. However, evidence regarding its relationship with treatment costs and resource utilization in Malaysian public hospitals remains limited. To evaluate the relationship between FISS scores, treatment costs, and healthcare resource utilization among maxillofacial trauma patients treated in Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) hospitals. A retrospective multicenter cohort study included 132 adult patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) for maxillofacial fractures between January and December 2022 in 3 MOH hospitals. FISS scores were characterized as low (1-5), moderate (6-10), and high (>10) severity groups. Healthcare resource utilization was assessed using operating theatre (OT) duration, length of stay (LOS), and treatment cost. Treatment costs were estimated from the healthcare provider's perspective using a combination of activity-based and top-down costing approaches. Unadjusted differences across FISS groups were evaluated, and multivariable-adjusted general linear models were used to examine associations between FISS severity groups and each outcome after adjustment for age, gender, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), study site, and injury-to-OT time. Increasing FISS severity was associated with significantly longer OT duration (118 versus 135 versus 162 min; P<0.001), prolonged LOS (4 d versus 4 d versus 9 d; P=0.048), and higher treatment costs (RM 6564.47 versus RM 8065.28 versus RM 9830.90; P=0.003). After adjustment for age, gender, GCS, study site, and injury-to-OT time, significant differences across FISS categories remained for OT duration (P=0.001) and treatment cost (P=0.001), whereas the association with LOS was no longer statistically significant (P=0.201). Adjusted mean OT duration increased from 145.42 minutes in the low-FISS group to 220.94 minutes in the high-FISS group, while adjusted mean treatment cost increased from RM 7158.23 to RM 9552.91. The mean treatment cost per patient was RM 7592.43 ± 2364.14 (USD 1807.72 ± 562.89). Plating and screw costs (28.97%) and personnel costs (20.44%) were the largest contributors to treatment expenditure, while the operating theatre accounted for 60.18% of the total cost. Higher FISS scores were associated with greater healthcare resource utilization and treatment costs among maxillofacial trauma patients treated in MOH hospitals. After adjustment for relevant and institutional factors, higher FISS severity remained significantly associated with longer operative duration and higher treatment cost, whereas the association with LOS was attenuated. These findings support the potential use of FISS as a practical indicator of operative resource requirements and treatment expenditure in maxillofacial trauma care.

cards.title: A Tissue Virus Microenvironment with Activated Stress Responses Underlies Durable SIV Persistence
cards.abstract: HIV persistence during suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART) remains a central barrier to cure, with the majority of reservoirs residing in gut-associated lymphoid tissues (GALT). Here, we define a spatially organized viral microenvironment (VME) that sustains reservoir durability and governs early viral rebound by comparing animals initiating ART early after infection (transient reservoirs) versus late (persistent reservoirs). Using immunoPET/CT-guided sampling of SIV-infected rhesus macaques combined with spatial transcriptomics, we interrogated tissue sites of viral production during the eclipse phase following analytical treatment interruption (ATI). Our results revealed that viral rebound from persistent reservoirs arises from discrete, transcriptionally active foci enriched in the mucosa lining the gut lumen. Eclipse phase persistent reservoirs were characterized by increased proviral burden and a distinct tissue state marked by activation of stress-response, metabolic, mitochondrial, and cell cycle programs coupled to repression of cytoplasmic translation and increased cellular senescence. These features co-occurred with immunosuppressive cellular architectures resembling tertiary lymphoid structures enriched for Treg cells, innate lymphoid cells, and mast cells, regulated by Treg-centered cell-cell interaction networks. In contrast, transient reservoirs displayed enhanced translational and metabolic activity and were embedded within immune-active environments enriched for CD8+ T cells, Th17, Tfh, and activated CD4+ T cells. Machine learning identified stress adaptation, hypoxia, metabolic rewiring, and cytoskeletal remodeling pathways as dominant predictors of viral density within persistent VMEs, with strong convergence on programs observed in tumor microenvironments (TME). Orthogonal validation confirmed activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) at sites of viral production in concurrence with results of immunofluorescent microscopy revealing SIV gag expression in two populations primarily in the mucosa, differentiated by the phosphorylation of eIF2alpha. Together, these findings establish the VME as a critical determinant of reservoir persistence, integrating immune regulation, tissue remodeling, and translational control to enable viral survival. This framework suggests that effective HIV cure strategies will require coordinated disruption of VME-supportive functions in addition to targeting infected cells.

cards.title: WISER: spectral whitening of fixed effects for improved breeding value estimation in structured, unbalanced, and genotype-environment-confounded populations
cards.abstract: This work introduces WISER (whitening and successive least squares estimation refinement), a whitening-based method designed to improve breeding value (BV) estimation by accounting for population structure and genetic covariance within experimental designs. WISER provides a generalized framework applicable across diverse experimental designs, species, and omics datasets, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), metabolomics, and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) used as phenomic predictors. Central to WISER is whitening, a statistical transformation that decorrelates variables and standardizes their variances. From a spectral perspective, WISER reweights the fixed-effect design according to the eigenspectrum of the genetic covariance matrix, attenuating dominant directions of genetic variation rather than explicitly correcting for a predefined subset of eigenvectors. This transformation aims to reduce confounding between genetic structure and environmental effects during BV estimation. WISER was evaluated across four species and 33 traits, including rice, maize, apple, and Scots pine, using several genomic prediction models and was compared with LS-means and BLUP-based BV estimation. Genomic predictive abilities based on WISER-estimated BVs consistently exceeded those obtained with LS-means and BLUP across the predictive models evaluated. These results support WISER as a flexible framework for BV estimation and downstream omics-based prediction in structured and unbalanced experimental populations. cards.title: Ctcf deficiency in myofibers induces pathological genome reprogramming toward the spontaneous development of myopathy
cards.abstract: How perennial, postmitotic multinucleated tissues, such as skeletal myofibers, maintain their identity and transcriptional adaptation to homeostatic perturbations through adult life is an outstanding question. To address this issue, we investigated the consequences of loss of 3D-genome architecture in skeletal muscles by generating myofiber-specific Ctcf-deficient (CtcfmKO) mice. CtcfmKO mice did not exhibit muscular phenotype at birth but spontaneously developed a severe myopathy. Integrated analysis of snRNAseq, ATACseq and promoter-capture Hi-C revealed both common and fiber-type specific patterns of dysregulated gene expression associated with alterations in chromatin accessibility and promoter-based interactions in Ctcf-deficient myonuclei at distinct stages of myopathy development. Decreased chromatin accessibility at promoters and changes in their connectivity with distal elements were observed across all myonuclei as a direct consequence of Ctcf deficiency at early stages and associated with downregulation of genes implicated in myofiber contraction and anabolism, metabolism, adhesion and neuromuscular transmission. Conversely, at later stages, upregulation of genes leading to persistent activation of ER stress/UPR and catabolism resulted from global reconfiguration of chromatin structure and connectivity, partly as indirect consequence of Ctcf deficiency. Notably, type-IIB myonuclei exhibited specific alterations in gene expression that culminated in loss of fiber-type identity and ectopic expression of inflammatory genes. These results reveal a requirement of Ctcf for maintenance of fiber-type identity and transcriptional adaptation in vivo, through multilayered control of 3D genome integrity. They also indicate an unprecedented association between Ctcf deficiency in myofibers and susceptibility to develop myopathies, whereby Ctcf dispensability for developmental myogenesis confers vulnerability to develop myopathic syndromes.

cards.title: Comment on "Inpatient mortality following hip fracture in the United States: an updated analysis of over one million cases".
cards.abstract: This commentary examines the statistical and methodological limitations of a recent national analysis of inpatient hip fracture mortality using the Epic Cosmos database. Four concerns are raised. First, the reported Spearman correlation between a four-category Social Vulnerability Index and mortality lacked statistical power because it was calculated across only four aggregated data points, and collapsing a continuous index into ordinal bins discarded patient-level variation needed to detect a dose-response relationship. Second, do-not-resuscitate status, documented in over one-third of patients, was omitted from the analysis of racial mortality differences, despite its direct influence on in-hospital mortality timing and its potential to confound comparisons unrelated to surgical risk. Third, the regional analysis reported the distribution of deaths across regions rather than region-specific mortality rates, conflating hospital volume with mortality risk. These limitations should be addressed before the reported demographic and regional patterns are used to guide resource allocation or clinical practice.

cards.title: Probabilistic forecasting of prefecture-level influenza in Japan accounting for surveillance data release histories
cards.abstract: Background. Public-health use of influenza surveillance - situational awareness, planning for clinical surge, and issuing advisories or warnings - needs more than an accurate point estimate of next week's count. What matters operationally is whether a rise is caught early, whether the direction of change is right, and whether an alert threshold is about to be crossed, all with honest uncertainty. For such use a forecast must also respect reporting delay, later data revision, and the calibration of its prediction intervals. Using Japan's sentinel surveillance, we evaluated short-term probabilistic forecasts that respect the data release history, and we measured what adding other surveillance series contributes, focusing on the properties that matter for public-health decisions. Methods. The target was the number of influenza reports per sentinel site in each of the 47 prefectures. For each forecast we predicted, as quantiles, the value 1-4 weeks after the most recent observed week. We compared three models: a ridge regression trained jointly across prefectures; a gradient-boosting quantile regression (GBQR) that learns from many surveillance series; and their equal-weight combination on the log scale. Six seasons were used to develop the models. The 2025/26 season was held out as a temporal evaluation period after the specification was fixed; because its epidemic profile had already been seen, it is not a fully independent prospective test. We scored forecasts with the weighted interval score (WIS) and checked prediction-interval coverage. For the Japanese target series we used the value first published for each week; some auxiliary series were taken as retrieved and therefore include later revisions. Results. In 2025/26, the combination's WIS relative to a persistence forecast was 0.841, 0.811, 0.794 and 0.818 at horizons of 1-4 observed weeks - that is, 16-21% lower than persistence. Coverage of the 80% prediction interval was 79.7%, 77.1%, 74.5% and 75.1%, and of the 95% interval 94.3%, 93.4%, 92.6% and 91.8%. Adding auxiliary series improved the GBQR over the development period. However, on the original scale the combination's edge over ridge regression was not statistically clear, and in some low-level rising phases the combination did worse than ridge. Conclusions. Over the period studied, models that share information across regions scored better than a persistence forecast. For public-health use, however, the operative questions are the real lead time once reporting delay is accounted for, whether rises from low levels and threshold exceedances are caught in time, and whether the upper prediction intervals are wide enough; on these, the present evidence is not yet sufficient. The 2025 change to the sentinel system also means that pre-change advisory and warning thresholds cannot be read mechanically. A prospective evaluation with strictly controlled data availability is needed before such forecasts are used to support advisories or planning.

cards.title: Mutation in Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum F1C1 cytochrome p450 homologue impairs virulence through root but not through shoot of tomato plants
cards.abstract: Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum causes a lethal bacterial wilt disease in many plants. The pathogen enters through roots and systemically colonizes the xylem tissue, resulting in wilting and eventual death of the host. Using transposon mutagenesis followed by screening in tomato seedlings, we identified a mutant exhibiting virulence deficiency by root inoculation, but not by leaf inoculation. The mutation was recreated in the wild-type genome via natural transformation to prove the linkage of virulence deficiency with the transposon insertion. Whole genome sequencing revealed that the transposon insertion was in a cyp450 homologue, encoding cytochrome P450 monooxygenase. Two independent targeted mutations were generated in the cyp450 gene, and both the mutants recapitulated the root-specific virulence deficiency. The mutants rarely cause disease in mature plants following soil drenching but remained fully virulent upon petiole pricking inoculation. Complementation with the full length cyp450 gene amplified from the wild-type strain F1C1 restored virulence in the mutant. Compared to the wild-type F1C1, the cyp450 mutants exhibited greater sensitivity to tomato root extracts. HR-LCMS of tomato root extracts revealed the occurrence of several antimicrobial compounds. Cytochrome P450 enzymes are known to mediate the degradation or biosynthesis of diverse metabolites in bacteria. Considering the virulence difference due to the mode of inoculation, our findings indicate that cyp450 contributes to tissue-specific adaptation of the pathogen during infection has opened an avenue for integrating tissue metabolomics with bacterial wilt susceptibility research.

cards.title: Delayed Multi-Compartment Traumatic Hernias After Blunt Abdominal Trauma: A Case-Based Review of Diagnosis and Staged Management.
cards.abstract: BackgroundTraumatic diaphragmatic hernias (TDHs) and traumatic abdominal wall hernias (TAWHs) are uncommon sequelae of blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) and may be missed during the initial evaluation. Delayed presentation can occur months to years later, resulting in incarceration, obstruction, or respiratory compromise.Case PresentationA 61-year-old woman presented 1 year after a motor vehicle collision with abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, and dyspnea. Computed tomography demonstrated an incarcerated left diaphragmatic hernia containing colon and omentum, along with a right flank hernia containing ascending colon. Review of prior imaging revealed a flank hematoma and subtle abdominal wall disruption at the time of initial injury. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic repair of the diaphragmatic hernia followed by elective robotic transabdominal preperitoneal repair of the flank hernia 2 months later.DiscussionThis case illustrates a pattern of delayed multi-compartment traumatic herniation resulting from thoracoabdominal force transmission. Diagnostic delays may occur because of competing priorities during polytrauma management, limitations of initial imaging, and delayed development of herniation, especially when the injuries are subtle. Findings such as rib fractures, pneumothorax, abdominal wall hematoma, and persistent symptoms should prompt continued surveillance.ConclusionDelayed multi-compartment traumatic hernias represent a diagnostic challenge requiring a high index of suspicion, longitudinal surveillance, and individualized management. A staged operative approach based on symptom severity and anatomic location can effectively address differing levels of clinical urgency.

cards.title: An integrated experimental-computational framework for elasto-plastic characterization and spatial mapping of canine bone properties.
cards.abstract: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental-computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load-displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

cards.title: Pediatric emergency medicine in Lebanon: Physician-perceived comfort levels, challenges, and educational needs.
cards.abstract: Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) is a rapidly evolving subspecialty that improves the quality and safety of care for children. Despite global advancements, PEM remains underdeveloped in many low- and middle-income countries, including Lebanon. Despite a large pediatric population there is no formal paediatric emergency medicine system in place, and care largely delivered by physicians practicing without standardized or specialized training. This lack of dedicated PEM training and organized emergency care pathways may compromise the timely recognition and management of pediatric emergencies, potentially affecting patient outcomes. The present study aimed to assess physicians perceived comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, identify training gaps, and explore systemic and institutional challenges affecting pediatric emergency care in Lebanon. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians involved in pediatric emergency care across Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed self-reported comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, perceived challenges, and priorities for training and PEM workforce development. Responses from 59 physicians were analysed. Most were male 38 (64.4%), with a median clinical experience of 7 years. General pediatricians represented 28 (47.5%), emergency physicians 17 (28.8%), PEM specialists 8 (13.6%), and pediatric intensivists 6 (10.2%). Physicians reported high perceived comfort in pediatric fluid management 52(88.1%), chest X-ray interpretation 46 (77.9%), and general pediatric emergencies 42 (71.2%), but lower comfort in procedural sedation, suturing 35 (59.6%), fracture stabilization 35 (59.4%), and Extended Focused Assessment Sonography in Trauma (EFAST) 22 (41.8%). General pediatricians reported greater comfort with general pediatric emergencies, while emergency-focused physicians had higher comfort with trauma-related skills and procedural interventions. Major challenges included gaps in practical and theoretical training, limited hospital infrastructure, shortages of devices and human resources, and the need for continuing medical education. Nearly all participants 57 (96.6%) supported the establishing a dedicated PEM fellowship, highlighting training priorities in trauma, medical emergencies, life support, procedural skills, and pediatric imaging. Pediatric emergency care in Lebanon is constrained by gaps in skills, training, and systemic resources. There is an urgent need to establish standardized PEM training pathways, enhance curricula, and strengthen system-level preparedness. Implementing these measures will support a competent PEM workforce and improve the quality and safety of emergency care for children nationwide.

cards.title: Examining the patient- and system-related forces influencing the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe: Findings from an ethnographic study.
cards.abstract: Rapidly rising longevity and the projected increase in fractures among older adults in Southern Africa underscores the necessity to strengthen healthcare systems in the region. Delivering orthopaedic care to older people within a multi-disciplinary framework is widely recommended. This ethnographic study sought to examine the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe and the influence of patient- and system-related forces We used ethnographic methods to examine the experiences of patients and caregivers and characterise hip fracture care provision. Case studies were undertaken with 40 patients (22 male, 18 female) and 33 caregivers (6 male, 27 female), including family members and friends. These data were complemented by interviews and observations of clinical practice with 42 healthcare professionals (23 female, 19 male) involved in the delivery of hip fracture services, including orthopaedic surgeons, physicians and physiotherapists. Participants were purposively sampled from six hospitals providing hip fracture care across Northern Zimbabwe. Snowball sampling was also used to recruit additional study participants. Data were analysed using an abductive analytical approach. Patients' and caregivers' experiences revealed lengthy hospital stays, poor communication concerning diagnosis and treatment, undignified continence management, and limited access to social support. Patients' experiences highlighted the importance of access to pain relief medication, and the impact of unaffordable care - elements distinct from those within current responsiveness frameworks. Health professionals explained how resource constraints, understaffing, and changes in pain management processes impacted their ability to meet patients' needs. Yet, their narratives told of the various actions they employed to circumvent health system constraints and respond to patient priorities. Considering these findings, we highlight key considerations for health systems responsiveness, including considering the role of socioeconomic factors. We also propose practical recommendations for improving responsive hip fracture care in Zimbabwe, such as developing guidelines for patient optimisation and standardisation of hip implant costs.

cards.title: Targeting the gut-bone axis in osteoporosis: probiotic interventions and other microbiota-based therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic bone metabolic disorder characterized by impaired bone homeostasis and increased fracture susceptibility. With the rapid aging of the global population, the number of fractures related to osteoporosis continues to increase, along with persistently high rates of disability and mortality, thereby imposing a huge and constantly growing burden on the healthcare system. Emerging evidence indicates that probiotics, as key regulators of host metabolic and immune networks, play critical roles in the pathogenesis, progression, and therapeutic modulation of OP. Through a bidirectional regulatory network known as the gut-bone axis, probiotics influence the dynamic balance between bone formation and bone resorption via multiple interconnected mechanisms, including immune modulation, microbial metabolite production, intestinal barrier integrity, and endocrine signaling. Recent animal and clinical studies further demonstrate that targeted modulation of the gut microbiota to restore gut-bone axis homeostasis can significantly improve bone mineral density and related skeletal parameters, highlighting the translational potential of probiotic-based interventions. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which probiotics regulate bone metabolism and places particular emphasis on emerging microbiota-based mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, with a specific focus on probiotics, aiming to provide a theoretical framework and future translational directions for the development of innovative microbiota-based treatments for OP.

cards.title: Osteoporosis medication initiation after proximal humerus fractures is low, but associated with decreased secondary fragility fracture risk.
cards.abstract: To 1) identify factors associated with osteoporosis medication (OPM) prescription after proximal humerus fractures and 2) evaluate rates of secondary osteoporotic fragility fracture (OFF) between patients treated with OPM vs those who were not. Retrospective cohort analysis. TriNetX Health Research Network. Patients aged 60 years or older who sustained a proximal humerus fracture (PHF) (OTA/AO 11) between 2005 and 2025 were categorized into groups based on if they were or were not prescribed OPM within 1 year after a PHF. The primary outcome was prescription of OPM after PHF. Patient demographics were assessed between patients who were or were not prescribed OPM. Pairwise comparisons of proportions were performed using two-proportion Z-tests with Bonferroni correction. A matched cohort analysis was conducted to assess rates of secondary OFF after PHF. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios (OR). A total of 180,304 patients with PHFs were identified, with 6627 (3.7%) patients prescribed OPM after a PHF. Female patients were more likely to be prescribed OPM (84.6% vs 68.0%, P < 0.001). Black patients were less likely to be prescribed OPM (2.7% vs 5.1%, P < 0.001). After matching, patients who were prescribed OPM after a PHF had a decreased 1-year mortality rate (OR = 0.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.66-0.94; P = 0.008) and lower rate of secondary fragility fractures (OR = 0.63, 95% confidence interval, 0.56-0.72; P < 0.001). Osteoporosis medications are not commonly initiated after geriatric PHFs. OPM initiation after PHF was associated with lower rates of secondary OFF and 1-year mortality. Level III, Prognostic.

cards.title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
cards.abstract: To evaluate the impact of estrogen hormone therapy on venous thrombotic events for femoral neck fractures treated with either total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA). Retrospective cohort analysis. TriNetX Health Research Network. Patients who sustained a femoral neck fracture (OTA/AO 31B) between 2005 and 2025 who were treated with either THA or HA were categorized into groups based on whether they were prescribed systemic estrogen hormone therapy (EHT) within 3 months before or after their fracture. The primary outcomes were deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 3 months after their fracture. A matched cohort was created after a 1:1 propensity match for demographics, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios. A total of 39,631 patients with femoral neck fractures treated with either a THA or HA were identified. Of these, 330 (0.8%) patients with femoral neck fractures were prescribed estrogen within 3 months before or after their fracture. After a matched cohort comparison, there were no statistically significant differences in rates of PE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-3.03; P = 0.525) or for DVT (OR = 1.67; 95% CI, 0.78-3.61; P = 0.184). Systemic EHT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of DVT or PE after operatively treated femoral neck fractures with THA or HA. Level III, Prognostic.

cards.title: The potential of psychological intervention to decrease the risk of anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis.
cards.abstract: Emotional distress in pulmonary fibrosis remains under-recognised and poorly addressed. This study assessed changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms following an individualised psychological intervention. Single-centre, single-arm before-and-after observational study of an individualised psychological intervention delivered in routine ILD care, combining acceptance and commitment therapy, humanistic-existential techniques, and psychophysiological interventions. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) before and after the intervention. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience measures (PREMs) were collected. Response was analysed across characteristics defined before any analysis of outcome data (age, sex, disease severity [ILD-GAP], frailty [CFS], time since diagnosis, and baseline HADS). Thirty patients were included (50.0% women; mean age 71.0 years). At baseline, 76.7% scored ≥8 on HADS-anxiety and 76.7% on HADS-depression, indicatingclinically relevant symptom risk. Six patients discontinued (lung transplantation, palliative care, or death; n = 2 each). Among 24 evaluable patients, mean HADS-anxiety decreased from 11.3 to 6.6 (mean difference 4.7; 97.5% CI 2.6-6.9; p < 0.001) and HADS-depression from 10.7 to 5.5 (mean difference 5.2; 97.5% CI 3.2-7.2; p < 0.001). HADS-anxiety score improved in 19 patients, was unchanged in 3 and worsened in 2; HADS-depression score improved in 20, was unchanged in 2 and worsened in 2. No patient worsened in HADS category. No differences in response were detected by age, sex, disease severity, frailtyor time since diagnosis. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience scores were high (totalscore 9.4 [SD 0.7] in patients and 9.5 [SD 0.7] in caregivers). In this uncontrolled study, an individualised psychological intervention was associated with reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms and a lower proportion of patients at risk of clinically relevant anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis. These findings suggest the potential of psychological care within routine ILD follow-up and require confirmation in randomised controlled trials.

cards.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
cards.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

cards.title: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.
cards.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD. AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction. AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

cards.title: Harnessing the power of Scutellaria baicalensis: Advances in active compounds and their impact on skeletal system diseases (Review).
cards.abstract: Skeletal system diseases (SSDs) encompass a variety of conditions affecting bones, cartilage and joints, including osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteosarcoma. These diseases significantly impair physical function, rank among the leading causes of disability worldwide, and can even lead to mortality, affecting the lives of hundreds of millions of individuals. Scutellaria baicalensis, a widely used traditional Chinese medicinal herb, is rich in flavonoids, including baicalein, baicalin, wogonin, oroxylin A and wogonoside. Given the increasing prevalence of SSDs and their profound impact on quality of life, existing research highlights the promising therapeutic effects of Scutellaria baicalensis. The present review explores the therapeutic potential of Scutellaria baicalensis and its active compounds in combating SSDs. By investigating their mechanisms of action, the current study highlights how these compounds influence key biological functions, including proliferation, apoptosis, senescence, inflammation, oxidative stress, ferroptosis and autophagy in stem cells, osteoblasts, chondrocytes, osteoclasts and immune cells. Furthermore, it explores critical signaling pathways such as MAPK, NF‑κB, AKT, mTOR, TGF‑β/Smad3, c‑Fos/AP‑1 and Wnt/β‑catenin. The present review also discusses various nanoparticle and microparticle drug delivery systems, including functionalized metal‑organic frameworks, injectable hydrogels and calcium polyphosphate microparticles, which are designed to improve the bioavailability and targeted delivery of active compounds from Scutellaria baicalensis, thereby enhancing their therapeutic efficacy. The current findings underscore the promising role of Scutellaria baicalensis in the management of SSDs, offering valuable insights into innovative treatment strategies and the intricate biological processes involved.

cards.title: Frailty Burden in Patients with HFrEF Undergoing Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: Clinical Outcomes and Readmissions.
cards.abstract: Frailty is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes across cardiovascular populations. However, its prognostic significance, particularly the impact of graded frailty burden, among patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between frailty burden and in-hospital outcomes among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation using the Nationwide Readmissions Database. Frailty was defined using the validated Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) frailty indicator. Cumulative frailty burden was quantified as the number of domains (range: 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations with outcomes, and in-hospital mortality probabilities were estimated across increasing frailty burden. Among 17,367 hospitalizations for VT ablation in patients with HFrEF, 7.4% were classified as frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.59; 95% CI, 1.19-2.13; p<0.001), and increased complication rates. Frail patients had higher 30-day (13.6% vs. 9.1%) and 90-day (33.7% vs. 28.1%) readmission rates compared with non-frail patients. Frailty burden demonstrated a graded association with in-hospital mortality, with estimated mortality increasing progressively with each additional frailty domain. Frailty is independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes and higher readmission rates among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation, with a graded increase in risk across increasing frailty domains. These findings suggest that frailty burden may serve as a clinically relevant risk stratification marker in this vulnerable cohort.

cards.title: Back extensor strength and incident GERD in women receiving osteoporosis treatment: a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: We investigated factors associated with incident gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in women receiving osteoporosis treatment. This retrospective cohort study included 82 women with osteoporosis, baseline Frequency Scale for the Symptoms of GERD (FSSG) scores < 8, and an available follow-up assessment at least 4 years later. Incident questionnaire-defined GERD was defined as a final follow-up FSSG score ≥ 8 among participants with baseline scores < 8. Clinical characteristics, radiographic parameters, bone mineral density (BMD), body composition, and muscle strength were compared between groups. Separate age-adjusted logistic regression models assessed follow-up back extensor strength and percentage changes in back extensor strength and lumbar spine BMD expressed as a percentage of the young adult mean (%YAM). At the final follow-up assessment, 19 participants (23.2%) were classified as GERD-positive. Follow-up back extensor strength was lower in the GERD group (10.6 ± 4.5 vs 14.3 ± 5.7 kg; p = 0.011). Higher follow-up back extensor strength was associated with lower odds of incident GERD (age-adjusted odds ratio, 0.86 per 1-kg increase; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-0.98; p = 0.019). Neither percentage change was significantly associated with incident GERD. BMD increased during follow-up, and radiographic parameters did not differ significantly between groups. Lower back extensor strength at follow-up was associated with questionnaire-defined GERD in women receiving osteoporosis treatment. Although temporal and causal relationships remain uncertain, prospective studies with strength assessments before symptom onset could clarify this association and inform future trials of back extensor strengthening.

cards.title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.

cards.title: Resistant hypertension and accelerated vascular aging: evidence for PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Resistant hypertension (RH) is increasingly linked to accelerated vascular aging and is particularly prevalent among older and obese individuals. Cellular senescence has emerged as a potential driver of vascular aging, but its contribution to RH remains unclear. We examined age and body mass index (BMI) in the WalkByLab cohort and assessed whether RH was associated with vascular features consistent with accelerated aging. Obesity-related transcriptomic datasets were integrated with a curated senescence-associated gene set to identify candidate regulators, followed by validation in an independent RH dataset, PBMCs, and human endothelial cells. An exploratory clinical-molecular nomogram was also developed. BMI and age increased progressively from normotension to RH. RH was characterized by reduced flow-mediated dilation, increased pulse wave index, and unchanged ankle-brachial index, consistent with endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffness. Transcriptomic analyses identified enrichment of inflammatory, PI3K-AKT, and senescence-associated pathways. In PBMCs from RH patients, PTEN expression was reduced, AKT phosphorylation was increased, and p16/p21 levels were elevated, indicating a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile. In human endothelial cells, exposure to obese serum or pharmacological PTEN inhibition induced AKT activation and cellular senescence, whereas AKT inhibition attenuated these effects. Together, transcriptomic, clinical, and experimental findings indicate that RH is associated with vascular and molecular features consistent with accelerated vascular aging. Human data indicate a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile, whereas endothelial cell experiments support endothelial senescence as a mechanistically relevant cellular component. PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence may represent one mechanistically relevant component linking obesity to vascular dysfunction in RH.

cards.title: Non-linear associations between parity and long-term risk of osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Our findings suggest that although pregnancy and lactation are periods of physiological calcium loss, higher parity is not associated with an increased risk of postmenopausal osteoporosis; rather, it appears to confer a long-term protective effect. Osteoporosis is a significant public health burden. While parity induces transient bone loss, their long-term skeletal impact remains poorly understood. This study aimed to clarify the associations between parity, defined as the number of live births, and the risk of osteoporosis, osteoporotic fractures, and bone mineral density (BMD). We analyzed data from 119,969 women in the UK Biobank. Associations between parity and incident osteoporosis or fractures were evaluated using unweighted and inverse probability of treatment weighting Cox proportional hazards models. Generalized linear models assessed associations with femoral neck and lumbar spine BMD. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic, genetic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Compared with nulliparous women, those with a parity of 2 or 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporosis in the weighted fully adjusted model. In addition, parity of 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporotic fracture compared with the nulliparous group. This protection was evident in women ≥ 60 years and those with normal body mass index. Parity was not significantly associated with areal BMD changes after full covariate adjustment. In women aged 40-69 years at baseline, a parity of 2 or 3 confers long-term protection against osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture (a arity of 3), occurring independently of BMD changes. These findings support the integration of parity into clinical risk assessment tools, ultimately contributing to more effective osteoporosis prevention and a reduced fracture burden across women's lifespan.

cards.title: Outcome Disparities in Geriatric Hip Fracture: Orthogeriatric Co-Management Versus Internal Medicine Admission.
cards.abstract: Hip fracture carries substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Orthogeriatric co-management has emerged as the evidence-based standard of care, yet the influence of admitting service on outcomes at institutions where such programs exist remains poorly characterized. Patients aged 65 or older who underwent operative management of hip fractures at an urban academic safety-net institution between January 2019 and December 2022. After excluding patients admitted to other services or requiring intensive care, the final cohort comprised 443 patients (349 orthogeriatric co-management, 94 internal medicine). This retrospective cohort study compared outcomes between patients admitted to an orthogeriatric co-management service versus internal medicine. Internal medicine patients received no formal geriatric involvement. Univariate logistic regression assessed associations between admitting service and binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression for 1-year mortality adjusted for age, sex, and ASA score. A matched analysis paired patients 1:1 on ASA score, sex, and age within 3 years using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, including ASA score, age, comorbidity burden, and fracture type. Internal medicine admission was associated with higher 1-year mortality (OR: 3.01, 95% CI: 1.53-5.83, p = 0.001), greater surgical delay beyond 24 h (OR: 3.16, 95% CI: 1.98-5.12, p < 0.001), longer length of stay (p < 0.001), and reduced follow-up within 3 weeks (OR: 0.32, p < 0.001). In 91 matched pairs, these associations persisted for 1-year mortality (p = 0.035), surgical delay (p < 0.001), follow-up (p = 0.003), and length of stay (p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was consistent with the univariate and matched analyses (OR: 2.66, 95% CI: 1.32-5.25, p = 0.005). Admitting service is associated with hip fracture outcomes, and this association was not explained by measured patient complexity. These findings support implementation of service-agnostic hip fracture protocols ensuring consistent surgical timing and perioperative management regardless of admitting service, particularly when serving high-risk populations.

cards.title: Evaluating clinical outcomes associated with regional versus general anesthesia approach in blunt geriatric trauma patients undergoing major operative procedures for hip fractures.
cards.abstract: The optimal anesthetic approach for operative management of geriatric hip fractures remains debated, particularly among geriatric trauma patients with limited physiologic reserve and high comorbidity burden. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes associated with anesthesia type in geriatric patients undergoing surgery for isolated hip fractures. This retrospective cohort study was conducted to evaluate geriatric trauma patients (≥ 65 years) with isolated, blunt, moderate to severe (ISS ≥ 9) hip fractures utilizing the ACS-TQIP database from 2017 to 2023. Patients were grouped by anesthetic technique: regional or general anesthesia. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included regional anesthesia failure rate, complication rates, hospital length of stay (LOS), and ventilator-free days (VFDs). Among geriatric trauma patients with moderate to severe hip fractures undergoing hip fixation, no statistically significant association was detected between regional and general anesthesia regarding in-hospital mortality (aOR: 0.316, 95% CI: 0.076-1.311, p = 0.112) or VFDs (β = 4.548, 95% CI - 2.478-11.573, p = 0.202). Also, no statistically significant association was detected between patients receiving regional compared to those receiving general anesthesia for major complications, including DVT, PE, and stroke. The conversion-to-general-anesthesia rate was 0.96%. No statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were detected between regional and general anesthesia among patients with moderate-to-severe hip fractures undergoing major operative fixation. Anesthetic selection should remain individualized. Level III, Therapeutic/Care Management.

cards.title: Disability in chronic kidney disease.
cards.abstract: Frailty, sarcopenia, depression, and cognitive impairment are each well documented in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and have each been the subject of detailed, single-domain reviews, but are rarely considered together as a single construct that determines whether a patient can work, self-manage, and participate in decisions about their own care. This narrative review positions these overlapping yet distinct conditions within the World Health Organization International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, arguing for a dedicated, cross-domain assessment pathway in nephrology. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for literature (2006-2026) combining "chronic kidney disease" with "disability", "frailty", "sarcopenia", "depression", "cognitive impairment", "employment", and "rehabilitation". Reference lists were hand-searched. This synthesis focuses on epidemiology, mechanisms, assessment, and management, emphasizing data from 2022 to 2026. As a narrative review without formal risk-of-bias assessment, selection bias is an acknowledged limitation. Disability in CKD arises from five overlapping categories-the risk factors for CKD, CKD-related complications, co-existing conditions, treatment-related factors, and multifactorial contributors, such as sarcopenia and frailty. Once established, disability is perpetuated by two structurally parallel, self-reinforcing processes: a physical spiral of fatigue, symptom burden, and deconditioning, and an economic spiral of employment loss and financial hardship. Validated tools assess individual domains, but no integrated, CKD-specific disability instrument exists. Kidney replacement therapy can trigger abrupt functional decline, while kidney transplantation may improve long-term function but can temporarily worsen early post-operative frailty. The ICF-derived WHODAS 2.0 remains underutilized in nephrology. Disability in CKD is common but historically studied piecemeal through isolated literatures. Shifting the paradigm to recognize disability as a unifying, assessable construct, rather than a by-product of individual complications, may enable earlier identification. This framework supports the implementation of structured, cross-domain assessments and coordinated rehabilitation and prevention strategies in routine nephrology care.

cards.title: From T-cell renewal to immune longevity: a multilevel capacity framework for immune aging
cards.abstract: Consider what the T-cell compartment accomplishes. For decades it sustains immune competence while the thymus shrinks, antigens accumulate, and tissues change around it. We propose that this longevity rests on four coupled capacities: input renewal, repertoire maintenance and clonal dynamics, lineage-constrained plasticity, and tissue-contextual fitness. Input renewal is treated as a proxy domain inferred from calibrated peripheral correlates, not as a direct measure of thymic flux. Our claim is simple: these capacities need not age in concert, whether one compares individuals, tissues, or challenges. The biology behind them is well known. Thymic involution restricts the entry of naive T cells, antigen history reshapes the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, metabolic and epigenetic changes erode proliferative reserve, and aged tissue niches alter survival, trafficking, and local function. Nevertheless, some individuals retain protective responses in particular subsets and tissues, a pattern consistent with compensation during aging and exceptional longevity. We introduce renewable potential as a broader concept than T-cell stemness and distinguish terminal differentiation from exhaustion and senescence-like phenotypes. We then consider how longitudinal turnover measurements, clone-aware analyses, and perturbation studies can move the field beyond cross-sectional, age-associated signatures. Its predictions are concrete: capacities may disagree within a person, compartments may age at different rates, the limiting capacity may depend on context, compensation may give way to maladaptive fixation, and intervention responses may vary with the baseline capacity profile. Vaccination and infection, cancer, transplantation, autoimmunity, and tissue inflammation illustrate these constraints. On this view, the T-cell immune-longevity capacity profile describes a context-dependent pattern of deficits and compensations, not a universal immune-age score or a proxy for chronological age.

cards.title: Intraoperative hypotension in older adults with hip fracture: a comparative analysis of different definitions.
cards.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with adverse outcomes, but its definition varies widely and most definitions are derived from younger or mixed-age populations. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery are particularly susceptible due to reduced physiological reserve. This study compared absolute, relative, and duration-based definitions of IOH and evaluated their associations with postoperative adverse outcomes. This retrospective single-center cohort study included all patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre+ between January 2021 and December 2022. IOH was defined using absolute thresholds (MAP < 65 mmHg, SBP < 100 mmHg), relative reductions (≥ 20%), post-induction decreases, and duration below thresholds. Outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI, KDIGO criteria), and 30 day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, ASA classification, medication use, and nursing home residency. A total of 473 patients were included (mean age 80.9 years, 69.8% female). Postoperative AKI occurred in 9.9% and 30 day mortality in 5.5%. Absolute and relative IOH thresholds were not significantly associated with outcomes. In contrast, longer IOH duration (SBP < 100 mmHg) was associated with 30 day mortality (OR 1.09 per minute, 95%CI 1.02-1.16). After adjustment, higher ASA classification remained associated with AKI, while IOH duration remained significantly associated with mortality. In older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, the duration of IOH, rather than static thresholds, appeared more strongly associated with adverse outcomes, particularly 30 day mortality. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of hypotension duration and support further prospective research to establish geriatric-specific IOH definitions and optimal perioperative blood pressure management strategies.

cards.title: Short-Term Risk of Pneumonia After Fracture by Anatomical Site in Adults Aged 65 Years or Older: A Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: To compare short-term recorded pneumonia risk across fracture sites in adults aged 65 years or older, focusing on thoracic-region versus lumbar-region vertebral compression fracture (VCF). This retrospective TriNetX cohort study included adults with a first qualifying recorded diagnosis of one of six fractures. Pair-specific cohorts underwent 1:1 propensity score matching. The primary outcome was at least one recorded pneumonia diagnosis during Days 3-90; Days 3-30 were secondary. After matching, the maximum standardized mean difference was 0.031 or less in every comparison. In the primary analysis, 42 959 patients were included in each cohort. During Days 3-90, pneumonia occurred in 1469 patients (3.42%) after thoracic-region VCF and 1171 (2.73%) after lumbar-region VCF (risk ratio [RR], 1.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.35); the 3-30-day RR was 1.31 (95% CI, 1.17-1.46). Versus pair-specifically matched distal-radius cohorts, 3-90-day RRs were 2.29 for thoracic-region VCF, 1.91 for lumbar-region VCF, 2.33 for proximal femur fracture, 1.97 for single-rib fracture, and 2.39 for multiple-rib fractures. Multiple-rib fractures had greater risk than single-rib fracture (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.18-1.31). Relative associations with recorded pneumonia were generally stronger during Days 3-30 than during Days 3-90. Risk was higher in the thoracic-region VCF cohort than in the lumbar-region VCF cohort and in the multiple-rib fracture cohort than in the single-rib fracture cohort. These findings may inform respiratory surveillance based on fracture site and rib-fracture burden, subject to residual confounding and diagnostic-code limitations.

cards.title: Associations Between the Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients and the Risk of Bone Fractures in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis: The Q-Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis have elevated fracture risk, partly owing to undernutrition and protein-energy wasting. The Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients (NRI-JH) has been proposed as a surrogate marker of protein-energy wasting; however, its association with fracture risk has not been evaluated. Multicenter, prospective cohort study. This study analyzed 3,038 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis, enrolled in the Q-Cohort Study. The baseline NRI-JH was calculated based on age, sex, body mass index, and serum levels of albumin, creatinine, and total cholesterol, and patients were categorized into 3 groups based on baseline NRI-JH values: group 1, 0-2; group 2, 3-6; and group 3, 7-13. First occurrence of clinically diagnosed bone fractures. Incidence rates were evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with death as a competing event) were used to estimate HRs and 95% CIs. During a median follow-up period of 4 years, 140 fractures occurred. Groups 2 and 3 had a significantly higher incidence of fractures than group 1 (log-rank test; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, fracture risk remained higher in group 2 (HR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.24-3.06) and group 3 (HR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.25-3.38) than in group 1. Competing risk analyses yielded similar results. Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across age, sex, diabetic nephropathy, inflammation, and chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder parameters without significant interactions. Single baseline measurement of exposure; lack of differentiation between fracture types; potential residual confounding. Higher NRI-JH values were independently associated with an increased fracture risk in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. The NRI-JH may serve as a comprehensive nutritional marker for identifying individuals at an elevated risk of fractures.

cards.title: Pharmacological Interventions for Osteoporosis in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a common complication after kidney transplantation and contributes to fracture risk and morbidity among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs). However, the efficacy of pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in this population remains uncertain. Systematic review and meta-analysis. KTRs. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through December 2024 for randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments' effects on bone turnover markers, bone mineral density (BMD), and fracture incidence in KTRs. Three independent reviewers extracted study characteristics, type of pharmacological interventions and comparators, and outcomes, including bone turnover markers, BMD, and fracture rates. A random-effects model was used to calculate weighted mean differences (WMD) for continuous outcomes and relative risks for categorical outcomes. A total of 33 randomized controlled trials (2,623 KTRs) were included in this meta-analysis. Pharmacological treatment was not associated with significant changes in parathyroid hormone, bone alkaline phosphatase, and osteocalcin levels. In subgroup analysis, only active vitamin D showed a significant reduction in parathyroid hormone levels (WMD -25.18 pg/mL [-32.59 to -17.77]). Interestingly, pharmacological therapy significantly improved BMD at lumbar spine (WMD 0.04 g/cm2 [0.00 to 0.08]; P = 0.04), radius (WMD 0.14 g/cm2 [0.08-0.19]; P < 0.001), and femoral neck (WMD 0.05 g/cm2 [0.03-0.07]; P < 0.001). However, no significant improvement in BMD was observed at the hip (WMD 0.03 g/cm2 [-0.01 to 0.07]; P = 0.12). Furthermore, there was no statistically significant reduction in fracture risk (RR 0.38 [0.14-1.01]; P = 0.05). Significant clinical and statistical heterogeneity (I2) because of varied pharmacological agents, initiation timing, and recipient characteristics. Pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in KTRs significantly improved BMD at several skeletal sites, particularly radius site. However, a nonsignificant trend toward reduced fracture incidence was observed.

cards.title: Macrophage reprogramming in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases: From tissue-niche biology to therapeutic translation.
cards.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMSDs), including osteoarthritis (OA), osteoporosis (OP), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and sarcopenia (SP), impose a major burden through pain, structural deterioration, mobility loss, fracture risk, and functional decline. Although these disorders are often grouped as age-related musculoskeletal conditions, they arise from distinct tissue niches and cannot be explained by a single pathogenic mechanism. Macrophages occupy a central position at the interface between degenerative stress and tissue outcome, but their functions extend far beyond a binary M1/M2 polarization model. This Review proposes a disease-niche-adapted framework for macrophage reprogramming in DMSDs. In this framework, macrophages are interpreted according to the pathological tasks they perform within each tissue environment: inflammatory amplification and pain-related synovial crosstalk in OA, osteoimmune remodeling in OP, immune-barrier disruption and macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell feedback in IVDD, and impaired regenerative support in aging muscle in SP. We discuss how macrophage functional states are shaped by transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, immunometabolic rewiring, inflammatory signaling, autophagy and organelle quality control, and local niche-derived cues. Therapeutic strategies are then evaluated according to whether they interrupt upstream niche stress, redirect inflammatory and metabolic decoding, restore quality-control capacity, or reshape macrophage-mediated tissue communication. Finally, we propose that macrophage-targeted therapy should be assessed through a hierarchy of evidence, progressing from marker changes to functional reprogramming, macrophage-causal validation, and disease-specific structural or functional improvement. This framework may help convert macrophage plasticity from a broad immunological concept into a more precise, testable, and disease-adapted therapeutic strategy for musculoskeletal degeneration. This Review provides a disease-niche-adapted framework for evaluating macrophage reprogramming in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases. By linking disease-specific macrophage tasks with regulatory mechanisms, therapeutic entry points, causal validation, delivery feasibility, and tissue-relevant endpoints, this framework may help guide both the design and translational assessment of macrophage-targeted interventions for musculoskeletal degeneration.

cards.title: Endothelial Matrin-3 Limits Cellular Senescence and Lipid Dysregulation to Protect Against Murine Atherosclerosis.
cards.abstract: Matrin-3 is a DNA- and RNA-binding protein implicated in cardiovascular development. However, the role of endothelial Matrin-3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, we found that Matrin-3 silencing induces endothelial senescence, characterized by reduced cell proliferation, increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, and impaired mitochondrial function in vitro. Quantitative proteomics and bulk RNA-sequencing identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes and proteins in human endothelial cells. Bioinformatic analyses revealed enrichment of pathways related to DNA replication, p53 signaling, cell-cycle regulation, and cellular senescence. To examine the role of endothelial Matrin-3 in atherosclerosis, we generated Matrin-3 floxed mice on a low-density lipoprotein receptor-knockout background and crossed them with mice carrying an endothelial cell-specific, tamoxifen-inducible Cre driver. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, endothelial cell-specific Matrin-3 deficiency increased atherosclerotic lesion area by 1.41-fold and was associated with increased plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides, increased hepatic cholesterol and triglycerides, and substantial transcriptional alterations in the aortic intima. Endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency also induced hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation, and endothelial senescence. Single-nucleus RNA-sequencing of the liver further revealed transcriptional reprogramming of hepatocytes, including alterations in pathways related to lipid metabolism, inflammation, and constitutive androstane receptor signaling, consistent with a functional link between endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency and hepatocyte transcriptional responses. Finally, Matrin-3 expression was reduced in mouse and human atherosclerotic plaques. Together, these findings identify endothelial Matrin-3 as an important regulator of endothelial senescence and lipid homeostasis and demonstrate that endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency is associated with both local vascular alterations and systemic metabolic dysfunction in atherosclerosis.
