cards.title: Discharge Mobility After Osteoporotic Thoracolumbar Fractures Using a 2-Stage Machine Learning Prediction Model: Prospective Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Discharge mobility after osteoporotic vertebral fractures is heterogeneous and difficult to predict at admission. Machine learning offers structured approaches for multiclass functional outcome prediction, but existing models predominantly address binary end points and report global performance metrics without explicit analysis of the error structure. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a 2-stage machine learning framework with a predefined decision policy designed to reduce extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification for graded discharge mobility prediction in hospitalized patients with osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures. This prospective, single-center cohort study enrolled consecutive patients aged 65 years or older admitted for acute osteoporotic thoracic or lumbar fractures (N=158). Discharge mobility was categorized as LOW (<50 m or nonambulatory), MID (50-500 m), or HIGH (>500 m or stair climbing). Clinical associations were analyzed using proportional odds ordinal regression. A predefined 2-stage architecture combined gradient-boosted trees (stage A: HIGH vs non-HIGH) and a random forest classifier (stage L: LOW vs non-LOW). The final 3-class prediction was assigned by a predefined decision policy designed to reduce clinically relevant extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification. All preprocessing steps, including fold-wise multiple imputation, were performed within training partitions only. The decision policy was additionally reevaluated in a nested cross-validation with fold-internal threshold selection across 10 repeated partitions. Prefracture HIGH mobility was the only significant independent predictor of discharge mobility (odds ratio [OR] 3.38, 95% CI 1.68-6.80; P<.001); age, comorbidity burden, fracture grade, and treatment were not. In the prespecified analysis with fixed thresholds, performance was moderate (accuracy 0.494; balanced accuracy 0.450; macro-F1 0.444). Binary discrimination yielded an area under the curve of 0.693 (HIGH vs non-HIGH) and 0.625 (LOW vs non-LOW). Using the predefined decision policy, major LOW-HIGH errors were less frequent than with the prefracture mobility-only baseline (5 vs 22), and no HIGH-to-LOW misclassification occurred in the prespecified analysis. In the leakage-free nested cross-validation, macro-F1 was 0.388 (SD 0.031) and major errors had a mean of 8.3 (SD 3.4) vs 22.5 (SD 1.1) for the baseline, with fewer major errors in all 10 partitions. HIGH-to-LOW errors had a mean of 2.6 (SD 2.2) in this analysis. Discharge mobility after osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures is primarily determined by prefracture functional reserve rather than fracture severity or comorbidity. A 2-stage machine learning framework achieved moderate multiclass discrimination and reduced extreme LOW-HIGH misclassification relative to a mobility-only baseline; this reduction persisted under nested cross-validation, whereas the absence of HIGH-to-LOW errors was specific to the prespecified partition. External validation is required before clinical deployment.

cards.title: Effect of home blood pressure monitoring on major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality: results from the VA HOMESTEAD study
cards.abstract: Importance: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) has been shown to lower blood pressure (BP) in randomized trials, however its real-world effect on clinical outcomes is not known. Objective: To determine the association between HBPM and clinical outcomes including cardiovascular events and mortality. Design: Target trial emulation employing matched cohorts with index-date follow-up. Setting: Veterans Health Administration (VHA) telehealth program. Participants: Eligible Veterans had uncontrolled BP (defined as a systolic BP >140 mmHg) at a primary care visit within VHA, with a systolic BP >140 mmHg at the prior primary care visit or average systolic BP >140 mmHg over the year prior. The HBPM (intervention) group included eligible Veterans who were enrolled in a HBPM program for hypertension between January 1, 2013 and December 31, 2019. Individuals in the control group (usual care) were selected from eligible Veterans who were not enrolled in HBPM. Controls were matched with those in the intervention, in part, on demographics, baseline blood pressure and antihypertensive medication use, baseline frailty, mortality risk, and selected comorbidities. Exposure: HBPM in the VHA telehealth program Main Outcomes: All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the first occurrence during follow-up of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, or unstable angina. Results: Among 30,203 Veterans enrolled in HBPM and 30,096 non-enrolled controls, with a median duration of 202 days of HBPM and 6.4 years of follow-up, HBPM was associated with 8.3% lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% confidence interval 0.89, 0.95) and a 4.1% higher risk of MACE (HR 1.04; 95% CI 1.01, 1.08). In analyses calibrated for negative control outcomes, there was no longer a statistically significant association between HBPM and MACE. Conclusions and Relevance: HBPM as utilized in routine clinical care among a large national cohort of adults with uncontrolled hypertension was associated with reduced risk of mortality. The association between HBPM with increased risk of MACE may have been due to ascertainment differences between those enrolled and not enrolled in HBPM.

cards.title: Preoperative Frailty as a Predictor of Quality of Life Outcomes Following Cytoreductive Surgery.
cards.abstract: Frailty has emerged as a critical determinant of postoperative risk in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS + HIPEC). However, its impact on postoperative quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative frailty and postoperative QoL in patients undergoing CRS + HIPEC. This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital between May 2017 and June 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), with patients classified as frail (CFS ≥ 4) or non-frail (CFS < 4). QoL outcomes were evaluated using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5 L) and Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey at five time points. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years). Of the 364 included patients, 49 (13.5%) were classified as frail. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes, particularly in mobility, self-care, usual activities, and physical component summary (PCS) scores (all p ≤ 0.003) at baseline. These impairments persisted at three and 6 months postoperatively. Pain and discomfort also emerged as significant issues for frail patients at both three- and 6-months following surgery (p = 0.018 and p = 0.005, respectively). Older frail patients (≥ 65 years) experienced significantly greater impairments in self-care and usual activities at 6 months postoperatively, along with lower mental health summary (MCS) scores at 12 months compared to the non-frail group. Preoperative frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes following CRS + HIPEC, highlighting the importance of routine frailty screening and prehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes in vulnerable patients.

cards.title: Mortality and healthcare utilization after proximal humeral fractures in patients aged 65 years and older: a register-based cohort study.
cards.abstract: Proximal humeral fractures are associated with substantial pain, impaired mobility, and reduced quality of life, yet no widely accepted guidelines for post-fracture care exist. This study investigates one-year mortality and identifies pre-fracture risk factors associated with mortality. Further, it examines changes in healthcare utilization and associated risk factors across hospitals, municipalities, and primary care before and after the fracture. Patients aged ≥65 years with proximal humeral fracture were identified from the CROSS-TRACKS cohort. One-year mortality was analysed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, adjusting for sex, age, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), civil status, and residential status. Changes in hospital contacts, municipal services, and primary care contacts were assessed using paired t-tests, and their associations with sex, age, CCI, civil status, and residential status were examined using multiple linear regression. One-year mortality was 11.6% (95% confidence interval (CI) 10.8; 12.3). Male sex, older age, higher CCI, unmarried status, and nursing home residency were associated with increased mortality. From the year before to the year after the fracture, hospital contacts increased by a mean of 2.1 (95% CI: 2.0; 2.3), municipal services by 339.1 (95% CI: 294.6; 383.5), and primary care contacts by 4.4 (95% CI: 3.9; 4.8). Older age and higher CCI were associated with increased healthcare utilization. Patients with proximal humeral fractures had high one-year mortality and increased healthcare utilization. Older age and high CCI were associated with both outcomes. These findings highlight the need for standardized, evidence-based protocols with patient-centred principles for this frail population.

cards.title: The role of the CYP1A1 gene in long-term glucocorticoid-related adverse effects.
cards.abstract: CYP1A1 gene variants may influence the development of AE of chronic GC treatment. The rs1799814 polymorphism was associated with increased BMI and lower levels of bone turnover markers, independent of GC dose, suggesting reduced GC metabolism. No association was found with OP and/or Fx, BMD or TBS values. Long-term glucocorticoid (GC) use can produce adverse effects (AE) including obesity, diabetes, osteoporosis and fractures. The variability in AE severity suggests a genetic influence. CYP1A1, a cytochrome P450 family enzyme involved in GC metabolism, may play a role. This study aimed to genotype CYP1A1 variants in patients on chronic GC treatment and analyse their relationship with long-term AE. Seventy patients (56 ± 16.6 years; 71.4% female; 47.1% postmenopausal) receiving chronic GC treatment ( ≥5 mg/ day for >3 months) were included. Clinical data were collected at baseline and at 5 years of follow-up, including OP risk factors, previous and incidental fractures, GC dose and duration, disease activity, anthropometric data, bone metabolism parameters, bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular bone score (TBS) (by DXA), and vertebral fractures (X-ray). CYP1A1 gene sequencing was performed by NGS using Amplicon Deep Sequencing on an Ion Torrent platform. Four CYP1A1 polymorphisms were identified: rs41279188, rs1048943, rs1799814 and rs4646422. Nine patients had rs1048943, nine rs1799814, one rs4646422 and one rs41279188 polymorphisms, respectively. Patients with the rs1799814 polymorphism (13%) had higher BMI (29.3 vs. 25.5; p = 0.019) and greater BMI change over 5 years (ΔBMI: 1.7 vs. -0.32; p = 0.02; adjusted for cumulative GC dose). Additionally, they presented lower bone turnover markers (NTx: 21 vs. 40 nMol/mMol, p = 0.003, CTx: 0.16 vs. 0.29 ng/mL, p = 0.068, OC: 16.6 vs. 19.3 ng/mL, p = 0.059). No associations were found between CYP1A1 polymorphisms and the presence of osteoporosis and/or fractures, BMD or TBS values. The CYP1A1 rs1799814 polymorphism is associated with more severe GC-related AE, suggesting reduced GC metabolism.

cards.title: Homocitrulline and 3-year mortality in older hospitalised adults: an exploratory study.
cards.abstract: Reliable biomarkers may allow early risk stratification for mortality in older adults. Post-translational modification-derived products (PTMDPs), such as homocitrulline, and the tissue accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), measured by skin autofluorescence, have been suggested as potential biomarkers of adverse outcomes in older and frail individuals. The aim of this study was to assess their association with 3-year mortality following hospitalisation. We followed a cohort of 250 hospitalised patients over 3 years. Serum PTMDPs (homocitrulline, carboxymethyllysine, pentosidine, and MG-H1) were measured using liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry, and AGEs were quantified by skin autofluorescence. We examined associations with mortality using bivariable analyses and a multivariable Cox regression model. An exploratory cut-off for homocitrulline was established at the third quartile of its distribution within the study population. During follow-up, 92 deaths occurred. In bivariable analyses, all biomarkers were associated with mortality. In the multivariable model, homocitrulline levels of >400 μmol/mol Lys were significantly associated with mortality (hazard ratio 1.73, 95 % confidence interval 1.06-2.82), after adjustment for age, frailty, and comorbidities. The model's predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76, was only slightly affected by the exclusion of homocitrulline (AUC=0.755). These results indicate that although elevated homocitrulline was independently associated with mortality, its incremental value for risk prediction was modest. Larger studies are needed to further evaluate the clinical utility of PTMDPs, especially homocitrulline, for risk prediction and clinical decision-making.

cards.title: "Metabolic Diets and Fasting in Oncology: Integrating Guideline-Based Nutrition, Nutrition Assessments and Biomarker-Driven Clinical Pathology".
cards.abstract: Popular narratives often promote "special diets" as strategies to cure cancer, frequently invoking autophagy and Nobel-related discoveries. In contrast, international oncology nutrition guidelines state that no diet has been proven to reproducibly cure cancer. This review integrates guideline-based oncology nutrition, experimental metabolic diets and a biomarker-driven clinical pathology perspective within a translational framework. This narrative review synthesizes international and national oncology nutrition guidelines and clinical evidence on fasting, fasting-mimicking diets, time-restricted eating, intermittent fasting, Ramadan fasting and ketogenic diets in cancer. Priority was given to randomized and prospective trials, systematic reviews and selected mechanistic studies, with attention to nutritional risk, toxicity, metabolic and inflammatory markers, body composition, cachexia staging and pathological response. Current guidelines discourage restrictive diets outside evidence-based care and recommend early nutritional screening and stepwise nutrition support. Clinical studies suggest that fasting-related regimens and ketogenic diets may improve selected metabolic, hematological, quality-of-life and pathological endpoints in carefully selected patients, but reproducible survival benefit has not been established. Cachexia-oriented models indicate that cancer-related nutritional decline is multidimensional and partly integrates biochemical, inflammatory, functional and patient-reported domains. Mechanistic studies support plausible effects on autophagy, nutrient-sensing pathways, ketone metabolism, inflammation and the tumor microenvironment. The evidence supports a clear distinction between guideline-based oncology nutrition, which is fundamental supportive care, and metabolic diets or fasting regimens, which remain experimental adjuncts rather than curative treatments. The translational opportunity lies in embedding these interventions within malnutrition-, sarcopenia- and cachexia-aware frameworks and using biomarkers to improve risk stratification, patient selection and mechanistic interpretation.

cards.title: Vitamin D Deficiency and Up to 10-Year Risk of Incident Cataract in Adults Aged ≥50: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Age-related cataracts are a leading cause of blindness, and their prevalence increases markedly after age 50. Vitamin D may help maintain lens homeostasis, but evidence linking vitamin D deficiency (VDD) to cataract risk remains limited. We examined the association between VDD and incident age-related cataract during a follow-up of up to 10 years. This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients with persistent VDD (two serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels ≤19.90 ng/mL) were 1:1 propensity score-matched with those with sufficient levels (≥30.00 ng/mL), with a two-year landmark period. The primary outcome was incident age-related cataract. The secondary outcomes included cataract surgery and all-cause mortality. Positive and negative control outcomes were assessed as complementary evaluations of potential bias. Each matched cohort included 233,425 patients. VDD was associated with a higher risk of incident age-related cataracts (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.65-1.78; p<0.001). Cataract surgery (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.67-1.90; p<0.001) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.45-1.52; p<0.001) were also more frequent in the VDD group. The positive control (osteoporotic fracture, HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.51-1.83) supported exposure validity, whereas the negative control (diseases of the appendix) showed no significant association (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.97-1.16; p=0.180). After additional adjustment for pre-index ophthalmological service utilization, the association remained (adjusted HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.62-1.70). In an exploratory analysis, vitamin D insufficiency was also associated with incident cataract (HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.51-1.62). Sensitivity analyses showed attenuated but persistent associations when restricting the study period to 2016-2023 (HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.39-1.53) and to patients with documented pre-index ophthalmological service utilization (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.27-1.52). VDD was associated with an increased up to 10-year risk of incident age-related cataracts in adults aged ≥50 years. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

cards.title: Cystathionine beta-synthase alleviates intervertebral disc degeneration by inhibiting ferroptosis of nucleus pulposus cells via the PI3K-AKT Axis.
cards.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is the leading cause of low back pain, affecting 619 million people worldwide in 2020, yet no effective disease-modifying therapy is clinically available to reverse its progression. Ferroptosis has been proven to be a core driver of IVDD by inducing injury to nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs). The regulatory role of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) in IVDD and its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the biological function of CBS in IVDD and elucidate the mechanism by which it regulates NPC ferroptosis. We found that CBS expression was significantly downregulated in degenerated human NP tissues and rat IVDD models and was negatively correlated with degeneration severity and ferroptosis activation. Functional assays showed that CBS knockdown markedly exacerbated TBHP-induced matrix metabolic imbalance, senescence, and ferroptosis in NPCs, while CBS overexpression effectively alleviated these pathological phenotypes. Transcriptomic analysis, biochemical validation, and pharmacological inhibition experiments implicated PI3K-AKT signaling in the ferroptosis-related effects associated with CBS modulation in NPCs. In vivo, S-Adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) administration attenuated needle puncture-induced IVDD in rats, restored disc height and NP water content, and suppressed intradiscal ferroptosis. Because SAM has pleiotropic biological actions, these in vivo effects cannot be attributed exclusively to CBS. Collectively, our findings support a protective role for CBS against IVDD through suppression of NPC ferroptosis and implicate PI3K-AKT signaling as a contributing pathway.

cards.title: Osteoporosis Screening Gaps Among Patients Undergoing Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is associated with elevated complication rates after lumbar fusion surgery. Despite this, osteoporosis remains both underscreened and undertreated in the United States. Currently, rates of dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DEXA) screening before lumbar fusion surgery are unknown, as is the proportion of patients who, after being diagnosed with osteoporosis, receive appropriate treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess osteoporosis screening and treatment rates among patients undergoing lumbar fusion surgery. Patients older than 50 years undergoing lumbar fusion for lumbar stenosis with degenerative spondylolisthesis were identified using the TriNetX database. Patients receiving surgery for indications of malignancy or infection, as well as those with diagnoses of osteoporosis before the screening window, were excluded. The prevalence of DEXA scans in the 2 years before fusion was calculated for the overall cohort and for high-risk cohorts defined by Endocrinology Society guidelines. A secondary analysis assessed rates of osteoporosis treatment among patients receiving preoperative DEXA scans. Of 46,104 patients who underwent lumbar fusion surgery, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a preoperative DEXA scan in the 2 years before their fusion. Women were more likely to receive DEXA scans than men (OR, 3.93; 95% CI, 3.64 to 4.23; P < 0.001). Only 5.6% of high-risk men and 17.5% of high-risk women received preoperative DEXA screening. Among patients diagnosed with osteoporosis after DEXA screening, only 11.0% received anabolic therapy and 23.1% received antiresorptive therapy. Despite most patients undergoing lumbar fusion being at risk of osteoporosis (and eligible for screening), a small minority were screened using DEXA in the 2 years before surgery. Efforts are warranted to increase the prevalence of DEXA screening so that osteoporosis is appropriately diagnosed and treated before lumbar fusion surgery.

cards.title: Comorbidities and outcomes associated with young adult hip fracture: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: The prognosis of hip fracture in younger adults (YAs) aged 18-50 years is unestablished. Large studies that rigorously assess risk factors for hip fracture in YAs, their associated functional outcomes and mortality are lacking. While international guidelines recommend comprehensive bone health assessment and consideration of pharmacotherapy in YAs with major fragility fractures, rates of implementation of these guidelines are unknown. We systematically reviewed the existing literature on YAs with hip fracture to identify (1) clinical risk factors for hip fracture, (2) functional outcomes beyond 12 months from hip fracture (including employment and mortality) and (3) referral rates for bone health assessment. Forty-four studies were included from 1875 eligible abstracts. Twenty-three studies reported data on question 1. Psychiatric disease (15% [10-23%]), glucocorticoid exposure (5% [2-14%]), psychotropic exposure (12% [3-42%]), alcohol excess (15% [6-38%]) and cigarette smoking (36% [25-49%]) were highly prevalent in YAs with hip fracture. Twenty-six studies contributed data on question 2, including four that provided mortality data. There is either good or excellent functional recovery in ≥80% of YAs by 12 months following hip fracture; however, up to 15% experience poor outcomes at two years. Mortality rates beyond one year were only reported in one study. Only eight studies were designed specifically to investigate risk factors for, or outcomes associated with, YA hip fracture. Three studies reported outcomes of interest by fracture mechanism. The Quality in Prognosis Studies tool was used to assess the risk of bias of included studies. 24/44 (54.5%) were found to have a moderate or high risk of bias. One study reported data on question 3. Psychiatric morbidity, alcohol excess and smoking were the major risk factors associated with hip fracture in YAs. Further research is required to establish the risk factors for minimal trauma hip fracture in YAs. Limited data on mortality in YAs following hip fracture are concerning and deserve further investigation.

cards.title: Cerebrospinal fluid cell-free DNA methylation captures disease-specific biology in tauopathies.
cards.abstract: BackgroundDifferentiating tau-related dementias remains challenging, particularly during early disease stages when clinical symptoms overlap. Existing biomarkers mainly reflect downstream pathology and provide limited insight into disease-specific molecular processes.ObjectiveWe examined whether cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation could distinguish Alzheimer's disease (AD), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).MethodsPromoter methylation of 20 genes associated with AD risk, neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and glymphatic or lymphatic regulation was analyzed in CSF and matched plasma cfDNA from controls (n = 15), AD (n = 21), bvFTD (n = 14), and PSP (n = 17). cfDNA concentration and fragmentomic profiles were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Findings were validated in an independent cohort.ResultsCSF cfDNA concentrations were increased in AD, whereas fragment size distributions were similar across diagnostic groups. Disease-associated methylation signatures were prominent in CSF but weak or absent in plasma. AD demonstrated widespread hypomethylation of inflammatory and senescence-associated genes together with hypermethylation of glymphatic and lymphatic regulators. bvFTD showed intermediate glial- and stress-related methylation changes, while PSP retained relatively preserved inflammatory and clearance-associated profiles. CSF methylation panels consistently outperformed plasma-derived markers for disease classification. ROC analyses demonstrated strong discrimination for AD, with AUC values reaching 0.84-0.85, while plasma-based markers showed limited diagnostic utility.ConclusionsCSF cfDNA methylation captures disease-specific epigenetic states linked to core pathogenic pathways in tau-related dementias. This approach may provide a biologically informative and clinically useful platform for molecular classification and diagnostic stratification.

cards.title: Denosumab Biosimilars Versus Denosumab in Postmenopausal Osteoporosis: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
cards.abstract: Denosumab is one of the first-line drugs for postmenopausal osteoporosis with high risk of fracture, but the cost limits its use. Denosumab biosimilars are a more affordable solution, though it is underutilized due to hesitation among clinicians and patients due to concerns for differences in efficacy and safety. We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing efficacy and safety of denosumab biosimilars to denosumab. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane databases and Clinical Trials.gov were searched for studies comparing denosumab biosimilars to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis. We pooled mean differences (MD) for continuous outcomes and risk ratios (RR) for binary outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using REML-based I2 statistics and Cochran's Q test. Statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.6.0. Fourteen RCTs comprising 5595 participants were included, of whom 2825 participants (50.5%) received biosimilars. There was no statistical difference between percent change from baseline at 6 and 12 months respectively for lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD), total hip, femoral neck BMD between the two groups. Similarly, change in C-telopeptide, procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide levels at 1, 6 and 12 months from baseline and vertebral fractures were similar between the two groups. There was no difference between the two groups in terms of safety outcomes including treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE), grade ≥ 3 TEAEs. Denosumab biosimilars were comparable in efficacy and short-term safety compared to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

cards.title: Pretreatment bone turnover status and long-term bone mineral density response to denosumab
cards.abstract: Abstract Summary Pretreatment low-turnover status identified patients with attenuated total hip BMD gain after denosumab. Integrated assessment of bone resorption and formation markers may help stratify long-term hip response. Introduction Denosumab increases bone mineral density (BMD) and reduces fracture risk, but BMD response varies among patients. Given its potent antiresorptive action, denosumab may produce greater BMD gains in patients with higher pretreatment bone turnover; however, its relationship with long-term BMD response remains unclear. We developed a turnover index (TI) integrating bone resorption and formation markers and evaluated its association with BMD response trajectories up to 5 years after denosumab initiation. Methods This retrospective observational study included 230 patients with primary osteoporosis who initiated denosumab between January 2014 and January 2025. TI was calculated as the mean of standardized log-transformed TRACP-5b and total P1NP values. Patients were classified into high-, intermediate-, and low-turnover groups according to TI quartiles. Lumbar spine and total hip BMD changes were analyzed using mixed-effects models. Results The cohort included 52 high-turnover, 114 intermediate-turnover, and 64 low-turnover patients. In both unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted models, BMD gain trajectories differed significantly among TI groups at the lumbar spine and total hip (all p < 0.001). Adjusted BMD gains showed a stepwise gradient across TI groups. Five-year adjusted lumbar spine BMD gains were 20.31%, 17.01%, and 12.16% in the high-, intermediate-, and low-turnover groups, respectively. Corresponding total hip BMD gains were 10.56%, 6.76%, and 2.49%, with significantly lower gains in the low-turnover group compared to the other two groups. Conclusions Baseline bone turnover status was associated with long-term BMD response to denosumab. Low pretreatment turnover may identify patients at risk for attenuated BMD gain during denosumab treatment.

cards.title: A Web-Based Registry Framework Linking Transfusion Practice to Long-Term Patient Outcomes: Design and Single-Center Feasibility Study.
cards.abstract: Blood transfusions are among the most common medical interventions performed worldwide. Several comprehensive databases link transfusions to routinely collected health data but do not include the indication and the decision-making basis for a particular administration, nor patient-reported long-term outcomes. We developed a web-based registry for the standardized assessment of transfusion practice and patient outcomes, designed for an observation period of up to 30 years. The framework combines clinical data captured at the point of care with patient-reported outcome measures collected through automated digital follow-up, ensures privacy by design through physical separation of identifying and medical data, and codes diagnoses and procedures in SNOMED CT. We evaluated feasibility in a single-center pilot at Goethe University Hospital Frankfurt (11 September 2024-15 January 2026), with patient-reported follow-up collected through 13 August 2026. A total of 408 patients were enrolled, yielding 1,298 administrations across nine treatment categories in a predominantly cardiac surgical cohort. The pilot demonstrated that the registry integrates into routine clinical workflows, captures the parameters required for guideline-adherence monitoring, and supports sex-disaggregated, descriptive analyses of transfusion practice. Follow-up was completed by 12.5% of patients at 3 months and 15.2% of patients at 1 year; paired baseline-follow-up assessments of physical capacity and frailty demonstrate the data structure for capturing functional recovery. Risk-adjusted benchmarking, network-wide analyses, and donor outcomes are designed capabilities of the framework that were not evaluated in this pilot. The platform is available in 16 languages and participation is open to further institutions.

cards.title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration.
cards.abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the SOD1 G93A ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas maps shared and divergent mechanisms of muscle degeneration in ALS and sarcopenia and provides a resource for identifying therapeutic targets tailored to each condition.

cards.title: [Translated article] Comparative analysis between intramedullary screw fixation and plate osteosynthesis in midshaft clavicle fractures: surgical efficiency and functional outcomes in contact athletes.
cards.abstract: Plate fixation is the current gold standard for displaced midshaft clavicle fractures, despite concerns regarding surgical morbidity and implant prominence. The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical, radiographic, and surgical outcomes of an intramedullary screw system versus conventional plate fixation. A comparative cohort study was performed on 72 patients (36 treated with the Screw system and 36 with plate fixation). Surgical variables (time and blood loss), radiographic consolidation (at 4, 8, and 12 weeks), and functional outcomes (DASH and Constant-Murley scores) were analyzed. Statistical significance was set at p < .05. The Screw group demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time (27.69+/- 9.39 vs. 105.47 +/- 55.18 minutes; p<.001) and minimal blood loss (10 vs. 228.33 ml; p<.001). Functional recovery was significantly faster in the DualTrack group, with an earlier return to physical activity (6.64 vs. 21.69 weeks; p<.001) and superior Constant scores (98.64 vs. 94.81; p = .0006). Radiographically, the screw group showed significantly lower fracture line visibility at 8 and 12 weeks compared to the plate group (p<.05). Complication rates were lower for the screw group (8.3%) than for the plate group (25.0%), although this did not reach statistical significance (p=.11). The intramedullary system is a highly effective alternative for clavicle fractures, providing superior surgical efficiency, faster functional recovery, and improved biological healing compared to conventional plate fixation. It should be considered a primary treatment option, particularly for patients seeking a rapid return to activity and minimally invasive surgery.

cards.title: IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory crosstalk drives DNA methylation and histone remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer.
cards.abstract: Chronic inflammation exerts paradoxical effects in breast cancer, inducing growth arrest while sustaining tumor progression. However, how autocrine and paracrine inflammatory cytokine induced senescence integrates with tumor-promoting behaviour remains unclear. Here, we identify a reciprocal IL-1β/IL-6 circuit that links inflammatory cues, epigenetic remodeling and cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer cells. Following treatment with IL-1β and IL-6, MCF-7 cells were examined using cell-cycle, apoptosis, reactive oxygen species flow cytometry assays, and senescence assays; RNA sequencing; global DNA methylation quantification; methylation-specific PCR; ChIP-qPCR for histone marks; cytokine ELISA; and western blotting for DNMTs and STAT3/AKT/NF-κB signaling proteins. The kinetics of IL-1β and IL-6 signaling were examined using receptor antagonism and pharmacological inhibition. IL-1β induced senescence characterized by G0/G1 arrest, elevated SA-β-gal activity, ROS accumulation and absence of apoptosis. Transcriptomic profiling revealed cell-cycle regulator repression, enrichment of senescence-associated signatures and a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype. Mechanistically, IL-1β induced increased DNMT1 and DNMT3A expression, elevated global DNA methylation, induced promoter-specific DNA methylation (IL-15, HMGB2) and histone mark remodeling (IL-6, IL1RN, BCL2,BAX) at inflammatory, senescence, and apoptotic loci. IL-1 receptor antagonism attenuated these effects. IL-6 induced downstream of IL-1β, in turn activated STAT3, increased DNMT1 and DNMT3B expression, amplified IL-1β expression and tumor-promoting phenotypes, while sustaining the IL-1β induced senescence state. IL-6R blockade disrupted this axis and reduced tumor-promoting effects. An IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory loop drives epigenetic remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence while promoting tumor-supportive signaling. IL-1β initiates the senescence program, whereas IL-6 reinforces and sustains this state through STAT3/DNMT signaling, highlighting inflammatory cytokine signaling pathways as potential therapeutic targets for breast cancer therapy.

cards.title: Complications and management of modified custom-made subperiosteal implants in severely atrophic maxilla and mandible: a retrospective cohort of 211 implants.
cards.abstract: Modified custom-made, additively manufactured subperiosteal implants incorporating guided crestal boneoplasty for abutment housing have re-emerged as a graftless option for selected patients with severe jaw atrophy. This study evaluated the incidence, timing, severity, and management of complications in a large consecutive cohort. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 124 patients who received 211 titanium custom-made subperiosteal implants between 2018 and 2025 at a single maxillofacial surgery unit. Indications included completely edentulous arches and segmental rehabilitation of atrophic edentulous regions where conventional endosseous implant placement was not feasible without major reconstructive procedures or unfavourable prosthetic compromises. All cases were digitally planned. Clinical and radiological records were reviewed to assess implant survival and intraoperative, early, and late biological or mechanical complications. The median follow-up was 28 months. The overall implant survival rate was 98.1%. Intraoperative and early postoperative complications were uncommon and mostly mild. Late biological events were dominated by limited framework exposure, recorded in 9.5% of implants, almost exclusively grade 1 and usually asymptomatic. A previously under-reported pattern of delayed, non-suppurative oedema was observed mainly in maxillary cases and was generally self-limiting or responsive to conservative treatment. Mechanical complications were rare, with no framework or fixation screw fractures and only two fractures of provisional prostheses. Modified custom-made subperiosteal implants may provide a predictable graftless rehabilitation option for selected patients with severely atrophic jaws, with high survival and a predominantly low-grade, manageable complication profile.

cards.title: MTR4 deficiency attenuates abdominal aortic aneurysm progression through suppressing VSMC senescence via the MTR4-RAP1a axis.
cards.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by progressive aortic dilation, with insidious onset but high mortality after rupture and limited treatment options. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) senescence is a key driver of AAA progression. RNA helicase MTR4 has been reported to function in cardiovascular disorders, laying a foundation for exploring its aortic pathological functions. Our research findings indicate that MTR4 was significantly upregulated in both human and murine AAA tissues. Mendelian randomization indicated a suggestive causal association between elevated MTR4 expression and increased AAA risk. In vivo, MTR4 deficiency markedly attenuated VSMC senescence and suppressed AAA formation in mice. Functional studies confirmed that MTR4 promotes VSMC senescence and AAA progression by activating the Rap1 pathway through regulation of RAP1a and its activator RASGRP2. RAP1a silencing abrogated MTR4-driven VSMC senescence. This work identifies MTR4 as a potential therapeutic target for AAA.

cards.title: Effects of blood flow restriction training in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A systematic review.
cards.abstract: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) has been proposed as a low-load rehabilitation strategy for symptomatic and postoperative upper-limb musculoskeletal conditions. This review evaluated the clinical effects, tolerability, and prescription characteristics of BFRT in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation. This systematic review was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261299726) and reported with reference to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. CENTRAL/Cochrane Library, Embase via Ovid, MEDLINE/PubMed, Science Citation Index/Web of Science, and Scopus were searched without a start-date restriction before February 18, 2026; backward reference-list/citation checking was also used. Randomized trials, case series, and case reports were eligible. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity, and studies were appraised using risk of bias 2 or design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Twenty reports were included: 9 parallel-group randomized trials, 1 randomized crossover trial, 2 case series, and 8 case-report publications. Across the reports, 340 participants were enrolled or randomized and 326 contributed to the analyzed/treated clinical samples; 158 were men (48.5%) and 168 were women (51.5%). In a sham-controlled lateral elbow tendinopathy trial, BFRT resulted in a significantly greater reduction in 12-week pain (between-group difference -1.54, 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.89 to -0.18; P = .026) and patient-rated tennis elbow evaluation (PRTEE) (-15.23, 95% CI -23.57 to -6.90; P < .001). In patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis, PRTEE reduction (-24.20 ± 4.02 vs -15.60 ± 3.71; P = .001) and quick disabilities of the arm, shoulder and hand reduction (-12.83 ± 4.97 vs -7.51 ± 4.72; P = .025) were significantly greater with BFRT plus conventional therapy, whereas between-group pain and strength changes were not significant. In nonoperative distal-radius-fracture rehabilitation, mean activity-pain reduction was 4.0 versus 2.3 points (P = .03). In rotator-cuff tendinopathy, BFRT resulted in significantly greater biceps thickness (P = .002) and internal-rotation strength (P = .040). Conversely, a pragmatic elbow trial found no significant between-group difference in 12-month PRTEE (adjusted contrast + 4.32, 95% CI -9.17 to 17.81; P = .53). BFRT may be considered a low-load adjunct in adult upper-limb musculoskeletal rehabilitation settings, but it is not consistently superior to active rehabilitation for pain, strength, or function. Confidence remains limited by small samples, heterogeneous prescriptions and co-interventions, uncontrolled designs, and incomplete adverse-event ascertainment.

cards.title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
cards.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

cards.title: Immunosenescence, inflammaging, and metabolic disease: A geroscience perspective on mechanisms and links.
cards.abstract: Population aging is accompanied by a rising burden of metabolic disorders, including obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cardiovascular complications. Aging is also associated with broad remodeling of the immune system, characterized by reduced protective capacity together with persistent low-grade inflammatory activity, commonly discussed in terms of immunosenescence and inflammaging. In this narrative review, informed by a structured literature search, we examine links between immune aging and metabolic dysfunction and evaluate inflammaging as a major process at this interface. We first distinguish the related but non-identical concepts of immunosenescence, inflammaging, metaflammation, cellular senescence, and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). We then summarize core pathways involving NF-κB, NLRP3, mTOR, AMPK, insulin/IGF-1, and JAK/STAT signaling. Next, we discuss how age-related immune remodeling may contribute to insulin resistance, tissue inflammation, and metabolic impairment across adipose tissue, liver, skeletal muscle, pancreatic islets, vasculature, and the gut barrier, while also considering how hyperglycemia, lipotoxicity, mitochondrial stress, and epigenetic reprogramming may promote selected features of immune aging. We further review emerging biomarker domains, major sources of biological heterogeneity, and candidate therapeutic strategies, including lifestyle interventions, senescence-targeting approaches, and metabolic modulators, with attention to evidence strength, translational limitations, and clinical risk-benefit considerations. The immunometabolic interface thus provides a useful geroscience framework for understanding aging-related metabolic disease, although the direction, reversibility, and modifiability of these relationships in humans remain incompletely resolved.

cards.title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.
cards.abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.

cards.title: Clinical validation of the DRoPH score: a preoperative tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fractures.
cards.abstract: Proximal humerus fractures are common injuries that are frequently associated with considerable technical challenges during surgical reduction and fixation. Although anatomical reduction is crucial for fracture healing and functional recovery, the anticipated difficulty of achieving satisfactory reduction is difficult to estimate preoperatively. The Difficulty of Reduction of Proximal Humerus Fractures (DRoPH) score was recently developed through a structured expert consensus process to estimate anticipated reduction difficulty based on predefined fracture- and patient-related characteristics. The aim of this study was to perform an initial clinical validation of the score. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent plate fixation of proximal humerus fractures at a tertiary trauma center between January 2014 and December 2024. DRoPH scores (0-10 points) were stratified into low (0-3), moderate (4-6), and high (7-10) difficulty categories. Validation was based on operative duration, postoperative reduction quality according to the criteria described by Schnetzke et al., and postoperative complications. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to assess the independent association of the DRoPH score with the primary outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, and surgical approach. Inter- and intra-rater reliability were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Of 1,012 patients treated for proximal humerus fractures, 392 met the inclusion criteria and had complete datasets available for analysis. Of these, 151 (38.5%) were classified as low, 186 (47.4%) as moderate, and 55 (14.0%) as high difficulty according to the DRoPH score. Operative duration increased significantly with increasing DRoPH scores, with an adjusted increase of 7.3 min per score point (95% CI 5.7-9.0; p < 0.001). Reduction quality deteriorated across difficulty categories, and higher DRoPH scores were independently associated with malreduction (OR 1.30 per point, 95% CI 1.12-1.50; p = 0.001). Overall complication rates increased from 15.2% in low-difficulty fractures to 34.5% in high-difficulty fractures, and the DRoPH score remained independently associated with complications in multivariable analysis (OR 1.15 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.28; p = 0.012). Inter- and intra-rater reliability of the overall DRoPH score were excellent (ICC 0.96 and 0.95, respectively). This study provides initial clinical validation of the DRoPH score as a reliable and clinically applicable tool for estimating reduction difficulty in proximal humerus fracture fixation. Higher DRoPH scores are independently associated with longer operative duration, increased risk of malreduction, and higher complication rates. The score may therefore serve as a useful adjunct for preoperative planning and risk stratification in surgically treated proximal humerus fractures. Further multicenter validation studies are warranted. Level III, retrospective cohort study.

cards.title: Procedural Complications and Implant Cutout of the SpineJack®-System in Thoracolumbar Vertebral Fractures: A Retrospective Analysis of 204 Implants from a Level-1 Trauma Center.
cards.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesImplant-related complications of SpineJack® stent-kyphoplasty, particularly endplate cutout, remain poorly characterized. This study determined the incidence of procedural complications, with a focus on cutout, and identified associated factors.MethodsAll patients treated with stand-alone SpineJack® stent-kyphoplasty at a level-1 trauma center (November 2014-December 2022) were retrospectively reviewed, excluding malignant fractures. In total, 204 implants were analyzed (129 OVFs, 75 VCFs). Intraoperative complications and postoperative endplate cutout, assessed on imaging after mobilization, were analyzed by fracture type, AO/OF classification, region and vertebral level.ResultsMean age was 64.9 years (SD 17.5); OVF patients were significantly older than VCF patients (74.3 vs 48.8 years, p<0.001). Vascular cement leakage occurred in 2 cases (1.0%); no technical failures or conversions were recorded. Cement leakage occurred in 18 implants (8.8%) and cutout in 16 (7.8%), neither differing by fracture type. Cutout incidence differed significantly across OF grades (p=0.018), though not after excluding the small OF1 subgroup (p=0.211) or in multivariable analysis (OR 1.03, p=0.918), suggesting limited power; cutout was not correlated with cement leakage or vertebral level.ConclusionsStand-alone SpineJack® stent-kyphoplasty is associated with infrequent vascular and cement-related complications. Endplate cutout (7.8%) was numerically more frequent in severely collapsed osteoporotic (OF4) fractures, but this association was not robust to sensitivity or multivariable analysis, consistent with limited power rather than a true absence of effect; no cutout event in this cohort had a demonstrated clinical consequence. Prospective, adequately powered study is needed to confirm this association.

cards.title: A Refined Lung Transplant Frailty Scale Incorporating Serum Albumin Is Associated With Risk of Mortality in Lung Transplant Candidates
cards.abstract: Background: The Lung Transplant Frailty Scale (LT-FS) is a validated binary measure of frailty in lung transplant candidates. We aimed to refine the LT-FS Base and Body Composition measures by developing a three-category classification to improve clinical risk stratification with serum albumin as a more clinically practical frailty biomarker. Methods: To develop the refined LT-FS, we applied a 4-step measure development method to a multicenter prospective cohort study of lung transplant candidates. Low albumin (<3.5 g/dL) replaced high serum C-reactive protein ([≥]10 mg/L) as the LT-FS biomarker. Cutpoints that balanced discrimination, risk prediction, and calibration were identified to define ''frail'', ''pre-frail'', and ''not frail'' categories. Next, we evaluated associations between the refined LT-FS and exercise capacity, patient-reported outcomes, and mortality using multivariate linear and Cox regression. Results: Among 419 participants, the refined LT-FS identified a graded increase in mortality risk across frailty categories. For example, compared with candidates who were not frail, pre-frailty and frailty by the LT-FS Body Composition were associated with a 2.9-fold (HR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.9) and 7-fold (HR 6.9, 95% CI 2.6-18.2) higher risk of waitlist delisting or death, respectively. Pre-frailty and frailty by LT-FS Body Composition were associated with 2-fold (HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2-3.8) and 3.6-fold (HR 3.6, 95% CI 1.8-7.3) higher risk of mortality after transplant. Relationships with exercise capacity and patient-reported disability were less consistent. Conclusions: A refined Lung Transplant Frailty Scale incorporating serum albumin demonstrates strong associations with waitlist and post-transplant mortality. The addition of a pre-frail category better captures the continuum of frailty and improves clinical risk stratification of lung transplant candidates.

cards.title: Trabecular Bone Score has Limited Ability to Discriminate Fragility Fractures in Postmenopausal Women with Osteopenia: A Danish Case-Control Study.
cards.abstract: Most fragility fractures occur in women with osteopenia, defined by a BMD T-score between - 1.0 and - 2.5. Although bone mineral density (BMD) is used to estimate fracture risk, bone strength is determined by both bone mass and quality. Degraded trabecular bone score (TBS) has been shown to be independently associated with increased fracture risk. Notably, some individuals with osteopenia have degraded TBS despite only modest reductions in BMD. We aimed to investigate the potential value of TBS in discriminating between postmenopausal women with osteopenia with and without fragility fractures. We conducted a retrospective case-control study (1:1) of women with osteopenia at Aarhus University Hospital. Cases had experienced a fragility fracture and were identified through attendance in our Fracture Liaison Service between 01.05.2022-29.04.2024 Controls were referrals for DXA with clinical risk factors. Cases and controls were matched on age (± 5 years). We matched 305 cases with 305 controls. TBS was significantly lower in cases (1.28 IQR(1.20;1.35) vs.1.31 (1.23;1.37), p < 0.01). No differences were found in BMD at any site. Each SD decrease in TBS was associated with a 24% greater odds ratio of a fracture (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.05;1.48; p < 0.01). Adjusting for weight, height and total hip BMD, the association between TBS and fracture was nonsignificant (p = 0.12). ROC curve analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.45, TBS failing to discriminate between cases and controls. TBS was significantly lower in women with a fragility fracture compared nonfractured controls but showed limited clinically relevant discriminatory performance between women with and without fractures in our Danish cohort.

cards.title: Deciphering the mechanisms of resveratrol in knee osteoarthritis treatment: insights from bioinformatics and experimental validation.
cards.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most prevalent chronic joint disorder in orthopedics, with its underlying pathogenic genes and effective treatment methods remaining unclear. Resveratrol (RES), a potent bioactive natural polyphenol, has been shown to effectively alleviate KOA; however, its complex regulatory mechanisms require further investigation. This research seeks to clarify the molecular mechanisms by which RES contributes to the treatment of KOA, utilizing a blend of bioinformatics approaches and experimental validation. First, gene expression profiles related to KOA were obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, differential gene analysis was conducted on the samples, and modular genes linked to KOA were extracted through the application of a weighted gene co-expression network. The LASSO algorithm was utilized to identify crucial pathogenic genes in KOA, which were later confirmed using clinical samples. Targets for RES were sourced from traditional Chinese medicine databases, and the therapeutic targets for KOA treatment were determined by finding the intersection of these sources. An enrichment analysis was carried out based on the therapeutic targets identified. Molecular docking studies were conducted to further assess the binding affinity of key therapeutic genes with RES. Lastly, animal experiments were implemented to substantiate the molecular mechanisms by which RES acts in the treatment of KOA. We identified 460 module genes and 10 key predictive genes through LASSO analysis. The findings from the enrichment analysis concerning potential therapeutic targets for RES in the treatment of KOA reveal that the significant genes implicated include VEGFA, IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1. Subsequent validation with clinical samples revealed that IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1 were significantly elevated during the progression of KOA, while VEGFA was markedly reduced in the context of KOA. The outcomes of the GO and KEGG analyses suggest that the primary biological processes implicated encompass apoptosis, the FoxO signaling pathway, the IL-17 signaling pathway, cellular senescence, and the NF-κB signaling pathway. The findings from the immune infiltration analysis indicate that resting CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, resting mast cells, eosinophils, and activated mast cells may have important functions in the immune mechanisms related to KOA. The results of animal experiments demonstrate that RES effectively inhibits the expression of inflammatory factors such as IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1 during the progression of KOA, promotes the expression of VEGFA, and concurrently suppresses the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, thereby reducing cartilage damage induced by MIA and delaying the progression of KOA. In summary, RES can regulate the expression of genes including VEGFA, IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1, inhibit the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, alleviate cartilage damage induced by MIA, and delay the progression of KOA.

cards.title: Survival modeling and assessing prognostic factors of colorectal cancer in Ethiopia: Addressing violation of statistical assumptions.
cards.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, with rapidly rising incidence in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Survival outcomes are compromised by late-stage presentation, limited therapeutic capacity, and weak post-treatment follow-up. Although survival analysis is critical for characterizing CRC prognosis, insufficient attention has been given to the performance and validity of commonly applied survival models in Ethiopian populations, particularly when statistical assumptions are violated. To identify key clinical and treatment-related prognostic factors influencing overall survival among Ethiopian CRC patients and to assess the robustness and interpretability of Cox proportional hazard model (Cox PH model), stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty model, and Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models, focusing on model adequacy under assumption violations. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 161 colorectal cancer patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2016. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, with group comparisons via log-rank tests. Multivariable modeling employed Cox proportional hazards, stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty, and accelerated failure time models. Model adequacy was evaluated through Akaike Information Criterion, concordance indices, and the Global Schoenfeld test for proportional hazards assessment. The Cox proportional hazard model violated the proportional hazards assumption (global p = 0.043), primarily due to histological subtype effects, indicating that the standard Cox proportional hazard model was not appropriate for this dataset. Assumption violations were mitigated using the stratified Cox proportional hazard model (global p = 0.122). Among accelerated failure time models, the log-logistic distribution provided superior model fit (AIC = 649.88; concordance = 0.724). Time-ratio (TR) interpretation showed that surgery extended survival by approximately 2.4-fold, whereas elevated baseline carcinoembryonic antigen levels and metastatic disease reduced survival duration by nearly half. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, distant metastasis, vascular invasion, and squamous cell histology were consistently associated with poorer prognosis, while surgery and chemotherapy remained protective across models. Rigorous model checking indicates that the conventional Cox proportional hazards model is inappropriate for this cohort due to proportional hazard assumption violations. Accelerated failure time modeling, particularly the log-logistic form, offered improved fit and clearer time-based interpretation of covariate effects. These findings underscore the importance of model validation in CRC survival research and highlight the need for improved early detection, surgical access, and targeted management of aggressive tumor subtypes to enhance patient outcomes in Ethiopia.

cards.title: Parity, skeletal health and osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Parity and lactation have long been investigated for their potential influence on bone health because of the substantial calcium demands and skeletal remodeling associated with reproduction. Whether these physiological adaptations have adverse long-term effects on maternal bone health remains uncertain. This review consolidates the existing evidence on the impact of pregnancy, lactation, and reproductive factors on bone mineral density (BMD), bone microarchitecture, and fracture risk. Pregnancy is associated with modest, site-specific changes in BMD, while lactation induces transient bone loss. Accelerated skeletal recovery after weaning restores bone mass in most women. Large prospective cohort studies consistently show that parity and lactation are not associated with an increased long-term risk of osteoporosis. However, adverse skeletal outcomes have been reported, potentially related to nutritional deficiencies, prolonged lactation, high reproductive burden, and metabolic comorbidities. Emerging evidence suggests that pregnancy-related skeletal adaptations extend beyond changes in areal BMD and include dynamic alterations in bone quality and microarchitecture. Current evidence suggests that pregnancy and lactation result in physiological, largely reversible skeletal adaptations without compromising long-term bone health in most women. Current evidence supports the largely reversible nature of pregnancy-related and lactation-related skeletal changes, but further longitudinal studies are needed to refine risk assessment and guide evidence-based management.

cards.title: Delayed diagnosis leading to severe complications in primary hyperparathyroidism caused by atypical parathyroid tumor.
cards.abstract: Severe skeletal complications at the onset of primary hyperparathyroidism are uncommon in contemporary Western clinical practice because routine serum calcium measurement usually allows early diagnosis. We describe a case of primary hyperparathyroidism in which delayed diagnosis, despite suggestive symptoms, led to an extremely severe presentation characterized by multiple fractures, osteolytic lesions, and prolonged postsurgical hungry bone syndrome requiring several months of intensive treatments and hospitalization. During hospitalization, the patient developed potentially life-threatening infectious and thrombotic complications. Management was further complicated by the diagnosis of an atypical parathyroid tumor, an uncommon and potentially aggressive cause of hyperparathyroidism.

cards.title: Autoimmune hepatitis following long-term denosumab therapy in a patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis.
cards.abstract: Denosumab, a receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL) inhibitor, is widely used to treat osteoporosis. Its role as a trigger for autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) remains uncertain. We report a 68-year-old woman with osteoporosis and Hashimoto thyroiditis who developed jaundice and severe hepatocellular liver injury after 3 years of denosumab therapy. Alternative viral, obstructive, and metabolic causes were excluded. Liver biopsy demonstrated interface hepatitis with a lymphoplasmacytic portal infiltrate consistent with AIH, and autoimmune serologies were positive. Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis was excluded, and an International AIH Score of 17 supported a diagnosis of definite AIH. Treatment with corticosteroid-based immunosuppression resulted in complete biochemical remission, and denosumab was discontinued with transition to zoledronic acid to prevent rebound bone loss. Whether this case represents drug-induced autoimmune-like hepatitis or de novo idiopathic AIH occurring in a susceptible individual cannot be determined definitively. Clinicians should maintain a low threshold for evaluating liver injury in patients receiving denosumab who develop jaundice or marked transaminase elevation.

cards.title: Mechanisms of the interaction between aging of the male reproductive system and obesity, and clinical management strategies (Review).
cards.abstract: With the intensification of the aging of the global population, reproductive health problems among middle‑aged and elderly males have emerged as a prominent public health issue. Late‑onset hypogonadism (LOH), primarily induced by an age‑related gradual reduction in serum testosterone, has garnered widespread clinical attention. The present review systematically elaborates the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying testicular aging. Specifically, age‑dependent alterations in Sertoli cells, interstitial cells and spermatogonial stem cells, as well as an imbalance in the testicular immune microenvironment, constitute the inherent pathological basis of testicular functional deterioration. A vicious cycle exists between obesity and testosterone deficiency: Obesity‑triggered insulin resistance, chronic low‑grade inflammation and oxidative stress directly inhibit testosterone synthesis and accelerate testicular aging; in turn, low testosterone levels promote visceral fat accumulation and insulin resistance, exacerbating obesity and metabolic disorders. Aging, obesity and testosterone deficiency synergistically drive the pathological progression of LOH. In terms of clinical intervention, the present review classifies the therapeutic strategies for testicular dysfunction induced by genetic, developmental and metabolic disorders based on etiological characteristics. The review also summarizes innovative therapeutic approaches targeting the testicular microenvironment and cellular senescence pathways, as well as frontier research hotspots, including natural product interventions and regenerative medicine. By integrating the interactive mechanisms of testicular aging and obesity and summarizing relevant multidimensional intervention strategies, this review provides a systematic theoretical basis for further exploring the pathogenesis and improving the clinical prevention and treatment system of LOH.

cards.title: Age and Neuroimmune Diseases.
cards.abstract: With the aging population accelerating, age has become a core factor influencing the clinical phenotypes, treatment responses, and prognoses of neuroimmune diseases (NDs), including those affecting the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS). This cross-disease review summarizes the shared and specific age-related characteristics of NDs, focusing on the pathological basis of immunosenescence and neurodegeneration underlying age-related ND progression. We extract the clinical manifestations, immune and neural mechanisms of elderly ND patients, and evaluate the challenges and individualized adjustment principles of therapeutic strategies for this population. We explore the age-related immune dysregulation features between NDs and other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), type 1 diabetes (T1D)). This review aims to construct a cross-disease framework for the precision management of NDs in the aging era, identify research gaps and future directions, and emphasize age-adapted intervention strategies for optimizing the prognosis of elderly ND patients.

cards.title: Treatment Patterns of Oral Glucocorticoids in Patients with IgG4-Related Disease: A Real-World Analysis based on a Japanese Claims Database.
cards.abstract: To describe the prescribing patterns of oral glucocorticoid and evaluate flares and glucocorticoid-related complications in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease. This retrospective observational study used a Japanese hospital claims database. Patients with a prescription for oral glucocorticoids, a diagnosis of immunoglobulin G4-related disease, and having at least two immunoglobulin G4 measurement tests were included. The index date was defined as the first oral glucocorticoid prescription recorded in the database (Day 0). Patients were followed for up to Day 1460 (4 years). The study included 3,167 patients. The mean dose of oral glucocorticoid was 28.76, 10.71, and 4.12 mg/day on Day 0, 90, and 1095, respectively. At Day 1460, 66.56% of the patients were still receiving oral glucocorticoid therapy and the dose exceeded 5 mg/day in 17.80% of patients. During the follow-up period, 453 patients (14.30%) experienced at least one flare. The incidence rates of hospitalized infections, osteoporotic fractures, and cardiovascular diseases, defined as serious glucocorticoid complications, were 7.46, 0.61, and 1.61 per 100 person-years, respectively. Over half of the patients continued glucocorticoid therapy at 4 years. Glucocorticoid withdrawal strategies could be associated with reducing the long-term glucocorticoid-related toxicity in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.

cards.title: Multilayer regulation of osteogenic reprogramming in human aortic valve interstitial cells in calcific aortic valve disease.
cards.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an active fibrocalcific disorder in which human aortic valve interstitial cells (hVICs) undergo heterogeneous osteogenic reprogramming. This narrative review provides an hVIC-centered synthesis of four interacting regulatory layers: pathological microenvironmental cues, intracellular signaling, non-coding RNA regulation, and cellular heterogeneity. Lipid dysregulation, inflammation, hypoxia, oxidative and metabolic stress, cellular senescence, and abnormal mechanical loading alter hVIC behavior through interconnected developmental, inflammatory, metabolic, and mechanosensitive pathways. Non-coding RNAs add post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, although many proposed axes remain incompletely validated. Single-cell transcriptomic studies further identify distinct disease-associated hVIC states and challenge a universal linear transition from quiescent to myofibroblast-like and osteogenic cells. We compare conventional and advanced experimental models and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies according to the strength of human, functional, and translational evidence. Current data support a context- and stage-dependent network rather than a single dominant pathway. Integrating human valve tissue, cell-state-resolved analyses, complementary disease models, clinically meaningful endpoints, and targeted delivery may improve biomarker development and support disease-modifying strategies for CAVD.

cards.title: Time- and posture-specific management of severe supine hypertension and neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in diabetic autonomic neuropathy: A case report.
cards.abstract: Coexistence of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension with supine or nocturnal hypertension creates a therapeutic challenge because treatment of either component may aggravate the other. This case illustrates a clinical management framework based on characterization of the full hemodynamic phenotype, repeated reassessment, and treatment adaptation according to posture and time of day, integrating postural blood pressure (BP) responses, 24-hour BP monitoring, symptoms, functional status, comorbidities, and safety findings. A 63-year-old man with hypertension and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presented with orthostatic dizziness and presyncope. Antihypertensive therapy was intensified for elevated seated BP. After intensification, upright tolerance worsened, with recurrent syncope, a rib fracture, and loss of functional independence. Symptoms remained disabling despite antihypertensive withdrawal and nonpharmacological measures. Supine-to-seated-to-standing assessment showed a BP fall from 197/99 mm Hg supine to 122/81 mm Hg seated and 79/56 mm Hg standing, with presyncope and heart rate increasing from 72 to 86 beats/min. Supine measurements and 24-hour BP monitoring documented severe supine and nocturnal hypertension, reverse dipping, and mean asleep BP 203/107 mm Hg. Autonomic testing demonstrated combined cardiovagal and adrenergic dysfunction, supporting neurogenic orthostatic hypotension due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Management was tailored to upright and recumbent periods. A removable transdermal nitroglycerin patch was used overnight. Nonpharmacological measures included repeated encouragement to increase fluid intake, but daily intake generally remained below 2 L. Clinical assessment suggested relative volume depletion. Low-dose morning fludrocortisone was introduced cautiously despite severe supine/nocturnal hypertension. After upright tolerance improved, morning lercanidipine was added. Subsequent 24-hour BP monitoring showed a more balanced profile. Orthostatic symptoms and upright tolerance improved. No further syncope or falls occurred, and functional independence improved. Later 24-hour BP monitoring showed reduced nocturnal predominance, with mean awake/asleep BP 164/86 and 165/89 mm Hg, respectively. Mild peripheral edema was managed with intermittent torasemide. This case illustrates how integrating postural BP responses with 24-hour BP patterns can identify competing hemodynamic phenotypes that may require different management during upright and recumbent periods. Repeated reassessment and individualized treatment adaptation according to the documented BP pattern and clinical context may help balance competing risks of upright hypoperfusion and supine/nocturnal hypertension.
