cards.title: Baseline history of primary fragility fracture is associated with medical complications and revision through 1 year in adult spinal deformity patients undergoing thoracolumbar spinal fusion.
cards.abstract: Fragility fractures (FFx) can indicate osteoporosis following posterior spinal fusion (PSF) in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients. We sought to evaluate the impact of a history of FFx on adverse postoperative outcomes following ≥ 3-level PSFs. This retrospective cohort study queried the Mariner10 PearlDiver database to identify patients aged ≥ 50 years undergoing ≥ 3-level PSF for ASD from 2010 to 2022. All trauma, infection, and tumor indications were excluded. Patients with and without a history of FFx (hip, proximal humerus, distal radius, vertebral body, or pelvis fracture) were stratified. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with adverse outcomes (covariates: age, sex, CCI, obesity, FFx history). 439 ASD patients were identified, of which 33 (7.5%) had FFx. These patients had higher overall medical complications (38.3% vs. 5.2%), respiratory failure (8.3% vs. 2%), DVT (8.3% vs. 0.6%), and infection (6.7% v 0.9%) at 90-day postoperatively, all p < 0.05. FFx patients had higher surgical complications (20% vs. 2.5%), revision/extension (15% vs. 0.4%), and decompression/laminectomy (6.7% vs. 0.8%) at 1-year, all p < 0.005. FFx history was associated with higher risk of wound disruption (OR = 3.9), respiratory failure (OR = 3.1), pneumonia (OR = 2.4), and PE (OR = 1.1). FFx history was associated with higher odds of revision/extension (OR = 3.5), all p < 0.05. FFx history was associated with both medical and surgical complications through 1-year postoperatively, demonstrating how important risk stratification/optimization data can be identified from simple preoperative assessment of FFx history. cards.title: Diet-wide association study (DWAS) of hip fracture risk in UK postmenopausal women: a prospective cohort study of 541,887 women with 27,318 incident cases over ~ 20 years.
cards.abstract: Previous research on diet and hip fracture risk focused on selected foods and nutrients. We aim to conduct a systematic diet-wide association study of 99 dietary factors. The study population comprised 541,887 postmenopausal women in the Million Women Study. Dietary information was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire in 2000-2004, and calibrated using a 24-hour dietary recall. Incident hip fracture was ascertained through linked hospital admission records. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). After an average of 19.7 years of follow-up, 27,318 incident hip fractures occurred. In multivariable-adjusted models, 60 dietary factors were associated with hip fracture risk after multiple testing correction. The top five foods (based on p-value) were: chicken (HR and 95% CI = 0.84, 0.80-0.87 per 20 g/day), vegetables (0.88, 0.85-0.91 per 100 g/day), pasta (0.87, 0.83-0.91 per 20 g/day), chips (1.14, 1.10-1.18 per 25 g/day), and fizzy drinks (1.18, 1.12-1.24 per 50 g/day). The top five nutrients were: protein (0.79, 0.75-0.84 per 15 g/day), zinc (0.81, 0.77-0.86 per 2 mg/day), carotene (0.91, 0.88-0.94 per 1000 µg/day), fibre (0.89, 0.85-0.92 per 5 g/day), and niacin (0.82, 0.77-0.87 per 10 mg/day). The results were consistent across subgroup analyses and in analyses excluding the first five years of follow-up. Many "healthy" foods were associated with lower risk of hip fracture, and "unhealthy" foods with higher risk. Further research is needed to assess whether these associations were causal or reflect overall diet quality or other lifestyle confounding.

cards.title: Correlation Between Paravertebral Muscles Degeneration and Spinopelvic Parameters in Patients With Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures.
cards.abstract: BACKGROUND Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) are correlated with thoracolumbar sagittal imbalance associated with paravertebral muscles (PVM) atrophy and fatty infiltration (FI). This study investigated PVM degeneration and its correlation with spinopelvic parameters in patients with OVCFs. MATERIAL AND METHODS This retrospective case-control study enrolled 50 patients with OVCFs and 50 controls with lumbar degeneration, frequency-matched for age (±5 years). Complete sex matching was not achieved. Primary comparisons were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and lumbar bone mineral density (BMD); subgroup analyses were exploratory and unadjusted. MRI measured the PVM from T11 to L2 and the cross-sectional area (CSA) and FI of the multifidus (MF) and erector spinae (ES) at L3. RESULTS Patients with OVCFs showed reduced CSA and increased FI (P<0.05). After adjustment, sagittal vertical axis, thoracic kyphosis, and pelvic tilt increased and lumbar lordosis (LL) decreased (all P≤0.003), whereas sacral slope (P=0.538) and pelvic incidence (P=0.602) did not differ. MF and ES CSA correlated negatively with SVA and positively with LL, while FI showed the opposite (all P<0.01). In exploratory analyses, patients aged ≥65 years had a larger SVA (P=0.040), and women a smaller LL and lower BMD (both P<0.05); no PVM differences were seen across subgroups. CONCLUSIONS In this cross-sectional cohort, PVM degeneration correlated with sagittal malalignment after adjustment for measured confounders (adjusted cross-sectional associations). Advanced age correlated with greater SVA, and female sex with smaller LL and lower BMD. No PVM differences were detected across subgroups. Further trials are required to validate targeted paravertebral rehabilitation strategies.

cards.title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
cards.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

cards.title: Driver or Passenger? A Bradford Hill Framework for Aging-Associated lncRNAs.
cards.abstract: Transcriptomic surveys of aging tissues routinely report hundreds to thousands of differentially expressed long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and the field has no agreed way of separating causal drivers from passengers that merely track the aging phenotype. I translate Sir Austin Bradford Hill's nine criteria for causal inference, formulated in 1965, into operational tests for aging-associated lncRNAs. Each criterion is recorded as 0, 1 or 2, and the per-criterion profile is the result: no sum or band decides a category. Hill offered viewpoints, not independent quantities to be added; here half of the cited studies support two or more criteria, so a total counts some evidence twice. Two axes are reported separately - molecular causal evidence, and organism-level validation (criterion 8), recorded as supportive, not evaluated, or in vivo at a non-aging endpoint - so that an animal experiment on development, reproduction, cancer or injury is not read as a negative test of aging. Applied to ten worked examples chosen to illustrate rather than to sample the field - NEAT1, MEG3, lincRNA-p21, MALAT1, MIR31HG, SALNR, TERRA, PANDAR, HOTAIR, TUG1 - the profiles separate candidates awaiting an animal experiment from those whose animal experiments addressed something else. MALAT1 is instructive: of six in-vivo perturbation studies, one assays a senescence endpoint. No candidate has an aging experiment that returned a negative result, and none reaches the top of criterion 8, which requires conditional deletion or a titrated antisense regimen with rescue. Organism-level evidence, not literature volume, is the structural bottleneck.

cards.title: Loss of KMT2D accelerates hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation and senescence by increasing mitochondrial ROS production
cards.abstract: Longitudinal bone growth occurs through endochondral ossification, which is accompanied by the differentiation of chondrocytes in the growth plate. Disruption in chondrocyte maturation can lead to skeletal growth abnormalities, such as those observed in Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1), a genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the KMT2D gene. KS1 patients exhibit postnatal growth deficiency, craniofacial hypoplasia, and skeletal deformities, yet the mechanisms underlying these phenotypic manifestations remain poorly understood. Our study investigated the effects of KMT2D deficiency on chondrocyte maturation and identified premature chondrocyte hypertrophy as a key driver of skeletal abnormalities in KS1. We previously observed reduced femur and tibia length in a KS1 mouse model, along with altered growth plate architecture, particularly affecting the heights of the proliferative and hypertrophic zones. Here, we show that KMT2D-deficient chondrocytes exhibit accelerated differentiation and early senescence upon exposure to supraphysiological oxygen levels (20% O2). These pathological changes were linked to increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production likely caused by deficiencies in electron transport chain function, leading to oxidative stress and premature hypertrophy. Pharmacological ROS neutralization or hypoxic conditions mitigated these effects, restoring normal chondrocyte differentiation and preventing premature ossification. These findings demonstrate that KMT2D loss induces oxidative stress-driven chondrocyte hypertrophy, disrupting the balance of cartilage growth and ossification. Our study provides crucial mechanistic insights into KS1-associated skeletal abnormalities and suggests mitochondrial ROS regulation as a potential therapeutic avenue.

cards.title: Five-Year Clinical Outcomes of Surgically Treated Different Types of Tibial Pilon Fractures.
cards.abstract: Intra-articular distal tibial pilon fractures are most commonly caused by high-energy trauma and are often associated with severe soft-tissue injuries. The literature on medium-to-long-term clinical outcomes is limited. The purpose of this follow-up study was to evaluate the 5-year clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction among patients with different types of tibial pilon fractures. One hundred twenty-six consecutive patients with operatively treated tibial pilon fractures were identified between 2012 and 2016 from a level 1 trauma center. A total of 105 patients (mean age 43 years, 30 females, 100% White, 100% European) were eligible for follow-up and were contacted 5 years after the initial trauma. Outcomes were assessed using a questionnaire, Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS), American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, functional tests, and posttraumatic osteoarthritis (OA) Kellgren-Lawrence (K-L) grade. For outcome analysis, patients were categorized into the following 3 groups according to AO-OTA fracture classification: type 43B2-B3 (Group 1), type 43C1-C2 (Group 2), and type 43C3 (Group 3) tibial pilon fractures. No statistically significant differences between study groups were observed in FAOS (mean 74, standard deviation [SD] 16.9) and AOFAS (mean 82, SD 12.7) scores. Posttraumatic OA (K-L grade 3-4) was diagnosed in 35% in Group 1, 8% in Group 2, and 48% in Group 3. Ten patients (8%) underwent ankle arthrodesis. The incidence of deep surgical-site infections increased with severity of fracture type (no patients in Group 1, 21% in Group 2, and 23% in Group 3). Two patients (1.6%) required below-the-knee amputation. Approximately 90% of the healthcare resources were needed within the first 2 years after injury; patients in Group 3 required the most surgeries and had the longest hospitalization. Surgically treated pilon fractures seem to result in good mid-term clinical outcomes, even for severe C3 fractures. However, type C3 fractures had more complications and required more surgical interventions, including ankle arthrodeses, longer hospitalization, and additional other healthcare resources than the less severe fractures. Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

cards.title: Depressive symptoms are associated with the incidence of frailty in older adults with cardiometabolic diseases: Interaction between depression and diabetes.
cards.abstract: Older adults with diabetes are prone to frailty and increased mortality. In this longitudinal study, we examined the association between depressive symptoms and the incidence of frailty in older people with cardiometabolic diseases. We also investigated whether comorbidities modified the association between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in this patient population. We analyzed longitudinal data from 431 outpatients aged 65 years or older with cardiometabolic diseases who visited a frailty clinic from 2015 to 2023. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS)-15. The outcome during follow-up (median, 2.9 years) was incident frailty, as defined by the modified Cardiovascular Health Study (mCHS) criteria or the Kihon Checklist (KCL). Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident frailty were estimated using multivariable Cox regression models. Depressive symptoms (GDS-15 ≥ 5) were independently associated with incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty across all models. The fully adjusted HRs for incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty were 1.92 and 2.05, respectively. Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent associations between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in participants with diabetes and hyperglycemia. Significant interactions between depressive symptoms and diabetes were observed for both mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty, whereas no significant interactions were observed for cognitive impairment or physical inactivity. Depressive symptoms were independently associated with incident frailty, as defined by both the mCHS and KCL criteria, in older outpatients attending a frailty clinic for cardiometabolic diseases. A significant interaction between depressive symptoms and diabetes was observed, suggesting that patients with coexisting depressive symptoms and diabetes may represent a high-risk group for incident frailty. Further studies are needed to determine whether interventions targeting depressive symptoms and diabetes management can reduce the risk of incident frailty.

cards.title: OsteoNet-X: A deep residual learning framework for automated osteoporosis detection from knee X-ray images.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mineral density and increased susceptibility to fractures, making early diagnosis essential for effective clinical intervention and long-term patient management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated significant potential for automated bone disease assessment using medical imaging modalities. In this study, a unified deep learning framework, termed OsteoNet-X, is proposed for automated osteoporosis detection and multi-class bone health classification using knee X-ray images. Unlike conventional image classification approaches, OsteoNet-X integrates YOLO-based Region of Interest (ROI) localization, DenseNet-based feature extraction, Feature-Aware Learning (FAL) optimization, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance both classification performance and model interpretability. The ROI extraction stage automatically identifies anatomically relevant knee joint regions, reducing background interference and enabling more discriminative feature learning. Subsequently, DenseNet facilitates efficient feature propagation and hierarchical representation learning for distinguishing normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis conditions. The incorporation of XAI further provides visual explanations of model decisions by highlighting clinically relevant regions within the knee joint. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that OsteoNet-X achieves a classification accuracy of 97.08%, a macro F1-score of 96.61%, and a weighted F1-score of 97.11%.

cards.title: Lumbar Spine BMD May Not Distinguish Extremity Long Bone Fracture Status in Adults with Severe Motor and Intellectual Disabilities: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: This study examined whether lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD) can distinguish extremity long bone fracture status in adults with severe motor and intellectual disabilities (SMID). We retrospectively analyzed 86 adults with SMID who underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) between 2023 and 2024. Patients younger than 18 years at the first DXA examination and those with fractures only at sites other than the extremity long bones were excluded. The cohort consisted of 23 patients in the fracture group and 63 in the non-fracture group. Fracture history was reviewed from April 2015 to March 2025. Group comparisons were conducted. Binary logistic regression was performed using age and mean lumbar spine BMD as independent variables. The intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.939 (95% confidence interval, 0.909-0.960), indicating high reproducibility of BMD measurements. Mean lumbar spine BMD was lower in the fracture group than in the non-fracture group (0.486 ± 0.137 vs 0.551 ± 0.145 g/cm2; P = 0.067). Mean Z-scores were markedly low in both groups (-2.93 ± 1.16 vs -3.15 ± 1.17; P = 0.451). Among 23 patients with fractures, 20 patients sustained fractures before the first DXA examination and 3 patients sustained fractures after the first DXA examination. In logistic regression analysis, age was associated with fracture status (odds ratio, 1.057; 95% confidence interval, 1.017-1.099; P = 0.005), whereas the association of mean lumbar spine BMD was not significant. Lumbar spine BMD alone may be insufficient to distinguish fracture status in adults with SMID.

cards.title: Predictors of return to work after shoulder injuries: The influence of health perception and job characteristics.
cards.abstract: Shoulder injuries are prevalent among working populations and may significantly delay return to work (RTW). Identifying predictors of successful RTW is crucial for designing effective interventions. This study aimed to assess the RTW status and its determinants among patients with shoulder injuries. In this retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up, 340 patients with shoulder injuries- such as acromioclavicular joint dislocation, clavicle fractures, and shoulder instability-treated between 2016 and 2020 were included. Data were obtained from medical records and structured telephone interviews. Demographic and clinical variables, health-related quality of life (SF-12), and perceived support from employer and colleagues were assessed. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify predictors of RTW. Among 340 participants, 67.9% returned to their previous job, 14.1% returned with modifications, 14.4% obtained new employment, and 3.5% did not return to work. Multivariate analysis showed that coworker support (OR=1.88, p < 0.001) was positively associated with RTW, whereas lower employer support (OR=0.585, p < 0.001), lower SF‑12 scores (OR=0.895, p = 0.023), and white‑collar occupation (OR=0.015, p < 0.001) were associated with reduced likelihood of RTW. In addition, health insurance coverage and certain injury types were significantly related to RTW outcomes. RTW after shoulder injuries is mainly influenced by multiple occupational, clinical, and psychosocial factors. Workplace support, overall health status, and job characteristics play important roles in facilitating occupational reintegration. Strengthening rehabilitation programs and workplace support systems may improve RTW outcomes among injured workers.

cards.title: Beyond reproduction: the emerging role of FSH in postmenopausal aging.
cards.abstract: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

cards.title: Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide attenuates BMSC senescence by inhibiting NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy.
cards.abstract: BMSC senescence is associated with osteoporosis progression. Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) shows potential anti-senescence activity, but its effects on bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) remain unclear. To investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of PSP against tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBH)-induced senescence in BMSCs. Senescence was induced in primary rat BMSCs with TBH, followed by PSP intervention. Viability was assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, while senescence-associated β-galactosidase, alkaline phosphatase, and Oil Red O staining assessed senescence and osteogenic/adipogenic differentiation. Ferritinophagy-associated proteins (NCOA4, FTH1, and LC3) and intracellular Fe2+ were quantified using western blot, immunofluorescence, and FerroOrange staining. Mitochondrial function was evaluated using MitoSOX and JC-1 assays and ATP quantification. Cytosolic mtDNA accumulation and the cGAS-STING pathway were assessed using immunofluorescence colocalization, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting. NCOA4 involvement was examined using an NCOA4-overexpressing lentiviral vector. PSP concentration-dependently attenuated TBH-induced senescence phenotypes in BMSCs, partially restored osteogenic differentiation, and reduced adipogenic differentiation. PSP downregulated NCOA4 expression, attenuating ferritinophagy-associated changes and intracellular Fe2+ accumulation. Reduced Fe2+ accumulation preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation, and reduced cytosolic mtDNA accumulation, alongside attenuated cGAS-STING signaling. Lentiviral overexpression of NCOA4 attenuated the protective effects of PSP on mitochondrial homeostasis and cGAS-STING pathway suppression. PSP may attenuate BMSC senescence by suppressing NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, thereby preserving mitochondrial homeostasis and inhibiting cGAS-STING signaling. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of PSP as a potential therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis-associated BMSC dysfunction.

cards.title: Inflammation factors mediate association of muscle mass and erectile dysfunction: NHANES 2001-2004.
cards.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) constitutes a global male health issue. Current evidence indicates that low muscle mass may exacerbate insulin resistance and vascular endothelial damage via inflammatory cascades, both of which are established determinants of ED. The relationship between muscle distribution and its effect on ED remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between muscle mass and ED prevalence and evaluate potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers. The study analyzed data from 2217 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Appendicular lean mass (ALM) is the total lean mass of the limbs. The Appendicular Skeletal Mass Index (ASMI) is calculated as ALM divided by height in meters squared. The association between ASMI and ED prevalence was evaluated through weighted logistic regression and subgroup analyses. Mediation analyses were conducted to examine the potential mediating roles of inflammatory markers in the relationship between ASMI and ED prevalence. Compared with the non-ED group, patients with ED exhibited significantly lower ASMI; Monocytes mediated the association between ASMI, vigorous activity, and ED. Patients diagnosed with ED exhibited significantly lower ALM compared to those in the non-ED group (25.27 ± 4.87 kg vs 27.35 ± 4.52 kg, P < .001). Participants in the highest ASMI tertile (Q3) had a 39.6% lower ED risk compared with those in Q1 (OR = 0.606, 95% CI, 0.396-0.925, P = .033). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed that there was a nonlinear relationship between ASMI and ED in the fully adjusted model 3 (P = .047). Except for drinking status, no statistically significant interactions were observed in any subgroup (P > .05). Vigorous activity showed a significant negative correlation with ED prevalence (OR = 0.604, 95% CI, 0.418-0.873, P = .013). Monocytes mediated 1.76% and 2.01% of the association between ASMI, vigorous activity, and ED, respectively. Early screening for sarcopenia and ED, followed by resistance training and anti-inflammatory interventions, may provide a comprehensive approach to protecting muscle mass and erectile health. Studies utilizing nationally representative databases to investigate the association between muscle mass and ED remain insufficiently explored, a gap that this research aims to fill. The diagnosis of ED relied on participant self-report via questionnaire, which may lead to underreporting or misclassification bias due to psychological factors. Current research suggests that increased muscle mass is associated with a reduced risk of ED, and that systemic inflammation mediates this relationship to some extent.

cards.title: Association of sugar rationing during the first 1000 days with long-term risk of osteoporosis: A natural experiment study.
cards.abstract: The first 1000 days, from conception to approximately the second birthday, are important for skeletal development. We examined whether lower sugar availability during this period was associated with osteoporosis in adulthood. We studied 65,346 UK-born UK Biobank participants born between October 1951 and March 1956 (mean baseline age, 54.6 years; 55.9% women). Birth month defined four categories of early-life sugar rationing exposure: never exposed, in utero only, in utero plus up to 1year, and in utero plus up to 2 years. Cox models estimated associations with hospital-recorded incident osteoporosis. We also examined differences by sex and polygenic risk score (PRS) and tested alternative time scales. During a median 13.8 years of follow-up, 1606 incident cases occurred. Compared with never exposed participants, fully adjusted hazard ratios were 0.94 (95% CI, 0.80-1.11), 0.78 (0.66-0.93), and 0.77 (0.63-0.95) across the three progressively longer exposure categories (P for trend=0.006). We found no evidence of interaction with sex (P=0.385) or PRS tertile (P=0.816). When attained age was the time scale, the estimate for the longest exposure was 0.93 (0.81-1.06). Sugar rationing exposure extending into infancy was associated with a lower hazard of adult osteoporosis in the primary analysis. The association weakened when attained age was the time scale, limiting causal interpretation. We found no evidence of greater benefit among participants with higher genetic risk.

cards.title: MRI-derived OsteoSarcoScore (OSS): a composite bone-muscle quality indicator associated with prevalent vertebral fracture in postmenopausal women.
cards.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers detailed visualization of vertebral and paravertebral anatomy, enabling direct assessment of pathophysiological conditions. This study aims to introduce OsteoSarcoScore (OSS), an MRI-derived bone-muscle quality measure, to assess vertebral fracture risk. This retrospective study included 234 postmenopausal women (mean age: 66.94 ± 8.87 years) who underwent both MRI and QCT. For muscle quality, the psoas-muscle (PM-Score), multifidus-erector-muscles (MF-Score), and MyoScore (PM-Score + MF-Score) were defined as muscles' signal intensities (SIs) at the L2/3‒L4/5 levels divided by subcutaneous fat SIs. For bone quality, the F-score and vertebral bone quality (VBQ) were defined as the median L1‒L4-5 vertebrae SIs, normalized to relevant controls. The OSS was derived as composite of F-Score-MyoScore and compared with VBQ-MyoScore. Analyses included ANOVA with post hoc correction, DeLong's test for ROC comparison, and multivariable logistic regression with standardized predictors (odds ratios for OSS per 1-SD). Primary models adjusted for age, BMI, vendor, and field strength, with additional adjustment for vBMD; propensity score matching served as a secondary analysis. Incremental value beyond vBMD was assessed by ∆AUC, continuous NRI/IDI, and decision-curve analysis. Reliability was assessed by ICC for scores and Cohen's kappa for fractures. Among osteoporotic patients, MyoScore, VBQ‑MyoScore, and OSS were higher by 3.9%, 10.1%, and 10.2%, respectively, than in non‑osteoporotic patients. In fractured patients, OSS, MyoScore, and VBQ‑MyoScore showed an increase of 136.1%, 132.5%, 132.5%, respectively, compared to non‑fractured patients. Also, OSS was significantly higher in the fracture group (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.001). Muscles scores weakly correlated with patient age with r = 0.22‒0.23, (all p = 0.001). In osteoporosis, higher AUCs favored bone quality scores (F-score = 0.72 and VBQ = 0.69) than PM-Score and MF-Score (0.54‒0.56). In patients with fractures, OSS and QCT-vBMD did not differ significantly in diagnostic performance (AUC: 0.681 vs. 0.725; DeLong z = - 0.95, p = 0.341). Adding OSS to a base model of age, BMI, vBMD, vendor, and field strength significantly improved discrimination (∆AUC = 0.044, 95% CI 0.004-0.084, p = 0.033; NRI = 0.61; IDI = 0.079). OSS remained significantly associated with fracture after adjustment for scanner vendor and field strength (OR per 1-SD = 2.36, 95% CI 1.58-3.52, p < 0.001). OsteoSarcoScore, a composite biomarker integrating bone and muscle quality, showed discriminatory ability for vertebral fracture that did not differ significantly from that of QCT-vBMD, highlighting the potential of combined bone‒muscle assessment for fracture risk evaluation; however, further validation is warranted.

cards.title: Pathological Ossification of Spinal Ligament-Derived Fibroblasts in an Inflammatory Micro-Environment via Activation of the ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT Pathway in Ankylosing Spondylitis.
cards.abstract: Chronic inflammation and heterotopic ossification (HO) were typical hallmarks of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Although existing target inflammation inhibitors could reduce inflammation but failed to halt HO progression, highlighting the need for osteogenesis-specific treatments. However, the role of fibroblasts (Fbs) responsible for extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling in AS-associated pathological ossification remained unclear. In this study, osteogenic capacity, pathological condition and underlying molecular pathways for Fbs derived from AS spinal ligaments were validated. Fbs from uncalcified spinal ligaments of age-matched AS patients/controls were compared. AS-Fbs were treated with a gradient concentration of TNF-α during osteogenic induction. Meanwhile, specific inhibition of AKT phosphorylation was applied to confirm the role of PI3K/AKT in osteogenesis. Upstream signalling pathways were also explored via RNA-sequencing. Additionally, in vivo, subcutaneous cell transplantation was performed to simulate ectopic ossification. AS-Fbs possessed superior osteogenic capacity than controls. Moreover, osteogenic signs could be promoted by low concentration TNF-α-induced inflammatory micro-environment. Functional analysis revealed a crucial role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Mechanistically, RNA-seq identified the ECM/integrin subunit alpha 5 (ITGA5)/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) upstream pathway. In detail, osteogenic induction increased ECM protein levels including thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) and fibulin-1 (FBLN1), activating ITGA5, subsequent FAK phosphorylation, osteogenic markers expression and eventually inducing Fb-to-osteocyte differentiation. ITGA5 knockdown or specific FAK inhibition attenuated osteogenic phenotypes and reduced osteogenic proteins expression. Regarding in vivo experiments, subcutaneous bone-like tissue formation derived from transplantation of AS-Fbs was identified and could be suppressed significantly via the AKT phosphorylation inhibition. In conclusion, the findings of this study revealed potential causes for HO progression derived from AS-Fbs in spite of effective anti-inflammation therapy. Furthermore, the crucial role of ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT axial signalling pathways in the aberrant osteogenesis of AS-Fbs was identified. Combined targeted intervention at the aforementioned signals and application of anti-inflammatory agents might be a novel potential strategy for the treatment of pathological ectopic ossification caused by AS.

cards.title: Opportunistic Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Attenuation is Independently Associated With Achievement of Substantial Clinical Benefit After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
cards.abstract: Preoperative computed tomography (CT) obtained for surgical planning may provide clinically relevant information beyond anatomical assessment. We investigated whether opportunistically assessed CT-derived psoas muscle attenuation was associated with achievement of substantial clinical benefit (SCB) after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and examined its relationships with frailty and nutritional status. This retrospective cohort study included 280 patients who underwent primary THA for hip osteoarthritis. Psoas muscle attenuation was measured on preoperative CT images at the mid-vertebral level of L3. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale and nutritional status using the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score. The primary outcome was achievement of SCB at 24 months, defined as a ≥ 22-point improvement in the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with SCB achievement, and restricted cubic spline analysis evaluated potential nonlinear associations. Model discrimination and calibration were also assessed for clinical and expanded models. The SCB was achieved in 184 patients (66%). Higher preoperative psoas muscle attenuation was independently associated with greater odds of achieving SCB (odds ratio 1.25 per 5-HU increase, 95% confidence interval 1.02 to 1.55; P = 0.031). Lower attenuation was associated with greater frailty, poorer nutritional status, and lower rates of SCB achievement (all trend P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association between muscle attenuation and the probability of achieving SCB (P for nonlinearity = 0.021). Adding psoas muscle attenuation to the clinical model produced only a small, nonsignificant increase in receiver operating characteristic curve (0.711 to 0.732; P = 0.209). Preoperative CT-derived psoas muscle attenuation was independently associated with achievement of SCB after THA. Opportunistic assessment of psoas muscle attenuation from CT images already obtained for surgical planning may provide complementary information for preoperative assessment.

cards.title: Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
cards.abstract: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM. We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression. The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages. Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

cards.title: Bidirectional frailty transitions in community-dwelling older adults: longitudinal findings from the Queenstown cohort.
cards.abstract: Frailty in older adults is dynamic and shaped by clinical, functional, and social factors, yet longitudinal transitions in community populations are not well characterised. We examined one-year changes in frailty and identified factors associated with improvement and progression. We performed a longitudinal analysis of community-dwelling adults aged ≥65 years from the population-based Queenstown Health District cohort. Baseline (Wave 1, 2023-2024) demographic, clinical, and lifestyle data were collected, with reassessment at one year (Wave 2). Frailty was measured using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Ordinal logistic regression modelled overall direction of frailty transition, while multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with improvement or worsening relative to stability. Alluvial plots illustrated transitions across frailty states over time. Among 1,153 participants (mean age 74.5 ± 6.6 years; 55.8% female), frailty remained stable in 627 (54.4%), improved in 211 (18.3%), and worsened in 315 (27.3%) over one year. Visualisation demonstrated predominant stability with bidirectional movement between frailty categories. In ordinal analyses, diabetes (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.06-1.83), smoking (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.19-3.03), and iADL impairment (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.01-2.41) were associated with worsening, while higher physical activity was protective (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.98). Multinomial models showed stroke history associated with improvement (OR 4.23, 95% CI 1.46-12.25), whereas iADL impairment reduced the likelihood of improvement (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.28-0.82). Frailty was largely stable but exhibited meaningful bidirectional transitions. Functional impairment and modifiable behaviours were key predictors, underscoring the importance of repeated assessment and function-focused prevention to mitigate frailty progression.

cards.title: Inherited cardiovascular risk and its impact on healthspan and lifespan.
cards.abstract: Genetic disposition for cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major determinant of aging-related traits, such as healthspan, dementia, and frailty. While rare monogenic disorders provide important mechanistic insights, most CVDs and aging-related traits are driven by the cumulative effects of numerous common genetic variants, resulting in a polygenic risk architecture. Analyses of genes and pathways affected by these variants revealed significant correlations in the genetic architectures of CVD and aging, which appear to promote each other bidirectionally. Thus, CVD and aging share common genetic mechanisms, linking inherited cardiovascular risk to frailty, dementia, reduced healthspan, and shortened lifespan-and, conversely, explaining why aging is the strongest risk factor for atherosclerosis. Advances in genome-wide association studies have also enabled the construction of a polygenic risk score (PRS), which quantifies inherited CVD risk and facilitates early risk stratification beyond conventional clinical assessment. Importantly, individuals at high polygenic risk for CVD derive greater benefit from preventive strategies, which reduce their lifelong burden of CVD risk and ultimately promote healthy aging. Therefore, personalizing clinical risk assessment by integrating genetic testing for both CVD and aging-related traits may be of clinical importance. Specifically, lifestyle modification and preventive therapies based not only on conventional risk assessment, but also on polygenic risks may offer an individualized life-course approach for precision prevention, shifting cardiovascular care from reactive disease management toward the promotion of healthy aging.

cards.title: Fracture Liaison Services in Switzerland: current status and challenges.
cards.abstract: Switzerland is one of the very high-risk countries for osteoporosis. The Fracture Liaison Service is the internationally endorsed model for secondary fracture prevention and for reducing mortality after a person has sustained a fragility fracture. In this article, we describe current Fracture Liaison Service coverage and structure in Switzerland and the challenges Fracture Liaison Services are facing. Good interdisciplinary cooperation, especially with general practitioners, is a key factor. Artificial intelligence (AI) for the detection of vertebral fractures, shared electronic medical records, digital platforms and telemedicine are emerging and evolving approaches to overcome the existing barriers to osteoporosis treatment.

cards.title: In Vitro Blood Clot Mechanical Properties are Associated with Fibrinogen and White Blood Cell Subtypes in Addition to Hematocrit and Sex.
cards.abstract: Understanding the role of blood composition in clot mechanics may provide critical cues toward their diagnosis and treatment. To this end, we previously showed that sex and standard blood composition measures explain some variability in clot mechanics, but much remains unaccounted for. Ours and others' studies largely ignored the roles of fibrinogen and white blood cell (WBC) subtypes, which is surprising given their physiological importance. To develop a more complete understanding of what influences clots' mechanical properties, we now study the role of fibrinogen levels and WBC subtypes in addition to sex and standard blood composition measures. We drew blood from healthy young adults and prepared in vitro clot samples. Using pure shear and mode-I fracture tests, we measured clots' stiffness, fracture toughness, strength, and work to rupture. We then used linear regression to assess associations between blood composition and clot mechanical properties, reporting R 2 to describe the strength of these associations. Fibrinogen shows the strongest associations with clot mechanical properties, positively correlating with all four metrics and achieving the highest average R 2 . For example, fibrinogen is associated with 70% of the variance in stiffness and 78% in fracture toughness. Among WBC subtypes, neutrophils positively correlate with strength and work to rupture, whereas eosinophils negatively correlate with strength. Our work identifies strong associations between fibrinogen levels and WBC subtypes and in vitro clot mechanical properties, relationships that were largely unexplored in whole blood. Future studies should connect these findings to in vivo clot behavior and clinical outcomes.

cards.title: [Conservative treatment of non-unions : Options and limitations].
cards.abstract: Despite modern medical care, non-unions occur in 2-5% of all fractures. The burden on patients involves prolonged rehabilitation and potentially further surgery. Costs for healthcare systems increase substantially. While surgical intervention represents the standard of care, a range of non-surgical treatment options is available. A particular advantage of non-surgical treatment is the avoidance of surgery itself. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound therapy (LIPUS) and the use of pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) are painless and applied by patients themselves once daily. With focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), administration by a physician-usually under general anesthesia-ensures the treatment takes effect precisely at the target site. Bony defects up to 5-10 mm in size can be treated without surgery, provided there is no infection and mechanical stability is adequate.

cards.title: Is a Higher Modified Frailty Index Associated with Increased Complications in Breast Reduction? A Single Center Retrospective Analysis of 1716 Patients.
cards.abstract: Macromastia is associated with significant physical symptoms and reduced quality of life. Although reduction mammaplasty is an effective, the role of frailty in predicting postoperative complications remains uncertain. To evaluate whether the five-factor modified Frailty Index (mFI-5) predicts postoperative complications following reduction mammaplasty, and to identify independent risk factors. This retrospective cohort study included 1,716 consecutive female patients who underwent bilateral breast reduction at a single center (2005-2024). Patients were stratified into low (mFI-5 ≤1, n=1,589) and high (mFI-5 ≥2, n=127) frailty groups. The primary outcome was any postoperative complication within 30 days. Secondary outcome were specific complications requiring surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors. High frailty patients were older, had higher BMI, and more comorbidities. High frailty group had significantly higher overall complication rates (22.2% vs. 14.9%; p=0.031), including wound dehiscence, hemorrhage requiring transfusion, and nipple-areola complex necrosis. However, mFI-5 was not an independent predictor of complications (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.62-2.33; p=0.588). Higher BMI (OR 1.09; p=0.007) and active smoking (OR 1.68; p=0.008) were the only independent predictors identified. The mFI-5 was associated with postoperative complications in unadjusted analysis, but this association was substantially explained by the higher prevalence of obesity and smoking in the high-frailty group and did not persist after multivariable adjustment. BMI and smoking remain the principal modifiable risk factors for preoperative optimization, supporting the need for more comprehensive frailty assessment tools in future studies.

cards.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Markers of Healthy Aging: A Systematic Review of Biological and Functional Outcomes.
cards.abstract: Aging involves molecular, cellular, and functional changes that increase vulnerability to chronic disease, cognitive decline, frailty, and loss of independence. Mediterranean-style dietary patterns are generally rich in plant foods, unsaturated fats, fiber, and bioactive compounds, but their composition varies across studies and may include modified or multicomponent interventions. This Systematic Review evaluated associations between Mediterranean-style dietary adherence and related interventions and markers of healthy aging, including biological aging biomarkers, cognition, frailty, physical performance, and overall health status. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published during 2013- 2025. Searches were conducted in April 2025 and updated in August 2025. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251107773). Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies in adults were eligible if they assessed Mediterranean-style dietary patterns or interventions and reported aging-related biomarkers or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently conducted study selection and data extraction. Eleven studies were included: 5 RCTs, 4 prospective cohort studies, and 2 cross-sectional studies. Greater adherence was associated with better cognitive performance and slower memory decline in some studies. Favorable findings were also reported for telomere dynamics, epigenetic age, and inflammatory biomarkers. Improvements in frailty and physical performance were mainly observed in interventions combining dietary modification with physical activity. Heterogeneity in dietary definitions, adherence measures, intervention components, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. The evidence suggests that favorable associations exist between Mediterranean-style dietary patterns and selected markers of healthy aging but does not establish uniform or causal effects. Interpretation is limited by methodological heterogeneity, self-reported dietary exposure, and the inclusion of modified or multicomponent interventions. Long-term studies using standardized dietary definitions, harmonized outcomes, objective adherence measures, and designs capable of isolating diet-specific effects are needed. cards.title: Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs.
cards.abstract: Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.

cards.title: From Hunterian to Hunterian: the posterior malleolar fracture.
cards.abstract: The posterior malleolar fracture (PMF) is now understood through three-dimensional imaging and mechanism-based classification, yet this understanding is not new. We argue that its central mechanism (rotation of an axially loaded talus within the ankle mortise) was inferred by Bonnin three-quarters of a century ago, obscured by an era of radiographic, size-based description, and later confirmed and made visible by computed tomography (CT). This continuity is frequently overlooked in the wider literature. We present a narrative review of the primary historical literature alongside contemporary CT-based and cadaveric studies. Bonnin's cadaveric experiments showed that a rotating, axially loaded talus behaves as a wedge within the mortise, splitting the posterior tibial margin (the injury we now term a rotational pilon fracture) and he held that damage to the plafond, not the size of the fragment, determined the prognosis. Attention later shifted to the proportion of articular surface involved - a quantity poorly measured on radiographs and divorced from mechanism. CT has since reintroduced the mechanism in living patients: the Mason-Molloy classification describes three pathomechanical types that confirm and refine Bonnin's observations, and management has moved from size thresholds to classification-guided fixation. Bonnin and Mason, two Hunterian Professors separated by more than half a century, performed essentially the same investigation with the tools available to them and reached the same conclusion. Recognising that the modern classification visualises a mechanism Bonnin had already inferred (rotation of a loaded talus) restores a continuity the wider literature has largely missed.

cards.title: Unraveling the Pathogenesis of Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw.
cards.abstract: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious complication associated with bone-modifying and antiangiogenic therapies. As the use of these agents expands in osteoporosis management and cancer care, the population at risk of MRONJ is increasing. Despite its substantial clinical burden, effective prevention and treatment remain limited by an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis and of the biological features that may confer susceptibility to the jaws. This review critically synthesizes current evidence across five potentially interacting pathogenic domains: impaired bone remodeling, compromised vascular and lymphatic support, impaired oral soft-tissue healing, microbial dysbiosis and biofilm formation, and immune dysregulation. Systemic comorbidities and concomitant therapies are also considered as potential modifiers of disease susceptibility and clinical course. In addition, we examine jaw-specific susceptibility by integrating evidence from developmental biology, comparative anatomy, cellular pharmacology, and local osteoimmune biology. Together, these observations support a multifactorial model of MRONJ in which drug-specific effects interact with local tissue characteristics and host factors, while the temporal sequence and relative contribution of individual mechanisms remain incompletely defined. A more precise understanding of these interactions may improve risk stratification and inform future preventive and therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Perioperative Single-Shot Regional Blocks and Associated Rebound Pain-Related Unscheduled Utilization of Health Care After Distal Radius Surgery.
cards.abstract: Perioperative single-shot regional blocks are commonly used for pain control in outpatient distal radius fixation surgery. While regional blocks provide initial postoperative pain control, patients often experience significant rebound pain as the block effect dissipates, which can lead to utilization of unscheduled health care (emergency department visits, phone calls, and messages sent via the electronic health record [EHR] to providers). We hypothesized that patients who received perioperative blocks are more likely to use unscheduled health care versus those who did not. A total of 619 patients underwent distal radius fracture fixation at a tertiary care academic center from 2013 to 2022. After excluding minors, inpatient and revision procedures, patients with insufficient records, and fixation of an impending pathologic fracture, 417 patients were included. Age, gender, mechanism, time to surgery, use of intraoperative local anesthetic, and whether a regional block was performed were collected. Returns to the emergency department, pain-related phone calls, and messages sent via the EHR system within 3 days of surgery were also collected. The adjusted relative risk of using unscheduled health care for pain was 4.0 (95% CI, 1.3-12.1; P = .01) on postoperative day 1 for patients who received perioperative blocks compared with those who did not. Similarly, the adjusted relative risk within 2 days of surgery was 3.9 (95% CI, 1.4-10.5; P = .007) and within 3 days was 3.2 (95% CI, 1.4-7.5; P = .008). Patients who receive perioperative regional blocks after distal radius fixation are more likely to use unscheduled health care within the first 3 days of surgery, compared with patients who did not receive blocks.

cards.title: Integrated multi-omics network by physical exercise across aging: molecular adaptation beyond single signaling pathways
cards.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive molecular dysregulation across interconnected biological systems, involving alterations in epigenetic regulation, gene expression, protein homeostasis, and metabolic function. Although physical exercise is widely recognized as one of the most effective nonpharmacological interventions to promote healthy aging, the integrative molecular mechanisms underlying its systemic effects remain incompletely understood. This review proposes a multi-omic framework in which exercise acts as a coordinated biological stimulus capable of remodeling age-associated molecular dysfunction across genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic layers. We discuss evidence showing that exercise modulates DNA methylation patterns associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and tissue regeneration. Epigenetically, exercise is associated with attenuation of age-associated hypermethylation in promoter regions and modulation of genes involved in oxidative stress defense and tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic studies further show that exercise is associated with more youthful expression patterns while attenuating inflammatory and senescence-related gene programs. Proteomic studies reveal that training is associated with mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and muscle contractile protein abundance, reducing proteostatic dysfunction. Metabolomic analyses demonstrate that exercise improves metabolic flexibility and remodels cellular energy networks. Importantly, the unique contribution of this review lies in synthesizing emerging evidence that these adaptations are highly cell- and tissue-specific, involving immune cells, skeletal muscle satellite cells, endothelial cells, microglia, and intestinal stem cells. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, exercise may induce convergent adaptations across interconnected molecular systems, supporting the concept that healthy aging is dynamically regulated and that age-associated molecular dysfunction retains a degree of biological plasticity.

cards.title: Stochastic failure accumulation as a foundation for exponential mortality and selective disappearance
cards.abstract: Most organisms become increasingly likely to die as they grow older, a phenomenon known as demographic senescence. We develop a general mathematical framework for modelling senescence in which individuals are viewed as comprising a fixed number of interacting intra-organismal sub-systems, each characterised by stochastic failure and repair rates. In many organisms, `failure begets failure' because sub-systems are typically interdependent. We use diffusion approximations to derive an expression for population-level mortality curves in this setting, and demonstrate that greater interdependence leads to faster rates of senescence. Since individuals who die can no longer age, observed cohorts become increasingly composed of `lucky' individuals that avoided death by (stochastically) taking paths in failure space associated with lower mortality despite no intrinsic differences in their quality. Selective disappearance of `unlucky' individuals generates deviations of population-level measurements from individual-level trajectories, causing late-life mortality plateaus. We show that while these deviations must always exist, they may often be too small to detect, either because the failure accumulation process is stereotyped or because detection requires unreasonably large cohort sizes. We provide necessary and asymptotically sufficient conditions for Gompertz-Makeham mortality in our framework, with falsifiable predictions in terms of a scaling law for mortality near complete failure. We also show that the simplest null model in our framework leads to exact Gompertz-Makeham curves. Our work establishes a general framework for modelling demographic senescence and selective disappearance from biological first principles, and provides concrete predictions for when Gompertz-Makeham mortality emerges in such models.

cards.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
cards.abstract: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength. Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Cross-sectional. Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728). CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3). Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis. Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated. Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women. In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

cards.title: Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula alleviates hepatic fibrosis in acute-on-chronic liver failure by regulating ferritinophagy-mediated hepatic stellate cell senescence.
cards.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) represents a severe clinical syndrome characterized by rapid exacerbation of chronic hepatic disease. Liver fibrosis (LF) significantly contributes to the advancement of ACLF pathology. The traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) preparation Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula (YQJPF) exhibits promising therapeutic effects on ACLF and LF; however, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms and active components remain incompletely understood. This study seeks to elucidate the pharmacodynamic properties, active constituents, and underlying mechanisms of YQJPF in treating liver fibrosis within an ACLF rat model, focusing specifically on ferritinophagy activation and the induction of hepatic stellate cell (HSC) senescence. A rat model of ACLF was induced via combined administration of CCl4 and LPS/D-GalN, and an in vitro model was established using human hepatic stellate cells (LX2). Liver-targeted active components were characterized using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis, with network pharmacology utilized to predict critical molecular targets. NCOA4 siRNA and ferrostatin-1 were used to validate mechanism specificity. The therapeutic effects and associated mechanisms were systematically evaluated through biochemical assays, histopathological examinations, and molecular and cellular analyses. YQJPF improved liver histopathology and attenuated fibrosis and ACLF in rats. It inhibited viability and proliferation of LX2 cells, decreased TGF-β1 secretion, and downregulated α-SMA and Collagen I expression. UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 82 liver-tropic components (including 50 prototypes and 32 metabolites) in rat liver tissues. Network pharmacology revealed 257 potential targets, with 135 overlapping with hepatic fibrosis-related targets (core targets included TP53, NCOA4, and CDKN2A). YQJPF induced HSC senescence (upregulated p16, p21, and HMGA1; downregulated TERT; triggered cell cycle arrest) and activated ferritinophagy (upregulated NCOA4, Beclin1, LC3BII/I; downregulated FTH1 and p62; increased ROS/iron accumulation). NCOA4 knockdown or Fer-1 treatment reduced YQJPF-induced HSC senescence and antifibrotic effects. YQJPF reduces ACLF-related LF by NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, which promotes HSC senescence. The 82 liver-tropic components and 135 overlapping targets highlight its multi-component, multi-target effects, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application.

cards.title: 4'-Hydroxywogonin Attenuates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Suppressing Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT Signaling.
cards.abstract: 4'-Hydroxywogonin, a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanism in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-tumor effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin and its regulatory role in Gas6/Axl-associated signaling. Human HCC cells were used to evaluate proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, senescence, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, molecular docking, and thermal shift analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanism, and antitumor efficacy and safety were further examined in a mouse xenograft model. 4'-Hydroxywogonin significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing G1-phase arrest, apoptosis, and senescence. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses identified Axl as a key affected target. 4'-Hydroxywogonin reduced Gas6 and Axl expression, suppressed PI3K/AKT activation, and downregulated cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between 4'-hydroxywogonin and Axl, which was supported by thermal shift analysis. Axl overexpression partially rescued the inhibitory effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin, suggesting involvement of Axl-dependent and additional pathways. In vivo, 4'-hydroxywogonin markedly reduced tumor growth with efficacy comparable to sorafenib and without evident hepatotoxicity. These findings indicate that 4'-hydroxywogonin suppresses HCC progression, at least in part, through inhibition of the Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, supporting its further development as a natural therapeutic candidate.

cards.title: Editorial Commentary: Arthroscopic Bony Bankart Fixation Stands the Test of Time-Preserve Native Glenoid Anatomy When You Can!
cards.abstract: Bony Bankart lesions provide an opportunity to restore native glenoid anatomy through direct fragment fixation. Arthroscopic bony Bankart repair can provide long-term shoulder stability, high patient satisfaction, and sustained participation in sport. Although we prefer double-row bridge fixation for its broad compression across the fracture bed, rotational control, and biomechanically stronger fixation, a properly indicated and well-executed single-row repair can achieve excellent results. Latarjet and other glenoid bone-augmentation procedures remain important options for patients with attritional or irreparable bone loss and high-risk bipolar lesions. However, increasing enthusiasm for these procedures should not displace anatomic repair when a viable bony Bankart fragment can be mobilized, anatomically reduced, and securely fixed. When native glenoid anatomy can be reliably restored, arthroscopic bony Bankart fixation is an effective and durable treatment.

cards.title: HCT-FS-Defined Frailty Is Associated With Lower Survival Across Diverse Hematologic Diagnoses After Allogeneic Transplantation.
cards.abstract: To evaluate whether Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Frailty Scale (HCT-FS)-defined frailty predicts overall survival (OS), nonrelapse mortality (NRM), and relapse across diverse hematologic diagnoses undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (alloHCT), including nonmalignant disorders. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of 992 adults undergoing alloHCT at 16 centers in Canada and Spain (2018-2023). Frailty was assessed at consultation using the HCT-FS (fit, prefrail, frail). OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier, competing-risks methods by cumulative incidence. Multivariable models assessed associations with OS and NRM. Frailty was assessed across six diagnostic categories, including nonmalignant disorders (4.8%). At consultation, 32.1% were fit, 54.7% prefrail, and 13.2% frail. Increasing frailty was associated with progressively lower 2-year OS (78.9%, 66.0%, 51.7%; p < 0.001) and higher 2-year NRM (10.5%, 18.9%, 33.2%; p < 0.001; HR 1.77 [95% CI 1.21-2.60] prefrail and 3.65 [2.36-5.65] frail vs. fit), while 2-year relapse incidence did not differ (19.0%, 23.5%, 22.3%; p = 0.229). Disease-specific estimates were exploratory and limited by small subgroup sizes. HCT-FS-defined frailty is associated with OS and NRM but not relapse in this multicenter alloHCT cohort. Larger disease-specific studies are needed to establish its prognostic value in less represented indications.

cards.title: A transient decrease in night-to-night variability of REM sleep before myocardial infarction
cards.abstract: Background. Myocardial infarction (MI) outcomes depend on time to treatment, and fatigue and sleep disturbance are often reported in the weeks before the event. Whether wearable-measured sleep changes within individuals before MI, and whether such change is specific to MI, is unknown. Methods. In the All of Us Research Program, adults with a first MI code and at least 180 valid Fitbit sleep nights in the preceding 360 days were matched to up to 10 controls on sex, comorbidities, sleep apnea, calendar time and a propensity score. The full matched cohort of all cases was the primary cohort, and cases with diabetes and/or hypertension formed a subgroup. The main endpoints were the within-person change in night-to-night variability (SD, RMSSD, CV) of the REM-sleep fraction at days 30-16 relative to each persons baseline (days 360-121) and from days 30-16 to days 15-1, tested against 10,000 randomly placed index dates with allowance for the choice of window (max-T). The same pipeline was applied to cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, to an index date at the first angina code, to a cohort including heart failure and to ischaemic stroke and admissions for heart failure, pneumonia, fracture or appendicitis and any cause, and the analysis was adjusted for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Results. The full matched cohort comprised 45 cases and 450 controls. REM-fraction variability changed transiently before MI, decreasing at days 30-16 and returning towards baseline over days 15-1; allowing for the choice of window, this decrease-then-return pattern was rarely matched at 10,000 randomly placed index dates (max-T p<0.001). Its components were the decrease in SD at days 30-16 (Cliffs {delta} -0.30, p=0.004; OR per SD 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.80; max-T p=0.0034) and the return in RMSSD over days 15-1 ({delta} +0.36, p<0.001; max-T p=0.0035); day by day, the decrease was not detected as a continuous change (cluster permutation test p=0.58). The decrease in SD was not seen at the same time before admissions for pneumonia (69 cases), fracture or appendicitis (130) or any cause (859) and was larger before MI than before each of them (difference in {delta} -0.25 to -0.34), whereas the rise over days 15-1 was shared with pneumonia; it was of similar size in the subgroup with diabetes and/or hypertension, in cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, with the index date at the first angina code, when people with heart failure were included and after adjustment for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Scoring each person against their own baseline discriminated cases from controls with AUCs of up to 0.66, probably an optimistic estimate because the decrease in RMSSD was attenuated in held-out halves of the matched sets. Conclusions. In adults who use consumer wearables, a first MI was preceded by a transient change in night-to-night REM-sleep variability, a decrease at days 30-16 and a return over the following two weeks. The decrease was not seen at the same time before other acute admissions, did not depend on recorded symptoms or treatment and was detectable against each persons own baseline with simple measures. The timing is an exploratory finding, to be confirmed in new cases.

cards.title: [Emphasizing the damage and repair of bone collagen in osteoporosis].
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized not only by reduced bone mass but also by impaired structure and function of the bone matrix and bone collagen. Although conventional bone mineral density assessment can reflect the level of bone mineralization, it cannot fully capture bone quality and the biomechanical performance of bone tissue. Bone collagen plays a critical role in maintaining bone tissue toughness, energy-absorbing capacity and the stability of bone microarchitecture. Its abnormal cross-linking, degradation and defective repair are closely associated with increased bone fragility. This article focuses on the roles and values of bone collagen in osteoporosis, elaborates on bone collagen-related pathological changes, influencing factors, and its mechanisms in osteoporotic fractures, and introduces the latest diagnostic and therapeutic technologies as well as future development directions. It highlights the great value of establishing a "mineralized-collagen two-dimensional" bone-quality evaluation system that takes both bone mineralization and bone collagen status into account, providing new insights for the precise diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fractures.

cards.title: Sonic hedgehog-matrix metalloproteinase crosstalk in neurovascular ageing and stroke: a potential mechanistic link.
cards.abstract: Neurovascular ageing is a major contributor to cerebrovascular vulnerability and poor stroke outcomes in older adults. Progressive deterioration of the neurovascular unit (NVU), driven by oxidative stress, neurovascular coupling dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, inflammageing, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy compromises neurovascular resilience and increases susceptibility to ischemic injury. Among the molecular pathways implicated in these processes, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are important regulators of neurovascular remodeling, BBB integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Although these pathways have largely been investigated independently, emerging evidence suggests potential bidirectional interactions between Shh signaling and MMP activity. In particular, Shh/Gli1 signaling has been associated with regulation of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in experimental models, whereas MMP-2 can disrupt SCUBE2, an extracellular regulator of Shh ligand presentation, providing a potential mechanism for reciprocal pathway modulation. This review examines the Shh-MMP axis as a potential mechanistic link between neurovascular ageing and ischemic vulnerability, integrating current evidence to evaluate how dysregulation of these pathways may contribute to BBB dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, neuroinflammation, and impaired neurovascular repair. We further discuss the potential therapeutic implications of modulating the Shh-MMP axis to preserve neurovascular resilience and improve cerebrovascular outcomes in the ageing brain, while highlighting the importance of temporal and cell-specific targeting.

cards.title: Association between remaining teeth and femoral neck bone mineral density in patients undergoing dialysis.
cards.abstract: Assessing bone mineral density and implementing fracture prevention measures are useful in managing dialysis patients. This study aimed to assess oral health, including the number of remaining teeth, and to investigate factors associated with the young adult mean (%YAM) of the femur and lumbar spine in this population. This cross-sectional study included 110 patients who initiated dialysis treatment at our hospital and underwent panoramic radiography, oral assessments and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans of the femur and lumbar spine within one month. Associations between oral health and YAM were examined using univariate and multivariable analyses, with the latter focusing on femoral YAM because of potential artefacts affecting lumbar measurements. In the univariate analysis, femoral YAM was significantly associated with sex (B = -21.62, p < 0.001), body mass index (BMI; B = 1.926, p < 0.001), and the number of remaining teeth (B = 0.388, p = 0.026). However, in the multivariable analysis, the final model did not include the number of remaining teeth. BMI (B = 1.12, p = 0.005) and sex (B = -18.49, p < 0.001) remained significant factors, with sex showing the strongest association. In incident dialysis patients, fewer remaining teeth were associated with lower femoral YAM in univariate analysis, but this association was not independent of age, sex and BMI in multivariable analysis. Tooth loss may therefore reflect the cumulative effects of these factors rather than representing an independent predictor of bone mineral density.
