cards.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Osteoporosis Treatments on Bone Strength and the Impact of Sequential Anabolic Therapy
cards.abstract: Purpose Evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of osteoporosis treatments in improving bone strength in clinical practice remains limited. This real-world study compared the effectiveness of different osteoporosis treatments in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO), including treatment-naive patients initiating Romo, TPTD, or DMAb (Study 1) and patients switching from one anabolic therapy to another (Study 2). Methods Japanese women with PMO aged >55 years were included. In Study 1, 57, 34, and 50 women received Romo, TPTD, or DMAb, respectively, for 12 months. In Study 2, 16 received Romo for 12 months after TPTD (TPTD-Romo) and 29 received twice-weekly TPTD for 12 months after Romo (Romo-TPTD). The primary and secondary endpoints were average percent change from baseline at 12 months in vertebral bone strength and volumetric BMD (vBMD), respectively, assessed using biomechanical CT analysis (BCT). Results At baseline, overall bone strength and vBMD were comparable across groups in both studies. In Study 1, average percent change (95% CI) in vertebral strength was highest with Romo (39.5% [34.2, 44.7]), followed by TPTD (24.4% [18.8, 30.0]), and DMAb (10.9% [7.6, 14.2]). In Study 2, vertebral strength increased by 16.1% (10.6, 21.6) with TPTD-Romo, and decreased by 7.7% (-10.7, -4.6) with Romo-TPTD despite subsequent TPTD treatment. Similar trends were observed for vertebral vBMD. Conclusion In this real-world BCT study, Romo showed greater increases in both vertebral bone strength and density versus TPTD and DMAb in treatment-naive women with PMO. Among prior TPTD, Romo further increased bone strength and density; however, twice-weekly TPTD failed to maintain the gains following prior Romo.

cards.title: Immediate weight bearing after dual orthogonal plate fixation of clavicle fractures: a propensity-matched retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: To evaluate whether immediate weight bearing as tolerated (WBAT) following open reduction and internal fixation of clavicle fractures with a dual mini-fragmentation plate construct increases complications, implant failure, or worsens functional and patient-reported outcomes compared to a restricted weight-bearing protocol. Adult patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent open reduction and internal fixation of a clavicle fracture were retrospectively identified and stratified into restricted weight-bearing or weight bearing as tolerated (WBAT) cohorts. Cohorts were matched for demographic and injury characteristics. All WBAT fractures were treated with dual orthogonal mini-fragmentation plate fixation, whereas restricted weight-bearing fractures were treated with either single- or dual-plate fixation. Outcomes included complications (infection, wound dehiscence, hardware prominence, implant failure, and loss of reduction) and PROMIS Physical Function and Pain Interference scores. Among 378 initial patients, 93 were included after propensity score matching: 62 in the restricted weight-bearing group and 31 in the WBAT group. Complication rates were similarly infrequent between groups (all p ≥ 0.326), with no fixation failures or deep surgical site infections occurring in the WBAT group. Early weight bearing as tolerated may be safe following dual mini-fragmentation plate fixation of clavicle fractures, with comparable complication rates, union rates, and patient-reported outcomes to restricted weight-bearing protocols. These findings support the use of early mobilization in patients with rigid internal fixation constructs and may facilitate improved functional recovery and earlier return to activity.

cards.title: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for a Neglected Type III Fracture of the Anterior Process of the Calcaneus in a Collegiate Hurdler: A Case Report.
cards.abstract: BackgroundFractures of the anterior process of the calcaneus (APC) are frequently misdiagnosed as ankle sprains and may progress to symptomatic nonunion. Degan type III APC fractures involve the calcaneocuboid joint and are conventionally managed surgically. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) has not previously been reported for this fracture type.Case presentationA 21-year-old male collegiate hurdler presented with a 2-year history of left lateral foot pain. Computed tomography confirmed a neglected Degan type III APC nonunion. After declining surgery, he underwent 9 sessions of focused ESWT (peak energy flux density 0.07-0.25 mJ/mm²) in 3-session sets over 19 weeks, combined with a 3-month sports restriction from the start of treatment. Pain resolved completely (visual analog scale 75/100 → 0/100), and he returned to competitive hurdling at 6 months after starting ESWT. Computed tomography at 14 months after ESWT initiation confirmed bony bridging.ConclusionExtracorporeal shock wave therapy was associated with clinical improvement and radiological healing in this individual case and may warrant further investigation as a non-surgical option in young athletes with a neglected Degan type III APC nonunion who decline surgery.

cards.title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
cards.abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.

cards.title: Dioscin attenuates aniline-induced liver injury by targeting the ACOT2-mediated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis and restoring mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and lysosomal lipophagy.
cards.abstract: Chronic aniline exposure causes prominent hepatotoxicity accompanied by hepatic lipid metabolic disorders and cellular senescence, yet the molecular cascade underlying aniline-triggered liver injury remains unclear. Here, a 90-day chronic aniline intoxication mouse model and an AML12 murine hepatocyte model were established to systematically dissect toxic mechanisms and identify candidate hepatoprotective agents. Adverse outcome pathway analysis revealed lipid metabolic disturbance and cellular senescence as core toxic events, with lipid metabolic disturbance acting as an upstream driver of aniline-induced hepatocyte senescence and injury. Integrated multi-omics analysis showed that acyl-CoA thioesterase 2 (ACOT2), a key rate-limiting enzyme in fatty acid β-oxidation, was markedly downregulated in aniline-damaged livers. Hepatic ACOT2 overexpression restored mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation capacity, alleviated lipid overload, excessive ROS accumulation and hepatic dysfunction, and reduced bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP) accumulation by suppressing neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis protein 5 (CLN5) expression. Mechanistically, ACOT2 deficiency caused ROS overproduction and activated JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Phosphorylated STAT3 translocated into the nucleus and directly bound the Cln5 promoter, enhancing its transcription. Elevated CLN5 disrupted lysosomal structural integrity and acidification, thereby blocking lipid degradation during lipophagy. Conversely, Cln5 silencing restored lysosomal homeostasis and autophagic flux and reduced hepatic lipid deposition. Virtual screening identified dioscin as a natural small molecule that directly interacts with ACOT2, as confirmed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance assays. PPARα-dependent transcriptional regulation contributed to ACOT2 suppression across multiple liver injury models, whereas dioscin restored ACOT2-dependent fatty acid oxidation and conferred broad hepatoprotection against aniline-, CCl4-, and APAP-induced liver injury. Collectively, this study reveals, in male mice and murine hepatocyte models, a previously unreported ACOT2-regulated ROS-JAK2/STAT3-CLN5 axis linking impaired mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation, lysosomal dysfunction and defective lipid clearance during aniline hepatotoxicity. These findings further support dioscin as a promising hepatoprotective candidate drug that directly targets ACOT2.

cards.title: Prevalence of Sarcopenic Obesity and Agreement Between Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis and Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry in Children with Idiopathic Nephrotic Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) is an increasingly recognised nutritional complication of chronic paediatric disease. Children with idiopathic nephrotic syndrome (INS) are predisposed to adverse body composition changes from persistent proteinuria, relapses, and corticosteroid exposure, but the prevalence of SO in this population is unknown. We aimed to determine SO prevalence, characterise body composition and bone health by SO status, and assess agreement between bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in children with INS. This cross-sectional study enrolled 128 children aged 3-16 years with INS in complete remission. Sarcopenia was defined as fat-free mass index below the 25th percentile (Indian reference standards); obesity was defined by BMI and by DXA-derived fat mass index above the 99th percentile. SO was therefore defined on body composition criteria alone, without functional muscle assessment, and is referred to as body composition-defined SO. All participants underwent simultaneous DXA and BIA. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient, Bland-Altman analysis with formal testing for proportional bias, and Cohen's kappa, with Pearson correlation reported descriptively. Because the Indian reference datasets do not span the full age range enrolled, the primary analysis was repeated in the subgroup covered by both references (6.0-15.0 years, n = 92). Sarcopenia was present in 46.9% (60/128) and obesity in 14.1% (BMI) versus 43.0% (DXA). SO occurred in 17.2% (22/128; 95% CI 10.6-23.8) by DXA criteria; no child met BMI-based SO criteria. In the subgroup covered by both reference datasets, SO prevalence was 13.0% (12/92; 95% CI 6.2-19.9). Children with SO were younger, with shorter disease duration, fewer relapses, and lower corticosteroid dose, and had lower whole-body BMC and BMD (both p < 0.001) despite comparable BMD Z-scores; these absolute bone differences did not persist after adjustment for age and height. BIA correlated strongly with DXA for fat-free mass (r = 0.964) and fat mass (r = 0.943) but systematically underestimated fat mass (mean bias -3.38 kg) and body fat percentage (-11.24%) and overestimated fat-free mass (+2.75 kg), with significant proportional bias for every compartment (all p < 0.001) and 0% sensitivity for DXA-confirmed SO (0/22; 95% CI 0.0-15.4). Body composition-defined SO affected roughly one in six children with INS in remission and was not detected by BMI. Within this cohort, across device and operational thresholds, BIA ranked continuous body composition well but did not reproduce the DXA-based SO classification. These estimates apply to body composition-defined SO and require confirmation in longitudinal, multicentre cohorts incorporating muscle function testing.

cards.title: Biological frailty and chemotherapy dose intensity independently predict survival in older adults with Stage II-III colon cancer.
cards.abstract: To evaluate the prognostic impact of chemotherapy dose intensity and frailty indices-including the laboratory-based Frailty Index (FI-Lab)-on survival in older adults with stage II-III colon cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy. This retrospective study included 94 patients aged ≥ 65 years with stage II (high-risk) or stage III colon cancer treated with adjuvant chemotherapy after curative surgery. Frailty was assessed using FI-Lab with a predefined cut-off of 0.25. Measures included the G8 geriatric screening tool, modified 5-item Frailty Index (mFI-5), and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Patients were categorised as optimal dose completed, optimal dose started with subsequent reduction, or not started at the optimal dose. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. With a median follow-up of 70 months, 28 recurrences (29.8%) and 22 deaths (23.4%) occurred. FI-Lab ≥ 0.25 independently predicted inferior OS (HR: 3.73; p = 0.023) and DFS (HR: 2.81; p = 0.029). G8, mFI-5, and CCI were not independently associated with survival. Dose initiation strategy was also independently associated with outcomes. Compared with the optimal dose completed group, patients not started at the optimal dose had worse OS (HR: 14.41; p = 0.011) and DFS (HR: 5.16; p = 0.013), whereas dose reduction after optimal initiation was not associated with survival. Laboratory-based frailty and initial dose intensity independently predicted survival in older adults receiving adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer. These findings support individualised treatment strategies integrating biological reserve and early treatment intensity.

cards.title: Association between the frequency of achieving recommended daily step counts and a decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a 4-year prospective study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort study.
cards.abstract: Achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week significantly reduced the risk of decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal women, but not in postmenopausal women. Less frequent achievement (1-2 days/week) showed no significant association in either group. To examine the association between the frequency of achieving the recommended daily step count (7000 steps/day) and the incidence of a decline in quantitative ultrasound (QUS) measurements among pre- and postmenopausal women. In this prospective cohort study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort, baseline and follow-up surveys were conducted between 2013-2016 and 2017-2021 (mean follow-up: 42.5 months). Participants were 3529 women (1013 premenopausal, 2516 postmenopausal). Daily steps were objectively measured using pedometers. The number of days per week achieving 7000 steps was categorized as Inactive (0 days), Low active (1-2 days), and Active (≥3 days). The outcome was the incidence of a decline in QUS measurements, defined as a QUS T-score ≤-2.5 or a self-reported diagnosis of osteoporosis. Adjusted risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using modified Poisson regression models, with the Inactive group as the reference. During follow-up, the outcome occurred in 70 premenopausal and 662 postmenopausal women. In premenopausal women, the Active group had a significantly lower risk of the outcome compared to the Inactive group (RR: 0.478, 95% CI: 0.271 to 0.843). In postmenopausal women, no statistically significant association was observed (RR for the Active group: 0.937, 95% CI: 0.807 to 1.088). The findings suggest that the association appeared to differ by menopausal status, achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week was associated with a significantly reduced risk of a decline in QUS measurements in premenopausal women. However, for postmenopausal women, walking alone may be an insufficient strategy.

cards.title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis.
cards.abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) are critical regulators of vascular function and exhibit tissue-specialized roles. During aging, these cells become dysfunctional, resulting in increased susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. Although single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive endothelial heterogeneity, a comprehensive atlas of human EC transcriptomes over the course of the adult human lifespan has been lacking. Here, we present the Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas (HAECA), a harmonized single-cell transcriptomic compendium of over 375,000 ECs from 12 human tissues throughout adulthood. We identified age-associated transcriptional shifts, including a decline in angiogenic gene expression in venous ECs and widespread alterations in extracellular matrix and mechanotransduction-associated signatures. Furthermore, we uncovered a p21-linked transcriptional program in ECs, which we linked to cellular senescence in both in vitro and in vivo models. Together, our study provides a high-resolution transcriptomic reference of the human endothelium across tissues and age.

cards.title: Mitochondria-targeted esculetin mitigates age-associated cardiac remodeling through coordinated activation of AMPK-SIRT1 and inhibition of p38 MAPK signaling.
cards.abstract: Age-associated cardiac remodeling, characterized by hypertrophy and fibrosis, is a major contributor to cardiovascular morbidity in the elderly and is often exacerbated by metabolic stressors such as hypercholesterolemia. Given the central role of mitochondrial dysfunction in these processes, we investigated whether mitochondria-targeted esculetin (Mito-Esc) could mitigate pathological cardiac remodeling associated with aging and hypercholesterolemia. To model this condition, we utilized 12-month-old Apoe-/- mice, which exhibit chronic hypercholesterolemia and develop age-related cardio-metabolic structural alterations. The efficacy of Mito-Esc was compared with metformin, a putative geroprotective agent. Treatment with Mito-Esc or metformin significantly attenuated cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in aged Apoe-/- mice. These protective effects were further validated in vitro using H9c2 cardiomyocytes and primary adult mouse cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, both Mito-Esc and metformin exerted cardioprotective effects through activation of the AMPK-SIRT1 signaling axis. Depletion of either AMPK or SIRT1 markedly reduced the ability of these compounds to suppress cellular senescence, hypertrophic responses, and fibrotic signaling, indicating a critical role for this pathway. AMPK functioned upstream of SIRT1, as SIRT1 activation was attenuated following AMPK depletion. In parallel, both compounds significantly suppressed p38 MAPK activation. While depletion of AMPK or SIRT1 did not affect p38 MAPK activity, pharmacological inhibition of p38 MAPK enhanced AMPK and SIRT1 activation, supporting a model in which p38 MAPK activation negatively regulates the AMPK-SIRT1 axis. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Mito-Esc alleviates pathological cardiac remodeling in the setting of aging and hypercholesterolemia through coordinated activation of AMPK-SIRT1 signaling and inhibition of p38 MAPK.

cards.title: Longitudinal Association Between Prefrailty/Frailty and HIV-associated Neurocognitive Disorder (HAND): a Mexican Prospective Study.
cards.abstract: Geriatric syndromes such as frailty may be more prevalent and occur earlier in people aging with HIV, negatively impacting outcomes like cognition. Cross-sectional data show strong associations between pre-frailty/frailty and HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). However, prospective studies suggest baseline HAND increases frailty risk, while pre-frailty/frailty do not predict HAND onset. We aimed to investigate longitudinal association between baseline frailty and HAND category progression. Longitudinal analysis of 194 participants aged ≥50 years from Mexico City referral center. Two standardized geriatric assessments performed at least one year apart. HAND defined using Antinori criteria, frailty by Fried phenotype. Inverse probability weighted Cox models adjusted for confounders from directed acyclic graph (age, educational level, detectable viral load, diabetes, stroke, ischemic heart disease) determined association between frailty and HAND progression. Median age 55 (53-61) years; 167 (86%) men; median follow-up 2.3 (1.6-3.1) years. Baseline: 129 (66.4%) robust, 62 (31.9%) pre-frail, 3 (1.5%) frail. No longitudinal association between pre-frailty/frailty and HAND progression was observed in this cohort (32 progression events; adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.27-1.48; p = 0.29). No evidence of a prospective association between prefrailty/frailty and HAND category progression was observed in this cohort; most participants remained cognitively stable. To our knowledge, this is the first study describing HAND trajectories and their relationship with prefrailty/frailty in older adults with HIV in Mexico and Latin America.

cards.title: Age- and sex-specific values of regional bone mineral density from opportunistic CT of the lower lumbar spine, pelvis, sacrum, and proximal femur.
cards.abstract: Standard osteoporosis assessment using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) provides limited 2D measures (BMD, T-score), potentially missing localized bone density differences relevant to fracture risk. Opportunistic CT allows comprehensive 3D volumetric bone density analysis. This study presents a detailed 3D statistical model of CT-derived apparent volumetric bone mineral density (CT-vBMD) covering the L4 and L5 vertebrae, pelvic bones, sacrum, and proximal femur and examines spatial distributions and associations with age and sex. Retrospective analysis included 330 routine abdominal CT scans (ages 20-91; approximately balanced by sex). Bones were segmented with a semi-automated workflow, internally calibrated, registered to bone-specific population templates, and projected onto corresponding tetrahedral meshes. Whole-bone averages were compared across age groups and between sexes. For each element, we calculated mean vBMD, variability, correlations with age and sex, and cluster-defined low-density and age-sensitive subregions. The global spatial pattern was similar in females and males. The highest CT-vBMD values were localized mainly to cortical load-bearing zones, whereas the lowest values were concentrated in trabecular spongiosa. Older age was associated with lower whole-bone CT-vBMD in all bones and with stronger negative associations in trabecular-rich regions, such as the subchondral acetabulum, femoral neck, sacral ala, and vertebral bodies. Cortical-dominant load-bearing regions showed weaker negative associations with age. This framework maps anatomically localized associations between age and CT-vBMD beyond the regions routinely assessed by DXA. Opportunistic CT mapping may complement standard osteoporosis assessment by providing spatial information for the pelvis, sacrum, lower lumbar spine, and proximal femur.

cards.title: CD274 Knockout Promotes Bone Formation and Reduces Osteoclast Activity.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic disease characterized by decreased bone density, and deterioration in the micro-architectural remodelling of bone tissue, leading to an increased susceptibility to bone fractures. One molecule implicated in bone metabolism is Programmed Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1), a pharmacologically targetable immune-checkpoint molecule encoded by the gene Cd274. The aim of this study was to investigate the bone phenotype of Cd274 knockout (KO) mice at 26 weeks of age compared to C57BL/6J control wildtype mice on radiological, histological and biomechanical level. The cortical wall thickness and cortical volume increased, and the trabecular space decreased significantly in both femur and tibia of Cd274 KO mice. Moreover, there was a significant increase in BV/TV and trabecular volume of lumbar vertebrae of Cd274 KO mice. Yield load, stiffness, anorganic amount increased and organic amount decreased significantly in femoral bones of Cd274 KO mice. Additionally, there was a significantly higher number of osteocytes and lower number of osteoclasts in both humerus and lumbar vertebra of Cd274 KO mice. The findings demonstrate that constitutive knockout of Cd274 was associated with significantly increased bone mass and strength. These results-obtained in healthy, skeletally mature constitutive knockout mice-indicate an improved bone phenotype in the absence of Cd274 and thus contrast with previous studies that associate disruption of the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, including immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, with bone loss and increased fracture risk. Further studies, particularly in dedicated osteoporosis models, are required to elucidate the influence of CD274 on bone metabolism before translational conclusions can be drawn.

cards.title: Comparative Evaluation of Dental and Craniofacial Injury Patterns in Conventional and Electric Two-Wheeler Riders in Urban Settings: A Cross-Sectional Survey-Based Study.
cards.abstract: To assess and compare the prevalence and pattern of dental and craniofacial injuries sustained by conventional two-wheeler riders versus electric two-wheeler (e-bike/e-scooter) riders involved in road traffic accidents (RTAs), and to evaluate the role of protective gear, riding practices, and behavioral factors on injury outcomes. Six hundred and fifty-two riders (340 conventional two-wheelers, 312 e-bike/e-scooter) were examined and interviewed from an urban setting using a structured questionnaire. Data encompassed demographics, vehicle type, compliance with protective gears, riding behavior and practices, accident characteristics, and oro-facial injury profile. Chi-square, Fisher's exact tests, and descriptive statistics were applied (significance: p < 0.05). A supplementary binary logistic regression, adjusted for vehicle type, helmet compliance, commercial rider status, age group, usual vehicle speed, and pre-ride training, was performed to identify independent predictors of facial injury. Road traffic accident involvement was significantly more prevalent among e-bike riders than conventional two-wheeler riders (70.8% vs. 47.1%; RR = 1.51; p < 0.001). Among accident cases, facial or oral injuries were significantly more frequent in e-bike riders (72.9%) than in conventional two-wheeler riders (39.4%; OR = 4.13; p < 0.001). Lacerations were the most common injury (39.3%), followed by chipped or broken teeth (21.0%), jaw or facial bone fractures (14.7%), tooth avulsion (9.8%), and tooth displacement/luxation injuries (7.1%). No significant intergroup differences were identified for any individual injury category. Accident rates were similar between commercial and personal use within vehicle groups: E-Bike: 70.6% vs. 71.0% (RR = 0.995; OR = 0.984); Road Bike: 50.0% vs. 45.5% (RR = 1.098; OR = 1.196). Consistent use of protective gear was reported by 72.6% of conventional two-wheeler riders, compared with only 5.8% of e-bike riders (p < 0.001). Pre-ride training was received by 63.8% of conventional riders, compared with 14.7% of e-bike riders. Electric two-wheeler riders demonstrate a markedly higher risk of accidents and orofacial injuries compared with conventional riders. After multivariable adjustment, the association between e-bike riding and injury remained significant (aOR = 4.213, p < 0.001). However, correlated behavioral predictors (such as helmet use and pre-ride training) could not be reliably disentangled. Low helmet compliance and urgency-driven riding behavior among delivery riders in quick commerce represent critical characteristics of the e-bike cohort that warrant further investigation.

cards.title: EXPRESS: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Much ado about eating: Intermittent fasting and post-stroke neuroprotection".
cards.abstract: Vemuganti and colleagues highlight intermittent fasting (IF)'s neuroprotective potential post-stroke via autophagy and mitochondrial biogenesis. However, clinical translation faces hurdles in metabolically vulnerable patients. This letter critiques IF's bedside applicability, emphasizing post-stroke catabolic stress, dysphagia (~50% cases), sarcopenia risk, and cardiovascular concerns. Recent evidence links short eating windows to higher mortality, countering IF benefits. The obesity paradox suggests nutritional reserves aid survival. Strategies: protein-prioritized planning, dysphagia screening, dietitian monitoring, and supplements. Until RCTs confirm safety/efficacy, prioritize nutritional adequacy. Preclinical insights warrant study.Keywords: dysphagia, intermittent fasting, neuroprotection, obesity paradox, sarcopenia.

cards.title: Cellular Senescence Dysregulates Antiviral Interferon Responses in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) are highly vulnerable to respiratory virus infections, but the cellular mechanisms linking fibrotic remodeling to impaired local antiviral defense remain unclear. Here, we investigated how cellular senescence shapes the response of patient‐derived healthy (HLF) and IPF primary lung fibroblasts to influenza A virus (IAV) infection. Transcriptomic profiling identified infection as the driver of gene expression in both DNA damage‐induced senescent HLF and IPF fibroblasts and revealed induction of canonical antiviral pathways in both cell states. However, senescent IPF fibroblasts adopted a distinct antiviral response state characterized by a broader set of uniquely induced genes and differential coordination of antiviral transcriptional networks. Functionally, senescence increased viral titers in HLF and IPF fibroblasts, while senescent IPF fibroblasts displayed an altered inflammatory response. Network analysis linked viral response‐ and cell cycle‐associated modules specifically to the senescent HLF infected state, whereas these programs were weaker in senescent IPF fibroblasts. Transcription factor inference identified IRF3 and STAT1 as candidate regulators of this altered antiviral state in both senescent HLF and IPF fibroblasts. Consistent with the network and transcription factor analyses, siRNA‐mediated depletion of IRF3 or STAT1 significantly reduced IFN‐β secretion in senescent HLF fibroblasts, whereas IPF fibroblasts showed only milder effects, indicating a disease‐specific dependence on these pathways for antiviral control. Together, these findings show that the combination of cellular senescence and fibrotic fibroblast identity creates a dysfunctional antiviral state that may help explain the high susceptibility of IPF patients to virus‐associated acute exacerbations and disease worsening.

cards.title: Key safety outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors versus DPP-4 inhibitors in general and vulnerable participants with T2DM: A target trial emulation study.
cards.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), a class of oral hypoglycaemic agents (OHAs), have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits. However, safety concerns may hinder their broader adoption, particularly among frail populations. We evaluated key safety outcomes associated with SGLT2i compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4i), an OHA class with low risks of complications. We conducted a target trial emulation (TTE) study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) and enrolled participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Eligible participants were categorized according to newly initiated SGLT2i (n = 224,510) or newly initiated DPP4i (n = 698,012) with continuous use for at least 30 days. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the SGLT2i group showed significantly lower incidence rate (per person-years) of several safety outcomes than the DPP4i group, including urinary tract infection (UTI) (23.84‰ vs. 27.88‰; hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.84-0.87), fractures or falls (16.55‰ vs. 17.79‰; HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.91-0.95), acute kidney injury (AKI) (1.06‰ vs. 1.91‰; HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.51-0.59), bullous pemphigoid (0.02‰ vs. 0.07‰; HR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.23-0.54), and all-cause mortality (13.05‰ vs. 19.72‰; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.65-0.67). Conversely, the risk of genital infection was higher in the SGLT2i group (2.96‰ vs. 2.05‰; HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.38-1.51). These findings remained consistent in the per-protocol analysis, across most vulnerable subgroups and individual SGLT2i and DPP4i agents. SGLT2i, compared with DPP4i, demonstrated a favourable safety profile across most evaluated outcomes, except for genital infections.

cards.title: Extracorporeal shockwave therapy in common tendinopathies.
cards.abstract: Extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) was initially used for urologic issues only. After Valchanou and Michailov started applying it in orthopedics in 1991, they focused on treatment of pseudarthrosis and delayed fracture healing. Some years later, shockwave therapy was also used for tendinopathies. Today, ESWT is the first-choice treatment for tendinopathies and is unsurpassed in terms of effectivity and side effects. This article discusses common regions of lower extremity tendinopathies (greater trochanter pain syndrome, quadriceps tendinopathy, patellar tendinopathy, Achilles tendinopathy) in a narrative review of the evidence-based literature and guidelines of leading shockwave societies such as the International Society for Medical Shockwave Treatment (ISMST) and the Deutschsprachige internationale Gesellschaft für Extrakorporale Stosswellentherapie (DIGEST). Additional case studies are also presented. Extracorporeal shockwave therapy shows excellent results in the evidence-based literature and in clinical application. No other conservative treatment option in orthopedics is described as intensively in the evidence-based literature as shockwave therapy. ESWT seems to be more effective when it is accompanied by an eccentric loading/physiotherapy program. Extracorporeal shockwave therapy enables tendon regeneration, long-term improvement, and faster return to sport, with predictable side effects and excellent tolerance.

cards.title: Topical application of urolithin A activates mitophagy and enhances mitochondrial function to promote skin longevity.
cards.abstract: Urolithin A (UA, Mitopure), a postbiotic that promotes mitophagy and mitochondrial function following oral administration, was evaluated for its effects on skin health in human skin models and when applied topically to healthy subjects in randomized clinical studies. UA tested in 2D and 3D reconstructed human skin and ex vivo human skin explants showed enhanced mitochondrial respiration, activated mitophagy markers, reduced inflammatory mediators and senescence-associated markers, and increased proteins involved in extracellular matrix structure and epidermal differentiation. Safety was confirmed in a human repeat-insult patch test. In randomized, placebo-controlled clinical studies, UA reduced periorbital wrinkle depth after 8 weeks and attenuated UVB-induced erythema. Skin transcriptomics supported increased extracellular matrix and epidermal development programs together with decreased inflammatory and senescence-associated signaling. These findings indicate that topical UA engages cellular pathways associated with skin resilience to promote skin health and longevity.

cards.title: Loss of SREBF1 disrupts lipid signaling and causes slow muscle fiber degeneration.
cards.abstract: SREBF1, encoding the lipogenic transcription factor SREBP1, has been linked to lean mass by human genomics. We used a CRISPR-Cas9 srebf1 zebrafish knockout combined with LC-MS/MS lipidomics, RNA-seq, Lugol-enhanced micro-CT imaging, and functional assays. Srebp1 loss disrupted slow-fiber organization, increased locomotion in larvae, and reduced muscle mass in adults. This knockout muscle showed altered fatty acid composition, reduced arachidonoylethanolamide (AEA), elevated palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), broad remodeling of polyunsaturated fatty (PUFA) acid-derived mediators, and differential expression of cardiolipin-pathway genes. Integrated transcriptomic-lipidomic analysis revealed srebf1-centered connections to myogenic regulators and calcium and lipid signaling, paralleling selective atrophy and loss of slow oxidative fibers under overfeeding and aging. Our data supports a model in which Srebp1 functions as a fiber-type-specific survival checkpoint that maintains lipid compositional and cardiolipin homeostasis, and whose disruption reprograms lipid mediators to drive slow-to-fast fiber switching and slow-fiber degeneration relevant to sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity.

cards.title: Association between frailty and multisite chronic pain in middle-aged and older adults: A population-based cross-sectional study with mediation analysis.
cards.abstract: The corrected modified frailty index (CMFI), based on the accumulation of multidimensional health impairments, provides a more comprehensive reflection of an individual's overall frailty. Although chronic pain is associated with aging, its relationship with CMFI, in population-based cohorts remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 5821 participants aged ≥45 years from the 2011 baseline wave of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Chronic pain, including low back pain, multisite pain, and the number of pain sites, was assessed via self-reported questionnaires. Frailty was assessed using the CMFI. Weighted logistic regression models, restricted cubic splines, and mediation analyses were employed to investigate associations and the potential roles of depression and C-reactive protein. Analysing data from 5281 participants, higher CMFI was strongly associated with increased risk and burden of chronic pain. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest CMFI quartile showed significantly higher risks of low back pain (odds ratio = 11.6, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 8.96-15.0), multisite pain (odds ratio = 17.0, 95% CI: 13.1-22.2), and a greater number of pain sites (incidence rate ratio = 11.5, 95% CI: 8.90-14.8). Associations varied across subgroups defined by age, education, and residence. Depression mediated approximately 30% of these associations. Higher CMFI levels were associated with greater risk and burden of chronic pain, with depression potentially accounting for part of the association. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating mental health assessments into frailty and pain management among the middle-aged and older adults included in China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.

cards.title: Biodegradable pins fixation for lateral condylar fracture of the humerus in children: A retrospective study of biodegradable pin fixation combined with versus without absorbable tension band wiring.
cards.abstract: Biodegradable pins are increasingly used in the treatment of lateral condylar fractures of the humerus (LCFH) in children, but the strength of the biodegradable pin is weaker than that of K-wire. However, to enhance the stability of LCFH fixed by biodegradable pins, absorbable tension band wiring is often combined with the application, yet high-quality comparative evidence verifying the clinical value of this auxiliary reinforcement remains lacking. This study aimed to compare and analyze whether auxiliary absorbable tension band wiring has clinical significance for Weiss type III LCFH and to clarify whether additional tension band fixation is clinically necessary in reducing postoperative complications and improving fracture stability. This study enrolled 96 children with Weiss type III LCFH admitted between January 2017 and September 2019. The patients were divided into 2 groups: A (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins alone, n = 45) and B (fixed by 3 biodegradable pins and combined with the application of absorbable figure-of-eight tension band wiring, n = 51). Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative indicators, including age, sex, operation time, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, and postoperative complications, were compared between the 2 groups. Postoperative elbow function was assessed by using the Flynn grading system. All radiographic measurements and functional evaluations were performed by 2 calibrated orthopedic surgeons with excellent inter-rater reliability. Sample size calculations were performed before data collection to guarantee statistical validity. There were no significant differences in age, sex, injured side, preoperative fracture displacement, operation duration, intraoperative blood loss, fracture healing time, elbow functional recovery time, or Flynn functional grading (all P > .05). Complete fracture union was observed in all patients, and no adverse complications, such as wound infection, bone nonunion, osteonecrosis, or elbow deformity, occurred in either group. Absorbable tension band wiring reinforcement is not required after biodegradable pin fixation in the treatment of LCFH in children.

cards.title: Platelet-derived microparticles induce CD8+ T cell senescence in chronic kidney disease via the transfer of microRNA-550a-5p.
cards.abstract: Infection is a leading cause of mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), in which T cell dysfunction is considered a typical feature. Although platelets are active participants in immune response, their role in regulating T cell function in patients with CKD remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that CD8+ T cell senescence may be a major contributor to the immunosuppressed state of patients with CKD, and that platelets derived from patients with CKD can induce premature CD8+ T cell senescence, potentially through mediating mitochondrial dysfunction. Further investigations reveal that platelet-derived microparticles (PMPs) from patients with CKD promote CD8+ T cell senescence via transferring miR-550a-5p, thereby decreasing PMPCB expression and inducing NDUFS8 cleavage failure. Finally, inhibition of miR-550a-5p and pretreatment with nicotinamide mononucleotide are capable of preventing platelet-induced CD8+ T cell senescence in CKD patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the ectopic transient expression of platelet-derived miR-550a-5p in CD8+ T cells promotes cellular senescence by regulating the PMPCB-NDUFS8 axis, which can be exploited to treat CKD-associated immunosenescence.

cards.title: Baicalein Ameliorates Postmenopausal Osteoporosis With Iron Accumulation by Inhibiting Osteoclastogenesis via Nrf2 Activation.
cards.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is frequently complicated by iron accumulation, which exacerbates bone loss. Baicalein, a natural flavonoid with iron-chelating and antioxidant properties, has shown bone-protective effects, but its role in iron-overloaded PMOP remains unclear. This study investigated whether baicalein ameliorates iron-accumulated PMOP by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis via Nrf2 activation. In vitro, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs) were induced into osteoclasts with RANKL under iron overload. Baicalein (10 μM) suppressed osteoclast differentiation, F-actin ring formation, and bone resorption, reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS, lowered Fe2+ and total iron content, and upregulated Nrf2 nuclear translocation and HO-1 expression. These effects were abrogated by the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 or Nrf2 siRNA. In vivo, an ovariectomized (OVX) mouse model with iron dextran injection (100 mg/kg/week) was used. Oral baicalein treatment (100 mg/kg/day) significantly prevented bone loss, improved bone microarchitecture and biomechanical properties, reduced iron deposition in bone, liver and spleen, lowered serum ferritin and bone ROS, and activated Nrf2 signaling in bone tissue. Co-administration of ML385 reversed these protective effects. Collectively, baicalein ameliorates iron-accumulated postmenopausal osteoporosis by activating the Nrf2 pathway, thereby inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption. Baicalein represents a promising multi-target candidate for treating PMOP, especially in patients with concomitant iron accumulation.

cards.title: Dynamic covalent network-functionalized holocellulose composite: A photocurable strategy toward transparent and reprocessable composites.
cards.abstract: The development of sustainable and high-performance alternatives to synthetic materials has become a key strategy for advancing the circular bioeconomy and maximizing the value of biomass resources. Transparent wood has emerged as a promising bio-based functional material, but its practical application remains constrained by limited functionality, energy-intensive fabrication processes, and poor recyclability. Herein, a photocurable functional holocellulose composite (FHC) was developed through the synergistic integration of a holocellulose scaffold, UV-curing technology, and a dynamic covalent network, with polymer rapidly polymerizing within the aligned microchannels of holocellulose scaffold, forming a robust interpenetrating structure combining optical management with mechanical reinforcement. The resulting FHC exhibited high haze (98.47%), relatively low thermal conductivity (0.23 W·m-1·K-1), outstanding thermal stability, and high mechanical strength (longitudinal fracture strength 28.25 MPa). Furthermore, the incorporation of β-hydroxy ester-based dynamic covalent bonds introduced thermal re-processability through transesterification at elevated temperature, enabling damaged FHC to be ground and hot-pressed into regenerated films with comparable even enhanced fracture strength (30.21 MPa). This work establishes a facile and cross strategy that combines transparent wood architecture, rapid UV-curing, and dynamic covalent chemistry, providing a scalable route toward recyclable, multifunctional, and high-value cellulose-based composites for energy-efficient buildings, privacy applications and light diffusers, and adaptive material systems.

cards.title: Advancing cellulose-based films: A systematic review of mechanical property enhancement strategies.
cards.abstract: The non-degradability of petroleum-based plastic films has caused irreversible global ecological damage, driving urgent demand for eco-friendly alternatives. As a sustainable, renewable, and biodegradable biomass material, cellulose emerges as an ideal substitute for plastic films, yet its industrial application is hindered by mechanical performance limitations. This review systematically summarizes strategies to enhance the mechanical properties of cellulose-based films, aiming to provide valuable references for researchers and engineers. First, a brief introduction about main cellulose types and common fabrication methods are introduced. Furthermore, core enhancement strategies are then elaborated from four aspects: scale optimization, structural design, densification treatments, and interfacial interaction regulation. In addition, advanced characterization techniques for film structure and fracture mechanisms are also summarized, including SEM/TEM for microstructure observation, universal testing machines for mechanical property measurement, and in-situ methods for real-time crack propagation analysis. Finally, key challenges and future development directions are discussed.

cards.title: Clinical performance of ultratranslucent monolithic zirconia posterior crowns compared with lithium disilicate crowns: A pilot, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial.
cards.abstract: To evaluate, through a pilot, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial, the clinical performance of ultratranslucent monolithic zirconia (UTZr) compared to lithium disilicate (LD) posterior crowns after 24 months of follow-up. Twenty-four crowns were fabricated and placed in 18 patients, assigned to 2 groups: Control (LD-IPS e.max CAD/Ivoclar) and Experimental (UTZr-Zircon FitPlus/Talmax). Longevity was assessed using the modified United States Public Health Service (USPHS) Ryge criteria, visual analog scales (VAS) for patients' self-perceived esthetics, and the Oral Impacts on Daily Performances (OIDP) index for quality-of-life evaluation. Evaluations were conducted at baseline (T0) and 1 (T1), 6 (T2), 12 (T3), and 24 (T4) months after cementation. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method with log-rank test (α = .05). OIDP and USPHS data were analyzed descriptively, while VAS esthetic satisfaction was analyzed using Mann-Whitney, Friedman, and Wilcoxon post-hoc tests. The mean age of participants was 38.5 years. Eleven crowns were fabricated with LD and 13 with UTZr. After 24 months, the cumulative survival rate was 100% for both groups. Both groups showed a significant improvement in esthetic satisfaction over time (P<.05). No ceramic fractures, occlusal changes, marginal integrity alterations, or secondary caries were observed; however, one UTZr crown presented minor marginal discoloration. Both materials, ultratranslucent monolithic zirconia and lithium disilicate, demonstrated high survival rates and satisfactory clinical performance after 24 months.

cards.title: Bone Marrow Macrophage STING Signaling is a Direct Nexus Linking Marrow Adipose Expansion to NAD <sup>+</sup> Depletion and Osteogenic Decline in Skeletal Aging
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Reversing the destructive remodeling of the bone marrow microenvironment during aging remains a major challenge. Here, we reveal an age‐dependent dual role of bone marrow macrophage (BMM) STING signaling during skeletal aging. While BMM STING deficiency is detrimental during early bone development and maturation, it paradoxically confers protection against age‐related bone loss from middle age onward. Mechanistically, accumulating bone marrow adipocytes secrete substantial soluble dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (sDPP4). This sDPP4 functions as an extracellular ligand for Toll‐like receptor 4 on BMMs, thereby collaborating with endogenous mitochondrial DNA to activate STING signaling. This STING activation concurrently induces a CD38‐dependent salvage synthesis pathway. Importantly, this STING‐driven upregulation of CD38 not only amplifies bone marrow inflammation but also, through its ecto‐nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) activity, depletes the precursor nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) required for NAD + salvage synthesis, thereby impairing NMN availability and osteogenic capacity in neighboring bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Finally, therapeutic intervention combining STING pharmacological inhibition with NMN supplementation effectively attenuated bone loss in preclinical models. Thus, we propose BMM STING signaling as a direct nexus connecting marrow adipose accumulation, innate immune inflammation, and diminished bone formation, and emphasize its targeting potential for managing the aged bone marrow microenvironment.

cards.title: Conus Medullaris Syndrome Following Traumatic Thoracolumbar Burst Fractures: Clinical Presentation, Surgical Management, and Early Outcomes in Three Cases.
cards.abstract: Burst fractures of the thoracolumbar spine can carry a neurological deficit, particularly where the conus medullaris is injured. Conus medullaris syndrome (CMS) typically disturbs bladder, bowel, and sexual function while sparing much of the leg power, and its earliest signs are easily missed. We report three patients in whom a traumatic thoracolumbar burst fracture produced features of CMS and describe their operative management. A 57-year-old man with an L1 burst fracture and intact leg power presented with bowel and bladder incontinence and underwent posterior stabilization (D11-L3), regaining continence early. A 25-year-old man with an L1 burst fracture and sacral involvement after a fall from height had impaired voiding and defecation with blunted S3-S5 sensation and was treated with L1 decompression with stabilization (D12-L2). A 62-year-old woman with a 2-month-old D12 nonunion, paraparesis, and multilevel disc protrusion underwent D10-L2 transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion. All three patients demonstrated neurological improvement after surgical decompression and stabilization. Early recovery of bladder function occurred in one patient, while the remaining two experienced symptomatic improvement with ongoing rehabilitation. Thoracolumbar burst fractures involving the T12-L2 region may compress the conus medullaris, resulting in a spectrum of neurological deficits ranging from isolated sphincter dysfunction to mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs. Early recognition requires careful neurological examination, particularly assessment of sacral sensation and sphincter function, and early magnetic resonance imaging and prompt posterior decompression with fixation favor recovery, though return of bladder and sphincter function stays unpredictable.

cards.title: The cation/H+ exchanger ChCAX3 fine-tunes fruit ripening by modulating cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis in Cerasus humilis.
cards.abstract: Cerasus humilis is a calcium-rich fruit crop with high nutritional value, but its synchronized ripening causes concentrated harvest and short shelf life. In this study, ChCAX3, a vacuolar cation/H+ exchanger, was identified as a key regulator of fruit ripening. ChCAX3 showed high expression in fruit and stem tissues and was upregulated by CaCl2 and ethephon treatments. however, repressed during fruit ripening by ChMYB16. Yeast complementation and Arabidopsis thaliana assays validated its Ca2+ transport activity. Overexpression of ChCAX3 in tomato increased fruit Ca2+ content, delayed coloration, reduced softening, and extended the ripening period by approximately 14 days. ChCAX3-mediated vacuolar Ca2+ sequestration may maintain low cytosolic Ca2+ levels, thereby potentially attenuate the expression and activity of a presumptive Ca2+ sensor ChCBL10 and its interacting kinase ChCIPK3 at the vacuolar membrane. This attenuation of the ChCBL10-ChCIPK3 module was accompanied by reduced expression of ethylene biosynthesis genes (ChACS1, ChACO1) and cell wall degradation-related genes (ChPG1, ChPG2), which may collectively delay the ethylene burst and preserving fruit firmness. Conversely, repression of ChCAX3 by ChMYB16 during late ripening may elevate cytosolic Ca2+, potentially activate the ChCBL10-ChCIPK3 signaling cascade, and accelerated senescence. Overall, these findings demonstrated that ChCAX3 positively regulates Ca2+ accumulation and delays fruit ripening via Ca2+ signaling-mediated modulation of ethylene pathways, providing new insights into Ca2+-hormone crosstalk in fruit physiology and identifying a potential target for extending shelf life and enhancing nutritional quality.

cards.title: Complications of self-drilling intermaxillary fixation screws with a focus on dental root damage.
cards.abstract: Intermaxillary fixation is often used in oral and maxillofacial surgery for temporary jaw stabilization. Self-drilling intermaxillary fixation screws are easy to use but can cause dental damage. This retrospective study was performed to examine the complications associated with self-drilling screws, with a focus on dental root damage. Overall, 274 screws were placed in 43 patients between 2010 and 2023 at University Medical Center Utrecht. Patients with missing postoperative imaging or screws placed in edentulous areas were excluded, leaving 162 screws in 28 patients for evaluation. Complications were documented from the patient records and postoperative imaging (panoramic radiographs and/or (cone-beam) computed tomography scans). Dental roots adjacent to 24 screws (14.8%) showed damage on imaging. Logistic regression analysis showed a significantly lower risk of dental root damage with larger interdental distances (OR (per millimetre increase) 0.379, 95% confidence interval 0.210-0.683, P = 0.001). A higher incidence of dental root damage was observed in the posterior region of the jaw; however, no significant association was found between screw location and root damage. Other complications among the 274 screws placed were irritated mucosa (associated with 6.2% of fixation screws), screw loosening (associated with 5.8%), screw overgrowth by oral mucosa (associated with 5.1%), and screw fracture (associated with 0.7%). The placement of self-drilling screws in regions with wider interdental distances is recommended to avoid dental root damage. Studies with larger sample sizes are required to clarify whether screw location independently influences the risk of root injury.

cards.title: [Spatiotemporal evolution of the immune microenvironment and mechanisms of impaired injury repair in acute respiratory distress syndrome].
cards.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by rapid progression and a high mortality rate. Current therapeutic strategies focus primarily on pathogen clearance, which may not adequately regulate the host's dysregulated immune response. The homeostasis of the local pulmonary immune microenvironment is a significant factor determining the severity of tissue injury and the efficacy of subsequent repair. Taking the evolution of ARDS from physiological defense to pathological injury as its main thread, this review examines the spatiotemporal transition mechanisms involved in this pathological process. It outlines the molecular basis of early-stage inflammatory dysregulation, identifying macrophage M1/M2 polarization imbalance, metabolic reprogramming, and the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps as key drivers of pulmonary inflammation. It further describes how a persistent inflammatory microenvironment can induce senescence of type Ⅱ alveolar epithelial cells and pathological remodeling of the extracellular matrix, which serve as primary barriers to alveolar regeneration and contribute to pulmonary fibrosis. Based on these mechanisms, this article summarizes recent advances in stage-specific interventions, focusing on mesenchymal stem cell therapy, immunometabolic reprogramming, and environment-responsive nanomedicines.

cards.title: Jaboticaba peel extract attenuates mesenchymal behavior and vasculogenic mimicry in castration-resistant prostate cancer cells under enzalutamide treatment.
cards.abstract: Jaboticaba (Plinia cauliflora) is a Brazilian fruit rich in bioactive substances that are concentrated in the fruit peel. Accordingly, jaboticaba peel extract (JPE) has emerged as a potential adjuvant therapy against prostatic lesions due to its antioxidant and chemopreventive properties verified in the prostatic microenvironment associated with senescence and hormone-dependent prostate cancer (PCa). At the same time, it is known that disease progression involves mechanisms of tumor neovascularization, such as vasculogenic mimicry (VM), which is frequently associated with therapeutic resistance. Therefore, this study aimed to expand previous investigations into the context of castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) by evaluating the modulation of cellular plasticity mechanisms, such as VM and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), in response to treatment with JPE, either alone or in combination with androgen ablation induced by enzalutamide. Results indicated that the CRPC cell line PC-3 exhibits greater resistance to both therapies when compared with the androgen-dependent LNCaP cell line. Despite this, JPE demonstrated the ability to inhibit the invasion and migration of PC-3 cells, in addition to negatively modulating the acquisition of mesenchymal traits and the formation of VM by these cells upon exposure to enzalutamide. Thus, our in vitro findings demonstrate that although its antitumor actions are more pronounced under hormonal dependence conditions, JPE also has potential as an adjuvant therapy in the treatment of CRPC, particularly by impairing tumor cell mesenchymal behaviors, such as increased migratory capacity and the formation of vascular channels through VM.

cards.title: Non-coding RNAs regulating autophagy in Osteoporosis: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic skeletal disease, defined by low bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration of bone, which increases the risk of fragility fractures. Autophagy is a dynamic and evolutionarily conserved process that regulates the degradation and recycling of cellular proteins and organelles in response to various physiological and pathophysiological conditions. Autophagy is a major stress-response pathway and it is critically involved in regulating the metabolic and homeostatic functions of bone cells. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are a diverse group of RNAs that do not code for proteins, but act as post-transcriptional and epigenetic modulators of gene expression, and thus play an important role in diverse biological processes. Accumulating evidence suggests that ncRNA-autophagy networks contribute to the development of OP. In this review, we summarize the mechanisms by which ncRNAs regulate autophagy and outline the roles of autophagy in osteoclasts, osteoblasts, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, and osteocytes. We further discuss the mechanistic roles of ncRNA-autophagy axes in OP pathogenesis and potential therapeutic strategies targeting these axes.

cards.title: Long-term follow-up outcomes and independent predictors of surgical failure following posterior urethroplasty for pelvic fracture-associated urethral strictures.
cards.abstract: To report long-term follow-up outcomes of posterior urethroplasty for pelvic fracture urethral strictures and identify independent predictors of surgical failure. We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent delayed posterior urethroplasty for pelvic fracture urethral injury at our center between December 2018 and December 2024. Perioperative and follow-up data were collected and analyzed. Patients with less than 12 months of postoperative follow-up were excluded. Seventy-six male patients were included. Median (IQR) age was 51.5 (40.5, 57.8) years. Injury mechanisms included crush trauma (n = 40, 52.6%), traffic accidents (n = 22, 29.0%), and falls (n = 14, 18.4%). Complete urethral obliteration was present in 54 patients (71.0%), and post-injury erectile dysfunction in 43 (56.6%). Thirty-two patients (42.1%) had prior urethral interventions. All procedures were successful. Median (IQR) urethral defect length was 2.5 (2.0, 3.5) cm. Direct anastomosis was performed in 48 patients (63.2%), and adjunctive maneuvers in 28 (36.8%). Median (IQR) follow-up was 30.0 (15.0, 59.5) months. Treatment success was achieved in 60 patients (79.0%), and failure in 16 (21.0%). On multivariate analysis, prior intervention (OR 11.558, 95% CI 1.356-98.515, P = 0.025) and longer urethral defect length (OR 4.394, 95% CI 1.262-15.292, P = 0.020) were independent predictors of surgical failure. Posterior urethroplasty is safe and effective for pelvic fracture urethral strictures with favorable long-term functional outcomes. Prior intervention and longer urethral defect length are independent predictors of surgical failure.

cards.title: MID-LIFE LEISURE-TIME PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IS ASSOCIATED WITH LOWER HIP FRACTURE RISK IN UK BIOBANK
cards.abstract: Leisure time physical activity (LTPA) in mid-life may have beneficial effects on risk factors for hip fracture in later life. Conversely, physical activity may increase fracture risk through risk of injury, and the optimal amount of physical activity for reducing hip fracture risk remains unclear. We explored the associations between volume and intensity of LTPA in mid-life, and subsequent risk of hip fracture ascertained from linked health data. This prospective observational study used middle aged adults aged 40- 65 years from UK Biobank. LTPA volume (LTPAv) was derived from self-reported walking, moderate and vigorous activity at baseline (2006- 2010). Cox proportional hazard and Fine-Gray sub-distribution models were used to estimate the association between activity and hip fracture, which was sex-stratified. From 324,284 participants with complete data 53% were female and mean age at baseline was 54.5 (SD 7.3). Across 16 years of follow-up there were 2,674 hip fractures. In terms of LTPA volume, the lowest risk of hip fracture occurred in quintile 3 for women (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.91), and men (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.60- 0.90), relating to approximately one hour/day of leisure time physical activity. When activity intensities were examined separately, the lowest estimated hazards were observed for vigorous activity, at quintile 4 in women (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.55 - 0.76) and quintile 3 in men (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52- 0.79), corresponding to approximately 60- 90 minutes of vigorous activity per week. In conclusion, moderately high volumes of mid-life physical activity, particularly vigorous activity, were related to lower risk of subsequent hip fracture, but these relationships appear to attenuate at higher volumes.

cards.title: Prehospital Variables Do Not Reliably Identify Pelvic Fracture Morphologies Amenable to Pelvic Binder Application: A Retrospective Imaging Review.
cards.abstract: BackgroundPelvic binders are used in prehospital settings for early stabilization when pelvic fractures are suspected. Although a rapid and cost-effective tool, uncertainties persist regarding their use prior to radiological confirmation of pelvic fracture.MethodsA review of adult patients with a pelvic fracture requiring trauma team activation who were admitted to a tertiary trauma center between 2020 and 2023 was conducted. The radiological studies were reviewed by four consultant orthopedic surgeons and were classified according to whether the application of a pelvic binder would be mechanically favorable, neutral, or potentially unfavorable. The area under the curve (AUC) was calculated to evaluate the ability of specific physiologic and injury-related variables (hypotension, tachycardia, shock index, Injury Severity Score (ISS), Glasgow Coma Scale, and mechanism of injury) to discriminate pelvic fracture morphologies for which pelvic binder application would be favorable.ResultsA total of 298 patients were included in the current investigation. Of these patients, applying a pelvic binder was favorable in 17% of cases (95% CI: 13%-22%, N = 50), would be mechanically neutral in 28% of cases (95% CI: 23%-33%, N = 82), and was potentially unfavorable in 56% of cases (95% CI: 50%-61%, N = 166) (P < .001). All investigated variables demonstrated limited discriminatory ability for identifying patients for whom pelvic binder application was favorable, with most AUCs <0.60. The highest predictive performance was observed for the ISS [AUC (95% CI): 0.65 (0.58-0.73)].ConclusionIn trauma patients with CT-confirmed pelvic ring injuries, readily available prehospital variables such as hemodynamic instability, associated injury patterns, and mechanism of injury appear to be insufficient for reliably identifying patients with a fracture morphology that could be amenable to pelvic binder application.

cards.title: Bone marrow myeloid skewing and preserved immunoregulation in hip osteoarthritis of elderly patients.
cards.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as a disease involving low-grade inflammation and immune remodeling, yet the contribution of the bone marrow (BM) myeloid compartment to hip OA remains poorly defined. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are immature myeloid cells with immunoregulatory activity and potential roles in inflammatory bone disease. Here, we investigated ex vivo BM myeloid composition and the functional properties of BM-MDSCs in elderly patients with hip OA compared with patients undergoing surgery for proximal femoral fracture. BM aspirates from both cohorts were analyzed by flow cytometry and cultured with G-CSF and GM-CSF to induce BM-MDSCs. Despite the lower mean age of the hip osteoarthritis cohort, these patients showed a significantly higher proportion of BM myeloid cells than fracture patients, whereas lymphoid cell frequencies were not significantly different. Analysis of myeloid maturation stages revealed enrichment of CD11b⁺/CD16low metamyelocyte-like cells in hip OA samples both ex vivo and after cytokine-driven expansion. Functional assays demonstrated that inhibition of activated T cell proliferation was confined to the most immature myeloid fraction, which displayed promyelocyte-like features. This suppressive activity was preserved in both hip OA and fracture cohorts, with no significant difference between groups. These findings indicate that hip OA is associated with BM myeloid skewing and selective enrichment of myeloid subsets reassembling metamyelocytes-like cells, while maintaining conserved immunoregulatory function. The BM may represent an active immunological compartment linked to the balance between chronic inflammation and immune regulation in hip OA.

cards.title: The Impact of Analgesic Opioid Use on Fracture Healing and Nonunion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
cards.abstract: Bone fractures are a major global health issue, with nonunion being a serious complication. While NSAIDs are known to impair bone healing, prompting increased opioid use for pain, the effect of opioids on fracture healing is poorly understood. This article assesses: (1) whether chronic opioid use increases all-bone nonunion risk; (2) whether risk varies by anatomic site; (3) whether duration or NSAID co-use modifies risk; and (4) whether time-to-union is prolonged in opioid users. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and CINAHL was conducted up to January 1, 2026. Included retrospective cohort studies reported opioid exposure and fracture healing outcomes. Study quality was assessed, and adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for nonunion were pooled using quality-effects and random-effects models. Seven studies, comprising over one million fracture cases, were included. Meta-analysis showed chronic opioid use was associated with higher odds of nonunion across all bone types (OR 5.10, 95% CI: 3.28-7.93). Site-specific analyses revealed elevated odds for the humerus (OR 4.28), radius (OR 4.93), tibia (OR 4.57), and metatarsals (OR 4.81). Concurrent use of opioids and NSAIDs was associated with higher odds compared to opioids alone in limited analyses. One study reported a modestly prolonged time to union in opioid users. Chronic opioid use is associated with a higher risk of fracture nonunion at multiple skeletal sites. This association appears stronger when opioids are combined with NSAIDs. These findings suggest caution regarding opioid safety in bone healing and highlight the need for cautious prescribing and exploration of multimodal, non-opioid analgesic strategies for fracture pain. III.

cards.title: Comparative outcomes of cannulated screws, dynamic hip screws and the femoral neck system for transcervical femoral neck fractures. a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Internal fixation of transcervical femoral neck fractures remains associated with substantial failure and reoperation rates. The Femoral Neck System (FNS) was developed to improve rotational stability while remaining minimally invasive, but comparative data against traditional implants are limited. We hypothesised that fixation with the FNS would be associated with lower reoperation rates compared with CS and DHS. We performed a retrospective comparative cohort study of adults undergoing fixation of transcervical femoral neck fractures at two centres between 2019 and 2024, with a minimum of 12-months of outcome ascertainment. Data were collected from medical records and radiographs. Negative binomial regression evaluated time to surgery; logistic regression assessed fixation method against union, reoperation and complications, adjusted for age, Charlson Comorbidity Index, Garden classification, side and time to surgery. After exclusions, 207 patients were analysed (CS 27, DHS 100, FNS 80). Age (CS 54.8, DHS 66.9, FNS 68.2 years; p = 0.02) and Garden distribution (Garden I 7/27 CS, 27/100 DHS, 52/80 FNS; p < 0.001) differed between groups; adjusted analyses accounted for these differences. Reoperation occurred in 37/207 (17.9%): 10/27 (37.0%) CS, 20/100 (20.0%) DHS and 7/80 (8.8%) FNS (p = 0.004). After adjustment, CS remained associated with reoperation versus FNS (OR 5.26, 95% CI 1.53-18.13), whereas DHS did not (OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.65-5.26). Union occurred in 184/207 (88.9%), with no association with fixation method (p = 0.065). Complications occurred in 61/207 (29.5%): 11/27 (40.7%) CS, 32/100 (32.0%) DHS and 18/80 (22.5%) FNS (p = 0.15); higher Garden classification was associated with more complications (Garden II OR 2.58, Garden III OR 3.44; p = 0.037). Time to surgery was shorter with DHS than FNS (IRR 0.49, 95% CI 0.35-0.69; p < 0.001), although the median was 1 day in all groups. Avascular necrosis occurred in 4/80 (5.0%) FNS, 11/100 (11.0%) DHS and 2/27 (7.4%) CS (p = 0.42). Union rates were high across fixation methods. cards.title: Neighborhood Walkability, Green Space, and Incident Hip Fracture among Older U.S. Adults: The Cardiovascular Health Study.
cards.abstract: Neighborhood walkability and green space are associated with walking behavior and physical activity, but evidence linking them to fracture is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex differences remain understudied. We evaluated associations of neighborhood walkability and green space with incident hip fracture in older, community-dwelling U.S. adults. We conducted a prospective cohort study of adults aged ≥65 years from the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS). Neighborhood exposures were defined using 1-km radial buffers around geocoded residential addresses from 1992-1993 (baseline). Walkability was the sum of standardized population and walkable destination densities. Green space was the proportion of satellite-derived green land cover. Hip fractures were prospectively ascertained over 12 years using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9) codes from hospital discharge abstracts. Cox hazard models adjusted for individual-level (age, sex, race, weight, height, smoking status, current heavy alcohol use, medication use, diabetes, renal function, marital status, education level, annual household income) and neighborhood-level (median household income, median value of owner-occupied housing, proportion of persons in managerial/professional occupations) covariates evaluated associations, overall and by sex. Among 3,676 participants (58% women), 359 experienced hip fracture over a median 10-years observation. Greater neighborhood walkability was significantly associated with lower hip fracture incidence among women (hazard ratio per 1 standard deviation increase of 0.72 [95% confidence interval, 0.53-0.98]), but not overall or among men. Neighborhood green space was not significantly associated with hip fracture. Greater neighborhood walkability, but not green space, was associated with lower hip fracture risk among older women.

cards.title: Management of Fractured Fragment With Reattachment: A Case Report With 2-Year Follow-Up.
cards.abstract: Fragment reattachment is the most conservative treatment approach for uncomplicated crown fractures, which enables the restoration of the original tooth structure and the preservation of the remaining tooth structure. A 15-year-old patient reported with an uncomplicated crown fracture of the maxillary left central incisor involving enamel and dentin. Pulp sensibility testing had a normal response and radiographic examination revealed no periapical pathology. The retrieved fractured fragment had good marginal adaptation. Following rehydration, fragment reattachment was performed under rubber dam isolation using an etch-and-rinse protocol, a two-coat adhesive application and nanohybrid flowable composite. At the second appointment, a V-shaped retentive groove of 0.7-mm depth was placed in both the labial and palatal aspects, extending 2 mm on either side of the fracture line, followed by composite restoration. The patient was reviewed at 6 weeks, 1 year and 2 years in accordance with the International Association of Dental Traumatology (IADT) guidelines. Throughout the follow-up period, the reattached fragment remained clinically intact with no evidence of debonding, marginal discolouration or fracture recurrence. Pulp sensibility testing remained normal, and radiographic examination revealed no periapical changes at all follow-up intervals, demonstrating sustained aesthetic and functional stability over a 2-year follow-up period.
