cards.title: Operational end-of-life trajectory categories among patients who died in the emergency department: associations with resuscitative and palliative care in a five-year retrospective cohort.
cards.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) increasingly care for patients approaching the end of life, yet the relationships between patterns of decline and final ED care remain poorly characterised. The objective was to describe the distribution of retrospectively assigned trajectory-oriented categories among ED decedents and examine associations with care processes. This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults who died in the ED between 2018 and 2022. Categories were acute event/low comorbidity (T1), terminal malignancy or pre-existing exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care (T2), advanced chronic disease with acute decompensation (T3), frailty/dementia or high comorbidity with severe functional dependency (T4), and residual unclassified cases (T5). Primary outcomes were CPR and documented initiation of exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care; documented end-of-life recognition or discussion was secondary. Of 628 patients, 1.3% were T1, 10.8% T2, 10.0% T3, 49.4% T4, and 28.5% T5. CPR ranged from 75% in T1 to 24% in T2 and T4 (p<0.001). Exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care was initiated in 35% of T2 and 11% of T3-T5 patients (p<0.001). End-of-life recognition or discussion ranged from 12% in T1 to 51% in T2 (p=0.034). Frailty and dementia represented the main trajectory of death in the ED, while nearly one-third of patients could not be classified within the predefined categories. A pragmatic trajectory-oriented framework may help interpret observed patterns of care. However, retrospective assignment and the large residual group make these findings hypothesis-generating; prospective validation is required before decision-support use.

cards.title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
cards.abstract: Periprosthetic femoral fracture is a severe complication following hip arthroplasty, influenced by the design of the femoral component and the method of fixation. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of sex and age on the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture. We analyzed 204,041 primary hip arthroplasties from the Norwegian Arthroplasty Register and the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register (1 January 2005 to 31 December 2025). Femoral components were categorized as cemented composite beam (CB), cemented polished taper-slip (PTS), uncemented collarless (UCC-), and uncemented collared (UCC+). Cox regression analysis was used to compare the risk (adjusted hazard rate ratio (aHRR)) of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture stratified by sex and age. In males, PTS and UCC- had a nine-times higher risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture than CB. For UCC+, the risk was four times higher than CB. The risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in males aged > 65 years for UCC-; for UCC+ the risk was increased in males aged > 75 years, whereas PTS had higher risk for periprosthetic femoral fracture at all ages, compared with CB. In females, the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in those aged > 70 years for PTS and UCC+ compared with CB, whereas for UCC- the risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture was higher in those aged > 60 years, compared with CB. Our findings suggest that CB should be the preferred choice of femoral component, at least for males aged > 75 years and females aged > 70 years. UCC+ components were the best uncemented option, while the use of PTS components was associated with a high risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture among males of all ages.

cards.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
cards.abstract: Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD. A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability. Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures). This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip.

cards.title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis.
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age‐associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age‐associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis‐based model in which MSCs translate age‐associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell‐supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine‐directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC‐derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue‐resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

cards.title: Peripheral and Placental KLRG1+ Senescence-Associated T Cells in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: Diagnostic and Clinical Correlations.
cards.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) disorders are considered to be iatrogenic conditions. There is growing evidence for the role of T cell senescence in the pathophysiology of pregnancy complications. This study aimed to investigate peripheral and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets and senescence-associated/highly differentiated T cell frequencies in PAS and to explore their diagnostic performance and correlations with clinical, inflammatory, and proliferative (Ki-67) parameters. Placental tissue and maternal peripheral blood were obtained from PAS pregnancies and controls in their third trimester. Flow cytometric immunophenotyping was conducted for peripheral blood and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets, senescence-associated subsets, and their KLRG1 expression intensity. Immunohistochemical analysis of Ki-67 expression in placental tissue of subjects and controls was performed. PAS placental tissue showed an increase in CD28-CD57+ senescence-associated, KLRG1+ senescence-associated T cells, and KLRG1 MFI within all T-cell compartments. KLRG1 MFI increased progressively toward senescence-associated (CD28-CD57+) T cell phenotypes across all T-cell lineages in PAS placental tissue. In contrast, analysis of KLRG1+ percentages in PAS PB revealed limited, largely non-significant dysregulation of T cells. Ki-67 expression correlated positively with senescence-associated DP T cells and KLRG1+ senescence-associated CD4+ Th cells cells, linking the possible association of trophoblastic proliferation with T-cell senescence. This is the first study analyzing senescence-associated T cell subsets in PAS patients as well as the previously unexplored double-positive and double-negative lineages. Localized immunosenescence at the implantation site may contribute to the pathogenesis of PAS. Senescence-associated T-cell signatures show promise as exploratory tissue-based indicators of the immune dysregulation in PAS.

cards.title: Impact of body composition on toxicity and response in patients with advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma treated with BV-AVD.
cards.abstract: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin, doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine) has improved outcomes in advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma (ASHL); however, toxicity such as peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains a concern. Previous studies in oncology have demonstrated an association between sarcopenia and chemotoxicity. Therefore, we examined the effects of body composition parameters, including skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous fat (SF), and visceral fat (VF), along with quantitative biomarkers including metabolic tumor volume (MTV), on PN, treatment response, and progression-free survival. This study retrospectively reviewed the baseline, interim, and end-of-treatment (EOT) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) for 39 patients with ASHL treated with BV-AVD and assessed changes in MTV and body composition. MTV declined significantly from baseline to interim PET and EOT PET-CT (EOT PET), with no significant difference between the latter time points, indicating an early treatment response. SM:VF and SF:VF ratios followed a similar pattern, suggesting that changes in body composition including SM loss (sarcopenia) and changes in fat distribution (SF:VF), occurred early during treatment. Patients with stable SM:VF ratios were more likely to achieve a complete response (CR), whereas larger changes in SM:VF and SF:VF ratios and an early increase in VF were associated with failure to achieve CR, possibly due to increased inflammation. Stage IV disease and higher MTV were both associated with increased PN and may reflect the wider distribution of BV and an amplified inflammatory response. These findings demonstrate that body composition and PET-CT indices are relevant biomarkers in ASHL, and their integration with MTV may enhance risk stratification and deepen our understanding of toxicity risk.

cards.title: Optimizing Volar Lunate Facet Fracture Fixation: Finite Element Analysis and Cadaveric Testing.
cards.abstract: Volar lunate facet (VLF) fractures are prone to loss of reduction after volar plating. We used finite element analysis (FEA) and cadaveric testing to identify failure mechanisms and determine how screw configuration alters load transfer. A CT-derived radius model with a 10 × 15 × 5-mm VLF fragment was fixed with a 4-hole hook plate using locking and nonlocking (NL) screws. A 500-N radiolunate compressive load was applied, and von Mises stresses were quantified. Sensitivity analyses varied loading, bone density, fracture characteristics, and implant material. Ten distal radii underwent cyclic loading followed by load-to-failure testing; failure modes and locations were compared with FEA hotspots. FEA identified two stress concentrations: the distal plate contour/screw-hole region and the ulnar hook insertion into the VLF fragment. In the baseline 1[NL]&3[NL] construct, peak construct and radius stresses were 697.2 and 154.6 MPa. The 1[NL]&2[NL] configuration produced the lowest stresses (54.5 and 27.3 MPa), whereas locking hole 3 reduced construct stress to 587.2 MPa. Cadaver failure load was 1239.2 ± 438.5 N (range: 630.0-1990.1 N); failures were loss of reduction/fracture dislocation (4/10) or plate failure (6/10), with failure locations corresponding to FEA hotspots. Off-axis loading, reduced bone density, and fracture-line translation increased construct stress and altered hotspot location. FEA-predicted hook-fragment stress corresponded to loss of reduction, whereas distal plate stress corresponded to plate failure. Among modeled configurations, 1[NL]&2[NL] minimized construct and radius stress, although unbalanced cadaveric groups preclude claims of clinical superiority. These findings support fragment capture while minimizing distal plate stress.

cards.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases.
cards.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

cards.title: Dual-stent decompression of an extensive orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst: a case report and technical innovation.
cards.abstract: Orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst (OOC) is a rare developmental entity with a low recurrence rate in pediatric patients, voluminous cysts can compromise mandibular integrity and displace teeth, necessitating conservative management to preserve vital structures. We report an extensive mandibular OOC in a 12-year-old female managed via a dual-stent decompression strategy. A 12-year-old female presented with an 8-cm midline-crossing OOC involving both mental foramina. To minimize risks of nerve damage and pathologic fracture, a two-stage protocol was initiated. Initial decompression was performed with a single stent; however, to optimize the drainage gradient across the midline, a dual-stent modification was implemented. This dynamic adjustment appeared to facilitate significant centripetal bone apposition over 8 months. The resulting volume reduction allowed for definitive enucleation under local anesthesia, completed within a 30-minute operative window to ensure pediatric cooperation. Histopathology confirmed OOC. Serial radiographic monitoring over 32 months demonstrated complete bone regeneration, spontaneous repositioning of incisors, and no recurrence. To our knowledge, this represents one of the first reported cases of dual-stent decompression in pediatric oral surgery. This technique may facilitate conservative intervention for extensive odontogenic cysts in children, supporting optimal healing, preservation of neurovascular integrity, and minimal morbidity while respecting pediatric behavioral management constraints.

cards.title: Cardiac-specific Lmpt knockdown induces heart dysfunction via mitochondrial quality decline and metabolic disturbance in Drosophila.
cards.abstract: Lmpt (Limpet, CG42679) is a Drosophila LIM domain protein homologous to human FHL2. Our prior work demonstrated it represses Wnt signaling during embryonic cardiac development. However, its role in adult cardiac homeostasis remains unclear. Here, we generated Hand-gal4-driven Lmpt knockdown flies (predominantly targeting adult cardiomyocytes) using the Hand-gal4/UAS-RNAi system and examined its function in adult flies. Lmpt knockdown significantly reduced climbing ability and triggered intrinsic cardiac contractile dysfunction, manifested as bradycardia, impaired fractional shortening and prolonged diastolic intervals in 3-week-old flies. These flies also exhibited systemic metabolic disorders and ATP depletion, decreased lipid accumulation in multiple tissues, and elevated ROS levels in the heart and gut. Meanwhile, Lmpt knockdown led to disorganized and fractured myocardial fibers and progressive age-dependent mitochondrial quality decline. qPCR analysis revealed abnormal expression of genes related to mitochondrial dynamics, respiratory chain, and quality control. In conclusion, Lmpt maintains adult cardiac function by preserving mitochondrial quality, energy metabolism, and myocardial structural integrity. This study provides new insights into the mitochondrial and metabolic mechanisms maintaining adult cardiac homeostasis, with potential implications for FHL2-related cardiomyopathies.

cards.title: Integration of network pharmacology, deep learning, and molecular biology reveals the efficacy of Citrus aurantium L. var. amara Engl. blossom extract in ameliorating diabetic osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Diabetic osteoporosis (DOP) is a type of metabolic bone disease. Blossom of Citrus aurantium L. var. amara Engl. (CAVA), a medicinal and edible herb widely employed in China which can alleviate indigestion and replenish qi, has been demonstrated to be effective in treating metabolic disorders such as obesity and diabetes. However, its effects on DOP remains uncertain. To explore the protective effects and mechanisms of blossom of CAVA against DOP. Ethanol extract of blossom of CAVA (CAVAE) was characterized using HPLC/MS. Network pharmacology, deep learning, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to predict key constituents and possible pathways. High-fat diet and streptozocin-induced type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice were established and Micro-CT, X-ray imaging, morphological analysis and molecular biology assays were performed to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of CAVAE on DOP. The 44 compounds identified by HPLC/MS analysis suggest that CAVAE may prevent DOP via PI3K/AKT and Wnt/β-catenin pathways. Experimental validation demonstrated that CAVAE significantly improved diabetes and osteoporosis in T2DM mice, as evidenced by the decreased blood glucose content, increased bone mineral density, enhanced trabecular bone number, improved femoral bone microstructure, restored femur stability, bone metabolism and reduced serum calcium ion levels, etc. Mechanistic investigations further confirmed that CAVAE probably alleviated DOP in T2DM mice by modulating PI3K/AKT and Wnt-3a/β-catenin pathways. CAVAE might exert anti-osteoporotic effects on T2DM mice through concurrent activation of PI3K/AKT and Wnt-3a/β-catenin pathways.

cards.title: Intraoperative neuromonitoring findings after erector spinae plane block during posterior thoracolumbar fusion surgery.
cards.abstract: To investigate the potential adverse influence of erector spinae plane block (ESPB) on intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) during posterior spinal fusion for thoracolumbar fractures. We conducted a retrospective review of patients who underwent posterior spinal fusion for thoracolumbar fractures between January 2018 and December 2022. Patients were categorized into ESPB and non-ESPB groups based on whether ESPB was administered. The primary endpoint was the change in transcranial motor evoked potential (Tc-MEP) and posterior tibial nerve somatosensory evoked potential (PTN-SEP) waveform derivation rates. Secondary outcomes included Tc-MEP and PTN-SEP alarm occurrence and postoperative neurological deterioration. Overall, 154 patients were included in the final analysis (89 males, 65 females; mean age: 68.6 years; mean BMI: 22.1). There were 52 patients in the ESPB group and 102 in the non-ESPB group. No significant differences were observed in preoperative neurological findings between the two groups. ESPB did not significantly affect Tc-MEP or PTN-SEP waveform derivation rates. Tc-MEP alarms occurred in the quadriceps femoris muscle (QC) in 2 patients in the ESPB group, but not in the non-ESPB group. Both alarms occurred during T11-level procedures, and waveform recovery was obtained after surgical interruption. No postoperative motor deficits were noted in these patients. ESPB did not significantly affect Tc-MEP or PTN-SEP rates. Two unexplained QC Tc-MEP alarms occurred only in the ESPB group. These findings do not establish a clinically actionable association between ESPB and IONM changes, but unexpected isolated QC Tc-MEP changes during surgery with ESPB should be interpreted cautiously.

cards.title: [Study on regulatory effects of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis].
cards.abstract: To investigate the effect of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), and to compare its efficacy with that of mild moxibustion. Forty-eight Wistar rats were randomly assigned to 4 groups (n=12):normal, model, mild moxibustion, and warm needling. KOA was induced by intra-articular injection of monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) into the right knee. Rats in the mild moxibustion and warm needling moxibustion groups received interventions at the acupoints "Futu" (ST32) and "Zusanli" (ST36), 30 min per session, once every other day for 4 weeks. After intervention, Lequesne MG scores, the right knee joint horizontal diameter, and right hind paw pain threshold were assessed. Histopathological changes in the rat knee joints were observed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) and safranin O staining, and were scored using the Mankin's and OARSI systems. Serum contents of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-18 (IL-18), and matrix metalloproteinase-13 (MMP-13) were measured by ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, MMP-13, and type Ⅱ collagen (Collagen-Ⅱ) in knee cartilage. Western blot was performed to detect the relative protein expression levels of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, Collagen-Ⅱ, IL-6, and MMP-13 in cartilage tissue. Compared with the normal group, the model group showed a significantly higher Lequesne MG score (P<0.01), an increased horizontal diameter of the right knee joint (P<0.01), and a decreased pain threshold (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups exhibited significantly lower Lequesne MG scores (P<0.01), reduced joint horizontal diameters (P<0.01), and increased pain thresholds (P<0.01). Compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group showed a lower Lequesne MG score (P<0.01) and a higher pain threshold (P<0.01). Histopathological staining revealed degenerative features in the model group, including damage to the superficial cartilage layer and disappearance of the tidemark, while both treatment groups exhibited milder degeneration. Compared with the normal group, both the Mankin's and OARSI scores were significantly increased in the model group (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both scores were decreased in the mild moxibustion and warm needling groups (P<0.01), and the scores in the warm needling group were significantly lower than those in the mild moxibustion group (P<0.05). Compared with the normal group, the serum contents of IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 were significantly elevated in the model group (P<0.01);in cartilage tissue, the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins were increased (P<0.01), while Collagen-Ⅱ expression was reduced (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups showed decreased serum IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 contents, and reduced expression of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins in cartilage tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05), along with increased Collagen-Ⅱ expression (P<0.01). Furthermore, compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group exhibited more significant changes in the above indicators except joint horizontal diameter (P<0.01, P<0.05). Warm needling moxibustion effectively improves knee osteoarthritis in rats and shows superior efficacy compared with mild moxibustion. Its therapeutic mechanism may be associated with the inhibition of chondrocyte senescence.

cards.title: Diaphyseal forearm malunions with distal radioulnar joint instability treated by 3D-planned osseous correction.
cards.abstract: This study evaluates the effect of a three-dimensional (3D)-planned corrective osteotomy using patient-specific drilling and cutting guides in patients with a diaphyseal forearm malunion and distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability following a childhood forearm fracture. Nine patients (mean age at trauma, 12 years) with malunion and preserved forearm rotation but symptomatic DRUJ instability underwent a corrective osteotomy of the radius and/or ulna. Function and pain were assessed using the Patient-Rated Wrist/Hand Evaluation (PRWHE) score, the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and the Patient-Specific Functional Scale (PSFS). Furthermore, baseline clinical assessments were compared with findings at 12 months of follow-up. At 12 months, all patients demonstrated significant and clinically relevant improvement in function and pain as well as a stable DRUJ without additional soft-tissue repair. Median PRWHE scores improved from 44.5 to 5.5 (p = 0.009). NRS pain scores improved from 2 to 0 (p = 0.057) at rest and from 7 to 1 (p = 0.014) during activity. The PSFS scores improved from 7 to 2 (p = 0.010). All outcomes showed clinically relevant improvements according to the minimal clinically important difference. These findings indicate that precision 3D-guided osteotomy can restore DRUJ stability and improve symptoms in patients with a diaphyseal forearm malunion without the need for (additional) soft-tissue reconstruction. cards.title: Building Bridges Belowground: Pythium oligandrum En-hances Rhizosphere Network Connectivity
cards.abstract: Biological control agents (BCAs) offer a potential sustainable alternative to fungicides for crop dis-ease management, but their effects on resident plant microbiomes and microbial interactions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of the BCA Pythium oligandrum on disease con-trol and the rhizosphere microbiome of starch potato cv. Kuras in a field trial. We compared a labora-tory strain and a commercial formulation (Polygandron) with commonly used fungicides during early blight development. The laboratory strain suppressed early blight at plant senescence, but this effect did not persist until harvest, whereas fungicide treatment provided near-complete disease suppression throughout the growing season. P. oligandrum caused transient changes in rhizosphere fungal com-munity composition at flowering, while bacterial community richness varied among sampling times in untreated controls. However, bacterial co-occurrence network analysis revealed pronounced treat-ment-specific changes in microbial connectivity. Application of the laboratory strain increased net-work connectivity, resulting in almost a threefold increase in mean degree and greater interconnected-ness among bacterial taxa. In contrast, Polygandron and fungicide treatments reduced mean degree, indicating reduced connectivity within the bacterial network. Fungicide treatment additionally altered network organisation, including increased betweenness centrality and changes in modularity. Togeth-er, our results show that P. oligandrum can modify microbial interactions in the potato rhizosphere without substantially altering overall bacterial community composition, highlighting the value of in-tegrating microbial network structure with community-level analyses when evaluating the ecological effects of BCAs.

cards.title: [The incidence and 1-year prognosis of heart failure following myocardial infarction during hospitalization in patients with first STEMI].
cards.abstract: Objective: To investigate the incidence of in-hospital heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) and 1-year mortality in patients with first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to compare the 1-year mortality risk among different types of HF. Methods: Data were derived from the Henan STEMI registry, which was a multicentre, prospective, observational study in central China. After excluding patients with a history of MI or HF, patients with first STEMI were divided into the HF and non-HF groups according to the occurrence of in-hospital HF. Based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measured on the last echocardiogram during hospitalization, patients with HF were classified into HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF≥50%), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF, LVEF 41%-49%), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF≤40%), and HF with missing LVEF. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed with the log-rank test. Multivariate Cox frailty models were used to analyze the associations of HF status (present vs. absent) and different LVEF subgroups with 1-year mortality, using the non-HF group as the reference. Results: A total of 4 737 patients with first STEMI were included in the final analysis, with a median age of 62.8 (52.4, 70.8) years, of whom 1 158 (24.4%) were female. During hospitalization, 1 978 cases (41.8%) developed HF following MI, including 268 (13.5%) with HFrEF, 309 (15.6%) with HFmrEF, 707 (35.7%) with HFpEF, and 694 (35.1%) with missing LVEF. A total of 3 967 (83.7%) patients completed the 1-year follow-up. The 1-year mortality was significantly higher among STEMI patients complicated by HF than in those without (23.3% (391/1 680) vs. 5.8% (132/2 287), log-rank P<0.001). Specifically, the rates were 29.6% (67/226) for HFrEF, 20.8% (53/255) for HFmrEF, 11.7% (72/615) for HFpEF and 34.1% (199/584) for HF with missing LVEF. Multivariate Cox frailty models identified in-hospital HF following MI as a risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR=2.13, 95%CI: 1.70-2.67). Notably, HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk of 1-year mortality (HR=1.59, 95%CI: 1.16-2.17), while the HF group with missing LVEF carried the highest risk (HR=2.49, 95%CI: 1.91-3.26). Conclusions: The incidence of HF following first STEMI during hospitalization was 41.8%, with a corresponding 1-year mortality of 23.3%. In-hospital HF following MI is a risk factor for 1-year mortality in patients with STEMI. Prognosis differed notably across HF subgroups: HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk, whereas patients with missing LVEF had the worst outcome.

cards.title: Cortical and trabecular deficits in patients with recent hip fractures assessed by DXA and 3D-DXA.
cards.abstract: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is the standard for osteoporosis assessment, but areal BMD (aBMD) does not fully capture volumetric or microstructural deficits associated with hip fractures. We aimed to characterize cortical and trabecular parameters using 3D-DXA in patients with hip fractures and assess whether these measures improve discrimination of prevalent fracture status beyond aBMD. Descriptive analyses included 499 individuals: femoral neck fractures (FNfx, n=110), intertrochanteric fractures (ITfx, n=123), and controls (n=266). Patients were assessed within 15 days of fracture at the contralateral hip. DXA and 3D-DXA provided trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), cortical surface BMD (sBMD), and cortical thickness. TBS and FRAX were evaluated descriptively but excluded from penalized models. LASSO models were evaluated in 515 unique participants with complete predictor data. Among fractured patients, 51% did not meet densitometric criteria for osteoporosis. In the low bone mass subgroup, fractured individuals showed lower trabecular vBMD, whereas osteoporotic subjects also exhibited reduced cortical sBMD. Exploratory comparisons suggested lower trochanteric trabecular measures in ITfx and lower femoral neck cortical thickness in FNfx, although most differences occurred between fracture groups and controls. Total hip aBMD alone yielded an AUC of 0.646. The LASSO λmin model improved discrimination modestly (AUC 0.692; p<0.001), while the λ1se model achieved an AUC of 0.663 (p=0.034). 3D-DXA identified cortical and trabecular deficits in patients with recent hip fractures, including those without densitometric osteoporosis, and provided complementary structural information beyond aBMD. However, the improvement in discrimination was modest and requires prospective external validation.

cards.title: Epidemiology of paediatric traumatology: history, evolution, and perspectives.
cards.abstract: Paediatric traumatology sits at the crossroads of orthopaedics, paediatric surgery, and public health. This instructional lecture addresses four questions: what is the global epidemiological burden of acute paediatric trauma? What are the specific features and growing importance of sports-related injuries, both acute and chronic? What are the specificities of paediatric polytrauma assessment and care organisation? How have evolving surgical practises and prevention policies transformed patient outcomes? After a brief historical overview, the article presents global epidemiological data, details acute and overuse sports injuries as a major twenty-first-century challenge, analyses validated polytrauma assessment tools and discusses surgical management trends for long-bone fractures. Future perspectives emphasise multidisciplinary collaboration, SROS-based care pathways, harmonised EPOS training programmes and evidence-based reassessment of surgical thresholds.

cards.title: Inferior Vena Cava Filters in Adolescents with Thromboembolic Disease: Technical Outcomes, Retrieval, and the Role of Skeletal Maturity.
cards.abstract: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity. Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage. Retrieval was attempted once the initial indication had resolved and anticoagulation was feasible. Implantation succeeded in every case; mean caval diameter was 17.9 ± 3.0 mm. Retrieval was attempted in 22 of 26 filters and succeeded in 19 (86% of attempts, 79% by intent to retrieve, 73% overall). One successful retrieval required a second attempt with an adjunctive loop-snare maneuver. Median indwelling time was 89 days (range 1-489). All three unsuccessful retrievals occurred at Risser stage 3 or below (3 of 7 versus 0 of 15 attempted; P = .02), not explained by caval diameter (P = .33). Seven filters (27%) remained in situ. No periprocedural adverse events occurred. Both retained filters assessed by CT showed caval wall penetration, one with strut fracture and asymptomatic migration at 16 years; chronic caval occlusion developed in one patient. Off-label IVCF placement in adolescents achieved high technical and retrieval success. Retrieval failure was confined to skeletally immature patients and was not explained by caval diameter. Strut fracture with migration at long-term imaging reinforces the need for timely retrieval.

cards.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs.
cards.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 "FADDosome" complexes, restrained by cFLIPL. Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor-driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor-initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor-driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

cards.title: Claims-based frailty and short-term adverse events after esophageal or gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection in older adults.
cards.abstract: Risk stratification before esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in older adults often relies on age and comorbidity; however, these measures may not capture vulnerability reflected in routinely collected claims data. We aimed to evaluate the claims-based frailty and short-term adverse events association after esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection. We used a nationwide Japanese administrative database to identify patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent first esophageal or gastric ESD. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), calculated from diagnoses during a 2 year lookback period. After 1:1 propensity score matching, frail and non-frail patients were compared. The primary outcome was binary composite of short-term adverse events, including in-hospital perforation/peritonitis, delayed bleeding, thromboembolism, aspiration pneumonia, and 30 day all-cause mortality. Component outcomes, survival, length of stay, costs, and readmission were also evaluated. Among 15,184 eligible patients, 4,970 matched pairs were included. Frailty was associated with the composite adverse outcome (adjusted odds ratio 1.35; 95% confidence interval 1.19-1.53), driven mainly by perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. No significant differences were observed for 30 day mortality, thromboembolic events, or aspiration pneumonia. Frailty was also associated with lower overall survival during follow-up, whereas median length of stay was identical between groups. Among older adults undergoing esophageal or gastric ESD, HFRS-defined claims-based frailty was associated with higher rates of short-term adverse events, particularly perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. These findings suggest that routinely collected claims data may help identify vulnerable patients who warrant closer peri-procedural assessment and monitoring.

cards.title: A proposed three‑dimensional anatomical definition and morphometric quantification of the lateral femoral wall: a reliable CT‑based measurement system validated across two software platforms.
cards.abstract: The lateral femoral wall serves as a critical determinant of intertrochanteric fracture stability, internal fixation strategy, and postoperative clinical outcomes, and has emerged as one of the core research focuses in orthopedic trauma. However, no consensus exists on the anatomical boundaries, standardized measurement criteria, and morphometric parameter system of the lateral femoral wall. Consecutive individuals aged 18 years and above who had full-length or upper-half CT scans of the femur were included from January 2015 to June 2024. Complete three‑dimensional boundaries and a comprehensive measurement system for the lateral femoral wall were established. All morphometric parameters were independently quantified using two software platforms (Mimics and SuperImage). Statistical analyses were performed to assess inter‑software consistency, intra‑ and inter‑observer reliability, sex‑based morphological differences, and correlations between lateral wall morphology and age as well as body height. A total of 171 participants were enrolled in this study, consisting of 91 females and 80 males. No statistically significant inter-software differences were detected for any of the morphometric parameters (all P > 0.05). Inter-software measurements showed significant positive correlations (Pearson r = 0.740-0.986, all P < 0.001), and no systematic bias via Bland-Altman analyses. Intra- and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) revealed substantial to almost perfect agreement for the central coronal curvature diameter (0.811-0.836, 95% CIs 0.764-0.876), while all other morphometric parameters achieved almost perfect agreement, with intra-observer ICCs of 0.858-0.993 and inter-observer ICCs of 0.841-0.984. Significant sexual dimorphisms were observed: males had greater lateral wall height, segmental width and cortical thickness at most planes (all P < 0.05). Body height was the dominant positive determinant of most morphological parameters (ρ = 0.194 to 0.909, all P < 0.05), whereas age exerted only mild-to-moderate negative effects on segmental width and thickness (ρ = - 0.578 to - 0.174, all P < 0.05). Significant positive width-thickness correlations existed at all transverse planes (all P < 0.001). Notably, the central coronal curvature diameter showed no sex-related difference (P = 0.216) and remained stable across age and height subgroups. This study proposed a reliable 3D measurement system for the lateral femoral wall with complete anatomical boundary definition. The central coronal curvature, independent of sex, age and height, can act as a universal baseline contour for implant design. In contrast, its overall dimensions differ across sex and height, supporting patient‑specific implant sizing.

cards.title: Physiological learning involves intrasynaptic reorganization of GluA1-containing AMPA receptors
cards.abstract: Learning and memory formation depend on persistent modifications of excitatory synaptic transmission in the hippocampus through changes in AMPA receptor (AMPAR) content and properties at potentiated synapses. However, directly demonstrating such changes after physiological, behavior-driven learning in the intact brain has remained technically difficult. Using SDS-digested freeze-fracture replica labeling (SDS-FRL), we examined the density and nanoscale localization of AMPAR subunits GluA1, GluA2, and GluA3 in the mouse hippocampal CA1 pyramidal cells. GluA2 density was higher than GluA1 and GluA3 densities at both synaptic and extrasynaptic sites, consistent with previous studies showing that AMPARs in CA1 pyramidal cells mostly contain GluA2. The extrasynaptic density of GluA3 was substantially lower than those of GluA1 and GluA2, pointing to distinct trafficking mechanisms. GluA1- and GluA2-containing receptors were enriched at synaptic peripheries, whereas GluA3 was more centrally localized and clustered, a subunit-specific intrasynaptic organization consistent with differential roles in plasticity. To investigate learning-induced reorganization, we combined the inhibitory avoidance, hippocampus-dependent contextual learning paradigm with SDS-FRL in the CA1 stratum radiatum. Learning induced a selective increase in synaptic GluA1 density accompanied by a concurrent decrease in GluA2 density, consistent with a compositional shift toward higher-conductance GluA1-containing receptors, specifically in the proximal CA1 area. Strikingly, we found a redistribution of GluA1 from the synaptic periphery toward the center, accompanied by increased clustering. These findings reveal intrasynaptic receptor redistribution alongside subunit composition change, a nanoscale molecular signature at CA3-CA1 synapses, which may constitute a mechanism of hippocampal memory formation in physiological learning.

cards.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of primary semi-constrained total elbow arthroplasty at 10-year mean follow-up.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term clinical and radiological outcomes in patients undergoing semi-constrained total elbow arthroplasty (TEA). Postoperative complications and implant survival rates were also investigated. Of 68 patients who underwent primary semi-constrained TEA, data from 62 with a minimum follow-up of 5 years were analyzed. The mean follow-up duration was 117.1 months (range, 60-246 months). Forty-one patients had posttraumatic conditions, 11 had rheumatoid arthritis, and 10 had osteoarthritis. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS) and Oxford Elbow Score (OES), whereas radiological outcomes were analyzed using radiolucent lines and bushing wear. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to determine the implant survival rate. At the final follow-up, the MEPS and OES were 88.2 (range, 55-100) and 31.6 (range, 22-42), respectively. Radiolucency of type 3 or 4 was observed on the humeral side in four patients and on the ulnar side in three patients. Grade 1 and 2 bushing wear was present in seven and three patients, respectively. The total complication rate was 25.8% (16/62), and the reoperation rate was 17.7% (11/62). Four patients underwent reoperation for periprosthetic infection after previous open reduction and internal fixation for acute fractures. In addition, three patients underwent hinge system change for hinge dissociation, four sustained periprosthetic fractures, one underwent revision TEA for gross loosening, and one underwent open repair for triceps rupture. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that the 5-, 10-, and 15-year survival rates of the implants were 100%, 92.8%, and 77.5%, respectively. Clinical and radiological outcomes of primary semi-constrained TEA were reasonably good at a mean 10-year follow-up. Type 3 or 4 radiolucency was observed in seven patients and complete bushing wear in three patients, while the 10-year implant survival rate was 92.8%. Level of evidence: IV.

cards.title: Bone-Targeting Antibodies for Skeletal Precision Therapy.
cards.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies have transformed the treatment of cancer, inflammation, infection, and disorders of bone biology by recognizing disease-associated molecular targets with high specificity. However, achieving therapeutically effective antibody concentrations at the site of disease remains a major challenge, as systemic administration does not inherently result in efficient tissue-specific delivery. Bone is a particularly demanding destination because mineralized matrix, limited vascular access, marrow complexity, and active remodeling can restrict local antibody exposure. Recent advances in bone-targeting antibody design point to a powerful reframing in which antibodies can be engineered not only for antigen specificity but also for tissue specificity. By attaching hydroxyapatite-binding motifs such as bisphosphonates or acidic peptides, antibodies can be endowed with bone-homing capabilities. The efficacy of this strategy has now been validated across multiple preclinical disease models, including breast cancer bone metastasis and osteoporosis-related bone loss. The next challenge is to define how affinity, valency, conjugation site, circulation time, and release should be tuned for each skeletal disease.

cards.title: Physiologic Stress During Walking and Cycling Early After Cardiac Surgery.
cards.abstract: To characterize cardiac effort and heart rate (HR) responses during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) early after cardiac surgery, compare HR patterns between walking and cycle ergometry, and evaluate differences by sex, frailty, and atrial fibrillation status. We analyzed a publicly available PhysioNet dataset of adults ≥65 years with pre-frailty/frailty undergoing cardiac surgery who completed a 6MWT and symptom-limited cycle ergometry with continuous single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring (Polar H10). Cardiac effort was defined as total 6MWT heartbeats divided by distance walked (beats/m). Associations with cycle-ergometry performance were assessed using Spearman correlations with bootstrap CI; paired t tests compared HR responses between modalities; subgroup differences were evaluated using Welch t tests and multivariable linear regression. Of 80 enrolled participants, 66 (83%) had analyzable 6MWT ECG recordings (mean age 73 ± 5 years; 67% male; 18 ± 8 days post-surgery). Mean 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) was 300 ± 79 m, and mean cardiac effort was 1.62 ± 0.52 beats/m. In 38 participants with paired cycle-ergometry data, HR responses were similar between walking and cycling. Greater 6MWD was associated with better cycle-ergometry performance, while higher cardiac effort was associated with lower cycle-ergometry performance. In multivariable analysis, female sex was independently associated with higher cardiac effort (β = .34 beats/m; P = .042), atrial fibrillation with lower average and end-of-test HR (P ≤ .035), and greater frailty with shorter 6MWD (P = .036). Cardiac effort is a feasible ECG-derived metric that complements 6MWD by integrating heart rate response with functional performance early after cardiac surgery. In this frail, predominantly beta-blocked cohort, HR responses during walking closely mirrored cycle ergometry.

cards.title: Mapping Perioperative Vulnerability and Optimization in Hepatectomy: A Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis of Sarcopenia, Frailty, and Prehabilitation.
cards.abstract: Risk assessment before hepatectomy is no longer based only on tumor burden, liver function, and technical resectability. Muscle status, frailty, nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation are now discussed more often in this setting. This study reviewed how these topics appear in the hepatectomy literature and how they relate to the more established body composition literature. Relevant publications were retrieved from the Science Citation Index Expanded of the Web of Science Core Collection. CiteSpace (version 6.4.R1), VOSviewer (version 1.6.20), and RStudio (version 2025.05.1 + 513) were used to analyze publication trends, collaboration networks, journal distributions, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence, citation bursts, and temporal patterns. A total of 498 publications were included. Publication output increased during the study period, especially after 2021. Japan, China, and the United States contributed the most papers, whereas several European countries had stronger positions in the collaboration network. Sarcopenia and body composition remained the main basis of this literature. Frailty, functional vulnerability, nutritional support, exercise, and prehabilitation appeared more often in recent years, but collaboration between institutions and author groups was still incomplete. Current hepatectomy research in this area is still centered on body composition-based risk assessment. Newer studies have added frailty, functional reserve, nutrition, exercise capacity, and prehabilitation to the same perioperative discussion. Future work should test practical pathways that connect these measures with surgical decision-making, patient selection, and preoperative optimization.

cards.title: Cellular senescence and the SASP in the oral-metabolic axis: a putative link between periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
cards.abstract: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic inflammatory disorders with a bidirectional clinical association. Although microbial, immune, and metabolic mechanisms contribute to this relationship, they do not fully explain the persistence of inflammation and defective tissue repair. Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) may provide an additional framework for understanding this interaction. Within periodontal tissues, sustained microbial and metabolic stress may promote senescence-associated changes that disturb local immune regulation, tissue regeneration and bone homeostasis. These processes could interact with microbial dysbiosis and systemic inflammation as part of the oral-metabolic axis. However, the available evidence remains uneven. Diabetes-related stress can promote senescence-like changes in periodontal tissues, whereas direct evidence that periodontal senescence impairs distant metabolic organs is limited. This review examines the evidence linking cellular senescence to periodontal inflammation and T2DM, and discusses the emerging preclinical evidence for targeting senescent cells and the SASP.

cards.title: Unveiling the Mica-Interlayer-Mediated Exfoliation of β-Ga2O3 Thin Films.
cards.abstract: Mechanically exfoliable oxide membranes on mica are promising for flexible optoelectronics, but the actual fracture pathway during oxide/mica delamination remains unclear. Here, β-Ga2O3 thin films were epitaxially grown on mica by pulsed laser deposition, and their tape-assisted exfoliation behavior was investigated. Although the films could be transferred onto adhesive supports, mica-related residues were repeatedly detected on the backside of the exfoliated β-Ga2O3 films. Combined XRD, SEM/EDS line-scan, XPS, and rocking-curve results show that exfoliation does not occur through clean separation at the β-Ga2O3/mica interface, but instead involves cleavage within the mica substrate. First-principles calculations show that the β-Ga2O3/mica adhesion energy reaches 40.6 meV Å-2, approximately 40% higher than the mica interlayer cleavage energy of 28.9 meV Å-2, supporting the preferential mica-interlayer fracture pathway. Energy decomposition further reveals that the DFT-D3 dispersion term accounts for 46.5% of the calculated β-Ga2O3/mica work of separation, challenging the simplified assumption of a purely vdW-bonded oxide/mica interface. This work identifies a mica-interlayer-mediated exfoliation mechanism and provides guidance for controlled transfer and interfacial cleanliness of flexible β-Ga2O3 membranes.

cards.title: Outcome following lag screw fixation of non-C3 carpal slab fractures in horses.
cards.abstract: To describe clinical features and short- and long-term outcomes of horses treated with lag screw fixation of slab fractures of the radial carpal (Cr), intermediate carpal (Ci), ulnar carpal (Cu), second (C2) or fourth (C4) carpal bones. Retrospective case study. Horses (n = 19) treated with lag screw fixation for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2 or C4. Medical records of patients with carpal slab fractures were reviewed, and those undergoing internal fixation of slab fractures involving Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4 carpal bones from January 2008 to January 2026 were included. Long-term outcomes were obtained by a standardized questionnaire. Descriptive data are presented. Predominant breeds included Thoroughbreds (7/19) and Warmbloods (7/19). A total of 10 of 19 fractures were caused by traumatic falls, including six during recovery from general anesthesia. Five of 19 surgeries were performed with arthroscopic guidance, and 14/19 surgeries were performed with computed tomography (CT) guidance. Survival beyond 1 year was 88%, with 53% returning to previous athletic function and 71% owner satisfaction. Prognosis for return to the previous level of work was good and comparable to that previously reported for internal fixation of C3 slab fractures. Lag screw fixation provides good outcomes in survival, return to work, and owner satisfaction for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4.

cards.title: Cytological Findings and Diagnostic Pitfalls of a Rare Tumor Arising From a Rare Site: "The Story of Chondromyxoid Fibroma of Great Toe".
cards.abstract: Chondromyxoid fibroma (CMF) is a rare, benign cartilaginous tumor composed of myxoid and fibrous components, accounting for approximately 1% of all bone tumors. It typically arises in the metaphysis of long bones, with epiphyseal involvement of the short tubular bones of the hand and foot being uncommon. We report the case of a 14-year-old girl who presented with pain and a gradually progressive swelling of the left great toe, occurring after a fracture sustained 2.5 years earlier. Radiological findings were suggestive of an aneurysmal bone cyst or giant cell tumor. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) revealed hypercellular smears comprising pleomorphic oval to spindle-shaped cells along with dense, pink osteochondroid material; the cytological diagnosis was rendered equivocal, and malignancy could not be excluded. Subsequent histopathological examination showed a well-circumscribed tumor with a lobular architecture composed of alternating hypocellular and hypercellular areas of myxomatous stroma and immature cartilaginous cells, confirming a diagnosis of chondromyxoid fibroma. Although a low-grade tumor, CMF may show nuclear atypia histologically and can mimic chondrosarcoma; distinguishing between the two is of paramount importance to avoid over-diagnosis and unnecessarily aggressive treatment of this benign entity. Complete surgical resection with long-term follow-up remains the mainstay of management, given the relatively high rate of recurrence.

cards.title: Robotic emergency surgery in geriatric care.
cards.abstract: Older adults present unique challenges in emergency general surgery (EGS) due to increased comorbidities and frailty. While minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including laparoscopic (lap) and robotic techniques, reduces perioperative morbidity, the role of minimally invasive EGS in geriatric patients remains unclear. This study compares outcomes for geriatric EGS patients following robotic, lap, and open procedures. We hypothesize that MIS approaches would improve perioperative outcomes in geriatric patients. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the ACS-NSQIP database (2022-2023) including patients ≥65 years undergoing emergent or urgent intra-abdominal surgery. Operative approach was categorized as robotic, lap, or open. The primary outcome was severe complication, and secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, and readmission. 58,940 patients were included: 1832 robotic, 30,137 lap, and 26,971 open. With robotic vs lap and open, operative time was shortest (82.5 vs 110 vs 96 min, p < 0.001), conversion to open was less frequent (6.2 vs 12.9%, p < 0.001), and LOS was shorter (4 vs 4 vs 8 days, p < 0.001). Readmission and reoperation were lowest following MIS (9.2 vs 7.9 vs 9.8%, and 3.7 vs 3.3% vs 7.6%, both p < 0.001). After propensity matching, robotic patients had higher ASA scores and more transfusions but lower rates of sepsis (2.6 vs 6.5%) and mortality (2.3 vs 2.7%) compared to the lap group (p < 0.001). Multivariable regression demonstrated decreased risk of severe complications for patients who underwent robotic surgery (p = 0.025) with no difference in operative time or LOS, and patients were more likely to be discharged home. Robotic EGS in geriatric patients is associated with fewer severe complications, lower conversion rates, shorter LOS, and favorable discharge disposition.

cards.title: Aqueous extract of Ormocarpum cochinchinense promotes fracture healing through coordinated angiogenic, osteogenic, and cytoprotective mechanisms.
cards.abstract: Ormocarpum cochinchinense has long been used in traditional medicine for the management of bone fractures. Despite its widespread ethnomedicinal use, scientific evidence supporting its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in fracture healing remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the safety and fracture-healing potential of the aqueous extract of O. cochinchinense (OCE) with emphasis on angiogenesis and osteogenesis, and to elucidate its role in modulating endothelial cell inflammation. The biological activity of OCE was assessed using a combination of in vitro and in vivo approaches. The phytochemical characterization of the extract was performed using GC-MS analysis. The safety profile of OCE was assessed through in vivo toxicity evaluation and the fracture-healing efficacy was investigated through radiographic and histological analyses. Molecular mechanisms were examined by assessing the expression of angiogenic and osteogenic marker genes. Additionally, endothelial protective effects were evaluated under lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory conditions by measuring oxidative stress markers and pro-inflammatory mediators. GC-MS analysis identified a total of 25 phytocompounds in OCE. OCE exhibited no observable toxicity in rats. It accelerated fracture healing by promoting advanced callus formation, enhancing collagen-rich matrix deposition, and improving mineralization. OCE significantly upregulated angiogenic (VEGFA, VEGFR2) and osteogenic (BMP2, SP7, RUNX2, ALP, Col1A1, OPN, OCN) gene expression, indicating coordinated activation of bone regeneration pathways. Furthermore, OCE protected endothelial cells from LPS-induced cytotoxicity by reducing reactive oxygen species and nitric oxide levels and downregulating inflammatory mediators including NOX1, NOX2, NOX4, iNOS, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α. OCE promoted fracture healing through a multifaceted mechanism involving enhanced angiogenesis and osteogenesis. It also confers endothelial protection by mitigating inflammation and oxidative stress that might aid in improved endothelial function and thereby fracture healing. These findings validate its traditional use and highlight its potential as a safe and effective natural therapeutic agent for bone regeneration.

cards.title: The Senokine Gas6 Promotes Aortic Valve Calcification Through CaMKII–DRP1–Mediated Terminal Scission of Mitochondrial‐Derived Vesicles
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an age‐associated valvular disorder in which calcification expands from discrete foci into adjacent tissue. We investigated whether mitochondrial‐derived vesicles (MDVs) released by human valvular interstitial cells (hVICs) exert pro‐calcific effects on recipient cells and how MDV release is regulated. Using ex vivo hemodynamic perfusion of human CAVD tissue, multi‐omics profiling, live‐cell single‐organelle tracking, MDV transfer assays, and in vivo Gas6 deletion, we found that calcifying hVICs hypersecreted MDVs that exerted pro‐calcific effects in recipient hVICs. High‐resolution imaging showed that mitochondria remodeled into donut‐shaped structures under pro‐osteogenic conditions; these structures served as physical platforms for MDV budding. Human CAVD valve tissues and hVICs treated with pro‐osteogenic medium also exhibited senescence‐associated features. Multi‐omics profiling identified growth arrest‐specific 6 (Gas6), a senokine, among 36 concordantly upregulated candidates. Functional analyzes showed that Gas6 promoted terminal MDV scission while leaving donut‐shaped mitochondrial precursor formation intact. Mechanistically, Gas6 promoted intracellular Ca 2+ accumulation, calcium/calmodulin‐dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) activation, and dynamin‐related protein 1 (DRP1) phosphorylation at Ser616, supporting a Ca 2+ –CaMKII–DRP1 axis that facilitates terminal MDV scission. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII or DRP1 reduced MDV hypersecretion and subsequent recipient‐cell calcification, and Gas6 deletion in vivo attenuated valvular stenosis, calcification, and fibrotic remodeling. These findings identify Gas6‐dependent terminal MDV scission as a mechanism contributing to the intercellular propagation of valvular calcification in a CAVD context characterized by senescence‐associated features.

cards.title: Beyond the Operating Room: Orthopaedic Advocacy, Identity, and Wider Impact.
cards.abstract: ➢ Orthopaedic identity is traditionally anchored in the operating room, where technical skill, decisive intervention, and operative outcomes remain central to professional validation. Yet orthopaedic surgeons also encounter realities that no implant can fully address: motor vehicle collisions, unsafe work, poverty, delayed access, disability, rehabilitation gaps, and loss of livelihood. We argue that orthopaedic responsibility may, in selected circumstances, extend beyond direct operative care into advocacy, education, systems improvement, disability inclusion, public engagement, and health-policy work.➢ Drawing on examples from global surgery, surgical safety, the Ponseti method, rural fracture-care ethics, and professional identity formation, we examine how surgeons may translate clinical experience into wider public benefit. We propose that nonoperative roles should not be justified by personal fulfillment alone, but by whether they multiply benefit: improving access, safety, training, dignity, public trust, policy, rehabilitation, or community outcomes beyond an individual operative caseload.➢ We also address the tension between the urgent need for operating surgeons and the potential societal benefit of surgeons serving in wider roles. In health systems already constrained by workforce pressures and waiting lists, advocacy beyond the operating room must remain accountable to patients and communities. The key ethical question is whether such work subtracts from surgical capacity or whether it strengthens the conditions under which musculoskeletal care is delivered.➢ Operative service remains foundational to orthopaedic identity. However, if orthopaedic surgery is understood as a moral practice directed toward restoring function, relieving pain, and protecting dignity, its responsibilities cannot be confined entirely within the operating room walls.

cards.title: Readability and Content Integrity of Discharge Documents for Common Pediatric Orthopaedic Procedures Before and After Artificial Intelligence Simplification.
cards.abstract: Caregivers of pediatric orthopaedic surgical patients routinely receive discharge documents written at reading levels exceeding established health literacy recommendations. This disparity creates a significant barrier to comprehension and adherence to postoperative instructions. While artificial intelligence (AI) language models offer a scalable solution for simplification of medical text, a systematic evaluation of the ability to preserve critical content in surgical discharge materials remains lacking. Publicly available caregiver-facing discharge documents for 3 common pediatric orthopaedic conditions, supracondylar humerus fractures (CRPP), pediatric forearm fractures (ORIF/CRPP), and slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE pinning), were collected. All documents underwent AI simplification using a standardized prompt with ChatGPT (version 5.2; OpenAI). Readability was assessed using 6 validated indices for both original and simplified documents. A structured content integrity review was conducted on all simplified documents by 2 independent reviewers to assess for safety-critical errors, completeness gaps, and factual accuracy, with inter-rater reliability quantified by Cohen kappa. Fifteen documents were obtained from institutions across 9 US states. After AI simplification, mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) decreased from 8.91 (SD: 1.38) to 4.97 (SD: 2.14), a mean reduction of 3.94 grade levels (95% CI: 2.65-5.23; P<0.001; Cohen d=1.69). All 6 readability indices improved across all documents. Eleven of 15 documents (73%) achieved the target readability threshold of FKGL 6 or below, compared with zero at baseline. Content integrity review identified 35 flags across 14 of 15 documents: 12 safety-critical errors, 16 completeness gaps, and 7 accuracy concerns. Cohen kappa was 0.87 for agreement on whether a change was clinically meaningful, 0.85 for severity classification, and 0.89 for flag category. Three documents had content omissions sufficient to require clinician revision before clinical use. Greater word-count reduction was associated with a higher burden of safety-critical flags (Spearman rho 0.63; P=0.012). While ChatGPT substantially reduced the reading complexity of pediatric orthopaedic discharge documents, it also introduced safety-critical alterations. AI-assisted simplification should be implemented only with structured clinician review. Larger word-count reductions were associated with more safety-critical alterations, so the magnitude of reduction may help prioritize which simplified documents receive the closest clinician review. Level III.

cards.title: Deep Learning-Based Anatomical Level Classification of Craniofacial CT Slices: Comparison of CNN Architectures and Ensemble Methods
cards.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) interpretation requires recognition of the anatomical level of each slice. Classification may facilitate preprocessing and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. We developed deep learning models to classify craniofacial CT slices into six anatomical categories. A total of 11,769 images were collected from a multicenter database involving 10 Japanese university hospitals and the public Head-Neck-Radiomics-HN1 dataset. Patients were divided into training (70%) and evaluation (30%) sets. Five CNN architectures were trained from scratch, and hard- and soft-voting ensembles were evaluated. Individual-model accuracy ranged from 94.72% to 96.09%; the hard-voting ensemble achieved 96.46% accuracy (Cohen's k = 0.954). Although performance differed among individual models (Cochran's Q = 99.29, p < 0.001), the ensemble did not significantly outperform EfficientNetV2B1 (McNemar's p = 0.163). Errors occurred mainly between adjacent anatomical regions. Deep learning can classify craniofacial CT slices accurately and may support automated dataset organization and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. External validation is needed.

cards.title: Targeting skin ageing at the source: a novel cellular reprogramming approach using natural extract combinations
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence is a driver of skin ageing that leads to structural deterioration and aesthetic changes. This study evaluated a novel senomorphic strategy, using synergistic combinations of natural small molecules to target RNA splicing regulation via upstream ERK/AKT signaling pathways. Nature-identical synthetic molecules, and corresponding extracts were assessed for cytotoxicity, impact on senescent cell load, proliferation, DNA damage load and SASP markers in naturally aged human primary skin cells. A topical, simple formulation was evaluated for impact on senescence and skin structure using 3D human ex vivo full-thickness skin explants exposed to 1.5 J/cm2 UVC irradiation. Combination of H. lupulus and G. biloba extracts produced a dose-dependent senomorphic impact of up to 45% in aged dermal fibroblasts and 10% in aged human primary keratinocytes (p [≤] 0.0001 & 0.001), without inducing cell proliferation. A 50% decrease in DNA damage load was also observed (p [≤] 0.0001). Qualitatively, the simple formulation mitigated UV-induced epidermal hyperplasia, restored collagen fiber organization, and reduced markers of senescence and inflammation. Targeting cellular senescence is an emerging traction point to address the root biological causes of skin ageing. Targeting the splicing dysregulation/senescence axis using combinations of natural plant extracts may provide a novel mode of action to reprogram senescent cells for repair and protection of skin structure and function.

cards.title: Spatiotemporal transcriptomic dynamic across the auditory pathway from young to old age in 5xFAD Alzheimer disease mice
cards.abstract: Auditory dysfunction can precede clinical dementia, but the molecular progression of Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology from the sensory periphery to auditory cortex remains poorly resolved. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of auditory cortex (AC), inferior colliculus (IC), cochlear nucleus (CN), and cochlea from 5xFAD and wild-type mice at postnatal day 50 (P50), 8 months, 11 months, and 16 months. Age-specific genotype effects and Genotype x Age interactions were evaluated using DESeq2, followed by Hallmark, KEGG, and Gene Ontology gene-set enrichment analyses and a cross-region synthesis of interaction trajectories. At P50, AC, IC, and cochlea showed coordinated suppression of mitochondrial metabolism, translation, RNA processing, and proteostasis, whereas CN displayed the opposite metabolic and biosynthetic profile together with reduced synaptic and adhesion programs. At 8 months, inflammatory interactions converged across all four regions, including interferon, complement, IL6-JAK-STAT3, and broader immune-response pathways. This coordination fractured at 11 months: AC and IC retained inflammatory and negative synaptic shifts, whereas CN and cochlea frequently changed in the opposite direction, including transient positive shifts in synaptic programs. By 16 months, immune interactions converged again, while metabolic, proteostatic, and synaptic trajectories remained region dependent; CN opposed AC, IC, and cochlea in several major metabolic programs. These findings define a distributed, asynchronous response rather than a monotonic bottom-up or top-down progression. The resulting spatiotemporal map links early metabolic stress, intermediate central-peripheral decoupling, and late inflammatory convergence, providing a molecular framework for evaluating peripheral to central auditory gain and temporal-processing measures as candidate indicators of AD progression.

cards.title: Wnt10b is required for the increase in cancellous bone caused by oxidized phospholipids blockade.
cards.abstract: Oxidized phospholipids containing phosphatidylcholine (PC-OxPLs), present on oxidized low-density lipoproteins (OxLDL) and apoptotic cells, are pathogenic in osteoporosis. PC-OxPLs are bound by the IgM E06 antibody, which blocks their deleterious effects. Overexpression of the antigen-binding domain of E06 (E06-scFv) increases bone mass in 6-month-old mice and attenuates high fat diet- and age-induced bone loss by increasing osteoblast number and function. The mechanisms mediating the anabolic effect of oxidized phospholipids blockade are unclear. In previous work, we showed that E06-scFv upregulates the expression of Wnt10b and Wnt signaling in vivo. We report herein that the bulk of Wnt10b in the bone microenvironment originates from osteoblast lineage cells. OxLDL decreases the expression of Wnt10b and Wnt target genes in osteoblastic cells, and single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of mesenchymal cells reveals an increase in Wnt10b and Wnt target genes in pre-osteoblasts and osteoblasts of E06-scFv transgenic mice compared to WT. Loss of Wnt10b prevents the increases in BMD by DXA and in vertebral and femoral cancellous bone in 6-month-old E06-scFv transgenic male mice, and attenuates these increases in female mice. Collectively, these findings indicate that oxidized phospholipids decrease bone mass, at least in part, by suppressing Wnt10b.
