cards.title: AI-derived panoramic score and its association with major systemic diseases: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: This study evaluated whether an AI-generated, panoramic radiograph-based score was associated with five selected systemic diseases. 26,550 panoramic radiographs from two hospitals were analyzed using an AI model that detected teeth and implants and quantified alveolar bone loss. A radiograph-based score (0-100) was derived from missing teeth and weighted bone-loss severity. Associations with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoporosis, ischemic heart disease, and hyperlipidemia were assessed using between-group comparisons, prevalence trends across score bins, and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Incremental discrimination over covariates alone was quantified using ΔAUC and the DeLong test. Patients with each condition had lower scores than controls (all P<0.001), with the largest adjusted difference for diabetes mellitus (β=-6.25). Prevalence of all five conditions showed a decreasing trend across ascending score strata (Cochran-Armitage P<0.001), with the highest Q1-to-Q5 relative risk for ischemic heart disease (4.73). After adjustment, the score remained independently associated with all diseases (AUC, 0.74-0.80), with significant incremental discrimination for diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia (ΔAUC =0.0015-0.0154; DeLong P<0.0188) but not ischemic heart disease or osteoporosis. An AI-derived panoramic radiograph-based score was independently associated with five selected systemic diagnoses. Clinical significance An AI-derived score obtained from routinely acquired panoramic radiographs was independently associated with major systemic diseases. This automated, quantitative score may serve as an exploratory image-based index, supporting integrated management between dental and medical care.

cards.title: Nonpharmacological interventions for frailty and sarcopenia in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers: A Bayesian network meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: To compare the effects of nonpharmacological interventions on frailty, sarcopenia, and related physical-function outcomes in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers, we conducted a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 21 randomized controlled trials from 10 countries. Most interventions did not show clear benefits for frailty, sarcopenia, gait speed, Timed Up and Go performance, sit-to-stand performance, skeletal muscle index, or 6-min walk distance. Prehabilitation exercise showed a low-certainty benefit for handgrip strength, whereas enhanced nutritional support and intensive physiotherapy showed limited benefits for patient-reported physical function. However, these findings were based on small, sparsely connected networks, and the certainty of evidence was generally low or very low. No single intervention was consistently effective across outcomes. These results highlight the need for larger, cancer-specific trials using standardized outcome definitions and clearer reporting of intervention intensity, adherence, safety, and feasibility.

cards.title: Astragaloside IV Attenuates Cardiac Aging Through Restoring Mitochondrial Dynamics Homeostasis by Promoting SIRT3-Mediated DRP1 Deacetylation.
cards.abstract: Cardiac aging is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, with an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics homeostasis being a pivotal aspect. Although Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) has been shown to delay aging, its specific effects on cardiac aging and the link to mitochondrial dynamics remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the role and regulatory mechanism of AS-IV in delaying cardiac aging by using naturally aged mouse models and D-galactose (D-gal)-induced H9c2 cell senescence models. The results demonstrated that AS-IV reduced the expression of senescence markers (p16INK4a, p21, and p53), β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal), and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors (Il6, Il1b, and Tnfa) while also significantly ameliorating aging-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis. Furthermore, AS-IV significantly enhanced mitochondrial morphology and function in cardiomyocytes. This improvement was demonstrated by increased mitochondrial membrane potential, elevated ATP production, and reduced ROS levels. Mechanistically, AS-IV upregulated SIRT3 and promoted its interaction with DRP1, leading to the inhibition of DRP1 acetylation. This action suppressed excessive mitochondrial fission and thereby improved mitochondrial dynamics. Transfection with SIRT3-siRNA attenuated the beneficial effects of AS-IV. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that AS-IV mitigates cardiac aging by activating SIRT3 to mediate DRP1 deacetylation, which in turn improves mitochondrial dynamics. These findings provide a strong theoretical and experimental foundation for the potential application of AS-IV in preventing and treating age-related cardiovascular diseases.

cards.title: IRAP deficiency preserves renal function and attenuates pathology in aged mice.
cards.abstract: Senescent cell accumulation and fibrosis play a fundamental role in kidney ageing. Our aim was to determine whether the angiotensin IV/insulin-regulated aminopeptidase (IRAP) axis of the renin-angiotensin system contributes to renal function decline, fibrosis, and senescent cell accumulation in aged mice. We studied the role of IRAP in kidney ageing using IRAP knockout (KO) mice, as well as in wild-type (WT) mice treated with an IRAP inhibitor. Complementary proximal tubule and collecting duct cell models were used to determine the mechanisms by which IRAP inhibition exerts protective effects. Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) declined by 25% in WT mice between 3 and 23 months of age, concomitant with marked increases in albumin excretion, glomerulosclerosis, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and accumulation of senescent cells in the proximal tubules of the kidney. IRAP KO mice were protected against age-related decline in GFR, renal fibrosis, and senescence burden compared with age-matched WT mice. IRAP inhibition for 4 weeks (HFI-419, 500 ng/kg/min) in 28-month-old WT mice similarly prevented age-related decline in GFR and attenuated expression of cellular senescence markers. Using an in vitro model of cultured proximal tubule cells, IRAP inhibition mitigated the pro-senescent effects of oxidative stress. This was associated with shifts in the metabolic phenotype of proximal tubular cells, indicating the senoprotective effects of IRAP inhibition may be mediated in part via mitochondrial function. These studies provide evidence that IRAP deficiency is protective against chronic renal cellular senescence, fibrosis, and functional decline. Therefore, IRAP inhibition has therapeutic potential to attenuate pathological cardiorenal ageing through senoprotective mechanisms.

cards.title: Late-onset preeclampsia is characterized by accelerated placental aging.
cards.abstract: Late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE) is a major pregnancy complication characterized by hypertension and placental dysfunction, resolving only upon delivery. Here, we show that LOPE placentae undergo accelerated molecular aging, marked by telomere attrition, DNA damage, and trophoblast senescence. Using primary placental tissue and trophoblast organoids, we demonstrate oxidative stress as a driver of telomere shortening and angiogenic imbalance. Inflammation did not alter placental aging trajectories. Antioxidant treatment (superoxide dismutase) preserved telomere length, reduced DNA damage, and restored angiogenic balance, highlighting oxidative stress as a modifiable determinant of placental aging. We identify reduced expression of telomeric repeat-containing RNAs (TERRAs) as a molecular hallmark of LOPE, and show that antisense oligonucleotide-mediated TERRA depletion exacerbates telomere erosion and senescence. Together, these findings delineate oxidative stress and TERRA loss as mechanisms driving placental decline, establish trophoblast organoids as a tractable model of placental aging, and reveal potential therapeutic avenues for mitigating preeclampsia-associated placental dysfunction.

cards.title: The S-technique: A Novel Dense Polytetrafluoroethylene-assisted Surgical Technique for Peri-implant Keratinized Mucosa Preservation - A Case Review.
cards.abstract: Immediate implant placement following tooth extraction often leads to peri-implant defects that require guided bone regeneration (GBR) to achieve complete bone fill and stable osseointegration. Conventional GBR techniques typically rely on primary flap closure, coronal advancement, and additional soft-tissue grafting, which increase surgical complexity and patient morbidity. The S-Technique was introduced to enable simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration under open-healing conditions while preserving the mucogingival junction. A patient presented with a grossly decayed, painful, vertically fractured, nonrestorable maxillary right second premolar (tooth 15). After atraumatic extraction and immediate implant placement, a peri-implant gap defect with limited soft-tissue availability was noted. GBR was performed using particulate xenograft and a resorbable collagen membrane. A dense polytetrafluoroethylene membrane was then placed according to the S-technique protocol, allowing secondary epithelialization without primary closure. Healing progressed uneventfully. At 4 months, clinical assessment showed complete coverage of the peri-implant site, an adequate band of keratinized mucosa, improved soft-tissue contour, a favorable emergence profile, and stable peri-implant architecture. Prosthetic rehabilitation resulted in satisfactory esthetic and functional outcomes with maintained bone support. This case demonstrates the S-Technique as a minimally invasive dual-layer membrane approach for simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration around immediate implants. By eliminating the need for primary closure and autogenous soft-tissue grafting, it offers a predictable alternative for managing peri-implant defects in sites with limited soft-tissue availability, while promoting keratinized mucosa formation and stable peri-implant tissue integration.

cards.title: Preoperative ultrasound in pediatric supracondylar fracture-related nerve injuries: intraoperative correlation in a tertiary referral retrospective case series.
cards.abstract: Nerve palsy is a recognized complication of paediatric supracondylar humeral fractures. Most injuries recover spontaneously, a subset require surgical exploration, and identifying those who may benefit from intervention remains challenging. High-resolution ultrasound has emerged as a potential adjunct for assessing nerve injury, although its utility in this setting remains incompletely defined. A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary peripheral nerve injury center. Children less than 16 years with persistent supracondylar fracture-related nerve palsy who underwent preoperative ultrasound and surgical exploration between 2018 and 2024 were included. Ultrasound findings were categorized as structural abnormality, compression/tethering, neuroma/swelling, or entrapment and were compared with intraoperative findings. Analysis was descriptive, focusing on ultrasound detection of nerve abnormality and concordance with surgical findings. Twenty-two patients were included (mean age: 7 years). All had surgically confirmed nerve pathology. Ultrasound demonstrated nerve abnormality in 21 out of 22 cases (95%). Compression/tethering was the most common finding (18/22), followed by structural abnormality (14/22), neuroma/swelling (7/22), and entrapment (2/22). Intraoperatively, structural abnormalities were identified in 17 cases, compression/tethering in 21, neuroma in 3, and entrapment in 4. Ultrasound frequently identified nerve abnormality but demonstrated variable concordance with intraoperative findings, including overestimation of neuroma (7 vs. 3 cases) and under-detection of entrapment (2 vs. 4 cases). Preoperative ultrasound frequently demonstrated abnormal nerve features in children with persistent palsy following supracondylar humeral fracture. However, its limited concordance in characterizing specific pathology restricts its role as a standalone decision-making tool. Ultrasound findings should be interpreted alongside clinical assessment when considering surgical exploration.

cards.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury associated with cast nephropathy and marked renal interstitial plasma cell infiltration in multiple myeloma: a case report.
cards.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is frequently associated with renal impairment, most commonly due to cast nephropathy. We report a case of severe and persistent postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) in an 84-year-old man with smoldering MM who underwent posterior lumbar fixation for a lumbar burst fracture. Twelve hours after surgery, he developed profound hypotension and severe anemia due to surgical-site bleeding, followed by progressive renal dysfunction despite prompt transfusion and fluid resuscitation. Urinalysis revealed heavy proteinuria, and kidney biopsy demonstrated marked accumulation of eosinophilic casts within the tubules, consistent with cast nephropathy. In addition, marked renal interstitial infiltration by λ light-chain-restricted monoclonal plasma cells and focal peritubular capillary (PTC) occlusion were observed. Congo red staining was negative, and no significant glomerular immune deposits were detected. Renal function partially improved with supportive care but did not return to the preoperative baseline. This case suggests that postoperative AKI in MM may be multifactorial, with perioperative circulatory failure precipitating clinically overt cast nephropathy, while coexisting interstitial myeloma cell infiltration and focal PTC occlusion may increase susceptibility to ischemic injury and contribute to the severity and persistence of renal dysfunction. In patients with MM, latent myeloma-related kidney injury should be considered a potential contributor to perioperative AKI even when serum creatinine is preserved, particularly in those with marked proteinuria or elevated free light chain levels.

cards.title: Case report: Bilateral infantile acromion fractures in the setting of congenital glenoid dysplasia.
cards.abstract: We report a rare case of a 5-week-old male who presented with isolated acromion fractures occurring bilaterally 10 days apart. As scapular fractures are a high-specificity fracture for abusive injury, these findings were concerning for child abuse. The patient was later diagnosed with congenital glenoid dysplasia. Given this diagnosis with an otherwise normal medical evaluation for physical abuse, this case was deemed indeterminate for abusive injury. The multidisciplinary team consensus was that the injuries were likely fractures resulting from restriction of normal range of glenohumeral motion caused by his glenoid deformity. Literature on congenital glenoid dysplasia is limited in the pediatric population. This case highlights the need for further investigation into early presentations of congenital glenoid dysplasia and its association with acromion fractures.

cards.title: From Treadmill to Textbook: Neurovascular and Immune Mechanisms of Exercise-Induced Cognitive Enhancement.
cards.abstract: It has been well established that physical exercise is associated with augmented cognitive function, but the exact mechanisms by which peripheral activity affects the plasticity of the brain remain mechanistically elusive. This narrative review synthesises evidence from mouse models and human studies to clarify how physical exercise may enhance hippocampus-dependent cognition through systemic, neurovascular, immune, and metabolic mechanisms instead of direct "brain training" alone. This distinction is supported by the limited far transfer shown in many cognitive training models, wherein improvements tend to remain task- or circuit-specific rather than reflecting general skill transfer. In rodent models, voluntary physical exercise improves learning, memory, and pattern separation, and these effects correlate with changes in hippocampal neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, vascular remodelling, and neuroimmune state. A smaller pool of plasma-transfer studies suggests that these effects carry over between individual mice via circulating exercise-induced factors, reproducing select molecular and behavioural effects in completely sedentary recipient mice, but in humans, the causal relevance of such pathways remains unresolved. In rodent transfer experiments, exercise-conditioned blood plasma has been reported to reduce neuroinflammation and to modulate brain endothelial cells, positioning the neurovascular unit as a critical interface for peripheral-to-central nervous system communication. Beyond clusterin and Gpld1, a conceptual muscle-brain endocrine axis is emerging, where specific myokines (e.g., irisin, cathepsin B) and downstream metabolites released during physical exercise may act on vascular and immune interfaces to modulate structural plasticity. Emerging human data reinforce some of these investigated mechanisms, although causal relationships have yet to be established and remain limited. Overall, the available evidence supports a model whereby physical exercise improves cognitive function through changes in the immunometabolic environment, supporting hippocampal plasticity. These pathways may inform future studies aiming to preserve cognitive health during ageing, and the development of exercise-mimetic therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Coordinated Enhancement of Molecular and Spatial Fidelity for Biological Inference in Spatial Transcriptomics
cards.abstract: Understanding tissue organization requires accurate molecular quantification and faithful spatial localization. Spatial omics, particularly spatial transcriptomics (ST), face measurement trade-offs that limit simultaneous achievement of molecular and spatial fidelity across spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, molecular-tissue alignment and cell-level fidelity. Existing computational methods typically target individual aspects and optimize them in isolation, despite their interdependence. Here we present FOCUS, a multimodal generative foundation model for coordinated ST enhancement. FOCUS integrates native ST with histology images, cell masks, scRNA-seq references and spatial co-expression priors through task-specific modules, with cross-task coordination enabling joint correction of co-occurring limitations. FOCUS improved the performance of individual enhancement tasks and provided additional gains with coordinated mitigation of coupled limitations. Across immunology, tissue development and oncology, FOCUS recovered biologically consistent patterns obscured in native ST or isolated enhancement, enabling clearer inference of neutrophil-tumor interactions, spatial osteocyte differentiation and primary-metastatic HNSCC programs. Together, FOCUS establishes coordinated enhancement of molecular and spatial fidelity as a strategy for downstream biological inference from ST.

cards.title: The Role of Glucose Metabolic Reprogramming in Exercise-Attenuated Osteoporosis: a Narrative Review.
cards.abstract: The aging population has led to a significant increase in the prevalence of osteoporosis, making it an important public health issue. Emerging evidence suggests that osteoporosis is related to glucose metabolic reprogramming (GMR). Exercise is an effective non-pharmacological intervention method, and regulating GMR may be one of the pathways through which exercise improves bone health. GMR plays a critical role in regulating the function of bone cells. It influences the proliferation and differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), osteoblasts, osteocytes, and osteoclasts. Although the exact mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated, emerging studies suggest that metabolic shifts in glycolysis, the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), and the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle are critical regulators of bone homeostasis. Furthermore, preliminary evidence suggests that exercise modulates these metabolic pathways, thereby contributing to improved bone health and reduced osteoporotic risk. This narrative review provides new insights into the mechanistic understanding that GMR plays essential roles in the initiation and progression of osteoporosis. Different types of exercise may attenuate osteoporosis through the regulation of GMR.

cards.title: Frailty in kidney transplant candidates is associated with reduced likelihood of transplantation.
cards.abstract: Kidney transplantation is the optimal treatment for kidney failure; however, it represents a major physiological stress. Frailty is a clinical syndrome also characterized by decreased physiological reserve and a reduced ability to cope with stressor events. The aim of this study was to assess the association between frailty status and the likelihood of undergoing kidney transplantation. This retrospective observational study included all kidney transplant candidates waitlisted at the Kidney Transplant Center of the Parma University Hospital, Italy, between July 2018 and February 2020. Frailty status was assessed using the Fried Frailty Phenotype. Frailty was defined as a Fried frailty phenotype score ≥3, while a score of 1 or 2 indicated a pre-frail condition. The Aalen-Johansen estimator was used to estimate the cumulative probability of transplantation and death/withdrawal according to frailty status (frail vs non-frail). Adjusted analyses were performed using Fine-Gray multivariable regression models. Of the 171 patients enrolled, 39% were non-frail, 51% were pre-frail, and 10% were frail. Patients were followed for a median of 17 months; during this period, 42% underwent transplantation, whereas 6% died or were permanently removed from the waiting list. In adjusted analyses, frail and pre-frail patients combined had a 42% lower likelihood of undergoing transplantation compared with non-frail patients (SubHR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86; P = .006). Frailty among patients with advanced CKD on the kidney transplant waiting list was associated with a lower probability of undergoing transplantation.

cards.title: Post-dexamethasone cortisol levels in non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas: a pooled individual participant data analysis.
cards.abstract: Non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas (NFAI) are defined by 1 mg-dexamethasone suppression test (F-1mgDST) cortisol levels < 1.8 µg/dL. However, many individuals with NFAI may exhibit subtle hypercortisolism associated with increased cardiometabolic and skeletal risk. The aims of the present study are to compare F-1mgDST distributions between individuals with NFAI and population-based controls and to explore whether alternative F-1mgDST thresholds would meaningfully modify patient classification. This is a pooled individual participant data analysis of 7 studies evaluating cortisol secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis and/or fragility fractures, hypertension, or adrenal incidentalomas. The study included 1681 participants (915 NFAI, 766 controls) with F-1mgDST < 1.8 µg/dL. Data included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), F-1mgDST, and adrenocorticotroph hormone (ACTH). We assessed the between-group differences in F-1mgDST and ACTH and the accuracy of different F-1mgDST thresholds for identifying NFAI. Compared to controls, patients with NFAI had lower age and ACTH levels (62.1 ± 9.8 and 59.8 ± 12.0 years, 25.1 ± 14.1 pg/mL and 16.3 ± 10.4, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons), but higher BMI and F-1mgDST values (28.1 ± 4.9 and 29.0 ± 5.0 kg/m2, 1.04 ± 0.37 µg/dL and 1.13 ± 0.39 µg/dL, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons) and were more less frequently females (48.0% and 38.6%, respectively, p < 0.001). A propensity score analysis performed on 730 patients and 730 age-, BMI- and gender-matched controls confirmed these findings. We did not identify any F-1mgDST threshold with an accuracy exceeding 60% for distinguishing controls from patients with NFAI. The F-1mgDST threshold the best balance between sensitivity (54.8%) and specificity (57.2%) was set at 1.1 µg/dL (30 nmol/L), although with a low accuracy of 55.8%. Individuals with NFAI have higher F-1mgDST levels than controls. More than 40% overlap exists in F-1mgDST values between NFAI and controls.

cards.title: Prolonged tadalafil exposure promotes skeletal muscle myogenesis and regulates early myogenic markers activation in C2C12 cell lines.
cards.abstract: The regeneration of skeletal muscle depends on the activation and differentiation of myogenic progenitor cells. Tadalafil, one of the phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors, is known to modulate nitric oxide/cGMP signaling; however, its prolonged effects on myogenic progression are not well understood. This study investigates the impact of prolonged tadalafil exposure on C2C12 myoblasts and early myogenic progenitor markers activation. C2C12 cells were treated with 1 µM tadalafil for up to seven days, and analyzed for proliferation, viability, myogenesis activation and myokine release. Prolonged tadalafil treatment significantly increased cell proliferation and survival, reducing cell death at all time points. Although tadalafil enhanced the expression of early myogenic factors, it simultaneously delayed terminal differentiation, reducing MHC-positive multinucleated myotubes, while maintaining higher expression levels of Pax7 and Myf6 after seven days, consistent with a less differentiated phenotype. This result was accompanied by the upregulation of Sirt3 and IL6, and the downregulation of myostatin and TGFβ. Tadalafil promoted a highly proliferative state and preventing premature differentiation. These findings suggest its potential use as an adjuvant pharmacological therapy in the treatment of muscle-wasting disorders. However, the potent improvement of muscle regenerative machinery raises critical concerns regarding its potential misuse as a performance-enhancing drug in sport, highlighting the need for evaluation by anti-doping agencies.

cards.title: Femoral de-escalation during revision total hip arthroplasty using a rectangular-taper shortened stem.
cards.abstract: Long stems with diaphyseal fixation are widely used in revision total hip arthroplasty (RTHA) but may increase surgical complexity and compromise femoral bone stock. Primary femoral stems, used as a de-escalation strategy, could simplify RTHA in selected patients as a bone preserving strategy. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of this technique using a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem during both components RTHA. Between January 2019 and January 2025, 301 both components RTHA were prospectively included in our institutional total joint registry. Among them, 23 RTHA (20 patients, 14 men, mean age at revision = 63 years [54-71]) with femoral de-escalation with the use of a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem and a dual mobility cup construct were identified and retrospectively reviewed at latest follow-up, focusing on complications related to this reconstruction technique. Clinical outcome was evaluated with the Harris Hip Score (HHS). At a mean follow-up of 48 months (23-75), no postoperative periprosthetic fracture, mechanical failure or early loosening of the femoral reconstruction occurred. One early dislocation occurred at 41 days, managed by closed reduction without recurrence at latest follow-up. The mean HHS significantly improved from 70 (59-83) preoperatively to 94 (64-100) postoperatively, with 96% of patients achieving HHS ≥ 80 at latest follow-up. In selected patients undergoing RTHA with limited femoral bone loss, femoral de-escalation with a cementless rectangular-taper shortened stem demonstrated reliability for femoral reconstruction with no component-related complication and significant functional improvement at short-term follow-up.

cards.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation: A cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: To determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and identify clinical and functional factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation. This cross-sectional study enrolled 209 adults with stroke admitted for neurological rehabilitation. Sarcopenia was defined according to the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) algorithm, using SARC-CalF, handgrip strength, five-times sit-to-stand test, physical performance measures and appendicular skeletal muscle mass by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia. Confirmed sarcopenia was identified in 55 of 209 participants (26.3%; 95% CI: 20.6% to 32.8%). Participants with sarcopenia were older and had lower body mass index (BMI), poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment than those without sarcopenia. In the multivariable model, lower BMI (OR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.59 to 0.83), positive SARC-CalF screening (OR = 6.37; 95% CI: 2.03 to 20.05), and lower Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores (OR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.69 to 0.99) remained independently associated with sarcopenia. Motor impairment severity, assessed using Fugl-Meyer motor categories, was also independently associated with sarcopenia. DXA-confirmed post-stroke sarcopenia affected approximately one in four individuals undergoing rehabilitation and was independently associated with lower BMI, poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment. These findings indicate that sarcopenia is closely linked to functional impairment after stroke and reinforce the importance of integrating muscle health and functional assessment during rehabilitation. Early identification of individuals at risk may support more individualized rehabilitation strategies and improve clinical decision-making.

cards.title: Unraveling the shared genetic architecture of metabolic bone diseases via genomic structural equation modeling and multi-omics integration.
cards.abstract: The shared genetic etiology underlying the comorbidity of skeletal degeneration and metabolic dysregulation remains poorly understood. This study aims to decipher the pleiotropic genetic architecture of multivariate metabolic bone diseases (mvMBDs) through an integrative summary-statistics framework. We applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling (Genomic SEM) to integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for six complex traits: osteoporosis (OP), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Subsequent analyses incorporated robust fine-mapping (SuSiE/FINEMAP), transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), and partitioned heritability assessments to identify putative functional loci and regulatory mechanisms. Genomic SEM revealed significant genetic covariance among the six traits, successfully deriving a latent mvMBD construct. We identified 197 genomic risk loci, including 193 lead SNPs that did not achieve genome-wide significance in the six constituent univariate GWAS, predominantly localized in non-coding cis-regulatory elements (e.g., super-enhancers and intronic regions). Fine-mapping and TWAS prioritized critical pleiotropic genes (e.g., MACF1, CETP, SPP1, and HNF1A). Gene-set enrichment analyses identified enrichment for terms related to bone biology, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Our findings robustly demonstrate that mvMBDs are not isolated clinical entities but rather interconnected systemic syndromes underpinned by glycolipid metabolic dysregulation and shared pleiotropic regulatory networks. This study establishes a novel theoretical paradigm for the genetic basis of metabolic bone diseases, offering promising functional targets for future precision medicine interventions.

cards.title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience.
cards.abstract: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal's only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method. Union was defined radiologically, and analyses were conducted using MS Excel and SPSS. This study included 70 CPT patients; 40 male (57.1%) and 30 female (42.9%). The mean age at presentation was 3.84 years, with the first surgery at 5.38 years. Most cases were Boyd type 5 (71.43%) and Crawford type 4 (71.43%). Of 35 patients who underwent surgery, the union rate was 41.93% (13/31), with a refracture rate of 23.08% among unions. Periosteal grafting had a 50% union rate, while the Masquelet technique achieved 41.67%. This study highlights the challenges in managing Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT), emphasizing the need for personalized surgical approaches based on patient age, limb length discrepancy, and classification. Effective patient counseling on risks and benefits is crucial for informed decisions.

cards.title: Hip Fracture Is Associated With Major Wealth Loss.
cards.abstract: The annual cost of hip fractures exceeds $6 billion in the United States. Although the direct healthcare costs related to these fractures are known, the full economic impact on individual families is not well studied. Understanding the economic impacts of disease informs policy and interventions. Therefore, we studied the socioeconomic effect of hip fractures on individual household wealth. Data were sourced from the Health and Retirement Study, a longitudinal panel survey. Individuals who sustained a hip fracture between 2000 and 2016 were identified, and total household wealth was tracked from 2 years before the fracture to 4 years after. Cases were matched with controls using propensity score matching based on age, sex, race, and initial wealth. Wilcoxon rank-sum and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to evaluate wealth changes due to the non-normal data distribution. Median wealth declined by 50% after hip fractures. In contrast, the controls' median wealth remained relatively stable, decreasing by 4.8%. Cases had significantly less wealth after 4 years than controls (P = 0.025) and compared with their prefracture levels (P < 0.001). Most wealth loss in cases was due to declines in cash accounts and the value of the primary residence. The middle tertile of initial wealth was most affected, experiencing an approximately 50% decrease. Cases saw decreased stability in permanent housing, and cases without spouses faced an approximately 28% greater decrease in household wealth compared with those with spouses. Hip fractures are associated with substantial household wealth reductions, comparable with the financial burden of major illnesses such as cancer. These findings highlight the enormous value of hip fracture prevention and rapid hip fracture recovery. Sustaining a hip fracture is associated with losing half of household wealth, comparable with the amount lost by people who have cancer.

cards.title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning.
cards.abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a "dirty" mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting "dirty" irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical "gene of scrap compatibility," this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

cards.title: Association between circadian syndrome and frailty progression among middle-aged and older adults in China: A longitudinal study based on CHARLS.
cards.abstract: Frailty is a significant predictor of adverse outcomes. Circadian syndrome (CircS), a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors linked to circadian disruption, may interact with frailty; however, evidence for this relationship remains limited. A total of 7330 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included. CircS was defined by seven components. Frailty was measured by the frailty index (FI). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was employed to identify different frailty trajectories. Multinomial logistic regression models were conducted to assess the association between baseline CircS status and frailty trajectories. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the association between the number of baseline CircS components and the subsequent rate of change in FI over time. Three frailty trajectories were identified: low-stable frailty (n = 4670, 63.71%), moderate-rising frailty (n = 2109, 28.77%), and high-stable frailty (n = 551, 7.52%). Compared to participants without CircS, those with CircS at baseline had a significantly higher risk of belonging to the moderate-rising trajectory (RRR = 2.48, 95% CI: 2.17, 2.84, p <0.001) and the high-stable trajectory (RRR = 4.37, 95% CI: 3.51, 5.45, p <0.001). Furthermore, participants with 4, 5, and ≥6 CircS components had greater annual increases in FI, with additional increases of 0.0022 (95% CI: 0.0011, 0.0033, p <0.001), 0.0020 (95% CI: 0.0007, 0.0033, p <0.01), and 0.0033 (95% CI: 0.0016, 0.0049, p <0.001) per year, respectively, compared with those with <4 components. This study showed that baseline CircS status was significantly associated with unfavorable frailty trajectories, while a greater CircS component burden was associated with both higher baseline FI levels and a faster subsequent increase in FI. These findings highlight the potential relevance of CircS for identifying individuals at increased risk of adverse frailty outcomes.

cards.title: Gamified spatial‑participatory model for urban social cohesion in a post‑conflict city: Bridging accessibility, inclusion, and intergroup trust through co‑design in Kabul.
cards.abstract: Post‑conflict cities exhibit profound socio‑spatial fractures, institutional weakness, and eroded public trust. Conventional planning repeatedly fails to address ethnic segregation, accessibility disparities, and social fragmentation. The aim of this study is to propose and empirically validate an integrated model, the Gamified Spatial-Participatory Model (GSPM), that combines spatial justice theory, participatory co-design, and conflict-sensitive gamification to foster social cohesion. Using Kabul, Afghanistan, as a paradigmatic case, a sequential mixed‑methods design was employed. Quantitative spatial diagnostics mapped severe accessibility deficits, while qualitative inquiry identified deep trust deficits and cultural barriers; these jointly informed gamified co‑design workshops as the intervention. Pilot results provide strong preliminary evidence of GSPM efficacy: 90% of participants reported substantially increased engagement; gamification correlated strongly with intergroup trust (r = 0.76, p < 0.01); perceived accessibility improved by 38% in intervention areas. Critically, 70% of women and 55% of ethnic minorities reported meaningfully stronger belonging. The study demonstrates that this approach shifts planning epistemology from technocratic to deeply human, operationalising spatial justice in fragile settings, and offers transferable principles for fostering inclusion in divided urban contexts.

cards.title: Vitamin D deficiency is associated with higher frailty risk among middle-aged and older adults: a national population-based analysis of NHANES 2007-2018.
cards.abstract: Although frailty is common in older adults, the relationship between vitamin D and frailty remains unclear. Using NHANES data, this study examined the association between frailty and serum vitamin D in middle-aged and older adults. Eight thousand and sixty-four participants aged 40 and older from NHANES (2007-2018) underwent cross-sectional analysis. Serum vitamin D was categorized as deficiency (<25 nmol/L), insufficiency (25-50 nmol/L), or adequate (≥50 nmol/L). Frailty was quantified using a 49-item Frailty Index (FI) based on the cumulative deficit model; frailty was defined as FI ≥ 0.21. Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were used. The deficiency group had the highest frailty prevalence (55.9%), followed by insufficiency (42.9%) and adequate (37.2%). Frailty was significantly associated with deficiency (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.42-3.25) after full adjustment, whereas insufficiency was not significantly associated with frailty (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.95-1.38). Serum vitamin D and FI showed a U-shaped dose-response relationship, robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In middle-aged and older adults, vitamin D deficiency, but not insufficiency, is associated with higher frailty risk. Serum vitamin D may have a U-shaped association with FI. Monitoring vitamin D levels may help inform frailty management in aging populations.

cards.title: Construction and validation of an identification model for frailty in maintenance hemodialysis patients using multiple machine learning algorithms: a cross-sectional study of retrospectively collected data.
cards.abstract: Frailty adversely affects survival and quality of life in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). This study aimed to develop a clinical multimodal model to identify prevalent frailty in MHD patients. Clinical data from 626 MHD patients across four tertiary hospitals were retrospectively collected, including demographics, clinical characteristics, laboratory indicators, and physical function assessments. Frailty was assessed using the FRAIL scale. Patients from Wuxi (n = 502) were divided into training (n = 352) and internal validation (n = 150) sets, while patients from Yancheng (n = 124) formed the external validation set. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Boruta were used for feature selection. Ten machine learning models were developed and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. SHAP was applied for model interpretation. Frailty prevalence was 48.6%. Six predictors were identified: age, grip strength, comorbidities, Charlson comorbidity index (CCI), albumin, and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (pro-BNP). The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best external validation performance (AUC=0.917, 95% CI: 0.867-0.967; accuracy=0.847; sensitivity=0.850; specificity=0.844), with good calibration and clinical net benefit. The shapley additive explanations (SHAP) identified pro-BNP as the most influential predictor and revealed nonlinear associations and clinically relevant thresholds. The interpretable XGBoost model effectively identified prevalent frailty in MHD patients, demonstrating strong discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability, and may support systematic frailty screening and individualized assessment.

cards.title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association (p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage. A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

cards.title: The impact of the gut microbiome on skeletal muscle in health and disease.
cards.abstract: The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria residing the lower gastrointestinal tract, is increasingly recognized as an important influence on skeletal muscle physiology, with critical implications for muscle disorders such as sarcopenia and muscular dystrophy. Researchers have uncovered multiple microbiome-derived metabolites that alter skeletal muscle protein synthesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, protein degradation, and glucose transport. Moreover, the microbiome mediates systemic cytokine release of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor alpha, which can drive muscle loss. These studies have led to the identification of gut bacterial species (such as Veillonella atypica and Roseburia inulinivorans) that improve muscle endurance and strength when administered as probiotics in animal models. Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

cards.title: Factors associated with skeletal muscle mass in patients with Behçet's disease: An exploratory study.
cards.abstract: To investigate the prevalence of low skeletal muscle mass and factors associated with skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) in Japanese outpatients with Behçet's disease (BD), while assessing sarcopenia according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 criteria. This cross-sectional study included ambulatory outpatients with BD aged ≥40 years. SMI was measured using multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Sarcopenia was defined as low SMI with low handgrip strength. Clinical characteristics, physical functions, nutrition- and body composition-related measures, rectus femoris ultrasonography, and laboratory parameters were compared between the low- and normal-SMI groups. Associations with SMI were examined using age- and sex-adjusted and domain-specific multivariable linear regression models. Among 48 patients (mean age: 65.4±11.8 years; 45.8% women), 52.1% had Low SMI, and 10.6% of 47 participants with available SMI and handgrip strength data had sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher SMI remained associated with higher body mass index, greater handgrip strength, larger calf circumference, higher phase angle, and greater rectus femoris muscle thickness. Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

cards.title: Skeletal Responses to Unilateral Tibial Loading During Disuse in Male and Female Mice: Bilateral Skeletal Responses and HPG-Axis-Associated Gene Expression.
cards.abstract: Disuse osteoporosis induced by immobilization, bed rest, or spaceflight remains an inadequately treated condition. Whether local mechanical stimulation on a single limb can exert systemic anabolic effects during disuse, and whether such mechanotherapy is sex-dependent, are unknown. Here, male and female C57BL/6J mice (28-week-old) were assigned to ground control (GC) or 14-day hindlimb unloading (HU) groups. In both conditions, the left tibia received daily unilateral axial compressive loading, whereas the contralateral right tibia served as the non-loaded reference limb. Bone microarchitecture of both loaded and contralateral non-loaded tibiae was assessed using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), while targeted analysis of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG)-associated and osteogenic genes was performed to investigate underlying molecular responses. Compared with GC, female HU mice had lower contralateral cortical thickness, cortical area, and trabecular bone volume fraction of the tibiae, whereas male HU mice had higher mean contralateral cortical thickness and cortical area. The findings revealed sex-associated differences in selected skeletal responses. In male HU mice, preservation of selected cortical and trabecular parameters was observed in both the loaded and contralateral non-loaded tibiae within the combined unloading and unilateral-loading paradigm. In contrast, female mice exhibited a different structural response pattern, with no comparable preservation of selected parameters in the contralateral non-loaded tibia. Gene expression analysis in male non-loaded tibiae demonstrated coordinated upregulation of HPG-associated and osteogenic genes, including NR5A1, LHR, FSHR, AR, BMP2, RUNX2, and TGF-β1, whereas the female RNA-seq analysis did not identify a comparable pattern of changes in the selected genes. The contralateral structural findings and accompanying transcriptional changes in male bone raise the possibility of systemic skeletal effects during combined unloading and unilateral loading. However, the study does not establish a systemic effect caused specifically by unilateral loading or demonstrate systemic HPG-axis activation. The results highlight the potential importance of sex-specific mechanobiological pathways in the development of therapeutic strategies for disuse osteoporosis.

cards.title: Demographic, comorbidity, and temporal trends in anterior (ALIF) versus posterior (PLIF/TLIF) single-level lumbar interbody fusion: a retrospective analysis from 2015 to 2023.
cards.abstract: The aim of this study is to characterize national demographic and comorbidity profiles associated with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) versus posterior interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) and evaluate temporal utilization patterns. Using a commercial insurance database from 2015 to 2023, adults undergoing single-level ALIF or posterior interbody fusion were identified. Univariate tests compared baseline characteristics. Annual utilization trends were estimated with Poisson regression or negative binomial regression if overdispersion was present. Significance was set at P < 0.05. Among 407,319 patients, 133,323 underwent ALIF and 273,996 underwent posterior interbody fusion. Mean age was higher for posterior interbody fusion (61.8 vs. 59.5 years; P < 0.001), as was mean Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (5.3 ± 3.6 vs. 5.2 ± 3.6; P < 0.001). Sex distribution and rheumatoid arthritis were similar (P > 0.05 for all). Posterior interbody fusion patients more frequently had obesity, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, osteoporosis, and tobacco use (P < 0.001 for all). ALIF procedures increased at an average annual rate of 6.66% (95% CI, 4.60-8.47; P < 0.001), whereas posterior interbody fusion increased 1.98% per year (95% CI, -0.19-4.19; P = 0.075); the annual growth-rate difference (ALIF - posterior interbody fusion) was 4.68% points (95% CI, 1.71-6.98; P < 0.001). In this national sample, posterior interbody fusion was more commonly used in older, more medically complex patients, while both approaches grew over time with faster growth for ALIF and increasing ALIF share. These descriptive patterns outline contemporary selection of anterior versus posterior approaches and motivate outcome-focused, risk-adjusted studies in key subgroups.

cards.title: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

cards.title: InSafeLock endopin versus conventional distal locking screws for femoral shaft fractures: A comparative laboratory biomechanical study.
cards.abstract: The InSafeLock femoral nail is a recently developed implant that uses endopin instead of screws in its distal locking mechanism. This study aimed to compare the biomechanical features of the distal locking mechanisms of InSafeLock and conventional nails. Twenty-four artificial femoral bones were used for mechanical tests. InSafeLock nails with endopin (Group 1) and conventional nails with distal locking screws (Group 2) were inserted into the artificial bones. The biomechanical features were evaluated using axial compression and rotational performance tests. There was no statistically significant difference between Group 1 and Group 2 in the axial compression displacement tests (P = .683). No visual damage was observed on the artificial bones or intramedullary nails after axial compression fatigue tests in either group. During axial compression failure testing performed after fatigue testing, the mean failure load of Group 1 was significantly lower than that of Group 2 (1132.5 ± 15.5 N vs 11,965.5 ± 9.5 N, respectively; P = .002). Rotational performance tests showed that the torsional yield strength of the groups was not statistically different (P = .333). While the InSafeLock endopin offers ease in distal locking, it exhibits a significantly lower failure load under high axial compression forces than conventional screws.

cards.title: Berberine attenuates cigarette smoke extract-induced stress and senescence-associated changes in human brain microvascular endothelial cells.
cards.abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the protective effects of berberine (BBR) against cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced injury in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and to identify candidate molecules and associated candidate molecules. hCMEC/D3 cells were exposed to 4% CSE and/or 7.5 μM BBR for 24 h. Inflammation, oxidative stress, and senescence-associated phenotypes were assessed. Previously generated CSE-responsive transcriptomic data were integrated with ChEMBL-derived candidates, followed by enrichment, weighted prioritization, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and docking. Compared with CSE alone, BBR co-treatment increased cell viability (P < 0.001), attenuated NF-κB-associated inflammation. IL-1β and TNF-α levels were significantly reduced (P < 0.05). BBR also reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and increased the reduced/oxidized glutathione (GSH/GSSG) ratio from 8.74 to 12.74 (P < 0.001). Senescence-associated β-galactosidase positivity decreased from 15.00% to 1.39% (P < 0.001), accompanied by reduced p16/p21 expression and G0/G1 accumulation (P < 0.01). Integrated analysis identified 23 overlapping candidates and prioritized GDF15, HMOX1, NQO1, IL1B, and CDKN1A. Docking predicted potential interactions with BBR; RT-qPCR and Western blot showed differential expression responses to BBR. BBR attenuates CSE-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and senescence-associated alterations in hCMEC/D3 cells. These effects may be associated with modulation of interconnected cellular stress responses.

cards.title: The epidemiology of frailty in urban and rural KwaZulu Natal, South Africa; a cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: We investigated the prevalence and clinical risk factors associated with frailty, and frailty's relationship with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in urban and rural South Africa. In a population-based cross-sectional study, using age- and sex-stratified random sampling of adults aged ≥40 years, researcher-administered questionnaires collected socio-demographic and clinical data. Physical assessments included body mass index (BMI), grip strength, short physical performance battery (SPPB), vision and hearing, and EuroQol 5-Dimensions 5-Levels measured HRQoL. A modified Fried's Frailty Phenotype defined frailty. Multivariable logistic regression calculated the odds of frailty for associated risk factors, and logistic and quantile regression examined HRQoL by frailty status. Amongst 1,893 participants, median age 60 years [IQR 50-70], 54% female, the overall study prevalence of frailty was 16.4%. Frailty was more common in those ≥70 years than those 40-49-years old (32.5% vs. 7.5%; OR 6.0 [95%CI 3.7,8.4], p < 0.001), and in females compared to males (19.2% vs. 13.1%; OR 1.6 [1.2,2.0], p < 0.001). Older age (≥60 years), urban residence, low educational attainment, moderate to severe food insecurity, visual and hearing impairments, self-reported disability, BMI<18kg/m2, and impaired SPPB were all independently associated with frailty. Compared to being robust, frailty was associated with a lower HRQoL utility score (median 0.81(IQR 0.71-0.86) in frail vs. 0.86 (0.83-0.90) in robust/prefrail, β -0.05 ([95%CI -0.07,-0.03], p < 0.001). Frailty is common and associated with poorer HRQoL. The identified clinical risk factors can be used to prioritise individuals for referral for clinical assessment of frailty in SA.

cards.title: Mechanisms and disease implications of inflammaging and potential therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Inflammaging is a chronic, low-grade inflammatory state associated with aging and age-related diseases. This review examines the mechanisms underlying inflammaging, emphasizing the interplay between oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, cellular senescence, and immune dysregulation. Persistent cellular stress promotes senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), while impaired immune clearance allows senescent cells to accumulate, sustaining a self-amplifying inflammatory cycle. We further discuss the involvement of inflammaging in neurodegenerative, infectious, autoimmune, cardiometabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases. Finally, we summarize current and emerging interventions, including lifestyle modifications, pharmacological approaches, senolytics, senomorphics, and strategies targeting mitochondrial quality control and cellular metabolism. Understanding the interconnected mechanisms and tissue-specific effects of inflammaging may facilitate the development of targeted interventions to mitigate age-related diseases and promote healthy aging.

cards.title: [Supramalleolar osteotomy for correction of malunited malleolar fractures : When and how?].
cards.abstract: Malunion after malleolar fractures most often results from a malunited fibula but can also involve the tibial plafond. Axial deviation of the talus and residual joint incongruity lead to destabilization of the ankle joint, asymmetrical loading and accelerated focal cartilage loss. Supramalleolar corrective osteotomy aims to restore the mechanical axis, improve tibiotalar congruity and redistribute loading toward preserved cartilage. The preoperative planning requires weight-bearing standard radiographs of the foot and ankle and, when needed, whole leg radiographs. Comparative radiographs of the contralateral unaffected ankle may be helpful. Computed tomography is useful for assessing the position of the talus in the malleolus as well as the position of the fibula in relation to the tibia, especially the rotational deformity, intra-articular step-off, syndesmotic incongruity, and fibular shortening. The plan should identify the apex of deformity, the correction angle and the osteotomy level. The surgical technique should be individually adapted to the deformity. Supramalleolar osteotomy is placed just proximal to the ankle joint while preserving distal bone stock for fixation. Guidewires inserted under fluoroscopy guidance are used to define the cut, hinge and planned correction. Closing-wedge supramalleolar osteotomy requires precise wedge removal, cortical compression and stable fixation, whereas opening-wedge gaps are supported with bone grafts and rigid plate fixation. After tibial realignment, the fibula and syndesmosis must be reassessed because persistent fibular shortening, malrotation or malposition can maintain talar incongruity. Fibular osteotomy, lengthening, and derotation are often needed to correctly reposition the talus in the ankle mortise and to restore joint congruity. Calcaneal osteotomy may be added if heel malalignment persists. In the treatment of malunited ankle fractures, supramalleolar osteotomy has been shown to be effective in restoring joint mechanics and balancing the ankle and to yield highly satisfactory results in the mid-term to long-term, making it a viable option for preserving the ankle.

cards.title: From cave adaptation to ageing resilience: the Mexican cavefish Astyanax mexicanus.
cards.abstract: The Mexican cavefish, Astyanax mexicanus, is a powerful evolutionary model for investigating how adaptation to extreme environments reshapes vertebrate physiology. Multiple cave populations have independently evolved under subterranean conditions, acquiring traits including insulin resistance, persistent hyperglycaemia, increased adiposity, altered sleep patterns, hypoxia tolerance and extensive metabolic reprogramming. Despite these differences, cavefish exhibit lifespans comparable to those of surface fish, while selected traits, including fertility and locomotor performance, appear to be better preserved with age. These observations challenge the assumption that persistent metabolic dysfunction necessarily entails accelerated functional decline and raise the possibility that cavefish have evolved mechanisms of ageing resilience. This narrative review examines evidence linking cave adaptation to biological processes relevant to ageing, focusing on nutrient sensing, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis and immune regulation. Rather than eliminating metabolic stress, cave-associated adaptations may buffer some of its downstream consequences, preserving selected physiological functions. Evidence is evaluated within the framework of the hallmarks of ageing, considering genomic instability, telomere dynamics, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, while identifying major knowledge gaps regarding epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, macroautophagy, cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication and dysbiosis. The available evidence supports A. mexicanus as a comparative model for investigating how chronic environmental and metabolic stress can be uncoupled from selected aspects of functional decline. Distinguishing delayed ageing from enhanced tolerance or compensation in response to accumulated damage will be essential to establish the extent and mechanisms of ageing resilience in this species.

cards.title: Osteoclastogenesis associated gene signatures in postmenopausal low bone mineral density: cross-dataset transcriptomics and whole-blood validation.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass and increased fracture risk, yet minimally invasive molecular correlates of postmenopausal low bone mineral density remain limited. We independently reanalysed two human osteoclastogenesis RNA-seq datasets, GSE225974 and GSE246769, using differential-expression, Gene Ontology, KEGG, Hallmark gene set enrichment, and cross-dataset concordance analyses. Six candidate genes, LGALSL, FAXDC2, DHCR7, MYL9, RHOC, and ITGB5, were subsequently evaluated by RT-qPCR in whole blood from 100 postmenopausal women with normal bone mineral density (n=30), osteopenia (n=30), or osteoporosis (n=40). Across the two RNA-seq datasets, 1,782 differentially expressed genes were shared, including 1,240 concordantly upregulated and 385 concordantly downregulated genes, with strong cross-dataset effect-size correlation (r=0.74). GO and KEGG analyses identified replicated sterol/lipid, skeletal-development, adhesion/integrin, and actin-cytoskeletal programs, while Hallmark GSEA identified 22 concordantly enriched gene sets, including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty-acid metabolism, and cholesterol homeostasis. BMD was positively correlated with calcium intake and physical activity. Conversely, deteriorating bone health was positively associated with high cholesterol, low BMI, early menopause. All six candidate genes were significantly and concordantly upregulated during osteoclastogenesis in both datasets. Whole-blood RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated progressively higher relative expression across normal-BMD, osteopenia, and osteoporosis groups for all six candidates. Expression analysis from the serum validated LGALSL, RHOC, MYL9 and ITGB5 elevated expression in osteoporosis cases. These findings identify reproducible osteoclastogenesis-associated transcriptional programs and support the six candidate genes as candidate signature correlating with the postmenopausal BMD status.

cards.title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring.
cards.abstract: Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm2. By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

cards.title: Healthy Eating Index and Bone in Obesity.
cards.abstract: Individuals living with overweight or obesity have a higher bone mineral density, however bone quality may be compromised, leading to an increased susceptibility to fractures and impaired skeletal integrity. Nutrition is a potentially modifiable factor that may influence both body weight and bone metabolism through effects on inflammation, body composition, and metabolic regulation. In particular, dietary quality indices such as the Healthy Eating Index (HEI) provide a comprehensive assessment of adherence to dietary guidelines and may offer insight into how overall eating patterns influence bone quality among individuals with excess body weight. In this review, we have summarized the impact of dietary quality using the HEI on bone health in individuals who are living with overweight or obesity. Recent studies show a positive relationship of high HEI with bone parameters in overweight and obese individuals. Specifically, studies report on a higher Trabecular bone score (TBS), lumbar and femoral neck BMD, lower osteoporosis risk and higher serum 25 hydroxy vitamin D levels in populations with a higher HEI. Currently studies assessing impact of HEI on bone health in obesity are cross sectional in nature. Future studies should assess the impact of increasing HEI on bone health in a prospective design and the impact of weight loss and increasing HEI on bone quality in individuals living with overweight and obesity.

cards.title: Revitalizing aging muscles: harnessing NAD⁺, sirtuins, and exercise to combat sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Aging is associated with systemic metabolic dysfunction that contributes to geriatric syndromes such as sarcopenia-the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function. Evidence from preclinical models suggests that age-associated depletion of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) may contribute to this decline by limiting the activity of sirtuin deacetylases (SIRT1-7). These enzymes act as metabolic sensors regulating mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative capacity, DNA repair and pathways related to muscle atrophy. Physical exercise enhances NAD⁺ salvage through upregulation of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT). Pharmacological approaches including NAD⁺ precursor supplementation (nicotinamide riboside or nicotinamide mononucleotide) and inhibition of NAD⁺-consuming enzymes have shown benefits in preclinical models. However, clinical translation remains inconsistent. Recent meta-analyses have found no significant effect of these precursors on muscle mass or strength in adults aged over 60 years. Moreover, experimental evidence indicates that even profound NAD⁺ depletion in adult mouse skeletal muscle does not necessarily compromise function or accelerate aging. We conclude that pharmacological NAD⁺ restoration alone is currently insufficient to reverse sarcopenia in humans. A synergistic approach combining exercise with targeted NAD⁺ support, together with emerging strategies involving precursor transporters, trigonelline and hypothalamic NAD⁺-sirtuin circuits, represents a testable avenue that requires rigorous, stratified clinical evaluation.

cards.title: Joint-preserving correction of malunited anterior and posterior malleolar fractures.
cards.abstract: The posterior and anterior rims of the distal tibial are essential for overall ankle function. They are referred to as third and fourth malleolus, respectively, which are commonly injured in the wake of ankle fractures. Residual displacement, malunion, or nonunion may cause fibular malposition in the tibial incisura (fibular notch), syndesmotic (tibiofibular mortise) instability, and joint incongruency leading to posttraumatic arthritis. Computed tomography scanning is required to assess the three-dimensional outline of the deformity and to make an appropriate treatment plan. Correction of anterior and posterior malleolar malalignment aims at restoring the following: (1) articular tibiotalar congruency, (2) sagittal ankle bone stability and talar containment, (3) the anatomy of the tibial incisura (fibular notch) to enable correct positioning of the distal fibula, and (4) tibiofibular alignment and syndesmotic (mortise) stability. To date, there is little evidence in the literature regarding the outcome of realignment of anterior and posterior malleolar malunions, and further studies are needed to establish evidence-based guidelines for surgical correction.

cards.title: Nontraumatic orbital roof blowout fracture following nose blowing: illustrative case.
cards.abstract: Orbital blowout fractures generally involve the floor or medial wall and usually result from blunt trauma. Nontraumatic orbital roof fractures associated with nose blowing are exceptionally rare. An 84-year-old man developed immediate left orbital swelling, epistaxis, diplopia, and impaired downgaze after forceful nose blowing. CT demonstrated fractures of the left medial orbital wall and orbital roof, with intracranial herniation of orbital tissue. MRI showed herniation of the superior rectus muscle and orbital fat through the roof defect and an adjacent inferior frontal lobe hematoma. During an extradural transcranial operation, herniated orbital fat was found to have penetrated the dura and adhered firmly to the frontal lobe. The adherent tissue was released, the dura and periorbita were repaired, and the orbital roof was reconstructed. Diplopia and downgaze limitation improved postoperatively. An orbital roof fracture should be considered when orbital swelling and diplopia develop immediately after forceful nose blowing, even without trauma. Intracranial herniation and adhesion of orbital tissue may contribute to persistent ocular motility disturbance and may warrant surgical treatment. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26847.

cards.title: The clinical use and applicability of magnetic resonance spectroscopy of the discovertebral segment: a scoping review.
cards.abstract: To map the available evidence on the clinical use and applicability of MRS applied to the spinal discovertebral segment. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, CINAHL, and EMBASE for articles that applied MRS to the discovertebral segment. Both in vivo and ex vivo studies (without immersion or preparation) in humans and animals were included, while studies were excluded if they employed non-clinical MRI scanners (e.g. small-bore scanners or ultra-high field MRI systems), or focused solely on the bone marrow (e.g., osteoporosis, anorexia). Two reviewers independently screened the articles and extracted data. The findings were reported descriptively. Eleven articles from eight studies applying proton (1H)-based MRS and published between 2009 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Seven studies were conducted in vivo in human participants, while one ex vivo study included human cadaveric and bovine discs. Substantial variations in methodologies were observed across the included studies in terms of MRI field strength, acquisition parameters, and post-processing software. MRS was used to quantify biochemical markers, such as water content, proteoglycans, lactate, and lipid peaks that may be related to intervertebral disc health and disc degeneration. Three studies assessed associations between MRS findings and clinical outcomes in patients with low back pain (LBP). MRS is an emerging technology in LBP research and has been used to non-invasively assess biochemical markers in the spinal discovertebral segment; however, the limited number of studies and the methodological heterogeneity preclude firm conclusions regarding its clinical relevance in LBP. Further large-scale in vivo studies with standardised MRS protocols and methods are required to evaluate the clinical significance of metabolic markers in the discovertebral segment.
