cards.title: Nanovaccines co-delivering antigen and dual TLR agonists potentiate aged immunity by orchestrating TCR repertoire.
cards.abstract: Immunosenescence increases susceptibility to varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection in the elderly while compromising vaccine responsiveness. Although clinical adjuvants such as AS01 have improved vaccine efficacy, challenges associated with saponin-based components and separate antigen-adjuvant formulations persist. Here, we developed a nanovaccine, NP(gEIM), that co-encapsulates VZV glycoprotein E (gE) with the TLR4 agonist MPLA and TLR7/8 agonist IMQ in lipid nanoparticles via flash nanocomplexation (FNC), enabling coordinated co-delivery of antigen and adjuvants. NP(gEIM) efficiently targeted draining lymph nodes and promoted antigen-presenting cell uptake and maturation. In young and aged mice, NP(gEIM) elicited gE-specific antibody responses and Th1-biased cellular immunity comparable to AS01-adjuvanted gE vaccines while exceeding aluminum-adjuvanted vaccines. Moreover, NP(gEIM) enhanced IFN-γ and TNF-α production by antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells while reducing immunosuppressive Treg and MDSC populations in aged mice. Notably, NP(gEIM) reshaped the TCR repertoire by promoting selective expansion of putative antigen-responsive T cell clones and altering TCR V/J gene usage and CDR3 length distribution, providing molecular insights into vaccine-induced T cell responses. Collectively, this study presents a nanovaccine strategy enabling coordinated delivery of antigen and dual TLR agonists. By integrating humoral and cellular immunity with TCR repertoire modulation, NP(gEIM) offers a potential strategy for improving vaccine responses in aging populations and developing vaccines against age-associated infectious diseases.

cards.title: Silicate Biomaterials-Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration.
cards.abstract: Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet-based microfluidic platform for the high-throughput generation of morphology-dependent magnesium silicate-engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology-dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube-engineered composite hydrogel (2NT-GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction-related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical-sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT-GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

cards.title: Periprosthetic tibial fracture in robotic-assisted versus conventional medial UKA: in vitro testing and finite element analysis of baseplate footprint.
cards.abstract: Periprosthetic tibial fracture after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is uncommon but clinically important. Although robotic-assisted UKA may improve the precision of bone preparation and component positioning, whether these technical differences influence fracture resistance or fracture morphology remains unclear. This in vitro study examined whether robotic-assisted medial UKA alters axial load-to-failure compared with conventional UKA, whether fracture morphology differs between the two techniques, and whether implant base footprint influences fracture behavior in complementary finite element (FE) simulations. Robotic-assisted medial UKA would alter tibial fracture behavior compared with conventional UKA, as reflected by differences in fracture resistance and fracture morphology. Fourteen fresh-frozen cadaveric specimens underwent medial UKA using either conventional instrumentation (n = 7) or a robotic-assisted workflow (n = 7). After implantation, the tibiae were isolated and subjected to monotonic axial compression at 0.5 mm/s until macroscopic periprosthetic fracture occurred. Load-to-failure, failure load normalized to body weight, and fracture morphology were evaluated. Complementary FE models incorporating implant baseplate sizes 8 and 10 were used to compare load-displacement behavior and crack propagation. Axial load-to-failure did not differ significantly between conventional and robotic-assisted UKA (3712.4 ± 1746.2 N vs. 3988.3 ± 1534.5 N, p = 0.90). Failure load normalized to body weight was also not significantly different between groups (524.42 ± 262.60% vs. 647.24 ± 212.54%, p = 0.71). Different predominant fracture patterns were observed despite similar fracture resistance. Robotic-assisted specimens primarily demonstrated metaphyseal depression-type fractures, whereas fractures in conventional specimens more frequently propagated toward the meta-diaphyseal region. In the FE simulations, peak loads were 3755.36 N for the size-8 baseplate model and 4005.36 N for the size-10 baseplate model, both within the variability observed experimentally, with differences in crack propagation between implant baseplate sizes. Robotic-assisted medial UKA did not significantly alter axial fracture resistance compared with conventional UKA, although different predominant fracture morphologies were observed between techniques. Complementary FE analysis showed that implant base footprint influenced simulated load-displacement behavior and crack propagation, suggesting that implant footprint may contribute mechanically to differences in fracture behavior after medial UKA. V; biomechanical cadaveric and in silico investigation.

cards.title: Impacted Fetal Head at Cesarean Birth: A Clinical Nursing Review.
cards.abstract: Fetal head impaction (IFH) occurs when the presenting part becomes wedged in the maternal pelvis during a cesarean section, requiring additional maneuvers to complete birth. As cesarean rates have risen, so has IFH, estimated to occur in 1.5% of all births annually in the United States. Maternal complications include uterine extension, hemorrhage, bladder injury, and intensive care unit admission. Neonatal complications include low cord pH, skull fracture, intracranial hemorrhage, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, and death. These outcomes are not inevitable. Management technique, clinician education, and interdisciplinary institutional preparation are modifiable factors with direct bearing on outcomes when IFH is encountered. Despite its frequency and consequence, the topic of IFH and the role of the nurse are absent from nursing education, professional standards, and scope-of-practice guidance. A search of CINAHL, PubMed, Ovid, and EBSCO identified no peer-reviewed nursing literature addressing IFH or its intraoperative management. Labor and delivery nurses commonly report first encountering manual vaginal disimpaction when urgently asked to perform it during an emergency, without education, competence validation, or institutional policy. Improving outcomes requires institutional infrastructure built before any individual emergency, and professional nursing organizations must clarify where manual vaginal disimpaction falls within nursing scope of practice.

cards.title: Association of runoff risk with private well contamination in a fractured dolostone aquifer.
cards.abstract: In the United States, private well owners are responsible for monitoring and maintaining their drinking water but have little control over neighboring contamination sources and limited information about daily water quality. Potential for rapid contamination in karst settings exacerbates the challenge. The Runoff Risk Advisory Forecast (RRAF) is a real-time online tool available in five US states that helps nutrient applicators avoid times and locations of high runoff risk. We wanted to determine if RRAF could be repurposed in areas susceptible to groundwater contamination to inform well owners of conditions when contamination is likely. Private wells were repeatedly sampled on seven dates (32-36 wells per date) and analyzed for nitrate-nitrogen, total coliforms, and bovine manure markers. Three-day windows of RRAF risk prior to sampling were selected post hoc, ranging from 1 to 3 days prior for manure markers to 10-12 days prior for nitrate. Contaminants were associated with RRAF values of ≥75% within these windows based on observed weather. A hydrologic association between RRAF risk and groundwater depth was also apparent. Overall, results suggest the RRAF model anticipates conditions of elevated contamination risk for susceptible wells. For nitrate, between-well variation and delayed peak concentration suggested that well location and construction factors may be more informative than runoff events. Microbial contamination was rapid and distributed among wells, with one or more detections of coliforms in 31% of wells and bovine markers in 61% of wells. Thus, a warning system based on the RRAF model could help identify conditions of acute pathogen exposure.

cards.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material.
cards.abstract: The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure. The synergistic enhancement mechanism of PVA induced hydration cementation film coating and slurry-rock interface was revealed. The results show that: (1) High content of CG weakens the early hydration activity of cement slurry system. After PVA is added, the fluidity of slurry increases, the initial and final setting time is further prolonged, and the bleeding rate decreases, indicating that PVA can improve the flow stability and water retention performance of coal-based solid waste slurry. (2) PVA content has obvious dosage dependence on the bearing capacity of the grout rock complex. The peak stresses of the 0%, 0.3%, 0.6% and 1.0% PVA groups are 4.87 ± 0.14 MPa, 5.35 ± 0.06 MPa, 6.04 ± 0.09 MPa and 5.12 ± 0.09 MPa, respectively. The 0.6% PVA group shows relatively better mechanical properties within the test range of this paper. (3) Appropriate amount of PVA can promote the filling of C-S-H gel, AFt rod crystals and C-H flake crystals on the surface of sandstone particles and in the pores and fracture, and adsorb and coordinate through hydroxyl groups to form hydration products and flexible polymer film. The hydration products provide a rigid skeleton, and the PVA flexible film plays a buffering role in the interface bonding and deformation, and synergistically realizes the densification, continuity and toughness enhancement of the weakly cemented sandstone-grout interface. The experimental results show that 0.6% PVA content can achieve a better balance between slurry performance, water retention stability, interface hydration cementation and mechanical bearing capacity, which can provide material design basis for grouting reinforcement of weakly cemented aquifer, thickening of aquiclude and prevention and control of mining-induced water disasters.

cards.title: Crack identification and detection in mine boreholes using deep learning: A case study of hexi coal mine.
cards.abstract: The internal cracks in deep rock masses are an important factor determining the safety of coal mining. The borehole peeping technology is an important method for obtaining the distribution of coal and rock fractures in deep geological engineering. However, there are often problems such as strong background interference and complex joints in real mines, which bring greater challenges to obtaining the distribution of cracks. Therefore, this study proposes a deep learning-based method for identifying internal cracks, which is used for the intelligent identification and analysis of cracks in drilled rock masses. The experimental verification was carried out based on the real borehole peeping images of the tunnels in Hexi Coal Mine as the data set. By embedding the ResCBAM attention mechanism into the YOLOv8 head network, the reliability and accuracy of identifying internal cracks in rock were further enhanced. The test results show that, the proposed Res-YOLOv8 algorithm can more accurately suppress the interference of complex backgrounds and present the morphological characteristics of rock cracks to compare with the fusion of typical attention mechanisms SE and CBAM with YOLOv8. The ResCBAM-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates strong performance in the evaluation indicators of confusion matrix, loss rate, precision, recall and MPA. The proposal of method has improved the efficiency of detecting and identifying cracks in coal and rock masses in real mines, and provided more reliable technical support for the stability evaluation of coal mine roof.

cards.title: Aggressive Hepatic AL Amyloidosis Encountering Therapeutic Frailty: Rapid Organ Reversal With Tailored Daratumumab-Based Therapy and Low-Dose Corticosteroids in a Patient With Steroid-Induced Psychosis.
cards.abstract: Hepatic AL amyloidosis can cause severe cholestasis independent of marrow tumor burden. In patients with absolute contraindications to high-dose steroids-such as steroid-induced psychosis-tailored daratumumab regimens with low-dose corticosteroids can drive rapid, life-saving organ reversal. However, intensive antimicrobial vigilance remains mandatory.

cards.title: [Expression of Concern] D‑galactose induces astrocytic aging and contributes to astrocytoma progression and chemoresistance via cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Following the publication of the above paper, it was drawn to the Editor's attention by a concerned reader that the p16 antibody that the authors reported to have used for the western blot experiment shown in Fig. 1C (cat. no. ab51243) is specific for the protein known as P16 ARC (or ARPC5), not the apoptosis‑associated protein p16INK4a, as was intended. The authors were contacted by the Editorial Office to offer an explanation for the apparent selection of an unsuitable antibody in this paper, and although they have replied, they have been unable to present the proof of purchase of the antibody in question given the lengthy time period that has elapsed since this study was published. Therefore, owing to the fact that the Editorial Office has been made aware of potential issues surrounding the scientific integrity of this paper, we are issuing an Expression of Concern to notify readers of this potential problem. [Molecular Medicine Reports 20: 4111‑4118, 2019; DOI: 10.3892/mmr.2019.10677].

cards.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis shapes brain T-cell immunity in accelerated aging.
cards.abstract: The bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota, immune system, and central nervous system-the gut‒brain axis-plays a vital role in maintaining brain health. Its disruption can lead to neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. However, the relationship between the gut microbiota and age-related changes in brain immunity remains unclear. This study examined gut microbiota composition and T-cell profiles in senescence-accelerated SAMP8 mice and senescence-resistant SAMR1 controls at young adult and aged stages. The accelerated-aging phenotype of SAMP8 mice was confirmed by reduced behavioral performance and brain transcriptomic alterations. Fecal microbiota profiles were obtained using culture-dependent plating and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. T-cell phenotypes were determined by flow cytometry on brain and splenic leukocytes. Strain, age, and sex were drivers of microbiota composition variation. Microbial diversity differed between strains independently of age. Several bacterial genera had altered abundances in young SAMP8 mice, with only Intestinimonas remaining higher in aged SAMP8. T-cell profiling revealed strain- and age-specific immune signatures. In the brain, SAMP8 mice exhibited a higher CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio, and higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine-producing CD4⁺ T cells compared to SAMR1. In contrast, the spleens of SAMP8 mice had a lower CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio. Only the spleens of aged SAMP8 mice showed increased T-cell activation (effector/naïve ratios) and higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine-producing CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells, suggesting age- and tissue-specific immune alterations. Nine bacterial genera correlated with immune cell frequencies and ratios. Notably, Intestinimonas showed a discordant association with the CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio in the brain (negative) and spleen (positive). Furthermore, CD8⁺ T cells correlated with microbiota composition variation more strongly than strain, age, and sex. Together, these findings link the gut microbiota to age-dependent immune remodeling in the brain and imply that altered microbial communities could influence pro-inflammatory T-cell responses, thereby contributing to accelerated brain aging.

cards.title: Ultrasound Identification of Calcific Patellar Tendinitis After Patellar Fracture Fixation.
cards.abstract: Calcific tendinopathy most commonly affects the rotator cuff, whereas involvement of the patellar tendon is exceedingly rare. Persistent anterior knee pain following patellar fracture fixation is usually attributed to postoperative stiffness, hardware irritation, or altered biomechanics, potentially leading to underrecognition of concomitant tendon pathology. Musculoskeletal ultrasound is well suited for evaluating postoperative tendon disorders because it enables detailed assessment of tendon abnormalities while simultaneously depicting adjacent soft tissues and surgical implants. This presentation highlights intratendinous calcification accompanied by active tendinopathic changes after patellar fracture fixation and emphasizes the diagnostic contribution of ultrasound in the evaluation of persistent postoperative anterior knee pain.

cards.title: [Corrigendum] Radiation induces primary osteocyte senescence phenotype and affects osteoclastogenesis in vitro.
cards.abstract: Following the publication of the above article, it was drawn to the Editor's attention by a concerned reader that the p16‑INK4a antibody that the authors reported to have used for the western blot experiment shown in Fig. 5D (cat. no. ab51243) is specific for the protein known as P16 ARC (or ARPC5), not the apoptosis‑associated protein p16‑INK4a, as was intended.Upon asking the authors to examine their records in the light of the possible selection of an inappropriate antibody for the affected experiment, after conducting a comprehensive audit of their laboratory records and archival documentation, the authors were able to provide the Editorial Office with proof that the antibody which was purchased to perform the western blot experiments shown in Fig. 5D had the catalog number ab211542, which correctly targeted p16‑INK4a. Therefore, in the Materials and method section, 'Identification of primary osteocytes' subsection on p. 2, right‑hand column, second paragraph, the sentence beginning on line 5 should have read as follows: 'After blocking with 5% skimmed milk ... P16 (cat. no. ab211542, Abcam; 1:1,000)...'. The authors wish to emphasize that this was an isolated clerical oversight, and they deeply regret any confusion or concern this may have generated. All experimental procedures and reported results were unequivocally performed using the anti‑p16‑INK4a antibody purchased from Abcam with the cat. no. ab211542. All the authors agree with the publication of this corrigendum. The authors express their gratitude to the Editor of International Journal of Molecular Medicine for allowing them the opportunity to publish this corrigendum, and apologize to the readership for any inconvenience caused. [International Journal of Molecular Medicine 47: 76, 2021; DOI: 10.3892/ijmm.2021.4909].

cards.title: Role of metabolites in mediating the effect of lipidomes on osteoporosis: A Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: We investigated the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes, osteoporosis (OP), and potential metabolite mediators using Mendelian randomization (MR). Using summary-level data from a genome-wide association study, bidirectional MR analyses to explore the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes and OP, and two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites. Sensitivity analyses were performed to validate the robustness of the results further. After primary analysis and a series of sensitivity analyses, 7 inflammation-related proteins were identified that have a causal relationship with OP. Ceramide (d40:1) levels (odds ratio [OR] = 0.923; 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.854-0.999; P = .046 < .05), phosphatidylcholine (16:0_18:2) levels (OR = 0.932; 95% CI: 0.883-0.985; P = .012 < .05), phosphatidylc holine (16:1_18:2) levels (OR = 0.939; 95% CI: 0.882-0.999; P = .047 < .05), triacylglycerol (48:3) levels (OR = 0.920; 95% CI: 0.854-0.971; P = .027 < .05), and triacylglycerol (51:4) levels (OR = 0.914; 95% CI: 0.840-0.995; P = .038 < .05) were negatively associated with OP, whereas phosphatidylcholine (O-17:0_15:0) levels (OR = 1.121; 95% CI: 1.019-1.233; P = .019 < .05), and triacylglycerol (48:0) levels (OR = 1.130; 95% CI: 1.042-1.226; P = .003 < .05) were positively associated with OP. Subsequently, we conducted a two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites. This study found that 14 plasma metabolites may play a mediating role in the relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, such as 5alpha-androstan-3alpha,17beta-diol monosulfate (1) levels, N6-methyllysine levels, 5-oxoproline levels, 2-hydroxyhippurate levels, glycosyl ceramide (d18:1/20:0, d16:1/22:0) levels, spermidine to 5-methylthioadenosine ratio, serine levels, phosphate to serine ratio, proline to trans-4-hydroxyproline ratio, 1-palmitoyl-GPC (16:0) levels, 7-methylxanthine levels, arachidonoylcholine levels, and spermidine to choline ratio. In conclusion, our study identified a causal relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, with a proportion of the effect mediated by plasma metabolites.

cards.title: Profile of Barbara Sherwood Lollar.
cards.abstract: In a laboratory nearly 2.4 kilometers under the Canadian Shield, geochemist Barbara Sherwood Lollar has tracked the sustained release of enough hydrogen gas from Earth's crust to produce 4.7 million kilowatt-hours of energy per year. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2022, Sherwood Lollar revisited the Kidd Creek Mine in Ontario, Canada where, in 2013, her explorations found that waters flowing from deep fractures were 1.6 billion years old. Reported in her Inaugural Article, the findings, aided by studies of noble gases in the samples, pushed the age of Earth's oldest waters back by hundreds of millions of years.

cards.title: A feasible and cost-effective method to induce distal radius fractures in full-length forearm human cadaveric specimens.
cards.abstract: Reported rates of loss of reduction in nonoperatively treated distal radius fractures (DRF) range from 17 to 71%. Thus, realistic biomechanical models are warranted to test novel immobilization devices that prevent loss of reduction in nonoperative fracture management. Currently available human cadaveric specimen models have several limitations: (i) disrupted soft tissue integrity, (ii) difficulty in replicating complex fracture patterns, and (iii) high technical demands and costs. Therefore, the aim of this study was to establish a feasible and accessible method for inducing DRFs, that accurately reflects in-vivo biomechanical fracture conditions in tissue-intact cadaveric specimens, suitable for testing of novel immobilization devices. Fifteen upper extremity cadaveric specimens were included. Specimens were prepared as full‑length forearm models. Using a repurposed strength training tower as a vertical drop tower, fractures were induced by proximally administering 120-135 J impacts. CT scans were performed pre- and post-fracture induction. All fractures were classified according to the AO/OTA classification. DRFs were successfully induced in all 15 specimens. A single 120 J impact produced a DRF in 11 out of 15 cases (73%). A second impact was administered in 4 out of 15 specimens (27%). Eleven of the 15 induced DRFs (73%) were classified as AO/OTA type C fractures, most commonly 2R3C3.2. Concomitant distal ulnar fractures were present in 6 cases, concomitant carpal fractures in 9 specimens. The overall cost of the setup amounted to 947 €. This study presents a feasible, cost-effective method to induce DRFs in tissue-intact, full-length human cadaveric forearm specimens. The setup consistently produces DRFs, predominantly AO/OTA type C, which can, with certain limitations, be utilized for biomechanical testing of immobilization devices, while also being uited for surgical and anatomical education.

cards.title: Low-cost and scalable synthesis of α-poly(L-glutamic acid) for superficial skin wound repair.
cards.abstract: Superficial skin repair demands high-performance, biocompatible medical dressings, drawing widespread attention to poly(glutamic acid) (PGA) in cosmetics and biomedicine. While γ-PGA, linked by γ-peptide bonds distinct from those in human proteins, is widely produced via scalable fermentation, it suffers from poor molecular weight control and cumbersome endotoxin removal. In contrast, α-PGA with native-like α-peptide bonds offers superior properties and biosafety but faces synthetic challenges. Here, we achieved a concise, hundreds-gram synthesis of well-defined, high-purity α-PGA via the ring-opening polymerization of unprotected glutamic N-carboxyanhydride. α-PGA-Na with a degree of polymerization of 20 displays superior hydration capacity compared with commercially fermented high-molecular-weight γ-PGA-Na and delivers comprehensive bioactivity in regulating cell viability, relative proliferative activity, migration, and alleviating UVB-induced cellular senescence. Furthermore, α-PGA-Na causes no acute skin or eye irritation in vivo, mitigates erythema, relieves pain-related behavioral responses, and facilitates early superficial wound healing. This work highlights α-PGA's dual potential as a cosmetic ingredient and liquid dressing, advancing tailored polypeptide materials for skincare and wound care.

cards.title: Nrf2 Activation Induces Fibroblast Senescence and Promotes Melanosome Accumulation in a Fibroblast-Keratinocyte Co-Culture Model.
cards.abstract: Solar lentigo (SL) is an age-associated hyperpigmented skin disorder linked to oxidative stress, impaired autophagy, and cellular senescence. However, experimental systems that recapitulate the senescence-associated skin microenvironment remain limited. In this study, we investigated the role of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) in fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses using transcriptomic analyses and a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture model. Public transcriptomic datasets revealed increased NFE2L2 expression together with altered autophagy-related and senescence-associated signatures in hyperpigmented skin lesions. In dermal fibroblasts, Nrf2 overexpression induced senescence-associated phenotypes, including increased SA-β-gal activity and elevated expression of SASP-related genes. In a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture system, Nrf2-activated fibroblasts promoted melanosome accumulation in keratinocytes, suggesting that senescence-associated dermal-epidermal interactions contribute to pigmentation-related alterations. SENOMUNE, a formulation with autophagy-modulating activity, enhanced LC3 puncta formation in keratinocytes and attenuated melanosome accumulation in the senescence-associated co-culture system. Collectively, these findings suggest that sustained Nrf2 activation contributes to fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses and provide a useful co-culture platform for evaluating senescence-associated pigmentation modulators.

cards.title: Use of thigh-based recipient vessels for free flap reconstruction in gustilo anderson type IIIC lower extremity open fractures: Description of two cases.
cards.abstract: Free tissue transfer is central to reconstruction of Gustilo IIIC lower-extremity injuries, but recipient vessel selection is challenging when local vasculature is compromised. We describe two Gustilo IIIC injuries reconstructed using thigh-based recipient vessels. Case 1: A 50-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with popliteal artery thrombosis and extensive tibial vessel injury. Following revascularization and serial debridement, a 25 × 15 cm tibial defect was reconstructed with a contralateral anterolateral thigh (ALT) free flap to the descending genicular artery (DGA), using an interposition great saphenous vein graft. The flap survived without complication.Case 2: A 35-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with complete popliteal artery transection requiring vascular reconstruction. A 20 × 14 cm defect was initially reconstructed with a free latissimus dorsi flap to the DGA using an interposition vein graft, complicated by venous thrombosis and flap loss. Subsequent reconstruction with an ALT flap and radial forearm flow-through flap to the superficial femoral vessels (SFA) achieved successful soft-tissue coverage. The DGA provides an accessible recipient outside the primary zone of injury, with consistent anatomy and suitable calibre for microsurgical anastomosis. Its location facilitates a two-team approach, avoids popliteal fossa exploration, and may reduce interference with subsequent skeletal procedures. The SFA is a valuable alternative recipient vessel, offering robust and reliable inflow with a good arterial pressure head. Thigh-based recipient vessels, particularly the DGA and SFA, should be considered in severe lower-limb trauma when conventional below-knee recipient vessels are unavailable or compromised.

cards.title: Refinement and initial characterization of a murine mandibular distraction osteogenesis model.
cards.abstract: To establish and initially characterize a reproducible mouse mandibular distraction osteogenesis (DO) model using a modular precision device. An external distractor was designed based on micro-CT data of C57BL/6 mouse mandibles. Fifty-four mice were randomized into sham, fracture, acute distraction, and gradual distraction groups. The gradual group underwent osteotomy, 5-day latency, 10-day distraction (0.15 mm/12 h, total 3 mm), and 4-week consolidation period. The acute group underwent 5-day latency and single 3 mm distraction on postoperative day 6 (POD 6). Fracture group underwent osteotomy only, while the sham underwent surgical exposure only. Samples were collected from the gradual group at POD 6, 10, 15, 22, 29, 43; other groups at POD 43. Bone regeneration was evaluated by micro-CT and histology. The distraction gap reached 3.02 ± 0.13 mm, consistent with the 3.0 mm target. Body weight recovered favorably. Micro-CT revealed that the gradual group exhibited characteristic DO temporal patterns: limited bone formation during distraction with low BV/TV (0.94 ± 0.44% at POD 6), followed by marked mineralization during consolidation, reaching 38.07 ± 2.86% at POD 43 (P < 0.0001 vs. POD 6). Histology showed ordered collagen deposition along the distraction vector during distraction, with subsequent trabecular maturation during consolidation. At POD 43, the gradual group had significantly higher BV/TV, Tb.Th, and Tb.N than both the fracture and acute groups (all P < 0.05). A reproducible mouse mandibular DO model was established, providing a reliable platform for investigating mechanically induced craniofacial bone regeneration.

cards.title: Serum Metabolomic Profiling Reveals Disrupted Amino Acid and Fatty Acid Metabolism in Older Adults with Sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia, an age-related syndrome characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass, decreased muscle strength, and/or reduced physical performance, is associated with disruptions in amino acid and lipid metabolism. This study aimed to investigate serum metabolic alterations associated with sarcopenia in older adults. In this cross-sectional study, 50 patients with sarcopenia (diagnosed per 2014 AWGS criteria) were matched 1:1 by age and sex with non-sarcopenic controls from a pool of 2,965 individuals. Assessments included skeletal muscle mass, grip strength, and gait speed. Serum metabolomic profiling was conducted using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). The screening of differential metabolites: variable importance in the projection (VIP) > 1 derived from the OPLS-DA model, and adjusted p-value based on false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 calculated by two-sample t-test. Among 100 participants aged 60-87 years, individuals with sarcopenia showed significantly lower BMI, grip strength, albumin, and ASMI than controls (all p < 0.05), whereas lipid levels were comparable. PCA suggested weak group separation, whereas PLS-DA achieved clearer discrimination by sex and sarcopenia status. Differential metabolites identified in the sarcopenia group included arginine, leucine and histidinyl-histidine, the latter of which exhibited decreased abundance. Concomitant alterations in the levels of lipid metabolites collectively suggest disrupted amino acid and lipid metabolism. Patterns of dysregulated amino acid and fatty acid metabolism were observed in older adults with sarcopenia. Such metabolic disturbances might serve as candidate biomarkers to inform early detection and nutritional intervention strategies.

cards.title: Anatomic Considerations of Retrograde Intramedullary Nail Placement in Distal Ulna Fractures.
cards.abstract: To characterize the anatomic relationship between retrograde intramedullary nail placement in distal ulna fractures and important surrounding structures, with particular focus on the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). Eight fresh-frozen cadaveric upper extremity specimens underwent simulated distal ulnar neck fracture fixation using a 4.5 mm retrograde intramedullary threaded nail. Pre- and postinsertion arthroscopy was performed to assess TFCC integrity. Dissection was used to evaluate proximity to surrounding structures, including the extensor retinaculum, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digiti minimi, and dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve. TFCC involvement was classified by location and quantified using surface area analysis. The nail path disrupted the distal extensor retinaculum in all specimens, with no direct injury to the extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digiti minimi, or dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve, although these structures were in close proximity. The superficial TFCC and the deep radioulnar ligament footprint were involved in the majority of specimens, with the dorsal peripheral region most commonly penetrated. However, the overall surface area of the TFCC impacted was minimal. Retrograde intramedullary nail placement for distal ulna fractures frequently involves both the superficial TFCC and deep radioulnar ligament footprint, with perforations most common in the dorsal peripheral region rather than the central disc of the TFCC. Despite this, the overall surface area of involvement is limited. Surgeons should be aware of the proximity of important surrounding structures and the likelihood of TFCC involvement when using a retrograde intramedullary approach for distal ulna fractures.

cards.title: A Bi‐Adjuvant Senolytic Nanovaccine Modulating Dendritic Cell Senescence Ameliorates Aging‐Related Metabolic Dysfunction
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Senolytic vaccines hold promise for eliminating senescent cells, but their efficacy is limited by poor seno‐antigen immunogenicity and age‐related dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction. Here, we engineered an active biomaterial‐enabled bi‐adjuvant senolytic nanovaccine (CK5‐GC‐NV) by co‐assembling CpG oligodeoxynucleotide with a fusion protein of the seno‐antigen Gpnmb and a cationic spider silk protein variant (CK5). Beyond antigen delivery, the CK5 scaffold acts as an intrinsic senomodulator associated with the downregulation of mitotic kinases Aurka/b and a concomitant decrease in senescence‐associated PI3K/AKT phosphorylation in DCs. This intervention attenuates aged DC phenotypes, restores antigen cross‐presentation, and synergizes with CpG to elicit potent cytotoxic T‐lymphocyte responses against senescent targets. Across multiple aging mouse models, CK5‐GC‐NV immunization orchestrated targeted clearance of Gpnmb + senescent adipocytes, profoundly ameliorating metabolic dysfunction and extending lifespan. This multifunctional biomaterial platform integrates seno‐antigen immunogenicity enhancement with the restoration of aged DC function, providing a promising proof‐of‐concept for antigen‐directed gerotherapeutics.

cards.title: Glycated albumin levels in roe deer: a marker of body condition modulated by environmental quality.
cards.abstract: In humans, it is now widely accepted that the glycation reaction plays a major role in the senescence process, as well as in the development of associated pathologies. While the links between glycation and senescence have also been studied in laboratory animal models, they have hardly been studied in the wild. We therefore investigated the links between glycation and senescence in two populations of roe deer (Capreolus capreolus) facing different environmental conditions, in which demographic and phenotypic senescence are well documented. Individuals of known age were captured in two years of differing quality. Individual data were collected (body mass, glycemia, sex), and we measured glycated albumin levels (GA) as well as six biochemical parameters known to show senescence in this species. We found that GA did not correlate with age, blood glucose, or sex, but varied between populations and years. In the population living in the low-quality environment, GA was negatively associated with inflammatory status while GA was positively associated with body mass. Overall, GA appears to reflect aspects of physiological condition and individual performance in an environment-dependent context, rather than senescence.

cards.title: Addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures reduces interfragmentary displacement - a biomechanical human cadaveric study.
cards.abstract: To investigate whether the addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures provides improved biomechanical construct stability and reduced interfragmentary displacement. A distal patellar pole fracture was simulated in sixteen fresh-frozen human cadaveric knees by a horizontal osteotomy in the distal third of the patella. Subsequently, locking plate fixation was performed. In a randomized half of the specimens, an additional McLaughlin wire cerclage was applied. The specimens were then subjected to 3000 cycles of extension starting at 90° of flexion under a maximum tensile load of 320 N. Using a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system, the interfragmentary displacement between the proximal and distal fragments was measured at 1, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 cycles. Statistical analysis was performed using repeated-measures ANOVA and Welch's unpaired t-t test at 3000 cycles. An additional McLaughlin cerclage significantly reduced interfragmentary displacement under cyclic loading in comparison to locking plate fixation alone. After 3000 cycles, displacement was 2.27 ± 1.84 mm with plate fixation alone and 0.36 ± 0.22 mm with additional McLaughlin cerclage (mean difference 1.91 mm; 95% CI 0.38-3.45 mm; p = 0.0215). An additional McLaughlin cerclage reduced interfragmentary displacement in distal patellar pole fractures. In cases of unstable distal pole patella fractures, the additional use of a McLaughlin cerclage may therefore be considered to enhance construct stability.

cards.title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles Enable Oral Alendronate Therapy for Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

cards.title: Convergent Early Dysregulation of Sarcopenia-Associated Genes in Skeletal Muscle During Aging and SOD1G93A ALS Models
cards.abstract: Skeletal muscle undergoes structural and functional decline due to aging and neuromuscular disorders such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), both of which impact protein expression and contribute to muscle atrophy. This study investigates how aging and the SOD1G93A ALS-related mutation affect the expression of eight genes previously linked to sarcopenia (PF4, OIT3, MMRN1, MASP1, C1R, SVEP1, VCAN and SPTB) but not yet characterized in muscle tissue. To this end, we analyzed their expression (1) during muscle aging in WT mice (5 and 24 months), (2) in SOD1G93A-transfected myotube cells in vitro, (3) in a muscle-specific SOD1G93A mouse model (5 and 24 months), and (4) in a systemic SOD1G93A transgenic mouse at different disease stages (60 and 120 days) by quantitative PCR. All eight target genes were expressed in skeletal muscle and most of them showed increased transcription with aging. In ALS models, gene expression was significantly overexpressed at early stages, particularly in muscle-specific (MLC/SOD1G93A) and systemic (SOD1G93A) models, mimicking aging-related profiles. These alterations attenuated with disease progression, suggesting an early transient muscle response to ALS-linked SOD1 mutations. Hence, this study demonstrates that sarcopenia-associated proteins are actively expressed and modulated in skeletal muscle during aging and ALS and suggests convergent response mechanisms.

cards.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta bone matrix alterations affect the resorptive function of human osteoclasts in-vitro.
cards.abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) results most commonly from altered collagen type I that impairs both bone formation and resorption, producing a fragile bone matrix prone to fracture. While most studies emphasize deficient osteoblast function, there is a paucity of data related to the contribution of osteoclast-mediated resorption. We investigated whether intrinsic alterations in OI bone matrix directly modulate human osteoclast activity. Identical human osteoclast populations were seeded onto bone samples from donors with OI types 1, 3, and 4 and compared with non-OI controls. In addition, cleaned calvarial bones from the Col1a1Aga2/+ and Col1a1Jrt/+ mouse OI models served as substrates for human osteoclasts. On OI type 1 bone, osteoclasts generated a greater eroded surface covered by pits, whereas trench formation remained unchanged. OI type 4 bone yielded significantly reduced eroded surface but produced deeper pits and trenches. Osteoclast behaviour on OI type 3 bone did not differ from that of healthy bone. Using Col1a1Jrt/+ substrates, human osteoclasts displayed a general increase in resorptive activity, particularly in pit formation. Col1a1Aga2/+ substrates similarly enhanced pit formation but reduced trench formation. Multiple linear regression confirmed that OI bone matrix preferentially stimulates pit-making osteoclasts while leaving trench-making osteoclasts largely unaffected. Independent of OI status, increasing donor age promoted trench formation. These findings demonstrate that OI-specific matrix characteristics directly influence osteoclast resorption patterns. More broadly, they highlight the importance of extracellular matrix properties in shaping osteoclast behaviour and underscore the need to consider matrix-driven effects when interpreting bone pathologies.

cards.title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions.
cards.abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system's multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

cards.title: Changes in gray matter volume associated with gait speed and muscle mass in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
cards.abstract: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early stage of cognitive decline between normal aging and dementia. Gait speed, a key marker of physical function, has been associated with both cognitive decline and brain atrophy. Sarcopenia, characterized by age-related loss of muscle mass and function, has also been linked to structural brain changes.ObjectiveTo investigate the associations between sarcopenia, its individual components and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in older adults with MCI.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 234 older adults with MCI. Sarcopenia, gait speed, handgrip strength, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) were assessed according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Brain T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging was analyzed using voxel-based morphometry. Voxel-wise group comparisons were performed to identify GMV differences after adjustment age, sex, comorbidity, depressive symptoms, nutritional status, and total intracranial volume.ResultsSlower gait speed was significantly associated with lower GMV in the bilateral putamen and left superior frontal cortex. Lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV in the left inferior temporal cortex. No significant GMV differences were found by sarcopenia status or handgrip strength.ConclusionsSlower gait speed is associated with reduced GMV in motor-related brain regions, indicating early brain structural changes in older adults with MCI. Although lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the complex interactions between physical function and brain structure, emphasizing gait speed as a potential indicator of brain health in older adults with MCI.

cards.title: Practical consideration for the application of continuous glucose monitoring in older adults with insulin treated diabetes.
cards.abstract: The increased prevalence of diabetes among older individuals presents challenges for delivery of effective care for each older person with diabetes, for their families, and for healthcare providers. Along with established risks for microvascular and macrovascular disease, diabetes in older adults is also associated with risk factors for cognitive impairment and dementia, depression and physical frailty. Many of these risk factors are linked to hypoglycaemia, which in turn can be related to polypharmacy and overprescribing in older individuals. Use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) technology is proven to prevent hypoglycaemia and can mitigate many averse outcomes of frailty, both in type 1 diabetes (T1D and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Similarly, use of CGM improves glucose stability, reducing risks for vascular complications of diabetes. Intrinsic capacity (IC) is a concept used in geriatric medicine to provide an objective composite of physical and mental capacities that an older individual can draw on. Reduced IC is associated with a number of CGM metrics, including time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), rather than hypoglycaemia. Use of CGM can also facilitate telemedicine for adults with diabetes and frailty, reducing the burden of clinic attendance and increasing the frequency of healthcare contacts, further increasing the quality of care and quality of life for older individuals with diabetes. Given the significant benefits, the application of CGM alongside geriatric principles can be proposed to improve overall care and outcomes for people with diabetes.

cards.title: Live Fast, Die Old: Lowering Insulin Signalling During Development Can Speed Growth, Increase Reproduction and Lifespan, but Impair Environmental Sensing and Harm Offspring in Caenorhabditis elegans
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Genetic trade‐offs can constrain life‐history evolution resulting in the evolution of ageing. Reduced insulin/insulin‐like signalling (rIIS) improves somatic maintenance and dramatically increases lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans , but the effects on fitness are unclear. Here we used a novel experimental approach to show that, contrary to the prevailing paradigm, rIIS via daf‐2 RNAi during development can improve development, reproduction, survival, individual fitness, and population growth rate in the laboratory and semi‐natural conditions. However, developmental rIIS extends lifespan and improves fitness only in some temperatures, which explains why our results differ from previous findings. Furthermore, while developmental rIIS can improve a suite of life‐history traits in parents, it slows down offspring development. Finally, because rIIS interferes with environmental sensing and compromises adaptive developmental plasticity in response to stress, a central part of C. elegans life history in nature, the ability to sense the environment correctly during development comes at the cost of accelerated senescence. These results suggest the complexity of gene‐by‐environment interactions during development imposes constraints on molecular signalling networks leading to genetic trade‐offs across the life course that natural selection in late‐life is unable to resolve. However, these constraints can be resolved by artificially fine‐tuning gene expression at different ages.

cards.title: Cracking and Self-Healing in a Molecular Crystal Driven by Topochemical Polymerization.
cards.abstract: Topochemical reactions in molecular crystals are often accompanied by severe lattice strain, frequently leading to crystal fracture and loss of crystallinity. Here we report an unusual case in which heat-driven topochemical azide-alkyne cycloaddition (TAAC) polymerization in a non-centrosymmetric molecular crystal induces macroscopic cracking that is followed by autonomous self-healing. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals a regiospecific single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation to a helical polymer, despite large-amplitude molecular motion and anisotropic lattice deformation (a +19.9%, b -2.9%, c -13.3%). Face-indexing and morphology analysis correlate the crystallographic axes with macroscopic crystal dimensions, rationalizing the observed breadth expansion, length contraction, and cleavage along a weakly bound crystallographic plane. Mechanistically, crack formation originates from reaction-induced bimorphic lattice strain, while self-healing is driven by electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged fracture surfaces in the polar crystal, followed by continued intradomain polymerization that eliminates the bimorphic interface. Autonomous healing occurs upon completion of the topochemical polymerization in the crystalline material.

cards.title: Influence of Screw Access Hole Diameter and Preparation Method on the Fit and Fracture Resistance of Implant-Supported Monolithic Zirconia Crowns.
cards.abstract: To evaluate how screw access hole (SAH) presence, diameter, and preparation method affect marginal and internal fit and fracture resistance of implant-supported monolithic zirconia crowns. Seventy-two crowns were assigned to six groups (n=12): no SAH; 1-, 2-, or 3-mm presintered SAHs; a 1-mm SAH enlarged to 3 mm after cementation; or a 3-mm SAH prepared after cementation in crowns without an initial SAH. Marginal and internal fit was assessed in the first four groups by the silicone replica technique. After thermocycling and cyclic loading, fracture load, Weibull parameters, fracture patterns, and scanning electron microscopy findings were evaluated. Overall discrepancy and internal gap were greater without an SAH (184.7 and 182.1 μm) than with an SAH (54.7-65.9 and 60.1-71.1 μm) (P<.05), with no differences among SAH diameters (P>.05). Fracture loads were higher for no SAH and a 1-mm SAH than for all groups with 2- or 3-mm openings (P<.001). cards.title: Jellyfish-inspired multilayered responsive hydrogels via micelle-confined photopolymerization for underwater communication and emergency rescue.
cards.abstract: Hydrogels offer considerable promise as flexible sensors. However, maintaining their stable performance in complex underwater environments characterized by high pressure, high salinity, and temperature fluctuations remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the dynamic adaptive capabilities of jellyfish, this study reports a biomimetic composite conductive hydrogel with multi-level environmental responsiveness, synthesized via the copolymerization of N-isopropylacrylamide, 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid, and octadecyl methacrylate (OMA), incorporating color-changing microcapsules through a cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) micelle-confined polymerization strategy. The long alkyl chains of OMA promote hydrophobic association networks inside CTAB micelles, endowing the hydrogel with both high strength and exceptional stretchability (fracture strength of 690 kPa; elongation at break 1370%). This hydrogel achieves multi-parameter, synchronized responses to complex marine conditions: strong temperature sensitivity (-15.344%/°C), an electrical response to water-depth pressure (7.13 kPa-1, corresponding to 0-500 m water depth), stable tensile responsiveness, and reversible color changes visible to the naked eye. Building on these capabilities, the hydrogel can monitor human motion in conventional settings and also enable underwater sensing and Morse-code-based information transmission, demonstrating substantial potential for applications for underwater communication and emergency rescue applications.

cards.title: Stretching Training of Microgel-Reinforced Composite Hydrogel for Tunable Strain-Stiffening Property.
cards.abstract: Achieving tunable strain-stiffening in tough hydrogels via muscle-mimicking training remains a key challenge for nonlinear biomimetic mechanics. Microgel-reinforced composite hydrogels (MR-gels), combine rigid polyelectrolyte microspheres with a soft polyacrylamide matrix, offering an ideal platform for programming strain-stiffening behavior via hierarchical microsphere fracture. Here, we report that physical training controlling stretching amplitude and number of repetitions enables stable and tunable strain-stiffening in MR-gels. Unlike conventional expectations, a single stretch is insufficient, training equilibrium requires approximately 300 cycles. The resulting MR-gel exhibit stable and broadly tunable soft-to-stiff transition (0.4-3.1), strain-stiffening capacity (3.1-17.8), and modulus of the soft (240 to 40 kPa) and stiff (814 to 713 kPa) regimes, matching the nonlinear mechanics of diverse biological mechanicals. Mechanistically, the training mode achieves tunable strain-stiffening by controlling the degree of microgel fracture and entangled polymer chain sliding. At equilibrium, fragmented microgels form an interconnected string-like network via topological entanglements and covalent crosslinks, raising the fatigue threshold from 689.6 to 1269.8 J/m2. Furthermore, the trained MR-gel enables full envelopment of a high-speed falling iron ball for effective deceleration and superior impact cushioning. This work establishes a versatile strategy for programming mechanical behavior in soft materials, with broad implications for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and biomedicine.

cards.title: Oral Astilbin Nanogels Modulate Senescence-Associated CD4+ T Cells and Promote Treg Induction in Aged Mice with Colitis.
cards.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in older individuals is characterized by immune senescence and deteriorating intestinal homeostasis, both of which limit the efficacy of current therapies. Here, we develop fluorinated β-glucan/pectin nanogels (F2-Ast@NGs) for oral delivery of astilbin, a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. This multifunctional platform integrates gastrointestinal protection, colon-targeted release, and local immune modulation. The β-glucan shell preserves nanogel stability during upper gastrointestinal transit while enabling β-glucanase-responsive disassembly in the colon. Fluorocarbon segments enhance mucus penetration, and the pectin matrix prolongs colonic retention, promoting drug accumulation at inflamed sites. In aged mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, F2-Ast@NGs alleviate disease severity, attenuate senescence-associated features of colonic CD4+ T cells, and enhance Foxp3+ regulatory T cell (Treg) responses. Concurrently, the β-glucan/pectin nanogel matrix contributes to increased short-chain fatty acid production and favorable alterations in gut microbial composition. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of F2-Ast@NGs is markedly attenuated in Foxp3+ Treg-depleted mice, supporting an important role for Treg-mediated immunoregulation. Collectively, F2-Ast@NGs enable precise colonic delivery while coordinately remodeling the intestinal immune and microbial microenvironment, providing a promising oral nanotherapeutic strategy for colitis in aged hosts.

cards.title: Robust polyvinyl alcohol based multifunctional films with pH-responsive via electrostatic self-assembly of TOCNF and quaternary ammonium chitosan by loading apple polyphenol.
cards.abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based materials with pH-responsive colorimetric properties have attracted increasing attention for sustainable and intelligent packaging applications. Although numerous studies have reported PVA-based pH-responsive packaging films with antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, further optimization is still required in achieving a balanced integration of multiple functionalities, including antioxidant performance, antimicrobial efficiency, and long-term structural stability. Thus, a new kind of multifunctional PVA based composite film was fabricated via direct solvent casting combined with ultrasonication by mixing PVA with TEMPO-oxidized nanocellulose (TOCNF), quaternary ammonium chitosan (QCS), and apple polyphenol (APP). The effects of APP and QCS incorporation on the structural, mechanical, barrier, biological, and intelligent-responsive properties of the films were systematically investigated. The optimized PT-1.5(QA) film exhibited a balanced mechanical performance, with a tensile strength of approximately 8.1 MPa and an elongation at break of approximately 243%, attributed to the formation of intermolecularly associated polymer networks. Meanwhile, APP incorporation significantly enhanced the antioxidant and UV-shielding properties, achieving approximately 92.8% DPPH and 96.5% ABTS radical scavenging activities. Furthermore, the composite film exhibited enhanced barrier properties, strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, and distinct pH-responsive color changes over a broad pH range (1-12). Cytotoxicity evaluation confirmed good in vitro biocompatibility. Importantly, the composite film effectively delayed postharvest senescence and quality deterioration of litchi fruit, while maintaining favorable biodegradability. These findings highlight the potential of TOCNF/QCS/APP/PVA films as sustainable active and intelligent packaging materials for food preservation.

cards.title: Association of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and physical frailty with cardiovascular health in US adults: A cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Evidence on the association between cardiovascular health (CVH) and frailty remains limited, and the role of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) in this relationship is not fully understood. This study aimed to examine the association between frailty and CVH and to investigate the independent association of serum 25(OH)D and its potential interaction with frailty. This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2007 to 2018, including 8015 adults aged ≥20 years. Frailty was assessed using a frailty index, and CVH was evaluated based on the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 metrics. Multinomial logistic regression models accounting for the complex survey design were applied to assess associations. Frailty was highly prevalent in the study population. After multivariable adjustment, higher frailty levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of poor CVH in a graded manner. Serum 25(OH)D levels were independently and inversely associated with poor CVH. Stratified analyses showed that the association between frailty and CVH varied by sex and 25(OH)D status. However, no statistically significant multiplicative interaction between frailty and serum 25(OH)D levels was observed. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer CVH in US adults, demonstrating a clear dose-response relationship. Serum 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with CVH, whereas no statistically significant multiplicative interaction between frailty and serum 25(OH)D was observed. These findings highlight the importance of addressing multiple modifiable risk factors to improve CVH.

cards.title: Sarcopenia in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: A cross-sectional radiological and functional assessment.
cards.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is a significant complication that impairs lung function and increases morbidity. Sarcopenia, characterized by the loss of muscle mass and function, is commonly found in chronic diseases such as systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with SSc-ILD and investigate its cross-sectional associations with pulmonary function test parameters, estimated pulmonary artery pressure and quantitative radiological lung involvement. In this cross-sectional study conducted between 2024 and 2025, 40 patients with systemic sclerosis (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) and high-resolution computed tomography-confirmed interstitial lung disease were evaluated. Patients with overlap myositis, acute infections, severe orthopedic/neurological limitations, and end-stage organ failure were excluded. Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 criteria using muscle mass (bioelectrical impedance analysis) and handgrip strength measurements. Pulmonary function tests (FVC, single-breath transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide), echocardiographic sPAP estimations, and quantitative high-resolution computed tomography lung density analysis were performed. These findings highlight the potential impact of sarcopenia on lung function and the association of sarcopenia with radiological findings in SSc-ILD SSc-ILD. Among the 40 analyzed patients (mean age: 55.8 ± 10.8 years, 85.0% female, mean BMI: 28.7 ± 5.0 kg/m2), sarcopenia was identified in 10 patients (25.0%). Patients with and without sarcopenia were compared to analyze its effects on pulmonary function and radiological findings. Patients with sarcopenia had significantly lower lung diffusion capacity (transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide) and forced vital capacity % values and significantly higher radiological lung involvement compared to those without sarcopenia (P = .004, P = .023, and P = .035, respectively). Systolic pulmonary artery pressure was also significantly higher in sarcopenic patients (P = .031). Additionally, fat-free mass index, fat-free mass, muscle mass, and handgrip strength were significantly lower in sarcopenic patients (P < .001).

cards.title: Socioeconomic position and preoperative characteristics in Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants: a UK national observational study.
cards.abstract: Patients from more deprived backgrounds experience poorer postoperative outcomes. We analysed preoperative characteristics in UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants according to socioeconomic position to explore opportunities for targeted interventions. Participants were adults aged ≥18 yr undergoing major elective surgery at UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme sites. Socioeconomic position was determined using postcode data and the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) standardised aggregate scale of area-level deprivation. Associations between IMD position and patient characteristics, health behaviours, and comorbidities were analysed using descriptive statistics with appropriate parametric and nonparametric testing. Of 55 938 participants included, quintile 1 (most deprived) represented the smallest subgroup (14.2%), with recruitment varying by region and site. Median age was 66 yr with IMD 1 participants 5 yr younger (62 yr) than IMD 5 (67 yr). Deprivation gradients (IMD 5 to 1) were seen for home ownership, occupation, and educational attainment. Prevalences of smoking, inactivity, and obesity increased from IMD 5 to 1. Higher prevalences of major long-term conditions including diabetes mellitus, heart failure, stroke, and ASA physical status 3-4 were observed in more deprived quintiles. Prevalence rates of dementia and renal impairment were similar across quintiles despite the age gradient. Notably, the proportions of patients living with frailty and disability increased with deprivation. Patients presenting for major surgery from more deprived backgrounds do so in poorer overall health. They can encounter barriers to both research participation and available preoperative support. Addressing this unmet need to prevent widening perioperative health inequalities requires interventions tailored to the patient's socioeconomic context.

cards.title: Exact solutions produce a full picture of crack behavior in dynamic fracture.
cards.abstract: The theory of fracture normally describes cracks as propagating discontinuities in a continuous medium where stresses vanish on free crack faces. We describe cracks instead at the particle level and obtain more general analytical results than were available previously. Using dynamical crack solutions for widely varying dissipation and general isotropic elastic moduli, we construct a catalog of 100,000 crack solutions and from it a general picture of when cracks are stable. For our exactly solvable model of dynamic fracture, the surface wave speed sometimes sets an upper limit on crack velocity, as expected. However tensile cracks traveling faster than the shear wave speed are possible and their stability is enhanced when they travel along weak interfaces, when dissipation increases, and when system sizes are small. Our results reinforce a standard view that supersonic cracks require supersonic energy transport near the tip, but we show it can come from dissipation as well as hyperelasticity.

cards.title: "It's quite a dark, long journey to the light at the end of the tunnel": a qualitative study of children's experiences of living with Long COVID.
cards.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic had a significant impact on global health, with some individuals experiencing long-term health effects known as Long COVID. This study explored the lived experiences of children with Long COVID, providing further insight into the impacts and needs within this group. Semi-structured interviews, facilitated by children's drawings, were conducted with 15 children. Thematic analysis was used to analyse the data. Four themes were identified: (1) 'I feel completely different': the physical and emotional burden of Long COVID (2) 'Like the buzz of people speaking and I can't concentrate': education challenges created by Long COVID, (3) 'I'm on my third friend group since I've had COVID': disrupted relationships and fractured connections and (4) 'What can I do now to get myself better?': managing life with Long COVID. These findings reveal a narrative of loss and change during key developmental periods. This research illustrates the life-altering impact of Long COVID on children across many domains. Despite these challenges children were hopeful for the future. A multi-faceted approach to management is needed, including utilising technology to aid self-management strategies such as pacing and to support social connection, as well as psychological support and school adjustments.

cards.title: Nanoscale Analysis of Large Deformation of Tough Microparticle-Based Polymer Films Revealed by Atomic Force Microscopy and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering.
cards.abstract: For understanding the mechanical properties of polymer materials and establishing design guidelines, elucidation of nanoscale structural changes under deformation is crucial. This study focused on microparticle-based polymer films exhibiting high fracture energies of several tens of MJ/m3 without additives, and the influence of intraparticle crosslinking on nanoscale deformation was investigated using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The improvement of an AFM equipped with a stretching device enabled nanoscale observation of films under strain conditions of up to 700%. As intraparticle crosslinking increased, a trade-off was observed in which the Young's modulus increased while the fracture strain decreased. AFM observations showed that, although the increase in intraparticle crosslinking density did not significantly affect the deformation of each microparticle or particle clusters constituting the assembly, their surface roughness increased with increasing crosslinking density. SAXS measurements under tensile deformation revealed that the strain-induced structural anisotropy decreased with increasing intraparticle crosslinking density, suggesting suppressed nanoscale deformation within highly crosslinked microparticles. These results suggest that the trade-off in macroscopic mechanical properties is associated with a change in nanoscale deformation, from smooth elongation to surface roughening, highlighting that particle design is an important factor contributing to tough microparticle-based film properties.

cards.title: Rhenium-Based β-Galactosidase Probe Allows Senescence Profiling by Mass Cytometry.
cards.abstract: Mass cytometry is an attractive analytical technique for the study of cellular senescence due to its ability to simultaneously interrogate the multiple biomarkers necessary to define senescent phenotypes. However, measuring senescence-associated β-Galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) activity, the gold standard biomarker for detection of senescent cells, requires a functional mass cytometry detectable probe compatible with an antibody-based panel. Herein, we report a small-molecule mass cytometry probe for SA-β-Gal, ReGal, that uses a piano-stool rhenium complex as a mass tag. We demonstrate that the probe measures β-Gal activity in vitro and in cellulo with minimal background signal. We further show that the probe improves the discrimination of senescence-induced mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) against untreated cells compared to using only antibody-based mass cytometry reagents. Finally, we demonstrate that the probe reveals a putatively senescent sub-population of mouse peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), which is enriched in old vs. young mice, that could not be segmented by antibody-based reagents alone.

cards.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is associated with higher bone mineral density: results from NHANES.
cards.abstract: We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to investigate the association between metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and bone mineral density (BMD) among U.S. adults. Our findings indicated that participants with MASLD had higher BMD than those without MASLD. Given the stigma associated with the term "NAFLD," experts participating in a Delphi consensus proposed renaming the condition "MASLD". Nevertheless, the association between MASLD and BMD remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between MASLD and BMD. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6470 participants aged 18 years or older using data from the 2005 to 2010, 2013 to 2014, and 2017 to 2018 cycles of the NHANES. MASLD was defined according to diagnostic criteria established through a Delphi consensus. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of MASLD with femoral neck and total femur BMD, while logistic regression analysis was used to investigate the association between MASLD and osteoporosis. Among the 6470 participants, the mean age was 53.16 ± 17.27 years, 49.54% were male, and 23.52% met the criteria for MASLD. After multivariable adjustment, participants with MASLD had higher femoral neck BMD (β = 0.0238; 95% CI, 0.0154-0.0321) and total femur BMD (β = 0.0332; 95% CI, 0.0244-0.0419) than those without MASLD. In subgroup analyses, participants with individual cardiometabolic components of MASLD, including BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, also exhibited higher femoral BMD after multivariable adjustment. Moreover, multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that MASLD was significantly associated with lower odds of osteoporosis. Our findings suggest that participants with MASLD have higher BMD compared to those without MASLD.

cards.title: Reliability, Readability, and Safety of Generative AI Chatbots for Osteoporosis Health Counseling: A Multidimensional Cross-Sectional Comparative Study.
cards.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots are increasingly used for health information, but their reliability, readability, and safety in osteoporosis counseling remain uncertain. This study compared four widely available chatbots under standardized conditions. Twenty-five standardized osteoporosis questions were submitted once to ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Copilot, and Perplexity Pro, generating 100 responses. Two model-blinded specialists evaluated the final responses using DISCERN, EQIP, the Global Quality Scale, JAMA benchmarks, and the NOHARM framework. Six automated indices assessed readability. Because each question was answered by all four models, outcomes were compared using Friedman tests, followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment. DISCERN scores differed across models (p < 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.82, 95% CI 0.76-0.89). Median scores were 55.0 for Perplexity Pro, 54.0 for Copilot, 44.0 for Gemini 2.5 Pro, and 42.0 for ChatGPT-5. JAMA benchmark scores did not differ significantly (p = 0.63). All six readability indices differed across models (all p < 0.001). Perplexity Pro had the highest median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score at 16.18, whereas Copilot had the lowest at 9.49; all models exceeded the sixth-grade benchmark. The qualitative safety assessment also identified clinically relevant omissions and an unsupported claim. In this set of osteoporosis questions, retrieval-enabled systems achieved higher scores on selected information-quality measures but produced more difficult text. These findings are limited to the tested models, prompts, and evaluation period and do not establish a universal effect of retrieval augmentation.
