cards.title: Mechanical properties and failure characteristics of geocells: A comparative experimental study.
cards.abstract: The tensile performance of geocells depends on the mechanical responses of both cell walls and junctions. Three commercial geocells, liquation-welded polypropylene (LW), injection-molded polyester (IM), and ultrasonic-welded high-density polyethylene (UW), were examined through tensile testing, macroscopic observation, and scanning electron microscopy of cell-wall fracture surfaces. Five configurations were used: cell-wall tension, junction-inclusive tension, and junction seam, shear, and split tests. The cell-wall peak strengths of LW, IM, and UW were 143.03 ± 4.43, 185.61 ± 7.96, and 39.42 ± 2.41 kN/m, respectively. Including a junction changed the strengths by +28.99%, -59.79%, and -23.76%. The LW and IM cell walls lost load rapidly after the peak. UW exhibited necking and extended post-yield deformation. SEM revealed microfibrillar bundles in LW, a smooth layered surface in IM, and dense drawn microfibrils in UW. Under junction-inclusive tension, LW tore near the raised-tab edge, IM cracked through the ligaments between the holes, and UW fractured at a weld-wall boundary. LW provided the highest seam and shear strengths of 66.16 ± 4.20 and 146.02 ± 8.46 kN/m. IM provided the highest split strength of 158.55 ± 10.34 kN/m. UW showed lower junction strengths but reached 343.09 ± 13.72% rupture strain under shear. Under seam and shear loading, LW failed near the tab-wall transition, while IM fractured from hole edges. UW failed within the weld region under seam loading and at a weld-wall boundary under shear loading. Under split loading, failure occurred at the heat-fused interface in LW, the molded body in IM, and the central weld in UW.

cards.title: Research on the design and mechanical properties of extended constant resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolts.
cards.abstract: To address the premature fracture of anchor bolts caused by the mismatched yielding distance between anchor bolts and hydraulic supports in the advanced support section of rock burst-prone roadways, an elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt was designed-with its yielding distance specifically coordinated to match that of hydraulic supports. ABAQUS numerical simulation was utilized to investigate the mechanical characteristics of this novel anchor bolt under static loading, as well as under varying impact energies and impact velocities. A comparative analysis was further performed against the mechanical performance of conventional anchor bolts. The results reveal the following: Under static loading, the elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt exhibits a fracture load of 160.6 kN, a fracture displacement of 523.2 mm, an elongation rate of 20.93%, and an energy absorption capacity of 69.7 kJ. Under impact velocities within 9 m/s, the impact velocity has little effect on the fracture load, elongation, and energy absorption of constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolts, while the impact resistance time exhibits a nonlinear decreasing trend with increasing impact velocity. Under both static and dynamic loading conditions, the extended constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolt exhibits superior impact resistance and can effectively address the problem of premature bolt fracture caused by the mismatch between the bolt yielding distance and that of the hydraulic support in the three-level energy-absorbing support system. The findings provide a new perspective for bolt design.

cards.title: Numerical study on infill fracturing of mature wells under free-drainage boundary conditions.
cards.abstract: Infill fracturing of mature wells involves re-fracturing within previously stimulated clusters, targeting unstimulated regions of the parent well's fracture network. This strategy sustainably enhances hydrocarbon recovery from depleted reservoirs without the environmental footprint of new drilling. Establishing a numerical simulation model for this process is essential for optimization. In this study, a numerical model for mature well infill fracturing was developed based on the extended finite element method and a free-drainage boundary module. The results indicate that prior production from mature wells primarily affects the fracture length and curvature in the infill wells. As infill fracturing-induced fractures propagate toward the far-field region, they are significantly influenced by the heterogeneous pore pressure distribution in the reservoir. This leads to a pronounced increase in fracture curvature. Compared with conventional fracturing, the curvature of fractures under infill fracturing is approximately 30% higher within the same simulation time, while the fracture length is notably shorter. With the increase in production time, fractures in infill wells tend to exhibit greater tortuosity. This enhanced complexity allows for more effective contact between the fractures and the reservoir, thereby improving the production potential of the infill wells to some extent.

cards.title: The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
cards.abstract: To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.

cards.title: Thioredoxin-2 Alleviates Osteoporosis by Restraining FOXO3a Nuclear Translocation.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent age- and disease-associated skeletal disorder characterized by bone loss, remodeling imbalance, and vascular niche deterioration, yet how endothelial redox dysfunction drives this process remains unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial thioredoxin-2 (TRX2) as an endothelial safeguard against osteoporotic bone loss. TRX2 was markedly reduced in aging bone vascular endothelial cells, and endothelial Trx2 deficiency accelerated skeletal degeneration by suppressing osteogenic activity and enhancing osteoclastogenesis. Mechanistically, TRX2 directly bound FOXO3a through a redox-sensitive Cys90-Cys31 disulfide interaction, retaining FOXO3a at the mitochondrial outer membrane and limiting its nuclear translocation. TRX2 loss or oxidative stress disrupted this complex, enabling FOXO3a-dependent transcriptional activation of tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL) and generating a pro-osteoclastogenic vascular niche. TRAIL neutralization or endothelial TRX2 restoration attenuated ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis by preserving angiogenic-osteogenic coupling. These findings establish the endothelial TRX2-FOXO3a-TRAIL axis as a vascular redox checkpoint and potential therapeutic target for osteoporosis.

cards.title: Very early swimming prevents the establishment of musculoskeletal dysfunction in a rodent model of Cerebral Palsy.
cards.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is characterized by motor and cognitive impairments resulting from injuries to the central nervous system. Targeting early muscle activity during critical developmental periods may prevent musculoskeletal damage associated with CP through muscle-derived antioxidant and trophic factors released upon activation. We investigated whether early-life swimming (SW) prevents the establishment of musculoskeletal deficits in a CP rat model. Pregnant Wistar rats received intraperitoneal injections of lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 200 mg/kg) on embryonic days 18 and 19. At birth (P0), CP pups were subjected to 20 min of anoxia (37°C) and underwent hindlimbs movement restriction from P2 to P21 (16 h/day). From P7 to P21, animals performed daily swimming sessions (from 5 to a maximum of 30 min/day) in a tank filled with water (32°C). Locomotor function was assessed using Rota-rod and open field; H-reflex excitability, spinal cord tissue and gastrocnemius muscles were collected at P29 for biochemical and histological analyses. Early SW improved gross motor abilities in CP animals without major effects on exploratory drive. Although SW did not rescue CP-induced sarcopenia in soleus/gastrocnemius muscles, it significantly attenuated hyperreflexia and prevented spinal cord impairments in synaptic markers induced by the model. CP increased the expression of oxidative stress-related genes in skeletal muscle. Swimming favored more mature-like muscle architecture despite persistent muscle mass deficits and increased the mRNA expression of genes involved in antioxidant function and myokines. Early swimming mitigated key features of CP in rats and has high therapeutic potential when used in this critical developmental window.

cards.title: Body Composition, Physical Activity and Energy Requirements Estimated Using Two Isotopic Methods in Old and Adult Beagle Dogs.
cards.abstract: Energy requirements (ER) are known to decline as dogs age into the senior stage. However, the implications of body composition and physical activity (PA) on this parameter remain poorly investigated. The aim of this study was to evaluate ER, body composition, water turnover rate (WTR), and voluntary PA by triaxial accelerometers in adults (5.2 ± 1.75 years; 11.8 ± 0.65 kg; body condition score (BCS) 5 ± 0.2/9) and old Beagle dogs (14.2 ± 2.65 years; 12.5 ± 0.37 kg; BCS 5 ± 0.31/9). The ER were assessed by the food intake to constant body weight (FI), 13C-Bicarbonate (13C-Bic) and doubly labelled water (DLW) methods. Animals were fed to maintain a constant body weight for 30 days. Food intake was recorded, and the diet's metabolisable energy was determined via total faecal collection method. Masks were used to measure 13C in expired air after 13C-Bic enrichment. Body water was enriched with 2H and 18O, and isotopes elimination was evaluated after 7, 10, and 15 days. ER was similar between methods (p = 0.99), but 30% higher for adult (511.9 ± 4.72 kJ/kg0.75/day) than old dogs (389.0 ± 5.07 kJ/kg0.75/day; p < 0.001). WTR was higher for adult (134.58 mL/kg0.75/day) than old dogs (106.51 mL/kg0.75/day; p = 0.005). Despite similar BCS, old dogs showed lower lean and higher fat mass, suggesting sarcopenia (p < 0.01). Old dogs presented lower PA (p < 0.01), which, may have contributed to their lower lean mass, ER and WTR. Considering that 13C-Bic and DLW resulted in similar estimations of energy expenditure to the FI method, the most appropriate approach might depend on experimental conditions and objectives. The implications of reduced ER on food and nutrient intake and its relationship with lower WTR, sarcopenia and obesity development, highlight the need for targeted nutritional recommendations for ageing dogs.
